How this book is laid out

Why it works this way

The owner's decision behind what the screen does, with its number, for example D27-249.

Watch out

The unusual cases: what happens with no connection, and what a role cannot see.

  • Steps are numbered. Do them in order.
  • Words in bold are exactly what the screen shows: a button, a heading, a menu entry.
  • A message the system shows is written like this: “No arrivals today”.
  • Each figure is a picture of the screen. The orange numbers in the picture match the numbered list under it.
  • A dash (-) on a screen means the system does not hold that figure. It is never a zero.
  • An address such as /h/5EL/arrivals is what follows pms.fidatohotels.com in the browser's address bar.
Chapter A0

Getting started

For your first day. How to sign in, how the screen is laid out, how to find any screen, and what happens when the internet drops.

A0.1Signing in and out

Fidato PMS runs in a web browser, on a desk computer, a tablet or a phone. Nothing needs to be installed. Your property gives you an email and a password. Use only your own: everything you do is saved under your name.

To sign in

  1. Open the browser and go to pms.fidatohotels.com.
  2. Type your email in Email.
  3. Type your password in Password. To see what you typed, click the eye at the end of the box (Show password). Click it again to hide it. It starts hidden because the desk screen faces the lobby.
  4. Click Sign in. A small spinner turns on the button while it works. Then your first screen opens (A0.2).

When you open the system on a device where you are already signed in, the screen says “Checking your session…” for a moment, then opens where you were.

Watch out

  • “That email and password do not match.” The message is the same whether the email or the password is wrong, so check both. (A different message for each would tell a stranger which emails belong to staff.)
  • “No active staff record for this account.” Your password was right, but your account is switched off or not set up at any property. Ask your general manager.
  • Forgot your password? The page says it: “Trouble signing in? Your general manager can reset your password from the People screen.” (On a phone the line is under the form and stops at “reset your password”.)
  • “Set a longer password”. If your role was raised to owner, Admin or General Manager and your password is shorter than 10 characters, this box appears right after you sign in. It cannot be closed. Type a new password and click Set it. Everybody else needs at least 8 characters.
  • The first sign-in on a device needs the internet. After that, if the line drops, a reload keeps you signed in (A0.8).

To sign out

  1. Click your name at the top right. This is the account menu.
  2. Click Sign out. The sign-in page opens.

Closing the browser or the tab does not sign you out. On a desk computer that other people use, always sign out when you leave.

Watch out

  • Signing out clears the lists kept on the computer, so the next person does not open on your screens.
  • If you made changes with no connection and they are not sent yet, they stay on the computer, under your name. The sign-in page says “1 change is kept on this computer and will be sent when you sign in here again.” They go when you sign in on this computer again, not on another one.

Two-step sign-in: a code from your phone as well

With two-step sign-in on, signing in takes your password and a 6-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone (Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator, both free). Somebody who learns your password still cannot get in without your phone. Anybody may switch it on for themselves. The owner may also make it required for the owner, Admins, GMs and Accountants (A17.13); then the system asks you to set it up before anything else.

To set it up

  1. Put Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator on your phone, from the phone's app store.
  2. In the system, click your name at the top right, then Two-step sign-in, then Set it up.
  3. In the app, add an account and scan the square code on the screen. If the phone cannot scan it, choose “enter a setup key” in the app and type the key shown under the code.
  4. Type the 6 digits the app now shows in Code from the app and click Go on.
  5. Ten recovery codes appear. Each one lets you in once if your phone is lost or not with you. Write them down or print them, keep them away from the phone, and click I have kept them. They are never shown again.

To sign in with it

  1. Sign in with your email and password as always.
  2. The Two-step sign-in page opens. Open the app on your phone and type the 6 digits it shows for this account.
  3. Click Go on. Your first screen opens.

Without the phone, click Use a recovery code instead and type one of your ten. Each works once. The code is asked once per sign-in on each device, not on every screen.

Watch out

  • “That code is not right. The app shows a new one every 30 seconds: type the one showing now.” Type the code showing now. A code already used is not taken again; wait for the next one.
  • “Five wrong codes in a quarter of an hour...” Wait 15 minutes, then try again. Every code typed is kept on record.
  • Lost your phone and your recovery codes? The owner, or an Admin at your hotel, switches two-step sign-in off for you on the People screen (A16.6), with a reason. Then you set it up again on your new phone.
  • “Your role needs two-step sign-in. Set it up to go on.” The owner made it required for your role. The page shows the same three steps as above; nothing else opens until it is done.
  • Your account menu's Two-step sign-in says whether it is on for you and how many recovery codes are left.

Why it works this way

Longer passwords for the people who reach the most: D27-243 (10 characters for the owner, Admin and GM, 8 for others) and D27-245 (a person given one of those roles sets a 10-character password at their next sign-in). Clearing the computer at sign-out was one of the four security fixes the owner asked for before the release: D27-88. Unsent work stays under the name of the person who did it, because the bill and the ledger never forget who made an entry (the owner, 28 September). Two-step sign-in is the safety work the owner put before every feature, D27-384; built in our own system, because Firebase's needs a paid plan, and off until the owner requires it, so switching it on locks nobody out: D27-396.

A0.2Your first screen and the Start here card

After signing in you land on your first screen. For most people it is the Dashboard. It can also be Rooms or Calendar. Your general manager sets it for each person, and you can change your own.

To change where you start

  1. Click your name at the top right.
  2. Under Start on, click Dashboard, Rooms or Calendar. A tick shows the one chosen.
  3. The message “You will start on Rooms. From your next sign-in, on any device.” confirms it.

Some people have no Dashboard, because it shows the hotel's revenue and their day starts at their own work. Unless they chose Rooms or Calendar themselves, they land on their own work: housekeeping on Housekeeping, the chef and the kitchen manager on Kitchen, the waiter and the bar on Tables, the Inventory Manager on the Store.

The Start here card

Reception, housekeeping, the waiter and the chef see a card called Start here on their first screen. It lists the jobs they will do most. Each line opens the screen where the job is done and says which button finishes it. (Reception's card is in A1.9.)

  1. Click a line to go to that screen. A job done on the screen you are already on says “On this screen” instead.
  2. When you know your way, click Got it. The card goes away: “Put away. Bring it back any time from your account menu.”
  3. To see it again: account menu, Show Start here again.

Why it works this way

The first screen per person, set by the GM and changeable by the person: the owner, 14 September. No Dashboard for housekeeping, the kitchen, the restaurant floor and the store, because it carries revenue: the owner, 15 September, made firm in D27-141. A Start here card for reception, housekeeping, the waiter and the chef, none for the GM or the owner, gone when they tap Got it: the owner, 15 September.

A0.3The screen at a glance

Every screen has the same frame. Learn it once.

PartWhat it does
The menu (dark, on the left)Your working menu, in sections such as Front desk and Bookings. Click a section's name to fold or open it: one click does it, also for a section that starts folded (Point of sale, Banquet, Laundry, Spa, Reports, System, Sales and marketing and Distribution); the computer remembers. A folded section shows how many screens it holds. The section holding the screen you are on never folds. Only the Front office menu starts with sections folded; the Restaurant's and Settings' menus are short, and start open. Collapse at the foot shrinks the menu to icons.
Find a screen… (top)Finds any screen you may open, and guests and bookings (A0.6). Ctrl K opens it from anywhere.
The space switcher (top right)Front office · Restaurant · Settings. Only shown to people who have two or more (A0.4).
The bellYour notifications: things the system or a colleague wants you to know.
Your name and roleThe account menu: your property, where you start, Start here, and Sign out.
A yellow line under the top barOnly when the hotel's business date is behind the real date, on every screen, with a link to Night audit for those who may open it (A1.1).
An orange line under the top barOnly for the owner, an Admin or the GM, while they walk through Set up this hotel: it names the step and has Back to setup (A17.2).
The pageThe heading says which screen this is. The Dashboard, Rooms and Calendar show the business date just above it, for example “Business date · Friday, 9 October 2026”, and the property's name just under it.

Your menu is short on purpose. It lists the screens you work from, not everything you are allowed. Everything else you may open is still one search away: if your menu leaves anything out, a Find a screen button sits at its foot. The owner, Admin and GM also see entries marked Not built yet: services planned but not built. They open a page that says what the service will do.

Why it works this way

A shorter menu per person, with nothing lost because every screen stays findable: the owner, 15 September. Housekeeping's menu gained Rooms and the kitchen manager's the Store in D22-19. Services not built yet sit in the section they will belong to, marked “Not built yet”, for the owner, admins and GMs only: D27-87. Sections that a property may not even have (banquet, laundry, spa, reports, system) start folded, and so do point of sale, sales and marketing and distribution: the owner, 19 September. A section opens or folds on the first click, even one that came folded, which the first click used to leave folded: D27-316.

A0.4The three spaces: Front office, Restaurant, Settings

The system has three parts, each with its own menu. They are called spaces.

SpaceWhat is in itOpens onWho has it
Front officeRooms, bookings, guests, bills, housekeeping, reports: the hotel's work.The DashboardEverybody except the waiter, the chef and the kitchen manager.
RestaurantTables, Table bookings, Till, Terminal, Kitchen, Menu, Close restaurant day, Charges to rooms, Restaurant setup (each person sees their own share).The top of your Restaurant menuOwner, Admin, GM, Hotel Manager, Accountant, Viewer. Reception only where the hotel has “Reception can use the POS” on. The waiter, the chef and the kitchen manager have the Restaurant only. Nobody, at a hotel without a restaurant.
SettingsHow the hotel is set up, in groups: Property, Rooms, Rates and tax, Money, Lists, Front desk, Messages, People and security, Modules and connections.The first settings page you may open (for the owner, Profile)Owner, Admin and GM.

To move between spaces

  1. Find the switcher: at a desk or tablet it is in the top bar; on a phone it is at the top of the menu drawer (A0.7).
  2. Click the space's name. The highlighted name is the space you are in.
  3. In Settings, Back to front office at the top of the menu also takes you back.

In Settings, an entry with a small arrow (↗) opens a Front office screen, for example Rates or Cancellation terms. It takes you out of Settings.

The Restaurant's own menu section is Point of sale. The waiter, the chef and the kitchen manager have the Restaurant only, so their whole working menu is there: Guest requests as well, Kitchen stock for the chef and the kitchen manager, and for the kitchen manager the Store.

Watch out

  • No switcher at all? You have one space only. Housekeeping, the Inventory Manager and the Revenue Manager work in the Front office alone; the waiter, the chef and the kitchen manager in the Restaurant alone.
  • The Hotel Manager has Front office and Restaurant, not Settings.
  • The spaces change only how the menu is grouped. They do not change who may open a screen.

Why it works this way

Three spaces, each with its own menu, and who switches: D27-249. The details (↗ links in Settings, the Accountant and the Viewer getting Front office and Restaurant, the restaurant staff keeping one space with no switcher, the switcher at the top of the phone's menu drawer): D27-256.

A0.5Choosing the hotel

Every screen works on one property at a time. The property's short code is in the address, for example /h/5EL/arrivals for 5 Elements Akkalkot. Its name is under the heading of the Dashboard, Rooms and Calendar.

Most staff work at one property. The system opens on it, and the account menu shows it under Property (its name, then its code and city).

If you work at more than one property

  • Account menu. Under Property, each property you may work in is listed; a tick marks the chosen one. Click another and the same screen opens for that hotel: the address, the lists and the business date change together. On one record (a guest's bill, one equipment item) you land on that hotel's matching list instead (In house, Equipment). If you may not open that screen at the other hotel, its first screen opens. On the Dashboard and in Settings, the screen stays and the property changes.
  • Dashboard. A Property box at the top right picks which hotel the Dashboard's figures are for. It changes the Dashboard only; the rest of the system stays on the property it was on. The four tiles at the top then open that hotel's lists (A1.2).
  • The owner and Admin. All properties, in the Across properties section of the menu, shows every property on one page. Click a property's name to open its Rooms.

A test hotel

A test hotel is a practice copy of a real hotel, for learning the system without touching the real one, for example “Hotel Amrapali · TEST”. It starts with the real hotel's whole setup (rooms, rates, the menu, settings) and no guests, bookings or money.

  • The orange stripe. On every screen of a test hotel, an orange stripe across the top says “TEST HOTEL · practice only · nothing here is real”. It cannot be closed. While you see it, nothing you do counts.
  • TEST beside its name. In the account menu under Property, in the Dashboard's Property box and on People, a test hotel has TEST beside its name. It is never in All properties.
  • Its paper. Every bill, KOT, invoice, credit note, report and Form III printed there says “TEST · NOT VALID” in large letters and carries no GSTIN.
  • Nothing leaves it. Send voucher, Send check-in link, Send invoice and the review requests are off, with the line “This is a test hotel: nothing is sent from it.”
  • Who works in it. Only the people the owner or a group administrator puts in it. Somebody added on People with Test on works only in test hotels, never the real one. A member of staff may also be given the test hotel as a second place.

The owner and group administrators make a test hotel on Properties, under the real hotel: Make a test hotel. Once it is made, the same place has Open (go to it), Reset (deletes everything done in it, keeping its setup and its people; type RESET to go on) and Re-copy setup (brings the real hotel's rooms, rates, menu and settings again, deleting the test activity first; type RE-COPY).

Watch out

  • Each property has its own business date. Two hotels can be on different days (A1.1).
  • Your role can be different at each property, for example GM at one and Reception at another. The screens use your role at the property in the address, the same rule the server uses.

Why it works this way

The property is in the address so a booking can be linked to and a task survives switching. The role read for the property in the address: D26-13. All properties on one page for the owner, in place of the table that was at the Dashboard's foot: D27-243. Picking a property opens the same screen for it, address, lists and date together: D27-271; from a record, that hotel's matching list: D27-273. Test hotels inside the live system, one per real hotel, kept apart from everything real: D27-296.

A0.6Find a screen (Ctrl K)

The quickest way to anywhere. It finds every screen you may open, whether it is in your menu or not, and, if you work with bookings, guests and bookings too.

  1. Press Ctrl and K together (on a Mac, ⌘ K). Or click Find a screen… at the top. On a phone, tap the magnifying glass.
  2. Type a word: the screen's name, or the word you would say. Old and trade words work too: folio finds Folios, day end finds Close restaurant day, floor finds Tables.
  3. Move with the arrow keys ↑ ↓ and press Enter, or click the line.

Each line shows the screen's section on the right (not on a phone). A screen that is yours to open but not in your menu says “Not in your menu”. A service not built yet says “Not built yet”.

To find a guest or a booking

  1. Open Find a screen. If you work with bookings, the box says “Find a screen, a guest or a booking”.
  2. Type at least three letters of the guest's name or of the booking reference, or at least four digits of their phone number.
  3. Up to eight bookings appear under Bookings, below the screens: guests in the house first, then those coming, then those gone. Each line shows the guest, the reference, the dates and the room, and its status on the right (Due in, In house …).
  4. Click one. It opens in All bookings with its panel open.

If nothing matches: “Nothing called that. Try a shorter word, or what a guest would call it.” (For somebody who does not work with bookings it says “No screen called that”.)

Watch out

  • It lists only what your role may open. A screen you may not open is not listed at all.
  • Bookings are found only by people who work with bookings. A phone number finds a guest only for people who may see guests' details; for others the phone is blank.

Why it works this way

“Off the menu, still findable by search” was the owner's condition for shorter menus (15 September). Finding guests and bookings from the same box: D27-239. Guests' phone and email kept from roles that read bookings but not guests: D27-143.

A0.7At the desk and on a phone

It is the same system at the same address on every device. Only the layout changes with the width of the screen.

 Wide: a desk computer (1024 px and wider)Medium: a tablet held upright (640 to 1023 px)Phone (under 640 px)
MenuAlways on the leftHidden; open it with the menu button (☰, Open navigation) at the top left
Space switcherIn the top barAt the top of the menu drawer
Find a screenA box with Ctrl KA boxA magnifying glass
Lists (Arrivals, In house…)A table or cards: your choice, with the two small buttons beside the search box (Show as a table, Show as cards). This device remembers it.Always cards
RoomsFour tiles across, five from 1280 pxTwo across
CalendarThe whole fortnightThe fortnight; if it does not fit, the chart scrolls sideways inside itselfThree nights and the edge of a fourth; swipe night by night. The room column stays put.

A tablet turned sideways is often 1024 px or wider, and then looks like the desk.

Two things follow you to every device, because they are saved on the server: where you start (A0.2), and whether Rooms and Calendar are grouped by Room type or Floor (A1.7).

Watch out

  • “A new version is ready. Reload when you are between guests to pick it up.” The system never reloads by itself, so it cannot interrupt a check-in. Reload the page when you have a quiet moment.
  • “Ready to work offline.” appears once on a new device: from then on the screens open even without a connection (A0.8).

Why it works this way

The web version first, the desktop and phone apps later: D21-98. On a phone the layout changes rather than squeezing: D22-49. Lists as cards on every phone: the owner, 16 September. Room type or Floor remembered per person: the owner, 14 September. The switcher at the top of the phone's drawer: D27-256.

A0.8When the connection drops: the offline bar

Hotels lose the internet. The system keeps working wherever that is safe, and a bar at the top of the page says what is happening. It decides “no connection” from whether its last request reached the server, not from the Wi-Fi sign: the Wi-Fi can be up while the line behind it is down.

The bar saysWhat it means, and what to do
“No connection. Working offline. Anything you can still do will be held.”The line is down. Nothing is waiting yet. Carry on.
“No connection. 1 change held: Housekeeping. They go when the line is back.”Your work is safe on this device and is sent by itself when the line returns.
“2 changes held.” with Send nowThe line is back and the changes are going. Send now sends them at once.
“One change was refused by the server.” with the reason and DiscardSomebody must look. Example: the room was given to another guest by another desk while you were offline. Read the reason, put it right, then Discard the line.
“1 change was made by someone else signed in on this device. They will send when that person signs in again.”Not your work, and not an error. It waits for that person.
“This browser will not keep a queue - a private window, or site data turned off…”Nothing can be held here. Work in a normal browser window.

What can be done offline, and what cannot

 Examples
Held, sent laterMarking rooms clean or inspected, housekeeping assignments, work orders, marking a guest VIP, restaurant orders and the kitchen, a dish on or off the menu, a function enquiry.
Held, with a warningA check-in or a room given to a booking. You are told: “Check-in is held and will be sent when the connection is back. It is not confirmed until then - the room could be taken by another desk in the meantime.” A restaurant bill charged to a room is held the same way.
Refused, with a reasonAn invoice, a payment, the cash drawer, settling a restaurant bill in cash, card or UPI, printing a restaurant bill, adding or changing add-ons on a dish (Customise), closing the restaurant day, the night audit, a charge or a correction on a bill, check-out, moving a guest, Form III, confirming a banquet function. Anything not named above is refused too. Each refusal says why and what to do instead, for example: “Take it on paper and enter it when the connection is back.”

What you can still see

The screens below keep a copy on the device for a week, so they open with no connection: the properties and rooms, Arrivals, In house, Due out, Rooms and Calendar, Housekeeping, Work orders, the banquet diary, the restaurant's Tables, its menu and numbered add-ons, and the rooms a bill can be charged to. Guests' documents, bills and reports are not kept: a shared desk computer is no place for a passport scan. A reload with no connection keeps you signed in, for up to a week.

Rooms says how old its copy is, in a yellow line above the rooms: “No connection - these rooms are as they were at 6:38 PM. They refresh by themselves when the connection is back.”

The screen you were on says it too: Housekeeping shows “1 change waiting to sync” under its heading and Offline at the top right, and the room's card says “Queued: mark inspected”.

Watch out

  • A room that reads Free on a copy from an hour ago may have been sold since. Check it again when the line is back, before you promise it to a guest.
  • Bills are not kept on the device. The In house and Due out lists do keep their last copy, balances included: with no connection, treat a balance there as possibly old. Online, every money figure is read again each time a screen opens.
  • A charge to a room held offline can reach the server after the guest has checked out. The server then refuses it, and the bar keeps the refusal on screen so somebody follows it up.

Why it works this way

A tax invoice number comes from a legal series; two desks offline could give two guests the same number, and it cannot be undone, so invoices are refused offline. Cash is counted against what the server knows, so payments are refused too. A waiter must be able to charge a meal to a room on a bad line: the owner, 8 September. Rooms kept on the desk computer for a reload with the server down: D22-23. Money figures re-checked every time a screen opens: D17-58.

Chapter A1

The front desk day

The screens reception lives in: the Dashboard to see the day, Arrivals to receive guests, In house and Due out to look after them and send them off, Rooms and Calendar to see the whole house, and a guide to the whole Front desk part of the menu (A1.10).

A1.1The business date

The business date is the hotel's working day. It is not always today's calendar date: it moves on only when the night audit closes the day (chapter A7). Every “today” in the system means the business date: today's arrivals, who is due out today, the Dashboard's Today figures.

The Dashboard, Rooms and Calendar show it above the heading: “Business date · Sunday, 4 October 2026”.

When the business date falls behind the real date, a yellow line appears under the top bar of every screen, for example: “Business date 11 Sep, 21 days behind today (2 Oct). Close the days in Night audit.” If you may run the night audit, Night audit in the line is a link to it.

Watch out

  • “Today” for this line is the real date at the hotel, from the server. It never comes from your computer's clock.
  • When the night audit is run on another desk, your screens pick up the new business date the next time you open a screen. Open any screen before you start the new day's work.

Why it works this way

One warning line on every screen while the date is behind: D27-237 (4.2), against the recommendation of showing it on the calendar only. Other devices kept yesterday's date after an audit until this was fixed: D27-89.

A1.2The Dashboard

The Dashboard shows the day at one look. Open it with Dashboard at the top of the menu. Read it from the top.

Today's work: four tiles

Each tile counts one job and opens its list. Its colour says what to do: orange, act now; yellow, due today; white with a green tick, done; white, nothing to do.

TileThe big numberThe line under itOpens
ArrivalsToday's arrivals, and “· 3 left” while some have not come“3 still to arrive · 2 checked in”, “All 5 checked in” or “None today”Arrivals (A1.3)
Due outToday's departures, and how many are leftFor those who see money: “2 owe ₹… · 1 checked out”, which turns the tile orange. For others: “2 still to leave · 1 checked out”. “All 3 checked out” when done.Due out (A1.6)
In houseRooms with a guest in them now“9 staying on · 2 leave today”In house (A1.5)
Needs cleaningRooms waiting for housekeeping“Free rooms ready · 4 of 6”: empty rooms that are clean, of all empty roomsHousekeeping (A6)

The figures

  • Occupancy (the dark card): today's share of rooms sold, then Month so far and Year so far. The year runs from 1 April.
  • Average rate (ARR), RevPAR and Room revenue: today in large figures. Under each, Last 14 days (a small line, from the day 13 days ago to today, today marked with a dark dot), then the month so far and the year so far. Point at the line, or tap it, to read a day. A night with no room sold has no average rate, so the Average rate line breaks there: it is a gap, never a zero.
  • Narrower than 1440 pixels wide, Occupancy has a row of its own and the three figures sit under it, three across from 768 pixels wide. Narrower than that (a phone, or a small tablet standing up) each figure is a block: its name and today's figure on a line, then Last 14 days, Month so far and Year so far side by side.
  • A word with a dotted underline explains itself: click or tap it. The small (i) beside a heading explains the whole card.

Occupancy by day, and Revenue

Under the figures, two cards side by side (one under the other on a narrower screen).

  • Occupancy by day: one bar for every night of the month, from the same figures as the Monthly statistics report. Nights up to today are in the blue of In house; nights after today are the same blue, paler, and show what is booked so far. Today's day number is in a dark mark, and today's share is written above its bar. Saturdays and Sundays are shaded. Every other night is read by pointing at its bar (or tapping it): a small box gives the share, the day and the rooms, with “booked so far” for a night to come. Press Tab to reach the chart, and the left and right arrow keys then move from night to night. Under the chart, Nights so far and Booked ahead say which blue is which; the key is left out when the month has only one kind of night.
  • Revenue (Without tax): the month so far, then a bar split into room revenue, extra revenue and each restaurant, with each part's share and amount. The bar is dark navy and greys, so no colour means anything else. Under it, Today and Year so far. The figures are the Manager report's Revenue Summary.

Nights ahead

Tonight and the 13 nights after it. Under each date: a bar, the share of rooms sold and “sold / rooms to sell”. Tonight is dark; Saturdays and Sundays are shaded. A night with no figures shows a dash. Click any night to open the Calendar.

Money

  • Collected today: payments taken today, by method, with a small bar under them that splits the day's total by method (navy, then greys). “Nothing taken yet today” before the first.
  • Owed by guests, less refunds: what every open guest bill still owes.
  • City ledger: what companies and booking sites owe on their accounts, with “Paid today ₹…”.
  • No-shows: today's, with the month so far. Click it for the No show report.

The house now, and quick reports

The house now draws every room as a small square in the Rooms colours: In house, Due out, Arriving, Free, Out of service. The line beside the heading gives the rooms, how many are empty and how many are out of service. Under it, Quick reports: Manager report, Monthly statistics, Lodging tax, City ledger, No show.

Watch out

  • A dash (-) in a money figure means the system does not hold that figure yet. It is never a zero. A count, such as arrivals, can be a real 0.
  • If the figures could not be read, a red box says “Today's figures did not load” with Try again. The dashes under it then mean “not loaded”, not “nothing”.
  • Housekeeping, the kitchen manager, the chef, the Inventory Manager and the waiter have no Dashboard. The Revenue Manager sees it, but not what departing guests owe.
  • A brand-new system with no property shows “No property yet” and an Add a property button.
  • The Dashboard's figures come from the same place as the Manager report, for the same business date, so the two always agree.
  • If the month's figures could not be read, Occupancy by day says “did not load” with Try again, and the Last 14 days rows show a dash. A dash there means “not loaded”, not “no figure”.

Why it works this way

The page is called Dashboard and carries quick reports: the owner, 14 September. Built as sketched, with today's four tiles first, colours by what staff must do, “ARR” on screens, Nights ahead and the Due out tile showing what departing guests owe: D27-243. No Dashboard for the working roles: D27-141. Money hidden from roles that do not handle bills: D27-143, D27-147. A fresh system asks for a property first: D27-248. The charts, the calendar month, the paler blue for nights to come, a gap and never a zero, Revenue leading with the month, navy-and-grey split bars, and Occupancy on its own row under 1440 pixels: D27-217 to D27-219, D27-365.

A1.3Arrivals

Who is coming today. Check-in starts here.

  1. In the menu, under Front desk, click Arrivals. It opens on Today.
  2. The line under the heading says “Expected on Sunday, 4 October 2026. Check in from the row - the panel opens over this list.” The pill beside the heading says how many are expected.
  3. To find one guest, type part of the name, the booking reference or the room number in Guest, reference or room…. The count on the right shows how many rows are left, for example “1 of 6”. Clear empties the box.
  4. Click the guest's row. The stay panel opens over the list (A1.4).
  5. Click Check in, the orange button at the top of the panel. Chapter A3 goes on from here.

The next fortnight

Click Upcoming beside Today (the same word as in the menu, under Arrivals). It lists bookings arriving from tomorrow to 14 days ahead, without cancelled or void ones (neither list counts them). It is for planning: a row opens the panel, but this list does not offer Check in.

The columns

Room, Guest (with the booking reference under the name), Type, Plan, Source, Departure, Nights (“Day use” for a room used within one day), Status and Rate per night (“Comp” when complimentary). On a narrower screen Plan and Source are hidden, then Type. A source the system does not know shows a dash; it is never guessed.

StatusMeans
Due inExpected, not yet checked in
In houseChecked in
Due outChecked in and leaving today
Checked outGone
No show · CancelledNever came · cancelled
Void · Waiting for the hotelVoided · held until the hotel confirms it (chapter A2)

Watch out

  • A red line above the list such as “… has the phone or email of …, who is blacklisted. Reason: …. Check-in is not refused - you decide.” means a booking site's guest matches a blacklisted guest. The system warns; it does not stop you.
  • An empty Room means no room is given yet. You give one at check-in (A3).
  • Check in is shown only to people who may check guests in. Housekeeping and the Revenue Manager see the list without it.
  • Nobody expected? “No arrivals today. Nobody is expected. A walk-in can be taken from any empty cell on the Calendar.”

Why it works this way

The blacklist warns and shows the reason, a person decides: D21-21, and the warning on Arrivals and at check-in: D22-8. A control is shown only to a role the server lets use it: D24-27.

A1.4The stay panel

Every booking opens in the same panel, from Arrivals, In house, Due out and All bookings, and from a tile on Rooms or a bar on the Calendar. Learn it once.

PartWhat it shows
The topThe guest's name; the booking reference; the phone (tap it on a phone to call) and the email when the booking has them. For a foreign guest, their nationality: they need Form III (A3).
The marksThe status, and the guest's marks such as VIP.
The one main buttonCheck in for a guest still to arrive (not on the Upcoming list); Settle and check out for a guest in the house (it opens the Bill tab).
More optionsThe rarer acts: Change dates or guests, View voucher, Move to another room, Exchange with another guest, What this booking includes, Change rate (owner, Admin and GM), and at the end, in red, Cancel this booking and Void this booking. An option you cannot use says why, for example “This stay is over.” Chapter A2 covers each one.
Stay tabStay: Arrival, Departure, Nights, Room (or “Deluxe · no room yet”), Guests. Rate: Rate plan, Per night, Rack rate. Booked through: Source, Business source, Segment, Sold by. For whoever records IDs, Adults in the room: everybody on the stay, and how many are recorded (A3.3).
Bill tabThe guest's bill (chapter A4).
The footAlways in view: Charged, Paid and the Balance. The last one reads Due while tonight's room charge is still to be added, with that charge and its GST counted in; In advance when the guest has paid ahead; Overpaid after they leave with credit.

For a group booking, the group's other rooms are listed on the right. Close the panel with the ✕ at its top, or Esc.

Watch out

  • People who do not handle bills (the Revenue Manager, housekeeping, the kitchen manager, the till) see no Bill tab and no totals at the foot, and the guest's phone and email are blank for them.
  • No More options at all? Your role may not change bookings.
  • Charged is what is on the bill so far. The first night's room charge is posted when the guest is checked in, and the night audit adds each later night; a guest still waiting to arrive shows nothing charged yet. That is not a free stay.

Why it works this way

One panel instead of two copies that drifted apart, rebuilt to the owner's reference layout on 14 September: the act at the top, what is owed always in view. The amount due counts tonight's room charge before the night audit posts it: D27-199. The first night is posted at check-in, and the night audit never posts it twice: D27-204. Bills and guest contacts hidden from roles that read bookings only: D27-143. Each act offered only to a role the server allows: D24-27.

A1.5In house

Every guest checked in now.

  1. In the menu, under Front desk, click In house. The heading says “Guests checked in now, on Sunday, 4 October 2026.” The pill counts the rooms, for example “11 rooms”.
  2. The switch at the top right has In house now (this list) and Due out (A1.6), each with its count.
  3. Click a guest to open the panel. For a guest who is leaving, Settle and check out takes you to their bill.

The columns are Room, Guest, Type, Plan, Arrival, Departure, Status and Balance. The balance is coloured:

BalanceMeans
₹… in redThe guest owes this
₹… over, in blueThe guest has paid more than the charges so far
₹0 in greenSettled
-No bill yet, or you do not see bills

Watch out

  • The pill counts rooms. The list can have more rows than rooms: a guest due out who has not left yet and the guest arriving into the same room are two rows for one room.
  • A guest stays “in house” until they are checked out, even after their departure date has passed. A late check-out still counts.
  • Empty list: “Nobody in house. The house is empty tonight.”

Why it works this way

“In house” means checked in and not yet checked out, the same on every screen: D17-10, D21-36. A stay with no bill shows a dash, never ₹0: D17-16.

A1.6Departures (Due out)

The guests leaving today, and what they still owe.

  1. Open it from the menu (In house, then Due out), from the Dashboard's Due out tile, or with the switch on In house.
  2. The heading says “Departing Sunday, 4 October 2026. Check-out unlocks when the bill reaches zero.”
  3. If anyone still owes money, a red box at the top says so, for example “2 departures still owing ₹…”, with “Settle from the Bill tab. Check-out stays disabled with its reason until each balance clears.”
  4. Click a guest. On this list the panel opens straight on the Bill tab.
  5. Take the payment, then check the guest out. Chapters A4 and A5 go on from here.

If the guest leaves after check-out time

The hotel's check-out time is set on Times and rules (A17.11), for example 11:00. A guest who leaves on their departure date, or after it, later than that is a late departure, and it is written down. The window comes up when you click Check out, not before.

  1. Click Check out on the guest's Bill tab. If it is a late departure, the window Leaving after check-out time opens, with the guest and the room. Its yellow note starts “Check-out here is 11:00.”
  2. Type Why. It cannot be left empty: a flight time, a manager's say-so, a room not ready on arrival.
  3. Read the line under it. Where the hotel charges for a late departure: “₹1,000 will be added to the folio. A manager can waive it - that is a decision about money and it is theirs to make.” Where it does not: “This property does not charge for a late departure, so nothing will be added. It is still recorded.” The owner, the GM and a group administrator instead have a tick, Waive the ₹1,000 charge: their decision, recorded against their name, and the late departure is still written down.
  4. Click Check out. The late check-out charge, with its GST, goes on the bill under Room before the balance is looked at. If that leaves something owed, the window closes with “Recorded - now settle the bill” and the amount. Settle it on the Bill tab (A4.7), then click Check out again.

The second click does not ask again and charges nothing more. A late departure is recorded once for a stay: its reason, its charge or its waiver.

A guest who leaves before the departure date is leaving early, whatever the hour: the window never comes up and no late fee is charged. The date that counts is the hotel's business date (A1.1), not the clock's.

Watch out

  • Check-out stays greyed out, with its reason, until the balance is zero. This is on purpose.
  • An early departure: chapter A5.
  • Nobody leaving: “Nobody departing today. Every room stays another night.”

Why it works this way

The Due out tile and list show what departing guests still owe, to the people who see money: D27-243, D27-143. Reception's card puts it in one line: “Open the guest, go to Bill - Check out opens once nothing is owed.” (Start here, the owner, 15 September.) A late departure is asked only on or after the departure date and recorded once, so a guest who paid after it is not asked or charged again: D27-314.

A1.7Rooms: the house today

Every room as a tile, for today. It answers three questions at a glance: is it free, who is in it, and what happens today.

  1. Click Rooms near the top of the menu. The heading shows the business date and the hotel's name.
  2. Read the row of count tiles. Click one to show only those rooms; the chosen tile turns dark. Click Sellable to see every room again.
  3. Click a tile with a guest's name to open their panel (A1.4).
  4. Click a tile with no guest on it, such as a Free one, to start a booking for that room, today: New booking opens with the room and the date filled in. This is how a walk-in is taken (chapter A2).

The count tiles

TileCounts
SellableEvery room that can be sold. Out-of-service rooms are left out, so it can be smaller than the number of rooms.
EmptySellable rooms with nobody in them: the free ones, those still to be cleaned, and those someone arrives into today.
In houseRooms with a checked-in guest.
ArrivingRooms given to a guest who arrives today. The tile is orange while there are some.
ReservedRooms already given to a booking that arrives on a later day. Not today's arrivals.
Out of serviceRooms that cannot be sold.
Due outRooms whose guest leaves today. Yellow while there are some.
Needs cleaningRooms waiting for housekeeping. A green tick at 0.

A room tile

The first line is the room number and its state. The second is the guest's name (or, for an empty room, its room type). The third says “to 6 Oct 2026”, or “out today” for a departure. An arrow at the end means the tile opens something. A small red dirty beside the state means the room also needs cleaning.

StateTile
FreeWhite: clean, empty, nobody expected
In houseBlue
ArrivingOrange
Due outYellow
Needs cleaningRed
Out of serviceGrey; it cannot be clicked

A room that is both in house and leaving today shows Due out: the job to act on comes first.

The controls at the top right

  • Calendar | Rooms: switch to the Calendar (A1.8). An open booking stays open.
  • Room type | Floor: group the tiles by room type or by floor (“Ground floor”, “Floor 1”…). The system remembers your choice on every device.
  • Assign room: give rooms to bookings that do not have one yet (chapter A3).

Watch out

  • With no connection, the last copy stays on screen with its time: “No connection - these rooms are as they were at 4:10 pm.” Check before you sell a room shown as Free (A0.8). If there is no copy at all: “No connection. This device is offline, so the rooms cannot load.”
  • Housekeeping sees Rooms but no Assign room, and a Free tile does not open a booking for them. The chef and the Inventory Manager have no Rooms.
  • A hotel with no rooms yet shows “No rooms set up yet. Add them in Room types.”

Why it works this way

Rooms and Calendar are two screens with their own menu entries; Room type or Floor remembered per person: the owner, 14 September. “Sellable” counts sellable rooms, as the Manager report does: D27-164. “Empty” means nobody in it and sellable tonight: D21-37. A free room opens the one-page New booking: D27-163. Controls a role cannot use are hidden: D24-18, D24-27. Rooms needs bookings access: D27-142. Rooms kept for a reload with the server down: D22-23.

A1.8Calendar: the fortnight chart

Fourteen nights across, every room down. It is for planning: who is where, and what is free on which night.

  1. Click Calendar near the top of the menu. It starts on the business date.
  2. Move a week at a time with the arrows ‹ and › (Previous week, Next week). Today brings you back.
  3. Point at a booking's bar to see the guest, the dates and nights, the price per night (or “Complimentary”) and, if you see bills, the balance.
  4. Click a bar to open the stay panel (A1.4).
  5. Click an empty cell to start a booking for that room on that night: New booking opens with both filled in (chapter A2).

Reading the chart

  • The dates run across the top. The business date's column is dark. Weekends and the hotel's holidays are shaded; point at a holiday's date to see its name.
  • Each room type has a grey row. Under each night: how many of its rooms are still free (red at 0), and the room type's rack rate in thousands (for example “4.5k”), or a dash when none is set. It is the same rack rate on every night. Grouped by floor, the rate is always a dash: a floor has no one rate.
  • Each room has a row: its number, then two small marks: a sparkle (yellow = dirty, grey = clean) and a spanner (red = out of service).
  • The foot of the chart: Available rooms and Occupancy for each night, with a small orange bar.
  • The same count tiles as Rooms sit above the chart and filter it the same way.

The bars

Each bar starts with a small mark for where the booking came from: a person for a walk-in, a building for Fidato Hotels, a globe for anything else or not known.

BarMeans
Solid blueIn house
YellowDue out
Pale blueConfirmed, still to arrive
GreyChecked out
Dark roseNo show
Pale red, struck throughCancelled or void
Grey, dashed edgeWaiting for the hotel

A hotel can choose its own colour for each of these in Settings. If yours looks different, that is why.

Watch out

  • While the next week loads, or with no connection, the last fortnight loaded stays on screen, with a line such as “The fortnight from 11 Oct 2026 has not loaded.”
  • Someone who may not take bookings, such as housekeeping, can read the chart, but an empty cell does not open a booking for them.
  • Room types never fold away on the Calendar, on a desk or a phone.

Why it works this way

Room type groups always open: D27-237 (4.1). Each hotel picks its weekend days, for shading only: D27-243. Holidays shaded with their name, with no effect on price, and the hotel's own colours for each state: D27-260. The foot's occupancy is the Manager report's rule (complimentary in; no-shows, waiting bookings and day use out): D27-151. Out of service follows the dated block: D17-11.

A1.9Your day in five jobs

Reception's Start here card names the five jobs done most. Here they are with the chapter that covers each.

JobOpensHow, in the card's wordsChapter
Take a bookingNew booking“Fill in the guest and the nights, then Save booking.”A2
Check a guest inArrivals“Pick the guest from today's arrivals, then Check in.”A3
Take a paymentIn house“Open the guest, go to Bill, Settle, then Take payment.”A4
Check a guest outDue out“Open the guest, go to Bill - Check out opens once nothing is owed.”A5
Count and close the cash drawerCashiering“Your drawer opens by itself with your first cash. At hand over, count it, type the float kept and who takes it.”A later chapter

Before you start, look at the Dashboard (A1.2): the four tiles tell you what is waiting. If the yellow business-date line is showing (A1.1), the days before have not been closed yet; the line says where they are closed.

A1.10The Front desk part of the menu

Above it, after the Dashboard, the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager and the Inventory Manager see Approvals: everything waiting for their yes, from every part of the system, with the bell counting it (A12.3).

The Front desk section of the menu holds nine screens. Where each one is described:

ScreenWhat it isSection
ArrivalsWho is coming: Today and Upcoming, with Check inA1.3
In houseIn house now and Due out, each guest's balanceA1.5, A1.6
Walk-insThe record of guests taken at the desk without a bookingbelow, A2.5
Online check-inWhat guests sent from their own page, waiting for the deskbelow
HousekeepingThe room board, rooms given to a housekeeper, clean and inspectedA6.2 to A6.4
Work ordersWhat needs fixing, from report to doneA6.8
Guest requestsWhat a guest in house asks for, sent to the team it is forA6.9
Wake-up callsCalls to make, on the hotel's clockA6.10
Lost propertyWhat was found, kept until it goes back to its owner or is disposed ofA6.11

Walk-ins

A record, not a form. The heading says “Guests taken at the desk without a booking, leaving from …” with the first day shown and how many came today, and a count of those shown. It opens on the walk-ins leaving in the last 90 days and everything ahead; to see older ones, choose an earlier day in the date box beside the heading. Each row is a stay with source Walk-in: room, guest, type, plan, arrival, departure, nights, status and rate, newest arrival first, with Check in where it is still to do. Nothing is entered here. The box Take a walk-in from the Calendar says how: “Click any empty cell on the chart. The room and the night are already chosen by the time the form opens”, with Open Calendar beside it. Taking a walk-in is A2.5. With none yet: “No walk-ins on record”.

Online check-in

A guest checks in from their own page (A10.7 says how the link reaches them). What they send waits here for a person, in three parts.

  1. Details waiting to be checked. Each entry shows the guest, the booking's reference and when it was sent, then what they typed: ID type and number, a passport's expiry, a visa, the address. Look at the ID in your hand, then click Confirm against the ID: only then does it reach the guest's record and Form C, and the entry leaves the list with “Confirmed”. If it is not right, click Not right - take them at the desk and take the guest's details at check-in as usual. Empty: “Nothing waiting”.
  2. Requests. A spa treatment or a laundry bag a guest asked for, where the hotel has them switched on. The (i) says “Book them on the spa's or the laundry's own screen, then mark them done here.” This screen books nothing; click Done or Declined. Empty: “No requests”.
  3. Room cards. One card for each room, with a QR code. The (i) says “One card per room. A guest scans it and a code goes to the phone on their booking. Printing a new card stops the old one at once.” Each room shows “No card yet” or “Card printed” with its date. Click Print a card (or Print a new card), or Print cards for every room, which asks “Print cards for every room?” and warns “Every card already in a room stops working the moment this is pressed. Put the new ones out straight away.” The sheet then opens: “These cards are shown once. Print them now - they cannot be shown again, only replaced.” Click Print, then Done. Four cards fit an A4 page, each with the hotel, the room, the QR code and “Scan to check in.”

Watch out

  • Printing a card is making a card: the card is shown once, so the old one stops at the same moment. Print only when the card is to go into the room.
  • A guest's details are not on their record until somebody has confirmed them against the ID.

Why it works this way

Everything the guest sends is a submission that the desk confirms against the ID, under the clerk's name: D21-8. A request is confirmed by the desk and booked on the spa's or laundry's own screen: D21-9. One fixed card per room, finding whoever is checked in there now: D21-7; a reprint stops the old card at once: D21-16; the system prints a sheet and the owner chooses how it is printed: D21-62.

Chapter A2

Bookings

For reception and whoever takes bookings. How to find a booking, take one on the phone, book and check in a walk-in, book several rooms as a group, hold a booking while it waits for the hotel, change the dates or the room, and cancel or void a booking. The last sections are for the owner: the cancellation terms, the booking sources and CRS bookings.

A2.1The bookings screens

The Bookings part of the menu holds these screens. The owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager and reception may make, change, cancel and void bookings; other roles may only look.

ScreenWho uses itWhat it is for
All bookingsReceptionThe last 90 days and everything ahead, in any state; a search finds any booking ever. Find one and open it.
GroupsReception, managersThe bookings of more than one room: their rooms, who pays, the lead guest (A2.6). Not in reception's menu: open it with Find a screen (A0.6).
CRS bookingsReception; the owner and an Admin for its connectionBookings the CRS sold for this hotel, and what became of each (A2.11).
New bookingWhoever may make a bookingOne page to take a booking, give it a room, or check the guest in (A2.2 to A2.5).

To find a booking

  1. Open All bookings. It opens on the bookings leaving in the last 90 days and everything ahead, says from which date, and how many are shown.
  2. Type in Guest, reference or room: part of the guest's name, the reference, a room number, or three or more digits of the phone. A search of three letters or more looks through every booking ever made, however old.
  3. To list older bookings without searching, choose an earlier date in the date box beside the search.
  4. Or tap a tile to see one state only: All, Due in, In house (guests due out today too), Checked out, Cancelled, void & no-show. Each tile shows its count; the one chosen is dark.
  5. Click a row. The booking opens in the stay panel (A1.4), where More options holds the changes in A2.8 and A2.9.

The list runs from the latest arrival down. Its columns: Room, Guest (with the reference under the name), Type, Plan, Source, Arrival, Departure, Nights, Status, Rate. The states are Due in (orange), In house (blue), Due out, Checked out, Cancelled, No show, Void, and Waiting for the hotel (A2.7).

Watch out

  • Nothing is ever deleted. A cancelled, voided or no-show booking stays on the file under its own tile.
  • A booking waiting for the hotel is under All, not under Due in: it is not confirmed yet.
  • Nothing found? Try a shorter search: a surname, or the last few digits of a reference.

A2.2A booking on the phone: the guest and the stay

New booking is one page: “One guest, one set of nights. Save it, give it a room, or check them in.” The guest, the dates, the room and its price, the ID and an advance are on the page; the rest folds away. On the right, The booking adds it up as you type.

To take a booking

  1. Open New booking. It opens on today's business date, one night, one room.
  2. Choose the Salutation (Mr, Ms, Mrs, Dr or None; the hotel's own default is chosen first) and type the name in Full name. The name is the only guest detail that must be typed.
  3. Type the Phone, and the Email if the guest gives one. If the system knows that phone or email, a line under them names the guest and how often they have stayed with the group, and asks “same person?”. Press Same person only if it is them (A10.6); nothing is joined until you do.
  4. Under The guest, leave Normal guest for a guest paying for themselves, a walk-in for one. Choose Company guest (GST registered) (on a phone, Company guest) if the guest wants the tax invoice in their company's name, and type its GSTIN and Company name (both needed) and the Company address. The stay's tax invoice is made out to that company; the guest still pays at the desk.
    • A GSTIN already on Companies and agents says “Found: … , on Companies and agents.” and fills the name and address from its record.
    • One that is not says “This company is not on your list. Saving the booking adds it to Companies and agents.” It is added with no credit; credit is given by the owner, an administrator or the GM (A10.4). For someone who may not add a company, the line says it is kept on this booking only.
    • A company already on the list under the same name with another GSTIN is not changed; the booking keeps the GSTIN you typed.
    For a returning guest, once you press Same person, the line also shows “Last company” - the company on their last booking that had one - and Use this company chooses Company guest and fills the three fields for you. Nothing is filled until you press it; check it with the guest. The guest is not shown when the hotel has switched off the Company section in Settings.
  5. Ask the guest if they agree to WhatsApp, and switch on Guest agreed to WhatsApp if they do.
  6. Set Arrival and Departure. The number of nights shows under Departure. The night of departure is not charged.
  7. Choose the Booking source: how the booking reached us. Nothing is chosen for you (except Walk-in for a walk-in, A2.5).
  8. Choose the Room type and the Meal plan, and set Rooms, Adults and Children.
  9. Leave Rate empty to use the price on Rates, or type the rate agreed with the guest.
  10. Pick a Room now if you want to; Assign later is fine.
  11. Read the price under the line and the total on the right, and tell the guest.
Meal plan, as the list says itMeans
EP · Room onlyThe room, no meals.
CP · Room + breakfastThe room and breakfast.
MAP · Room + breakfast + one mealThe room, breakfast and one more meal.
AP · Room + all mealsThe room and every meal.
AI · Everything charged to the roomAll inclusive.
  • The price line reads, for example, “₹3,699.00 a night + ₹184.95 tax (5%) · 2 nights”. A rate you typed adds “, agreed”.
  • “7 left” is how many rooms of that type are free on every night of the stay. All 7 left books all of them. Booking more than are left is allowed: the count then adds “this books more than that”. You decide.
  • Another room (top of the Stay card) adds a second line, for a second room type. The bin takes a line away. More than one room in all makes a group (A2.6).
  • Complimentary: no charge, nothing posted. Only the owner, an Admin or the GM can tick it; for others it reads Complimentary (owner, admin or GM only) and cannot be ticked.
  • Departure the same day as Arrival is a day use: type the day's price on the line. It is charged at check-in.
  • A booking site's source shows Prepaid on the booking site, ticked. Untick it when the guest pays at the hotel: the advance is then asked before check-in.

Watch out

  • No price, no total. If Rates has no price for this party, the line says “No price for …” and the total stays a dash: “Set it on Rates, or type a rate on the line.” The system never guesses a price.
  • The first night's price is kept for every night. If the calendar's price changes later in the stay, the line says so: “The first night's price is kept for every night; the calendar differs later.”
  • The booking source cannot be filled in later. Ask how the guest found you before you save.
  • A GSTIN is checked. It is 15 characters, and its last character is a check on the other fourteen. A mistyped one is refused: “That GSTIN is not right - a character is mistyped. Check it against the company's GST certificate.” Copy it from the certificate, not from memory.
  • The company typed here is not added to the Companies list, and it does not bill the company: that is Bill to in the Company fold (A2.3). When a booking has both, the invoice goes to the company billed.
  • WhatsApp unticked: messages go by email if there is one, else not at all.

Why it works this way

One page with three buttons, for booking, giving a room and checking in: D27-158. The WhatsApp tick stays in sight because the voucher and the check-in code need it; offers and “woman travelling alone” fold away: D27-176. Rate includes GST, a tick per line, off unless ticked: D27-187, D27-199. A day use's price is typed every time: D27-229. Prepaid on the booking site: D27-246. A returning guest is only suggested; a person confirms: D21-2. Salutation beside Full name, and the guest's company and GSTIN on the Guest card, all optional, the invoice in the company's name while the guest pays: D27-371. A returning guest's last company offered, never filled by itself; the Company section switched off hides the guest's company too: D27-372. Normal guest or Company guest (GST registered); a company guest's name and GSTIN needed; a GSTIN not on Companies and agents added to it on save, without credit; Business source asked of a company guest only, starting on the company, even where the hotel requires it: D27-392.

A2.3The ID, the advance, the folds and the three buttons

Under the room line are the ID and the advance, then five folded sections, then the three buttons.

  • ID. For a booking still to come it says “The document is taken when they check in.”: only the Nationality is asked now. For an arrival today, Document and Number are asked too, for Check in now (A2.5). A nationality other than IN puts the stay on the Form III register (A3).
  • Advance. Money the guest pays now: the Amount and how it was Paid by. It is held as the guest's credit until the nights are charged, and the total on the right takes it off.
FoldWhat is in it
More about the guestGuest agreed to offers, Woman travelling alone (placed away from stairwells and service corridors; not announced at the desk), Address, City, State, PIN code, Country. (The salutation is now at the top of the Guest card.)
Booking detailsThe booking: Confirmed or Waiting for the hotel (A2.7). Expected check-in and check-out, if they said. For a company guest only, Business source (the company or agent behind the booking): it starts on the guest's company, and lists Companies and agents and the names on this hotel's past bookings. Market segment, Sales person. Discount.
CompanyBill to: Guest or Company. For a company, its GSTIN is shown from its record; the tax invoice prints it.
Special requestThe guest's special request, up to 500 characters: “Printed on the booking voucher the guest receives.” A booking site's or the CRS's request is put here too. A guest's wish goes here; anything the hotel says about the guest goes in Notes (D27-347).
NotesNotes on the booking: “The hotel's own. Never on the voucher.”

Company and Notes can each be switched off for a hotel in Settings; Special request cannot. A hotel can also make some fields required, such as the phone or the market segment; the reason under the buttons then names the missing one, for example “The phone number is needed for a booking at this hotel.”

  • Discount. Up to 10% by hand, with a reason. ₹ off a night, with a reason. More than 10% only through a named Promotion.

The three buttons

ButtonWhat it does
Save bookingSaves the booking. A room picked on the line is given to it too.
Save and assign roomThe same save, once a room is picked on the line. Until then it says “Pick a room.”
Check in nowSaves the booking, takes the advance if one is typed, then checks the guest in, through the same check-in as Arrivals (A3), so an advance the hotel asks before check-in (A3.6) is already paid. Only for an arrival today, one room, with a room picked.

The filled (orange) button is the job the page was opened for: Save booking on the phone, Check in now for a walk-in. A button that cannot be used says why under the buttons, for example “Check in now: Check in now is for an arrival today.” or “Type the guest's name.”

Watch out

  • “Not booked” with a reason means nothing was written: fix what it names and save again.
  • If the booking is saved but a later step is refused (the room, the check-in or the advance), the booking stands, and the next screen says which step and why (A2.4).
  • Several rooms? Check in now checks in one room at a time: “save the booking, then check each room in from Arrivals.”

Why it works this way

The three buttons, Company and Notes switchable in Settings: D27-158, D27-163. The advance held as the guest's credit: D27-4. Discounts, 10% by hand with a reason, more only by a named promotion: D27-36. The hotel's default guarantee and required fields: D27-260.

A2.4Booked: the reference, the guest's page and the voucher

After Save booking the page shows Booked with the guest's name: the reference of each room and its room type, then what to do next, in the order you do it on the phone.

  • Send voucher goes once. After that the button is replaced by “Voucher sent” with the day, the time and who sent it. It goes to the guest by WhatsApp or email, as the WhatsApp tick decides (A10.7).
  • Where nothing can be sent, the buttons are greyed and say why. On the demo hotel the sentence is “Sending is not set up yet. Bills and vouchers print and download as usual; nothing goes by WhatsApp or email until …”.
  • Check in now shows here too for a guest arriving today, one room, not yet checked in.
  • Open the booking opens it in All bookings (a group: the group's page, A2.6). Another booking clears the page for the next call.
  • A room picked but not given says “No room given: … Assign one from Arrivals.” An advance that did not go through says “Advance not taken: … Take it on the bill.”

Why it works this way

One voucher, recorded so it never goes twice: D27-35. View voucher sends nothing: D27-187. The check-in link beside the voucher: D27-105. Messages go to guests only as A10.7 describes.

A2.5A walk-in: booked and checked in at once

A guest at the desk with no booking. Start from the room, not from the menu.

  1. Open Rooms (A1.7) and tap a free room. New booking opens on that room: today, one night, source Walk-in. Its heading says “A walk-in into room 301. Check them in, or save the booking.”
  2. Type the guest's name and phone, as in A2.2. Check the room type, meal plan, adults and the price.
  3. Under ID, choose the Document and type its Number. Check in now records them; Save booking keeps only the nationality.
  4. If the room is being given before the hotel's check-in time, type Why the room is being given early.
  5. Take an advance if the guest pays now.
  6. Tap Check in now, the filled button. The card that follows has Adults in the room, to add the other adults (A3.3). They never hold up the check-in.

Watch out

  • Check in now uses the same check-in as Arrivals, with all its checks: the room must be ready and free, the ID complete, a foreign guest's Form III filled (A3). If it refuses, the booking still stands, and the page says “Not checked in: … Check them in from Arrivals.”
  • An empty room opened from the Calendar for a later night is an ordinary booking of that room, not a walk-in: no Walk-in source, and Save booking is the filled button.

Why it works this way

The walk-in became this one page, opened from an empty room: room, today, one night, source Walk-in: D27-163.

A2.6A group: several rooms on one booking

A wedding, a conference, a family: one guest, one set of dates, several rooms. Book it once; more than one room becomes a group by itself.

  1. On New booking, set Rooms to the number of rooms (or add lines with Another room for other room types).
  2. Type a Group name, such as “Sharma Wedding, March”. Left empty, it is named after the guest.
  3. The booking on the right says “2 rooms are booked as one group.” Save it.
  4. Each room gets its own reference. Open the booking opens the group's page.

The Groups screen

Groups lists every group: its name, rooms, room-nights and dates, and two figures that are never added together: Rooms owe (the guests' own bills) and Host owes (the host's account; a dash when there is none). Here and coming shows the groups in the house or due; All adds the past ones. Tap a group to list its rooms, then Open the group.

One group: the host, the guests, the rooms

  • The host. “No host account. Every room settles its own.” until someone presses Open a host account. Then the rooms can be put on the host's account, and the page gets the card The host's account (below).
  • The guests. What the rooms owe on their own bills, across all of them.
  • Host pays. Tick a room to put its accommodation on the host's account; untick to give it back. It changes only the nights not yet charged.
  • Lead guest. The flag marks the guest who gets the group's one confirmation and its review request. It starts on the room booked first; tap another room's box to change it.

The host's account: taking the money, and the invoice

Once a host account is open, a card The host's account comes under the rooms. It says who the bill is made out to: “Billed to Sharma Wedding. Every line says which room it is for.” That is the company the group is booked for; with none, the guest who leads the group; with neither, the group's name. Each night routed to the host is a line, with its date and its room. Until there is one: “Nothing has been charged to the host yet. Route a room above, and tonight’s audit will post it here.”

  1. To take money: tap Settle on the card; it is grey while nothing is owed. The window is the one a guest's bill has: “Settle bill”, Method, Amount, Take payment, and any of the hotel's ways of paying will do. Bill to company moves the amount to the company's city ledger (A4). It is refused when the group is billed to no company: “… is not billed to a company, so its bill cannot go to the city ledger. Take the payment another way.” Over the company's credit limit it needs a reason from the owner, an Admin or the GM. More than the host owes is kept only if you tick Hold it as the host's credit. Cash is taken to the nearest rupee, as on a guest's bill: the window shows Cash to take and the Round-off, and the bill keeps the exact amount.
  2. To invoice: tap Issue tax invoice. It stays grey, and its reason shows when you point at it, until every room has left and nothing is owed: “Every room checks out first: a night still to come would land on this bill.”, “The bill still carries a balance. Settle it, or send it to the city ledger, before invoicing.” or “The bill is overpaid. Refund the difference before invoicing.” The window asks “Issue this tax invoice?”, says who it is billed to and the number it will take. Tap Issue the invoice, or Keep it. The card then shows Tax invoice with its number, which opens it.

Both buttons are shown only to a role that may take payments or issue invoices. Nothing sends the host's invoice by itself, and its page has no Send invoice.

Watch out

  • A group's rooms are given later, from Arrivals or the Calendar's Assign room: the Room box is not on the line when it books more than one room.
  • Ticking Host pays before the host account is open is refused: “This group has no open master folio yet. Open one, and the room charges will go to it.”
  • Nights already charged stay on the bill they were posted to. Moving one is a correction on the bill, with a reason (A4).
  • Host pays moves the room's accommodation only. Food and drink stay on the bill of the guest who signed for them.

Why it works this way

Two accounts, never one total: the host and the guests are different people asked for different money, and a sum would be a number nobody can be asked to pay. Who leads a group: the room booked first that still stands, unless the desk picks another: D22-52. The host's account is settled and invoiced on the group's page, with the same Settle and the same question before an invoice number is taken as a guest's bill: D27-305. Its cash to the rupee, as a room bill's: D27-337.

A2.7Waiting for the hotel

A booking the hotel has not accepted yet: the room is held, and nothing goes to the guest. Bookings from the CRS arrive this way (A2.11). The desk can make one too.

  1. On New booking, open Booking details and choose Waiting for the hotel (Figure A2-05). It says “Waiting holds the room and sends the guest nothing until it is confirmed.”
  2. Save booking. The page says Held, waiting for the hotel.
  3. When the hotel accepts it, tap Confirm the booking: here, or later in the booking's More options. The message says “Confirmed” and “the voucher can go now.”
  • Confirming confirms every waiting room booked with it.
  • While it waits, New booking neither gives it a room nor checks it in: “A booking waiting for the hotel gets its room once it is confirmed.” There is no voucher for it either: “Only a confirmed booking still to arrive has a voucher.”
  • Not accepted? More options, Cancel this booking. The window says “It was waiting for the hotel and was never confirmed: no charge, and nothing goes to the guest.” Type Why and tap Cancel the booking. The room is free at once.

Why it works this way

A booking waits with its room held; the hotel confirms; then one voucher goes: D27-35. A waiting booking is cancelled directly, by the same people who may cancel a confirmed one: D27-64.

A2.8Changing a booking: More options

Open the booking (All bookings, Arrivals, a room tile) and tap More options. The choices are listed by when they happen; an option you cannot use is grey and says why.

OptionWhat it does
Confirm the bookingOnly on a booking waiting for the hotel (A2.7).
Change dates or guestsNew arrival or departure, adults, children. Not on a stay that is over.
View voucherThe voucher to look at, print or save. Sends nothing. Only for a confirmed booking still to arrive.
Undo check-inOn a guest in the house: back to confirmed, arriving. The owner, an Admin, or the GM while Front desk rules allow it (A2.9). Reception sees Ask the GM to undo the check-in.
Move to another roomOnce the guest is in the house. Before that, change the room with Assign room on the Calendar.
Change room typeOn a guest in the house: a move to a room of another type, and the booking becomes that type (A2.8, below).
Exchange with another guestTwo guests in the house swap rooms.
What this booking includesThe extras on the booking.
Change rateThe owner, an Admin or the GM, on a confirmed booking or a guest in the house (A4.6). Reception, on a guest in the house: Ask the GM to change the rate.
Cancel this booking, Void this bookingIn red, at the end (A2.9). On a guest in the house, reception sees Ask the GM to cancel this booking and Ask the GM to void this booking.

To change the dates or the number of guests

  1. More options, Change dates or guests. The window is called “Amend A2 Test Sharma” and says the stay as it is.
  2. Change Arrival, Departure, Adults or Children. Once the guest has arrived, only the owner, an Admin or the GM can change the arrival: “They have arrived: no later than today, and never a closed day.” Reception reads “They have already arrived. The GM may change it.” and has Ask the GM to change the arrival date under the fields.
  3. Read the line under them: “2 → 3 nights · ₹11,097 of room charges at ₹3,699 a night”.
  4. Tap Save. The message says “Stay amended” and the change: “A2 Test Sharma: 2 nights becomes 3.”
  • The room held for the booking moves with it. If the room is taken for a night being added, nothing changes at all, and the message says which.
  • Added nights are charged at the rate already agreed. Changing the rate is separate (Change rate, or the bill).
  • A night already charged cannot be dropped here: correct it on the bill first (A4). A stay is at most 90 nights.

To move a guest in the house to another room

  1. More options, Move to another room. The window says where they are now: “Currently in 209.”
  2. Type To which room.
  3. Set From which night: the first night in the new room. It starts on the business date.
  4. Choose Why: Guest asked to move, Upgrade, Downgrade, Something wrong with the room, or Putting a group together.
  5. Type a New rate per night only if the price changes. Left empty, nothing about the money changes.
  6. Tap Move. The message names the new room and how the nights are split between the two.

To change the room type of a guest in the house

For a guest in a room, the room type is the type of the room they are in. So More options, Change room type, opens the move with only the rooms of the other types to choose from, and Upgrade chosen. Choose the room, the night, why, and a new rate if the price changes, then Move. From tonight the booking is the new type: the stay panel, the rooms left to sell and the reports count it there. A plain Move to another room into another type keeps the type booked, as an upgrade at check-in does.

  • Moving changes no charge on its own. Nights before tonight stay with the old room. A new rate applies from tonight; to change a night already billed, correct it on the bill, with its reason (A4).
  • Take them out of the room without assigning another leaves the booking standing with no room: “Out of the room”.

Why it works this way

Why a guest moved is kept, because “something wrong with the room” is the question asked when a complaint arrives a week later. A move is a change of room, not of price: the rate is a separate decision.

A2.9Cancel, void and no-show

Three ways a booking does not happen. None of them deletes it.

WordMeansWhat it costs
CancelledThe guest booked, then cancelled.What the booking's cancellation terms keep, on the guest's bill.
VoidIt should never have existed: entered twice, wrong property, a test.Nothing. Left out of revenue and out of cancellation figures.
No showA confirmed guest never came.Marked by the night audit (A7); the terms decide what is kept.

To cancel a confirmed booking

  1. Open the booking. More options, Cancel this booking. The window says “The guest cancelled. This room only; the terms it was booked under decide the charge.”
  2. Read the first line: what the terms charge, before you cancel. For example “This booking carries no cancellation terms, so nothing is charged.”
  3. Type Why, such as “Guest changed plans”.
  4. Tap Cancel the booking. Keep it closes the window and changes nothing.
  • Inside the terms' free window: “nothing is charged.” Otherwise the window says how much is kept and that it goes on the guest's bill; an advance already paid stays on the bill.
  • The owner, an Admin or the GM may switch on Waive the charge. Nothing then goes on the bill; the reason is kept with it.
  • It cancels this room only. For a group, cancel each room that is cancelled.

To void a booking

  1. More options, Void this booking. The window says “For one that never happened. Use Cancel if the guest cancelled.”
  2. Type Why: “Entered twice”, “wrong property”, “test booking”.
  3. Tap Void. The message says it “is on the record as never having happened.” It holds no room from then on.

A guest who has arrived: undo the check-in, cancel or void

A check-in that should not have happened (the wrong booking, a guest who left at once) is undone, cancelled or voided by the owner, an Admin, or the GM while The GM may undo a check-in is on in Front desk rules (A17.11; on at every hotel to begin with). The guest's More options then has Undo check-in, and Cancel this booking and Void this booking work on a guest in the house.

  1. More options, Undo check-in. The window Undo the check-in says the booking goes back to confirmed, arriving.
