  2. Type Why. It is kept on the booking, with your name and the time, in the Audit log.
  3. Tap Undo check-in. The message says “Check-in undone”: the booking is arriving again and its room is to be cleaned.
  • The room stays the booking's, vacant and sent for cleaning: the guest may have had the key. A key card cut for it stops.
  • The first night the check-in charged comes off the bill by itself, and is charged again if they check in again. Payments stay on the bill as an advance.
  • Any other charge on the bill (a night of a walk-in's stay, an early check-in, a restaurant bill charged to the room, laundry) has to be reversed on the bill first: “Laundry (₹300.00) is still on the bill. Reverse it on the bill first; payments stay on the bill as an advance.”
  • Form C: once a foreign guest's Form C has been submitted to the FRRO, the check-in stays, because the PMS cannot take back a report to the FRRO. Not yet submitted, it is simply no longer due, and the Form III screen no longer lists it.
  • A closed day: once a Night audit has closed the arrival day, the check-in stays. Check the guest out instead.
  • Cancel on a guest in the house undoes the check-in and cancels in one go: the window says so, and the booking's terms decide the charge as before; the owner, an Admin or the GM may waive it. Void does the same and is still refused once anything else is on the bill, payments included: cancel it instead. If either is refused, nothing of the undo happens.

Reception asks the GM

For reception (and anybody else who may change a booking but not do these), More options on a guest in the house shows Ask the GM to undo the check-in, Ask the GM to cancel this booking, Ask the GM to void this booking and Ask the GM to change the rate; Change dates has Ask the GM to change the arrival date, and the bill Ask the GM to change how it was paid (A4.7).

  1. Pick the Ask the GM to … line. The window says “Nothing changes until the GM approves it.”
  2. Fill in what it asks (the new arrival, the new rate, how it was paid) and Why.
  3. Tap Send to the GM. The message says “Sent to the GM”: it waits in the GM's Approvals and bell (A12.3). Approved, it is done, with every check asked again then.
  • A request that would be refused anyway is not sent: the message says why, such as a charge still on the bill.
  • One of each kind may wait for a stay at a time: “This is already with the GM.”
  • With nobody set to approve them at the hotel: “Nobody is set to approve these at this hotel. Call the GM.”
  • With The GM may undo a check-in off, nobody but the owner and an Admin undoes, cancels or voids a guest in the house, and reception cannot ask: “They have arrived, and undoing a check-in is off at this hotel. Check them out instead.” The rate, the arrival and how a payment was taken are not that switch's.

Watch out

  • Cancel and Void on a guest in the house are for the owner, an Admin and the GM (above); anybody else checks the guest out (A5) or asks the GM.
  • A booking with money on its bill cannot be voided: the system refuses and says why. Cancel it, so the terms apply.
  • A guest who has not arrived by the night audit becomes a no-show. Check in or cancel your arrivals before it runs.

Why it works this way

Cancelled and void mean opposite things to a report: a cancellation happened and measures demand; a void never happened, and counting it would inflate the figures the hotel sets its policy from. The terms are copied onto each booking when it is made, so a booking keeps the terms it was sold under even if the hotel changes them later. A waiting booking is cancelled with no charge: D27-64. After check-in, the GM has no lock and reception asks the GM, with a switch in the settings: D27-397.

A2.10For the owner: cancellation terms and booking sources

Two screens in Property setup decide what a booking carries.

Cancellation terms

Cancellation terms: “What a cancellation or a no-show costs at this property.” A hotel starts with none: “Until a policy exists, the night audit charges nothing on a no-show.” The owner, an Admin, the GM or the revenue manager writes them.

  1. Tap New policy.
  2. Type its Name, what the front desk will call it (“Flexible”).
  3. Type Free cancellation until: hours before arrival. Empty means no free window.
  4. Choose what A cancellation retains and what A no-show retains: Nothing, The first night, The whole stay, A percentage of the booking, or A fixed amount.
  5. Tap Save policy. Use for new bookings makes it the one new bookings carry.

Bookings already taken keep the terms they were made under.

Booking sources

Booking sources is the list New booking's Booking source is chosen from. “The list is the group's”: a source added here appears at every hotel. “The commission is this property's”: what this hotel agreed, copied onto each booking as it is taken. Add a source adds one. Commission on a source sets this hotel's per cent; blank means no rate has been agreed, which is not the same as 0. The owner, an Admin or the GM sets it.

A2.11CRS bookings

CRS bookings: “Bookings the CRS sold for this hotel, and what became of each”. A booking a salesperson makes in the CRS for this hotel arrives within five minutes as a booking waiting for the hotel, with the room held (A2.7). The desk confirms it. A change made in the CRS afterwards shows here as a note for the desk, with Done; nothing is changed by itself.

The owner and an Admin also see Connection to the CRS: the source CRS bookings are filed under, each CRS room type's match here, and Read bookings from the CRS. On the demo hotel it says “The CRS login is not in the server's settings yet, so nothing is read.”

A2.12In short

WhenDoSection
Where is a booking?All bookings: type a name, reference, room or phone. The search looks through every booking ever.A2.1
A booking on the phoneNew booking: name, phone, WhatsApp tick, dates, source, room type, read the price, Save booking. Read the reference.A2.2
The voucherBooked: Send voucher, once.A2.4
A walk-inRooms: tap a free room, name, phone, ID, Check in now.A2.5
Several roomsRooms more than 1, a Group name. Groups for the host's account and the lead guest.A2.6
Not accepted yetBooking details: Waiting for the hotel. Then Confirm the booking.A2.7
New dates, more guestsMore options: Change dates or guests.A2.8
A guest in the house changes roomMore options: Move to another room.A2.8
The guest cancelledMore options: Cancel this booking, with why.A2.9
Entered by mistakeMore options: Void this booking, with why.A2.9
Chapter A3

Check-in

For reception, the hotel manager, the general manager, an Admin and the owner: everyone who may check guests in. How to check a guest in from Arrivals, give a room ahead of arrival, take the guest's ID, check in a guest from abroad and keep the Form III register, ask for an advance, let a guest in early, and check in a guest who sent their ID from their own page.

A3.1Checking a guest in, from Arrivals

Check-in is one window. The room and the ID are on the left, the stay is on the right, and there is one button at the foot, Check in. A line under the button says what is still missing, so nobody has to guess why it is grey.

To check a guest in

  1. Open Arrivals (A1.3) and click the guest's row. The stay panel opens over the list (A1.4).
  2. Click Check in, the orange button at the top of the panel. The window Check in and the guest's name opens, with the booking's reference and room type under the name.
  3. The room. If the booking holds a room, it is shown on one line, for example “Room 204 · Inspected”, with Change room beside it. If it holds none, the rooms are listed for you to pick (A3.2).
  4. The ID. Choose the Document and type its Number, or give a reason for skipping it (A3.3). A guest from abroad has more to fill in (A3.4).
  5. The stay, in the box on the right: the dates and the nights (or “day use”), the adults and children, the meal plan, Rack rate and Offered. Offered is the rate this guest pays (“Complimentary” for a complimentary stay); Rack rate is the room type's listed rate, or a dash where it has none. If the guest turned up with more or fewer people, or a different meal plan, click Change beside it: the Adults and Children boxes, or the Meal plan list, open for editing.
  6. Ask the guest about offers and set Guest agreed to offers. Its own words: “Ask them. Unticked, no offers are sent. Kept against their phone and email at every hotel of the group.”
  7. Click Check in at the foot of the window.

When it goes through, a message says “A3 Test Iyer is in house” (the guest's name) with “Room 209 · the arrivals count has dropped.” and the panel behind changes: its status reads In house and its orange button becomes Settle and check out (A5). The first night's room charge and its GST are posted to the bill at that moment, so Charged at the foot is already filled in. A complimentary room is charged nothing. A hotel with no GST rule for rooms still checks the guest in, but posts nothing: the night audit, which will not run until that rule is set, posts the night.

Watch out

  • Where Check in is offered: on a booking opened from Arrivals (Today), All bookings or Walk-ins. The Upcoming list is for planning and does not offer it (A1.3). It is shown only to people who may change bookings: the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager and reception. Housekeeping and the Revenue Manager read the list without it.
  • A walk-in goes through this same check-in, from New booking's Check in now (A2.5), with the same checks.
  • A group's rooms are checked in one at a time, each from its own booking. The panel lists the group's other rooms on the right (A2.6).
  • If it is refused, the window stays open and a message, “Could not check in”, says why. Nothing was saved: the guest is still due in.
  • A red line at the top of the window, “… has the phone or email of …, who is blacklisted. Reason: …. Check-in is not refused - you decide.”, means a booking site's guest matches a blacklisted guest. It warns; a person decides (A1.3).

Why it works this way

Check-in was five steps and eight clicks; the owner's rule is two pages or three clicks, so the room, the ID and the stay are on one page under one button: D27-158, D27-163. It is laid out like New booking, with the room and the ID on the left and the stay on the right, each fact with its Change: D27-236. The first night is charged at check-in and the night audit never charges it twice: D27-204; with no GST rule for rooms the guest is still checked in: D27-205. Offers only to a guest who said yes, asked face to face: D25-39. A blacklisted guest is warned of, never refused: D22-8.

A3.2The room

A guest can be given a room the night before, or choose one at check-in. Either way, only a room that is ready and free can take a guest.

To give a room ahead of arrival

  1. Click Assign room, at the top right of Rooms and of the Calendar (A1.7). It is offered only to people who may change bookings.
  2. The window Assign a room says “Give an arriving booking a room before they get here.” and the business date. Under Waiting for a room are the bookings that are confirmed, have a room type and no room number yet: the guest, the room type, the dates and the reference. Click one.
  3. Under Room, choose a room from Choose a room…. Each line is the room number, its type and its rack rate, and “(different type)” after a room of another type. The list leaves out rooms that are out of service and rooms with a guest in them now.
  4. Click Assign the room. The message is “A3 Test Desai is in room 204” (the guest and the room). If the room is not the type booked, it adds “Note: … is not the room type they booked.”

If the room is taken for part of the stay or is out of service, the message says so, for example “Room 204 is out of service.”, and you choose again. When every arrival has a room, the window says “Every arrival has a room”. A booking that already has a room is not listed. To change a room already given, choose another at check-in with Change room: the room you check the guest into replaces the one the booking held.

The room at check-in

If the booking holds no room, the Check in window lists every room, the rooms of the room type booked first, one to a button. Each shows its number and its state. A room that can take the guest is white, with inspected or clean. The others are greyed and cannot be chosen; point at one to read why:

A greyed room saysMeans
dirty: “Not cleaned yet.”Housekeeping has not cleaned it (A6). Only a clean or inspected room can take a guest.
out-of-service: “Held out of service.”It is blocked for repair (A6.7).
Occupied: “… is in this room.”A guest is in it now.

A room of another type says “Deluxe (different type)” (its own type) beside its number. Choosing one is an upgrade, as one given with Assign room: the guest is checked in to it at the booked rate (below). The window's note says so: “A room of a different type is an upgrade: the booked rate stays.” The chosen room shows its type on its one line too, for example “Room 302 · Clean · Deluxe (different type)”.

Click a free room. The list folds into one line, “Room 301 · Inspected”, and Change room opens it again. Until a room is chosen, Check in is grey and the line under it says “Pick a room.” If the room the booking holds has turned dirty, the line says “Room 304: Not cleaned yet.” and the list opens for you to choose another.

A room whose last guest has not left yet shows a yellow line, “Omkar Shinde has not left this room yet.”, and “Guest still in” beside the room. Check in is not greyed for it, but the check-in is refused: “… is still in room 203. Check them out first, or choose another room.”

Watch out

  • The list offers the rooms of the type booked, and the room the booking already holds, whatever its type.
  • Another room type: Assign room accepts it, and says “Another type is allowed - it will be noted on the assignment.” The check-in accepts it too, and its message adds “Note: Deluxe is not the room type they booked.” The stay panel's Room then shows the room's own type and the type booked: “302 · Deluxe · booked Superior”.
  • The guest keeps the booked rate. A room of another type changes the room, not the price: the bill charges the rate agreed on the booking. To charge for the better room, change the rate on the Bill tab (A4.6).
  • The server asks the same questions as the window, and refuses by itself: a dirty room, “That room has not been cleaned yet.”; a room out of service, “That room is held out of service.”; a room held by another booking for part of the stay, “Room 301 is held by … for part of that stay.”

Why it works this way

A dirty room is shown, greyed, with the reason, rather than hidden: hiding it would teach nobody why. The check-in refuses a room a late guest is still in: D23-12. The booked room on one line, the grid only when it is needed: D27-236. A button the person may not use is hidden, not greyed: D24-18. An upgrade given with Assign room is checked in and noted, at the booked rate: D27-328. The Check in window lists every room type, so the upgrade can be given there: D27-330.

A3.3The guest's ID

The ID is asked on the same window, under the room. Indian properties must record a guest's identity document. It can be skipped, but then the reason is kept in the stay's note.

  • Nationality. Two letters, “IN” for India: “Two letters, IN for India. Anything else puts the stay on the Form III register.” It starts on the nationality on the guest's record, else the hotel's own (A17.11). A guest from abroad is A3.4.
  • Document. Not recorded, Passport, Aadhaar, Driving licence, Voter ID or Other. A hotel can leave some out and choose which one starts (A17.10, A17.11). Choosing one opens Number.
  • Number. The screen checks it by its type. An Aadhaar is 12 digits, never starting with 0 or 1, with UIDAI's check digit right: “That Aadhaar number is not right - a digit is mistyped. Check it against the card.” A passport is 6 to 15 letters and digits: “A passport number is 6 to 15 letters and digits, e.g. A1234567.” Any other document: “A document number is 4 to 40 characters.” The message is in red under the boxes and Check in stays grey.
  • A photo of the ID. Where the hotel keeps ID photos, the desk can add one for a guest who sent none: the front of the ID, the back if it has one, then a tick, “The guest agreed to the hotel keeping this photo”, and Add the photo. Cover the first eight digits of an Aadhaar first: “A photo showing the full number will be removed and we will ask you again.” It is kept encrypted for the owner, an Admin and the GM. Where the hotel cannot keep ID photos, the window says why in the server's words.

If the ID cannot be taken now

  1. Leave Document on Not recorded.
  2. Type Reason for skipping. It is required, for example “Scanner offline - to be captured at breakfast”.
  3. Until the ID is recorded, or a reason is given, Check in stays grey: “Record the ID document - type and number - or give a reason for skipping it.”

The other adults in the room

Every adult in the room is recorded: their name, nationality, and ID type and number. A foreigner also has the full Form III details and a row of their own on the Form III screen (A3.5). Under the ID, Adults in the room names the guest on the booking and each adult added, with a pill: “2 adults, 1 recorded”, yellow while somebody is missing. A child is not asked for, though one can be added.

The same block is on the stay panel, on the Stay tab, for anybody who arrives later or whose ID comes later; and on the card New booking shows when a walk-in has been checked in. It never stops a check-in: Check in does not wait for it, and each person is saved on their own.

To add an adult

  1. Click Add an adult.
  2. Type their Full name, as on the document. Nationality starts on the guest's: change it if theirs is different.
  3. Choose the Document and type its Number. The checks are those above. With no document to hand, leave it: no reason is asked, the name is saved, and the line says “ID not recorded”. They are counted as recorded once the number is typed.
  4. For a foreigner the Form III boxes open. Fill in what you have: none is needed now. Same as the guest copies the lead guest's visit answers (where they arrived from, the purpose, the reference address and the rest), so a family's are typed once; their phones and document stay their own, and any box can still be changed. The button shows once the lead guest has answered. The rest can be done with Edit, or with Complete details on the Form III screen.
  5. Click Save. It is on the stay at once, whether or not the check-in goes ahead.

Edit opens the same window with their details. It says what is on record, an Aadhaar as its last four digits, “Fill in the document only to replace it.” Remove asks “Remove them and their ID?”: Keep or Remove. Removed, their ID and their answers go with them. Once a Form III number is recorded for a person, the line says “Form III filed: corrected on the register.”: they stay on the stay (the record is kept for a year), and their details are corrected with Complete details (A3.5).

Watch out

  • A nationality that is not a country, such as ZZ, is refused: “"ZZ" is not a country code. Type the two letters, e.g. IN, GB or US.”
  • "IN" typed in the box never replaces a foreign nationality already on the guest's record. A wrong nationality is corrected on the guest's record (A10.3).
  • Adults in the room is for the people who record IDs: the owner, an Admin, the GM, the Hotel Manager and Reception. Nobody else sees it, and a companion's ID is kept as the guest's is.
  • Each room of a group has its own adults, on its own stay.
  • A room move, a longer stay or a change of dates does not touch them. With fewer adults on the booking than people recorded, nobody is taken off and there is no warning.
  • A cancelled, voided or no-show booking keeps who was on it, and nobody can be added to it.
  • The ID photo is still one per stay: the guest the booking is under.

Why it works this way

The ID and Form III's boxes are one set of fields shared by check-in and New booking, so they cannot ask different questions: D27-158. The hotel's own starting nationality and ID: D27-243; ID types the hotel does not take are left out: D27-260. "IN" never overwrites a foreign guest's nationality: D27-197. The desk adds the ID photo for a guest who sent none: D27-210. One ID photo per stay: D27-212. Every adult in a room is recorded, entered at check-in or later, and check-in is never blocked; a missing person is a warning: D27-382.

A3.4A guest from abroad: Form III at check-in

A guest whose nationality is anything but IN goes on the Form III register. Form III is the report of a foreign guest to the government's FRRO portal. It was called Form C until the 2025 Act. The arrival is reported within 24 hours of arrival, and the departure within 24 hours of leaving. The hotel is responsible for it.

To check in a guest from abroad

  1. Type the two letters of the guest's country in Nationality (for example GB). The Form III boxes open under the document.
  2. Choose the Document and type its Number, as in A3.3. A passport is the usual one.
  3. Fill in the starred boxes, which are needed now: Visa or OCI number, Visa type, Phone in India, Arrived from, Purpose of visit and Previous place of stay.
  4. The other boxes can be filled in later, from the Form III screen (A3.5): mobile numbers, gender, date of birth, the passport's and the visa's issue and expiry, the address abroad, the portal's arrival details and a reference address in India.
  5. Click Check in. Until the starred boxes are filled in it is grey, and the line under it says “Form III still needs: Arrived from, Purpose of visit, Previous place of stay.” (the boxes still blank).
  • Nepal and Bhutan. A citizen of Nepal (NP) or Bhutan (BT) needs no visa, so the two visa boxes are not asked.
  • An ID skipped for a reason. The visa boxes are not asked either. The visit's boxes still are: the guest answers those, no scanner needed.
  • An expired passport or visa is warned of, not refused: Check in anyway appears with “The passport expired on 2026-01-15. It is recorded as typed.” Until you switch it on, Check in stays grey: “The document has expired: say whether to check in anyway.” The date typed is kept as typed.
  • A date that cannot be right, or a phone that is not one, is refused in words: “The passport expires before it was issued.”, “"abc" is not a phone number. Type 10 to 15 digits, e.g. +91 98765 43210.”
  • A guest from abroad is never checked in by express (A3.8): the desk always fills in Form III.

Watch out

  • The server refuses by itself if a starred box is blank: “Form III needs a foreign guest's visa or OCI number, visa type, phone in India, ….”
  • Each foreigner in the room needs their own Form III: add them under Adults in the room (A3.3), and they have their own row on the Form III screen, under an Indian guest too (A3.5).
  • A test hotel's Form III card carries “TEST · NOT VALID”, so a practice guest's card is never filed.

Why it works this way

Form C was replaced by Form III under the Immigration and Foreigners Act 2025: arrival and departure each within 24 hours, with more details: D27-25. The law's own boxes are asked before check-in finishes and the rest may wait; an expired passport is warned of and recorded as typed. Nepal and Bhutan need no visa; an ID skipped for a reason takes its visa with it. The same boxes serve check-in, New booking and Complete details, so the three cannot ask different questions: D27-25.

A3.5The Form III screen

Open Form III (under Finance in the menu, A4.1; or Find a screen, Ctrl K). It shows passport numbers, so only people who check guests in see it: the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager and reception.

This system does not file with the FRRO. The screen says so itself. Filing happens on the government portal, where the guest's photo is taken. This screen is a register: it names who owes a filing, by when, and records the number the portal gives back.

To record a filing

  1. Read the badge beside the heading: “1 due” in yellow, or “1 overdue” in red. The line under the heading says “Foreign guests reported to the FRRO: arrival and departure, each within 24 hours (Form III, earlier called Form C).”
  2. Find the guest. Every foreigner on a stay has a row of their own: the person, their nationality, the room and how many are in it, and Passport (“not on record” in red where none is kept). A stay with an adult still to record says so on the row, in yellow: “2 adults, 1 recorded”. It is a warning: nothing is refused.
  3. In the Arrival cell, read the time of check-in and due or overdue with the time it is due by. File it on the portal.
  4. Click Record number, type the number the portal gives back in Portal number, and click Save. The number is required: Save stays grey until one is typed. The cell then reads filed with the number. Each person's number goes on their own row; the badge counts each person still owed. Add a number is for a second number, or for somebody who was never added: the stay's earlier numbers stay on the guest's row.
  5. When the guest has checked out, the Departure cell works the same way. Before that it says “In house”.

An Indian guest has no row here, and an adult nobody has recorded may be a foreigner. So above the list, for the stays in house with somebody missing: “Adults not recorded in house, each may be a foreigner: room 204 (2 adults, 1 recorded).” Add them on the stay.

  • Complete details opens the same boxes as check-in, with the guest's answers in them, and the Document and its Number. A passport skipped at check-in is recorded here, with the same checks as A3.3, and the row then shows it in place of “not on record”. After check-out it also asks Next destination (A5.8). Click Save.
  • The printer icon opens the Form III card: the premises, the foreigner, the arrival, the departure and the portal's other boxes, with two signature lines, one for arrival and one for departure. Click Print. A blank box prints as a dash, so the desk sees what is still to ask. The guest signs it on arrival and on departure; a guest who cannot write signs with a thumb impression. Keep the card.
  • When nobody is owed: “Every foreign national on record has been filed.” With no foreign guest at all: “No foreign nationals have stayed”.

Why it works this way

The portal has no upload and no way for a program to file, so the screen is a register and says so: a hotel that believed the PMS had filed would stop filing, and find out at an inspection. The number is required because a register with no evidence reads as compliance and is not: D27-25. Only the people who check guests in see passport numbers: D25-38.

A3.6An advance before check-in

A hotel may ask for money before it gives the room. Its rule is set in Settings (A17.11), under Advance before check-in: None (where every hotel starts), The first night or The whole stay. It asks the agreed rate with its GST. What is already paid counts: an advance taken on New booking (A2.3), or any payment on the guest's own bill.

When the guest still owes it, Check in is grey and the line under it says how much, for example “An advance of ₹4,303.95 is owed before check-in (the first night ₹4,303.95, paid ₹0). Take it on the Bill tab.” With the rule on The whole stay it reads “(the whole stay …, paid …)”.

  • It is never asked of a company's booking, a room the group's host pays for, a complimentary room, a stay with no agreed rate, or a booking prepaid on a booking site.
  • A booking-site guest has the switch Prepaid on the booking site, ticked at first, with “Untick when the guest pays at the hotel: the advance before check-in is then asked.” Untick it and the line under Check in is asked again at once.
  • Taking it: on the Bill tab (A4.7), click Settle. Before arrival it opens for the advance: the window says “₹… advance owed before check-in”, the Amount is the advance still owed, and “An advance before check-in: it is held as the guest's credit until the stay's charges are posted.” Click Take payment; no tick is asked. A part paid leaves the rest owed: Settle opens again for it, and the line under Check in shows what is left.
  • A deposit with no advance asked (the rule on None, or the advance paid): Settle still opens before arrival, as “A deposit before arrival”. The Amount is empty: type what the guest gives. “A deposit before arrival: it is held as the guest's credit until the stay's charges are posted.” Click Take payment; no tick is asked.
  • On New booking, an advance typed in Advance (A2.3) is taken first, then Check in now checks the guest in, so the advance counts.
  • There is no way round it at the desk. A hotel that does not want an advance sets the rule to None.

Why it works this way

The advance is a per-hotel rule, none to start, asked of the first night or the whole stay and never of a company's booking or a booking prepaid on a booking site: D27-243, D27-246. There is no override: the refusal names the amount, and the desk takes it on the Bill tab, or the hotel sets None: D27-246. Settle opens before arrival for it, and New booking takes it before checking in: D27-328. Settle takes a deposit before arrival with no advance asked, its amount typed, never filled in: D27-330.

A3.7An early arrival

There are two kinds of early, and a yellow box on the Check in window says which. Both need a reason, and both are allowed: this is a hotel, and a guest off an overnight train is a normal day.

Before the hotel's check-in time

The booking is for today, but it is before the time rooms are ready (Settings, Rooms ready from, A17.11). The box says “Rooms are ready from 14:00.” and then whether the hotel charges: “This property does not charge for an early arrival.” or “An early arrival is ₹….” The question is asked of the server, so the answer is the hotel's clock, not the computer's.

  1. Type Why the room is being given early. It is required, for example “Overnight train, room vacant and clean”. Until then Check in is grey: “Say why the room is being given early.”
  2. Where there is a charge, the owner, the GM and a group administrator also have a tick, Waive the charge. It reads “The reason is still recorded, and its absence from the bill is visible.” Anybody else records the reason and the charge goes on.
  3. Click Check in. The charge, with its GST, goes on the bill under Room, at the room's own GST rate.

Before the booked day

The booking is for a later day and the guest is standing here now. The box says “This booking is for 14 Oct 2026. Checking in now moves it to today, so tonight is charged.” Type the reason, as above. Checking in moves the booking: the arrival becomes today, which is what happened, and the room is held from today.

More than a day early, the first press of Check in shows the move before anything happens: “This moves the arrival from 14 Oct 2026 to 11 Oct 2026: 6 nights, ₹18,270.00 with GST.” Nothing moves until you click Confirm. Cancel leaves the booking as it was. Where there is no GST rule for the rate, the figure is before GST, and a complimentary stay says “complimentary.”

Watch out

  • Both kinds can apply at once. The box then gives the date sentence, and after it what an early arrival costs.
  • The room is still checked for the whole stay. A room somebody else has tomorrow is refused, with the other booking's reference: “Room 301 is held by … for part of that stay.”
  • Only the owner, the GM and a group administrator may waive. The server asks again: “Setting that charge aside is a manager's decision. Record it and let it charge, or ask a manager to waive it.”
  • The fee is set on Settings, Money, Extra charges (A17.9). Where none is set, the box says the property does not charge.

Why it works this way

A guest in a room that is not ready is a decision, not a formality, so it is allowed but never silent: somebody says why, their name goes with it, and any charge reaches the bill. More than a day early used to be refused; it is now allowed, warned of and confirmed: D27-193. The early fee sits under Room on the bill: D27-223. The booking moves with the guest, and its room hold with it: D27-205.

A3.8Express check-in: a guest who sent their ID online

A guest can send their ID and address from their own page before they arrive. The page's link comes with the voucher, and the desk can send it again (A2.4, A10.7). Online check-in is on for every hotel unless the hotel switches it off. A guest cannot pay or choose a room from their page.

What the guest sends is not on their record until the desk has looked at the real ID and confirmed it. Then, at check-in, the ID is not typed again.

To confirm what a guest sent

  1. Open Online check-in (under Front desk, A1.10). Under Details waiting to be checked, each card shows the guest, the booking's reference and when it was sent, then what they typed: the kind of ID and its number (an Aadhaar shows only its last four digits, a passport shows whole), a passport's expiry, a visa, the address, and the photo of the ID if they sent one, to look at beside what they typed.
  2. Look at the guest's real ID. If it matches, click Confirm against the ID.
  3. If it is not right, click Not right - take them at the desk. The desk then takes the ID at check-in as usual.

At check-in

While details are waiting that nobody has confirmed, the ID step of the Check in window says “This guest sent their ID details online - check them on Online check-in”. The link opens in a new tab, so the check-in in progress is not lost.

Once the desk has confirmed them, the ID step shows the confirmed ID in place of the boxes: “ID confirmed from online check-in: Aadhaar ••••••••••3458”, with only the last four digits. Nothing more is asked about the ID, and Check in is orange as soon as the room is chosen. Use a different ID opens the usual boxes again.

Watch out

  • Only this stay's own online check-in counts. A document kept from an earlier visit never does.
  • A guest from abroad is never express. The desk fills in their Form III (A3.4).
  • Only the people who run the desk see these screens and the link: the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager and reception.
  • Confirming is the clerk's act, under the clerk's name. Nothing the guest sends reaches their record or Form III unchecked.

Why it works this way

Everything the guest sends is a submission that the desk confirms against the ID, under the clerk's name: D21-8. An Aadhaar is shown as its last four digits on every screen: D21-18. An Indian guest whose ID the desk confirmed just collects the key; a foreign guest still goes through the full check: D27-236. Express counts only this stay's own confirmed submission: D27-242. Online check-in is on for every hotel: D27-281.

A3.9The registration card

The guest's registration card, the hotel's old card in Fidato's design, for the guest to sign. It is printed from a button, never by itself.

  1. Open the guest's stay panel: In house (A1.5), or the panel of a guest you have just checked in.
  2. Click Print registration card, in the row of buttons at the top. The card opens in a new tab.
  3. Click Print. Give it to the guest to sign, and to initial the box at the foot if they want no offers. With other adults recorded on the stay (A3.3), the card lists them under Other adults in the room: name, nationality and ID, an Aadhaar as its last four digits.

It shows the hotel; the guest's name, address, e-mail and phone; the stay: arrival, departure, room, persons and the tariff a night before GST, with the meal plan; the company that pays, and the travel agent with its voucher number; the ID and the nationality; where a guest from abroad arrived from and goes next (Form III, A3.4); a Remark box to write in; the hotel's house policies; the signature box and the box for no offers. Anything not known prints a dash.

  • G.R. card no: the card's number, 1, 2, 3 and on for each hotel, given when the guest is checked in. The tax invoice prints it too (A4.11). A guest checked in before 19 October has none, and the card prints a dash.
  • An Aadhaar prints as its last four digits only, for example “Aadhaar · XXXX XXXX 5674”. A passport or any other ID prints whole.
  • The house policies are the hotel's own lines, the same ones the booking voucher prints (Settings › Policies, A17.4).

Watch out

  • The Remark box is left blank, to write in. A booking's notes can be the hotel's own, so they are never printed on it.
  • Printing it changes nothing. Print it again whenever it is needed.
  • The button is for the people who may read guests' IDs: the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager and reception.
  • A test hotel's card is stamped “TEST · NOT VALID” and carries no GSTIN.

Why it works this way

The card as the old system printed it, numbered, with Aadhaar as its last four digits until the lawyer answers (D25-37), printed from a button: D27-344. The numbers start at 1 and only a check-in from 19 October gets one; the house policies over the signature; the Remark left blank: D27-345. An Aadhaar on every screen is its last four digits: D21-18.

A3.10Check-in in short

Chapter A4

The guest's bill

For reception, the general manager and the accountant. How to read a guest's bill, post a charge, take a wrong one off, correct a charge or the rate, take a payment, split the bill with a company, print the proforma bill, run your cash drawer, and what happens after check-out: the tax invoice and the credit note.

A4.1Where the money is: the Finance screens

At the desk, a guest's money is the bill: the Bill tab of the guest's panel (A4.2). In Finance the same thing is called a folio. The Finance part of the menu holds these screens. You see the ones your role uses; reception's menu shows Cashiering, and reaches the others with Find a screen (Ctrl K, A0).

ScreenWho uses itWhat it is for
FoliosThe GM, the accountant; reception by Find a screenEvery bill still owing, or owed back. Click a guest to open their bill.
InvoicesThe accountant, the GMDeparted stays ready to bill: the numbered tax invoice, the credit note, the VAT bills for alcohol (A4.11).
PaymentsThe accountant, the GMEvery receipt against a bill, newest first. Reversed receipts stay on the list.
CashieringReception, and whoever takes cash at the deskYour own cash drawer: what you took, money in and out, the count, the hand-over (A4.10).
Cash depositsThe owner, an administrator, the GM, the accountant, the ViewerEach closed day's cash to deposit, what was banked, and who verified it.
Company accountsThe desk and the accountantWhat each company or booking site owes and paid. Record payment when a company pays (A4.8).
Supplier duesThe accountant, the GM, the owner, an AdminWhat the hotel owes suppliers: the bills taken on credit, part payments, TDS, credit notes and each supplier's statement - the same list as Purchasing's Supplier dues tab (A9.11).
Form IIIWhoever checks guests inForeign guests reported to the FRRO (chapter A3).
Online paymentsThe owner, administrators, the GMMarked “Not built yet”: a page saying what it will do.

Why it works this way

“Bill” at the desk and “folio” in Finance are the owner's words (15 September). A balance in either direction is real: a guest overpaid is money the hotel owes, and it is shown, never as zero.

A4.2Reading the guest's bill

To open a guest's bill

  1. Open In house and click the guest. Their panel opens on the right.
  2. Click the Bill tab. (The orange Settle and check out at the top of the panel opens the same tab.) From Folios, a guest opens straight on the bill.
  • The first night is posted at check-in, each later night by the night audit. Until then, the nights to come are shown in the dashed box, at the agreed rate with their GST, and counted in Due. Any advance and anything paid are counted too.
  • If no GST rule covers the room's rate, the box shows a dash, never a figure the system guessed.
  • When no nights are to come, the top shows Balance, marked Outstanding, Overpaid or Settled.
  • The bill is in sections: Room, Restaurant, Bar (alcohol, under VAT), then Other charges. Each line shows its amount before tax; each section has its subtotal and its tax. The early check-in and late check-out fees charged when the guest checks in early or leaves late sit under Room.
  • Under the sections: Total charges, then Payments received, then the last row: what is due.

The bill's one orange button is the next step: Settle while money is owed, then Check out once nothing is (chapter A5). A button you may not use is not offered; one that cannot be used yet is greyed, and says why when you point at it.

Why it works this way

The headline counts the nights still to come, so the desk sees what is owed from check-in: D27-187, D27-199. The bill in sections, the same on the screen and on paper: D27-200; the early and late fees under Room: D27-223. Roles that do not handle money do not see the Bill tab: D27-143.

A4.3Posting a charge

To post a charge

  1. On the Bill tab, click Add charge. The window Post a charge names the room and the guest.
  2. If the hotel keeps a priced list of extra charges, From the hotel's list comes first: choosing one fills the words, the price and the category. Each can still be changed.
  3. Choose the Category: Room posting, Food, Beverages, Late check-out fee, Early check-in fee, Extra person fee, Laundry or Miscellaneous.
  4. Type the Description: the words the guest reads on the bill (“Laundry, 3 shirts”).
  5. Type the Amount, before tax.
  6. Leave Taxable ticked. It shows the GST rate this amount carries, and the box under it the tax, split CGST and SGST, and the total. Untick it only for a charge that bears no GST.
  7. Click Post charge. The message “Charge posted” gives the amount with tax and the room.

Watch out

  • No GST rule, no charge. If the hotel has not set the GST rule, Taxable shows “GST -” and the charge is refused with the reason. A missing rate is not zero; somebody sets it first (Finance, Invoices, or Settings).
  • Post charge stays off until there is a description and an amount above zero. To take money off a bill, reverse the charge it corrects (A4.4); a charge is never a minus figure.
  • One press is one charge: the button waits while the charge is sent.
  • A company over its credit limit: the window says so in a sentence. The owner, an administrator or the GM can post it anyway with a reason (Allow, with reason); anybody else asks one of them.
  • The bill has no discount button. A lower room price is a manager's Change rate (A4.6).

Why it works this way

Everything posted at the desk carries the room's GST rule for that amount, and the window shows that rate before you post, so the bill never has a rate nobody set. Each line names the person signed in when it was posted. Over a company's credit limit only with a manager's reason: D27-275.

A4.4Taking a wrong charge off: Reverse

A charge is never edited or deleted at the desk. A wrong one is reversed: it stays on the bill, struck through, and the reversal is its own line.

To reverse a charge

  1. Click the curved arrow at the end of the line (Figure A4-06, arrow 4).
  2. The window Reverse this charge? names the line and its amount with tax.
  3. Type Why. It is required. If the hotel has set ready reasons, they show under the box: click one to use it.
  4. Click Reverse (Keep it leaves the line as it is). The message: “Posting reversed - The reversal is its own line - nothing was edited.”

Watch out

  • A line is reversed once, and a reversal cannot itself be reversed. Post the charge again if it was right after all.
  • A line from a day the night audit has closed: “This day is closed - correct it on Closed days.” (chapter A7).
  • Once a tax invoice stands on the bill: “This bill has tax invoice … Only a credit note corrects it now.” (A4.11).
  • A payment is reversed only by the owner, an administrator, the GM or the accountant. Its window, Reverse this payment?, says the receipt stays on the bill, struck through, and the money is owed again.
  • A greyed arrow cannot be used: point at it to read why.

Why it works this way

The bill only ever grows: what was posted stays, so anyone can see what happened and who did it. Reversing asks first, with a reason: D27-117. Reception reverses charges; a payment only the four above: D27-125.

A4.5A manager corrects a charge

For the owner, an administrator and the GM. Their bill has a pencil on each charge: change its price, its words, or both, with a reason, in one step.

To correct a charge

  1. Click the pencil on the line. The window Edit this charge names it and its amount with tax.
  2. Change the Words, the Price before tax, or both. The tax stays at the rate it was charged.
  3. Type Why. It is required, and kept on the reversed line; the guest's bill never shows it.
  4. Click Correct the charge. The message: “Charge corrected - The old line is reversed with the reason, and the corrected one posted.”

Watch out

  • No pencil on a payment, a reversal, or a line already reversed: there is nothing to edit.
  • The pencil is greyed on a day the night audit closed (“This day is closed - correct it on Closed days.”) and once a tax invoice stands on the bill (a credit note corrects it then).
  • A room night: only its price changes. “A room night's words count its nights, so only its price changes.” Its tax follows the room's slab on the new price.
  • Drinks that already have a VAT bill are refused until that VAT bill is cancelled.

Why it works this way

The owner, an administrator and the GM may correct a charge; the old line stays, reversed with the reason, and the corrected one is posted in the same step: D27-157, D27-162.

A4.6Changing the rate

Also for the owner, an administrator and the GM: Change rate, after the other buttons, gives the whole stay a new rate a night.

To change the rate

  1. Click Change rate. The window Change the rate names the guest and the rate now.
  2. Type the New rate a night, before tax. The room's GST slab follows it.
  3. If the figure you typed already includes GST, tick Includes GST. The window then shows how it splits, for example “₹… a night + ₹… GST (5%).”
  4. Type Why. It is kept with every night it corrects.
  5. Click Change the rate. Nights already charged are corrected to it, with this reason (a closed day's on Closed days); nights still to come are charged at it. The message “Rate changed” says how many charged lines were corrected.

Watch out

  • All or nothing. If one charged night cannot be corrected, nothing changes and the message names that night.
  • Only a booking still to come or a guest in the house changes rate. After check-out, a bill is corrected on Closed days or by a credit note.
  • Before check-in, the same window opens from the guest panel's More options, Change rate: it changes only the agreed rate, since nothing is charged yet. On a guest in the house it opens there too. Reception sees Ask the GM to change the rate (A2.9).

Why it works this way

Change rate for the same three, nights already posted corrected through the Closed days correction where the day is closed: D27-157, D27-162. A rate that includes GST is split by the room's slab before it is kept: D27-199.

A4.7Taking a payment: Settle

To take a payment

  1. On the Bill tab, click Settle. The window Settle bill says what is outstanding, and whose bill it is.
  2. On a stay with two bills, choose Which bill (A4.8). One bill is settled at a time.
  3. Choose the Method. The list is the hotel's own ways of paying (Settings); the hotel's default is chosen first. Every hotel started with Cash, UPI, Credit Card, Debit Card and Bill to company.
  4. The Amount is filled in with what is owed. Change it for a part payment.
  5. Check Outstanding, Paying and Remaining, and click Take payment. The message names the amount received and the method.

The payment shows under Payments received: “Received - Cash”, or for Bill to company “Transferred to city ledger”. Cash goes into your drawer, which opens by itself with your first cash (A4.10). When nothing is owed, Check out opens (chapter A5).

Watch out

  • More than the bill: the window says “This is ₹… more than the bill; it will be held as the guest's credit.” Take payment stays off until you tick Hold it as the guest's credit.
  • Before arrival, Settle opens for an advance the hotel asks before check-in, filled in with what is still owed and held as the guest's credit without a tick (A3.6). With no advance asked and nothing posted, it opens for a deposit: “A deposit before arrival”, the Amount empty for you to type, held as the guest's credit the same way.
  • Cash above ₹1,00,000 at once asks for the Guest's PAN, or the tick No PAN: Form 97 taken. Cash of ₹2,00,000 or more from one guest is refused; take the rest another way.
  • A company's bill (A4.8) goes Bill to company only if the company is allowed credit. Otherwise the message says it is not: take the payment another way, or ask the owner, an administrator or the GM to allow credit on its record.
  • One press is one payment. A wrong payment is reversed only by the owner, an administrator, the GM or the accountant (A4.4).

To change how a payment was taken

Cash typed when the guest paid by UPI is the common mistake. Each payment line has a wallet button, Change how it was paid, for the owner, an administrator and the GM. Reception's says Ask the GM to change how it was paid and sends it to the GM (A2.9).

  1. Click the wallet button on the payment line.
  2. Choose How it was really paid. Bill to company is not offered: it is not a way of paying.
  3. Type Why and click Change it. The payment is reversed with the reason, and the same amount is received again, the same day, the new way: “Received - UPI (was Cash)”, in the name of whoever took it.
  • Refused on a day the Night audit has closed (the button is grey and says so), and for cash in a drawer already counted and closed: put the difference right on today's drawer.
  • Changed to cash, the person who took it must have their drawer open, so the cash is counted there. Over ₹1,00,000 in cash needs the PAN: reverse it and take it again in cash with the PAN.

Why it works this way

More than the bill is held as the guest's credit, once the desk ticks it: D27-4, D27-11. The PAN or Form 97 above ₹1,00,000 in cash (Income-tax Rule 159): D25-40. Cash opens your drawer by itself: D27-200.

A4.8Two bills: when a company pays

A company pays the room; the guest pays their own extras. Split the bill: the stay gets a second bill in the company's name, and each line goes on the bill that pays it.

To split the bill

  1. On the Bill tab, click Split the bill.
  2. Under Who is paying the second bill? choose the company, and click Open the second bill. The message: “Second bill opened - Move charges onto it from the ledger above.”
  3. Above the lines, the bills now show side by side: Everything, Guest, and the company, each with what it owes. Click one to see only its lines.
  4. To move a line, click the two-arrow button at its end, then under Move to the bill it belongs on. The message: “Moved - Reversed on one bill and posted on the other - nothing was edited.”
  5. Settle each bill on its own (A4.7). For the company's, choose it under Which bill and the Method Bill to company: “Transfers to the city ledger”. The amount goes to the company's account.

When the company pays, record it on Company accounts: Record payment, then Who paid, Amount received, Received on, How (bank transfer, cheque, UPI or card, never cash), Reference (the bank's UTR or the cheque's number), and an optional Note.

Beside each account on Company accounts, Statement opens its statement of account - the bills sent, the payments and the balance for the days chosen, to print or send as a PDF or Excel file. Under the table, Money owed by age shows how old each account's balance is (A11.6).

Watch out

  • Only a company on file can be chosen. With none, the window says to add one under Companies first: a company's bill carries its GSTIN and address.
  • A payment stays on the bill it was taken on, and a reversed line cannot be moved: neither has the move button.
  • Nights a group's company pays for are on the group's own bill, not on the guest's.

Why it works this way

A move is a reversal on one bill and a posting on the other, so nothing is edited. A guest's figures count only the guest's own bill: D27-226. A company's payment is never cash: D27-242.

A4.9The proforma bill

The guest asks to see the bill before paying, or a company wants a copy.

  1. On the Bill tab, click Proforma bill. The window Proforma bill is the print preview.
  2. Click Print. The bill opens on a page of its own; print it from there.

It is laid out as the tax invoice is (Figure A4-21): the hotel, the stay in two columns, every line with its HSN/SAC, its taxable value and each tax, the payments, the tax by rate and the totals. Under the Total come Paid, any night still to be posted tonight, and Balance due (or Overpaid). A reversed line and its reversal are left off it. It says “Proforma Bill” and that it is not a tax invoice, and carries the booking's reference, never an invoice number: the numbered tax invoice is issued at check-out (A5.9).

Why it works this way

The desk's print never says “Tax Invoice”, before check-out or after, so nobody takes it for the numbered tax invoice: D22-7; the button says what it opens: D24-25. The interim bill became the proforma bill, laid out as the tax invoice: D27-344.

A4.10Your cash drawer: Cashiering

Every rupee of cash taken at the desk belongs to somebody's drawer. Open Cashiering (Finance, in reception's menu) to see yours.

Opening

  • There is no step to open. Your drawer opens by itself the first time you take cash.
  • If the last person handed you a float by name, the line says so (“₹… was handed to you: your drawer opens on it.”) and your drawer opens on it. Otherwise it opens at ₹0.
  • Only when a float is given to you by hand, count it here: type how many of each note. The button becomes Open the drawer - ₹…; click it.

During the shift

  • Taken this shift lists what you took, by method. Only cash reaches the drawer: a card payment, or a bill sent to a company, is not in the tin.
  • Money that was not a payment: under In and out of the drawer, click Record. Choose What happened (Paid out, Cash in, To the safe), type How much and What was it for, and click Record.
  • A Paid out also needs its Category: Kitchen, Housekeeping, Maintenance, Office or Other (Record stays grey until one is chosen). Add the Photo of the bill if you have it: the phone's camera, or a file. It can be added later with Add photo under the paid-out; Photo of the bill opens it. A paid-out from before 27 October 2026 shows a dash for its category.
  • A Paid out waits for the GM's or the owner's yes. Until then it reads “Waiting for a yes - not taken off the drawer yet”. Every paid-out is in the Petty cash report (A11.6).
  • The drawer, on the right, adds it up: Opening float, Cash taken, money in and out, Expected, and Counted.

At the end of your shift

  1. Under Count the drawer, type how many of each note and coin, and click Save the count.
  2. The drawer says “The drawer balances”, or “Over by …” / “Short by …”. A difference does not stop the hand-over, but it has to be written down.
  3. Click Close and hand over. If the count differs, type Why.
  4. Hand the drawer to: the next person, or Nobody.
  5. Float kept for the next shift: always typed, from ₹0 up to what you counted. Above ₹0 it needs the next person's name. The rest is to deposit.
  6. Click Close the shift.

The cash to deposit is banked from Cash deposits: the GM records each day's deposit (amount, date, bank, slip number and the slip's photo), and the owner or the accountant verifies it.

Why it works this way

Each cash point counts in and counts out, and the deposits are logged and verified: D27-190. The drawer opens by itself with the first cash: D27-200. A float kept waits for the person named: D27-201; it is always typed, and the rest goes to deposit: D27-202. A paid-out counts only once the GM or the owner says yes: D27-242.

A4.11After check-out: the tax invoice and the credit note

The proforma bill is not a tax invoice. The numbered GST tax invoice is issued once the guest has checked out and the bill is settled: at check-out, by itself unless the hotel has chosen otherwise (A5.9), or here on Invoices.

To issue a tax invoice

  1. Open Invoices. Its list is the departed stays ready to bill.
  2. Click Issue on the stay. It is greyed while the bill still owes or is overpaid; point at it to read why.
  3. The window Issue this tax invoice? says who it is billed to and the next number in the GST series. Click Issue the invoice.
  • A stay with two bills gets an invoice for each bill.
  • Who it is made out to. A company's bill: that company. The guest's bill: the company the booking is billed to (Bill to company), as before; with none, the guest's own company when a GSTIN was typed for it on the booking (A2.2) or on the booking's panel (A10.3) - its name, GSTIN and address - and otherwise the guest. With only a GSTIN typed and no company name, the guest's own name is printed with that GSTIN. The guest still pays the bill at the desk: nothing about who pays changes.
  • Alcohol is under VAT: its own VAT bill is issued in the same step, from its own series.
  • The stay's row then shows the invoice's number. Click it to open the invoice on its own page, with Print and Send invoice (by email, with the PDF; the test hotel sends nothing).
  • The hotel's Tax invoice switch (A10.7, A17.12) sends an invoice by itself only when it is made out to the guest. One made out to a company, an agent or a booking site, for example Expedia, is not sent by itself: click Send invoice on its page. One made out to the guest's own company (typed on the booking) is the guest's bill, so it is sent to the guest by itself.
  • It can also be issued on the guest's bill right after check-out (A5.9).

What the printed invoice shows

Print prints it on the desk's own printer, on one A4 page for an ordinary stay, without the menu. The invoice e-mailed to the guest is the same document, as a PDF. It carries everything the hotel's old folio invoice did, in Fidato's document style:

  • At the top: the hotel's own logo and the Fidato Hotels logo side by side (each when uploaded: A17.3, A17.4), the hotel's name and "by" the group, and on the right TAX INVOICE with its number and time, over the orange rule; above it “ORIGINAL FOR RECIPIENT”, and on the second copy “DUPLICATE FOR SUPPLIER” (A5.9). Under it the hotel's address, phone, e-mail and website, and its GSTIN and PAN.
  • Two columns: the booking reference, the G.R. card no (the registration card's number, A3.9; a dash for a guest checked in before 19 October), invoice number, guest, who it is billed to (with their GSTIN or "not registered"), the source, the place of supply; the date of the invoice, the business date, the room type and number, the persons (adults and children), the rate type, the nights, arrival and departure.
  • The lines: each charge with its HSN/SAC, quantity, rate, total, discount, taxable value, SGST, CGST, IGST and CESS (IGST and CESS are always 0.00: a stay is supplied in the hotel's own state), and the totals under them.
  • Below: the amount in words, the payments received, the tax by rate; on the right the totals, what was paid and the balance.
  • At the foot: who checked the guest in (Reception (C/I)) and out (Cashier (C/O)) and who issued it, in a grey strip; the guest's signature and the hotel's authorised signatory; then the group's name and office (address, phone, e-mail, website, Instagram) from Settings, Group (A17.4), or the hotel's own address until those are typed.
  • A long bill runs onto a second page, with the columns' names again at its top.
  • The e-mailed PDF can show a logo only if it was uploaded as a PNG picture. An SVG logo shows on the printed invoice only.

To correct an issued invoice: the credit note

  1. Open the invoice from the list under Issued, and click Cancel this invoice.
  2. Type Why the invoice was wrong.
  3. Click Issue credit note. The invoice is not edited and not deleted: a credit note with its own number is issued against it, and both stay on the record.

Watch out

  • A credit note is for the owner, an administrator, the GM or the accountant. For anyone else the button is greyed, with that sentence.
  • Once a tax invoice stands on a bill, its charges cannot be reversed or edited at the desk: the credit note is the correction.
  • E-invoicing (an IRN and a signed QR) is not required: the group is under ₹5 crore of turnover. The Invoices screen says so.

Why it works this way

An issued GST document never changes, and its number is never lost from the series; a mistake is corrected by a document of its own. Who issues a credit note: D22-33. Alcohol's own VAT bill: D22-44. The printed invoice laid out as the hotel's old one, keeping "Tax Invoice" and both signatures, with no registration card number: D27-342. Fidato's document style, both logos, the group's office at the foot, and the e-mailed PDF the same document on A4: D27-343.

A4.12The bill in short

WhenDoSection

Something to addAdd charge: category, words, amount before tax, Post charge.A4.3
A charge is wrongThe curved arrow on its line, Why, Reverse.A4.4
A price or words need correcting (managers)The pencil, Why, Correct the charge.A4.5
A new rate for the stay (managers)Change rate, Why, Change the rate.A4.6

The guest paysSettle, the method, Take payment. Then Check out.A4.7

Chapter A5

Check-out

For reception, the hotel manager, the general manager, an Admin and the owner: everyone who may check guests out. How to take the last payment, print the bill, check a guest out, what happens when a guest leaves after the check-out time or before the booked day, how to give back money a guest paid too much, a foreign guest's next destination, the tax invoice that follows, and why every departure is checked out before the night audit.

A5.1Checking a guest out

Check-out ends the stay: the bill closes, the room goes to housekeeping as dirty, and the guest leaves the In house list. It is done on the guest's Bill tab, with the last button on it, Check out. The button opens only when the bill owes nothing.

To check a guest out

  1. Open Due out (A1.6), the guests leaving today, and click the guest. The panel opens on the Bill tab. For any other guest, one who leaves early or stays past the date, open In house (A1.5), click the guest and click Settle and check out, the orange button at the top of the panel. From Folios (A4.1) a guest also opens on the bill.
  2. Read the bill (A4.2). Total charges is everything posted, with tax.
  3. If money is owed, take the payment first (A5.2). If the guest asks to see the bill, print it (A5.3).
  4. For a guest from abroad, type their Next destination (A5.8).
  5. Click Check out, the full-width button at the foot of the bill. It turns orange once nothing is owed.
  6. The window Check … out? asks you to be sure (A5.4). Click Check out again.
  7. Depending on the date and the hour, the window may first ask why the guest is leaving late (A5.5) or early (A5.6).

When it is done, a message says “A5 Test Rane checked out” (the guest's name) with “Room 303 is now dirty and on housekeeping's board.” The panel stays open on the bill, and the guest's tax invoice is issued and printed by itself, two copies, unless the hotel has chosen otherwise (A5.9).

When Check out is grey

A button that cannot be used yet says why: the reason is written under it in red, and shows when you point at the button (Figure A4-04).

It saysWhat to do
“₹3,884 is still owed on this bill.” (the amount owed)Take the payment: Settle (A5.2).
“This bill is overpaid. Refund the difference first.”Give the money back (A5.7).
Nothing under it, and a Next destination box above itA guest from abroad: type where they go next (A5.8).
“This guest is not in house.”The guest has not been checked in (A3).
“Already checked out.”Nothing to do.

Watch out

  • Who may: the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager and reception. A role that sees bills but may not change bookings, such as the accountant, sees the bill without the button.
  • A stay with no bill at all shows a dash, never ₹0, and can be checked out without settling.
  • A guest stays In house until checked out, even after the departure date has passed (A1.5).
  • A group's rooms are checked out one at a time, each from its own booking. A room whose nights a group's company pays has those nights on the group's own bill, so the guest's Check out counts only the guest's own bill (A4.8). The group's bill is settled on the group's page (A2.6).
  • A guest who checks in and out on the same day owes that night, charged at check-in (A3.1): Check out waits until it is paid, or the charge is reversed with a reason (A4.4).

Why it works this way

Check-out is shown greyed with its reason, never hidden: a button that vanishes teaches nobody why. It asks "are you sure" first, because it closes the bill and sends the room to housekeeping: D27-117. It follows the one balance on screen, so it opens when a payment brings the bill to zero, and no longer greys with no reason for a few seconds after a payment: D27-313. A guest's own figures count only the guest's own bill: D27-226. A stay with no bill shows a dash: D17-16.

A5.2Taking the last payment

Check out needs the bill at zero. Take the payment with Settle: choose the Method, check the Amount (it is filled in with what is owed; change it only for a part payment) and click Take payment. A4.7 has every step and every warning; a stay with two bills settles each bill on its own (A4.8).

Cash is taken to the rupee

A room bill has paise in it, because GST is worked out on each night's rate, and nobody hands over paise. So when the method is cash, the cash taken is the nearest rupee, and the window shows how: under Paying it gives the exact amount, then Cash to take and Round-off, a plus or a minus, never more than 50 paise. For the demo's one night of ₹3,699 with its GST, for example, the bill is ₹3,883.95: Cash to take is ₹3,884.00 and Round-off is +₹0.05. The message afterwards reads “₹3,884.00 cash taken”.

  • The bill is credited with the exact amount, so it settles to ₹0 and Check out opens. The GST invoice keeps its exact figures.
  • The drawer expects what was really put in it: the rupees taken (A4.10).
  • UPI, cards and every other way pay the exact amount, with no round-off.
  • The restaurant's own Round off is a different thing (A8).

The payment shows under Payments received, for example “Received - UPI”, and the bill's closing row reads Settled. Check out turns orange as soon as the bill reads zero.

Watch out

  • A payment is reversed only by the owner, an Admin, the GM or the accountant (A4.4). Reverse a payment taken by mistake before the guest leaves.
  • More than the bill is held as the guest's credit, once the desk ticks Hold it as the guest's credit (A4.7). The bill is then overpaid, and Check out waits for the refund (A5.7).
  • Cash above ₹1,00,000 at once asks for the guest's PAN, or Form 97 (A4.7).

Why it works this way

Nobody hands over 37 paise, so the drawer was a few paise over at every count. Only cash is rounded, the bill is credited exactly and the invoice never changes: D27-317. The rule is the room bill's: the restaurant keeps its own Round off. More than the bill is warned of, then held as the guest's credit: D27-4, D27-11.

A5.3Printing the bill for the guest

The guest asks to see the bill before paying. On the Bill tab click Proforma bill. The window shows the print preview. Click Print: the bill opens on a page of its own, and you print it from there (A4.9).

  • It says “Proforma Bill”, with the booking's reference and the stay's dates and room under it, and the line “A proforma bill: what the stay comes to so far. It is not a tax invoice; the tax invoice is issued at check-out.”
  • It is laid out as the tax invoice: the hotel's address, GSTIN and PAN, the stay in two columns, every line with its HSN/SAC, its taxable value and each tax (drinks with their VAT, never CGST and SGST), the payments and the tax by rate.
  • At the foot: the totals and the Total, then Paid, any night To be posted tonight, and Balance due (or Overpaid).
  • The total is the exact figure, with no round-off.

Watch out

  • It is not a tax invoice. It carries the booking's reference and no invoice number; the numbered invoice is issued after check-out (A5.9).
  • Printing it closes nothing. If the guest is charged more, a new copy shows it.
  • A test hotel's bill is stamped “TEST · NOT VALID” and carries no GSTIN.

Why it works this way

The desk's print never says "Tax Invoice", so nobody takes it for the numbered tax invoice: D22-7; the button says what it opens: D24-25. Its total is the exact figure: D27-126. The interim bill became the proforma bill, laid out as the tax invoice: D27-344. The test hotel's mark: D27-296.

A5.4The Check out window

Check out asks first. Click Check out on the bill and a small window opens: Check A5 Test Rane out? (the guest's name), the room under it, and the line “The bill closes and the room goes to housekeeping as dirty.” Not yet closes the window and changes nothing. Check out finishes it.

  • The bill closes. Its lines stay as they are.
  • The room is released and goes to Needs cleaning on housekeeping's board (A6.2).
  • A loyalty member's points for the stay are added (A14.4).
  • The guest's tax invoice is issued and printed by itself, or offered, or left to Invoices, as the hotel has chosen (A5.9).

Watch out

  • If the server refuses, a message, “Could not check out”, says why, and the guest stays in house.
  • The server asks the same questions as the screen and decides: “₹… is still outstanding. Settle the folio, or transfer it to the city ledger, before checking out.” and “The guest has overpaid by ₹…. Refund it before checking out.”

Why it works this way

A check-out closes the bill and sends the room to housekeeping, and it used to go on one click: D27-117. A room is vacated and made dirty by the same step that releases it, so it reaches housekeeping's board the moment the guest walks out.

A5.5After the check-out time: Leaving after check-out time

A guest still in the room after the hotel's check-out time has kept it out of tonight's sale, and housekeeping cannot turn it round for an arrival already on the chart. So a late departure is written down. The hotel's check-out time is set on Settings, Check-out by (A17.11), for example 11:00.

The window Leaving after check-out time comes up when you confirm Check out, and only when all three are true:

  • the hotel's business date is on or after the departure date (A1.1);
  • the hour, on the hotel's own clock, is past its check-out time;
  • the stay is not a day use, which has its own hours.

It is asked once for a stay: a late departure already recorded, with its reason and its charge or its waiver, is not asked again or charged again.

To record a late departure

  1. Click Check out on the bill and confirm. The window Leaving after check-out time opens with the guest and the room. Its yellow note starts “Check-out here is 11:00.”
  2. Type Why. It is required: a flight time, a manager's say-so, a room not ready on arrival (“Late flight, agreed at reception”).
  3. Read the line under it. Where the hotel does not charge: “This property does not charge for a late departure, so nothing will be added. It is still recorded.” Where it does: “₹1,000 will be added to the folio. A manager can waive it - that is a decision about money and it is theirs to make.” The owner, the GM and a group administrator have a tick instead, Waive the ₹1,000 charge: “Your decision, recorded against your name. The late departure is still written down - waiving the money does not unwrite the fact.”
  4. Click Check out. If a charge was added, it goes on the bill under Room, with its GST, before the balance is looked at.

If a charge was added, the bill is no longer zero, so the check-out cannot finish. The window closes with “Recorded - now settle the bill” and the amount. Take the payment (A5.2), then click Check out again: it does not ask again and charges nothing more. If nothing is owed after the late departure (no charge, or it was waived), the guest is checked out at once, and the message says so: “The late departure is recorded. The property does not charge for one.”, “₹… added to the folio.” or “The late departure is recorded and the charge waived - both are on the stay.”

Watch out

  • Anyone at the desk records a late departure; only a manager waives the charge. The server asks again, and refuses a waiver from anybody else.
  • A guest who leaves before the departure date is not asked this at any hour and is never charged a late fee (A5.6). The date that counts is the business date, not the clock's.
  • A day use is never asked and never charged a late fee.
  • The check-out time and the late fee are the hotel's own settings (A17.9, A17.11). Where no fee is set, the window says so.

Why it works this way

The server used to refuse a late check-out without a reason, and the screen had no way to give one: press, read, press again. Now the window is the way through. Recording is an observation, waiving is a decision about money, so the waiver is a manager's. The question is asked only on or after the departure date, and once, so a guest who paid after it is not asked or charged again: D27-314. A day use is never late: D27-319. The late fee sits under Room on the bill: D27-223.

A5.6Leaving early

A guest who leaves before the booked departure date, by the hotel's business date, is leaving early, at any hour. They are never asked Leaving after check-out time and never charged a late fee. They are asked one other thing: why.

To check out a guest who is leaving early

  1. Find them on In house now (A1.5): a guest who leaves before the departure date is not on Due out. Click the guest and click Settle and check out.
  2. On the bill, Charges to come are the nights the night audit has not posted yet (A4.2). They are only shown, and Due counts them. But Check out needs only what is posted: take the payment for that (A5.2).
  3. When what is posted is paid, Check out opens, even with nights still to come.
  4. Click Check out. The window shows the leaving-early step above its usual line: “Booked to leave 13 Oct 2026. Today is 11 Oct 2026.” and “Nights not stayed: 1 - it is not charged and the room goes back on sale.” (For more than one night: “they are not charged”.) For a stay from a booking site it adds “Tell the booking site the guest left early.”
  5. Type Why are they leaving early? It is required, and kept on the booking: “Plans changed”. Check out in the window stays grey until it is typed.
  6. Click Check out.

What it changes

  • The stay now ends on the later of today and the day after the last night already posted, so the nights not stayed are not charged and go back on sale. The room's hold is shortened with it.
  • Nights already posted are never taken off. The night audit posts no more nights for the guest.
  • The reason is kept in the booking's notes: “Left early on 2026-10-11, booked to 2026-10-13: Plans changed”.
  • A guest who leaves on the day they arrive keeps their first night charged: it was posted at check-in (A3.1).
  • There is no fee for leaving early.

The step appears only when at least one night is freed. A day use never has it, and neither has a stay whose remaining nights are already charged.

Watch out

  • If the guest paid ahead for more than is posted, the bill reads overpaid before check-out, and Check out stays grey: “This bill is overpaid. Refund the difference first.” Give the money back (A5.7), then check out.
  • The dates are shortened for every stay. Money is given back only on a guest's own bill: a company's credit and a booking-site stay get a notice instead (A5.7).
  • For a booking-site stay the system does not tell the site. The desk does.
  • If you click Check out in the window before the step has appeared, the server refuses with “Booked to leave on …. 1 night is not stayed: say why the guest is leaving early.” Click Check out on the bill again and type the reason.
  • The business date, not the computer's clock, decides what "early" is (A1.1).

Why it works this way

Before this, an early leaver's dates were not shortened, so the nights not stayed stayed booked, and unused prepaid nights blocked the check-out with no way to refund them: D27-314. The step follows the night audit's own rule for what is charged, so a night posted on a group's master bill counts; nights go back on sale; there is no fee for leaving early; and the refund is a step of its own: D27-315. Leaving early is never a late departure: D27-314.

A5.7A guest who paid too much: Refund

A bill can owe the guest money: paid ahead for nights not stayed, or more than the bill held as the guest's credit (A4.7). It shows as Overpaid, and Check out stays grey: “This bill is overpaid. Refund the difference first.” The server says the same: “The guest has overpaid by ₹…. Refund it before checking out.” On Folios such guests come first (A4.1).

Under the bill's buttons a yellow step appears: “₹… is owed back to the guest.” Then one of three things:

  • The owner, an Admin, the GM and the accountant see a Refund button.
  • Anyone else reads: “Refunds are given by the owner, an administrator, the general manager or the accountant. Ask one of them.”
  • A notice, where the money is not refunded here. A company's credit: “This credit is the company's. It is settled with the company on the City ledger, not refunded to the guest here.” A booking-site stay with nothing paid at the hotel to give back (the booking site was paid): “A booking-site stay: the booking site refunds the guest. Tell the booking site; nothing is refunded here.”

A booking-site guest who paid the hotel, for example the whole stay by UPI at the desk and then left early, is refunded here like any guest, with the same people, the same ways and the same ₹20,000 cash rule. Only what was paid at the hotel goes back, and only by the ways it was paid there: Bill to company is never one. What the booking site was paid stays the booking site's to refund.

To give a refund

  1. Click Refund. The window Refund says “₹… is owed back on this bill”.
  2. Choose Back by: the way the guest paid, each with the most it may give back, for example “UPI - up to ₹…”. “The way the guest paid. Never cash for a card or UPI payment.” The Amount is filled in with the most it may be.
  3. For any way but cash, type the Reference: the UPI reference, the card approval code, the cheque number, the transfer number (UTR) or the wallet reference.
  4. Type Why. It is required, and stays on the refund.
  5. Click Give refund. The message is “₹… refunded” with the way. On the bill the line reads “Refunded - UPI (the reference)” under Payments and refunds, with a Refunded total, and the bill is back to ₹0. Check out opens.
  6. Click Print the refund receipt, under the step, for the guest to sign.

The receipt is a page of its own, with a Print button. It shows the hotel, the receipt's number and date, the guest, the booking and room, Amount refunded, Back by, Reference, Why and Given by, and two signature lines, the guest's and the hotel's.
