A refund that is reversed afterwards prints “This refund was taken back.”

Watch out

  • Cash only below ₹20,000 on a bill; above it, by bank transfer. The window says it: “Cash is given back only below ₹20,000 on a bill; above it, by bank transfer. This limit stands until the hotel's CA confirms it.” Two refunds of ₹15,000 count as ₹30,000. If bank transfer is not one of the hotel's ways of paying, the refusal says to add it in Settings first.
  • A cash refund comes out of the drawer of the person who gives it (A4.10).
  • The server refuses a way the bill was not paid by: “This bill was not paid by UPI. A refund goes back the way it was paid: …; never cash for a card or UPI payment.” And more than the limit: “At most ₹… goes back by UPI on this bill.” And no reason: “Say why it is being refunded. The reason stays on the refund.”
  • It is not the GST refund voucher: “This prints a plain refund receipt. The GST refund voucher (Rule 51) waits for the hotel's CA.”
  • For a company's credit, and a booking-site stay with nothing paid at the hotel, the notice is all the screen offers, and Check out stays grey while the bill as a whole is overpaid. Until a company's credit can go to its City ledger at check-out, a manager reverses the payment the same day (A4.4).

Why it works this way

A refund is its own line on the bill, back the way the guest paid, with a reference, the reason and the name of who gave it, so nothing is edited and money is never given back untraceably. It is for the four who may reverse a payment: D27-125, D27-315. Cash stays below ₹20,000 until the hotel's CA confirms the limit; the plain receipt stands in for the GST refund voucher until the CA says what it must hold: D27-315. A booking-site stay gives back what was paid at the hotel, like a guest's own bill; a company's credit to its City ledger comes after launch: D27-328.

A5.8A guest from abroad: the next destination

A foreign guest is reported when they leave too: Form III's departure goes to the portal within 24 hours of the guest leaving, and it carries where they are going next (A3.4). So on a foreign guest's bill, above Check out, is a box: Next destination, starred, with “Form III reports where a foreign guest goes next.” Check out stays grey until it is filled in. Type where they go, then check out as usual.

  • If it is missed, the server refuses: “Form III asks where a foreign guest is going next. Enter the next destination to check them out.”
  • A foreign adult recorded on the stay of an Indian guest (A3.3) is asked for too. The refusal comes when you press Check out, and the box opens: type where they go and check out again.
  • What you type goes on the guest's row and on every foreign adult's who has no next destination of their own.
  • Afterwards, on the Form III screen (A3.5), the Departure cell of each row takes the number the portal gives back for that person's departure. Complete details can add or change the next destination after check-out.

Why it works this way

Rule 17 asks the foreigner for the address they are going to at departure, so it is asked while they are still at the desk, and the check-out refuses without it: D27-25.

A5.9After check-out: the tax invoice

The proforma bill is not the tax invoice. Once the guest has left and the bill is settled, the numbered GST invoice is issued. What Check out does with it is the hotel's choice, on Settings › Front desk rules (A17.11):

  • Issue it and print it, by itself (the hotel starts on this). Check out issues the invoice and opens the print window with it, in two copies: “ORIGINAL FOR RECIPIENT” for the guest and “DUPLICATE FOR SUPPLIER” for the hotel's file. Choose the desk's printer and print. A hotel may choose one copy.
  • Offer an Issue tax invoice button: the bill shows Issue tax invoice where Check out was, and nothing is issued until it is clicked.
  • Nothing at check-out: the bill says “Not issued yet: this hotel issues the tax invoice on Invoices.”

At the desk, right after check-out (the hotel starts on this)

  1. Check the guest out (A5.1). The panel stays open on the bill and says “Issuing and printing the tax invoice…” for a moment.
  2. The print window opens with the invoice: the original and the duplicate, one after the other. Choose the desk's printer and click Print. It prints on the printer the computer already uses, on A4; nothing is set up for it in the PMS.
  3. Under Tax invoice the bill now shows Print or send with the invoice's number, for example Print or send 5EL/2026-27/00004, and the orange Print again. If the printer missed it, click Print again. To give it as a file, click Print or send and then Send invoice (A10.7), or choose Save as PDF in the print window.

A bill that still owes, or is overpaid, is not issued: the bill says why under Issue tax invoice; settle it and issue it there or on Invoices. A stay with two bills issues and prints each one, with who it is billed to (A4.8). Issuing is for reception, the hotel manager, the accountant, the GM, an Admin and the owner; anyone else sees “Not issued yet.” and who can. Cancelling an invoice with a credit note is only for the accountant, the GM, an Admin and the owner (A4.11).

Where the hotel offers the button

  1. After check-out, where Check out was, the bill says Tax invoice with the orange Issue tax invoice.
  2. Click it. The window Issue this tax invoice? says who it is billed to and the number it takes (Figure A5-13). Click Issue the invoice.
  3. The button becomes Print or send with the invoice's number. Click it: the tax invoice opens in a new tab, and its Print prints both copies.

Closing the panel without issuing leaves the bill on Invoices, ready to bill.

Later, on Invoices

A bill not invoiced at the desk waits on Invoices (Finance; or Find a screen). A4.11 has all of it, with the credit note. In short:

  1. Open Invoices. It lists the departed stays ready to bill, with how many.
  2. Click Issue on the stay. It is grey while the bill still owes (“The folio still carries a balance. Settle it, or transfer it to the city ledger, before invoicing.”) or is overpaid (“The folio is overpaid. Refund the difference before invoicing.”).
  3. The window Issue this tax invoice? says who it is billed to and the next number in the GST series. Click Issue the invoice. Keep it closes the window and changes nothing.

Watch out

  • An issued invoice is never edited: “An issued invoice is never edited: a wrong one needs a credit note.” Numbers come in sequence, so the series cannot gain a hole (A4.11).
  • The tax invoice goes by email by itself only when it is made out to the guest. One made out to a company, an agent or a booking site goes by the desk's Send invoice (A10.7).

Why it works this way

Asking "are you sure" before a legal number is taken, when it is asked for by hand: D27-117. A company's, an agent's or a booking site's invoice is not sent by itself: D27-284, D27-313. The tax invoice on the bill after check-out, with who may issue it unchanged: D27-341. Issued and printed at check-out by default, two copies, each hotel's choice: D27-344. GST's invoice for a service is in two copies, the original for the recipient and the duplicate for the supplier (CGST Rules, rule 48).

A5.10Before the night audit

A guest who has left must still be checked out, or the day cannot close. At the end of the day, Due out should be empty, or hold only guests who are really still here. When everyone has gone it says “Nobody departing today. Every room stays another night.” (A1.6).

  • In Night audit, the check Departures not yet checked out counts the guests due out today who are still checked in, and it stops the audit (A7.2).
  • The Run card then says “4 rooms are still showing due out. Check them out, or extend the stay - the audit will not decide which.” and Run night audit stays grey (A7.3).
  • For each guest: if they left, settle the bill and check them out. If they are staying on, use Change dates or guests (A2.8).

Why it works this way

A guest still due out at night either left and nobody checked them out, or is staying another night. The two lead to opposite charges, and only a person at the desk knows which, so the audit refuses and names the rooms: D27-305.

A5.11Check-out in short

WhenDoSection
A guest is leavingDue out, the guest, the Bill tab. In house, Settle and check out, for any other guest.A5.1
Money is owedSettle, the method, Take payment. Cash is taken to the rupee, with a round-off.A5.2
The guest asks for the billProforma bill, then Print.A5.3
The bill owes nothingCheck out, then Check out again in the window.A5.4
On the day, after the check-out timeSay why. A manager may waive a late charge. Settle it if there is one, then check out again.A5.5
Before the departure dateSettle what is posted. Say why they are leaving early. The nights not stayed are not charged and go back on sale.A5.6
The bill is overpaidRefund (owner, Admin, GM, accountant): the way paid, reference, why, Give refund. Print the receipt.A5.7
A guest from abroadType the Next destination first.A5.8
Checked outThe tax invoice prints by itself, two copies; Print again if the printer missed it. Where the hotel chose otherwise: Issue tax invoice, or Invoices, Issue.A5.9
End of the dayNobody left showing due out, or the night audit will not run.A5.10
Chapter A6

Housekeeping

For housekeepers, their supervisors and the desk. How to read the Housekeeping board, give rooms out, mark a room clean and then inspected (with or without a signal), report a repair, take a room out of service and put it back, follow work orders and what they cost, and look after guests' requests, wake-up calls and lost property.

A6.1The housekeeping screens

A housekeeper signs in and lands on the Housekeeping board. Their menu is short: the screens they work on. Every other screen they may use is still one search away (Find a screen, A0.6).

ScreenWho uses itWhat it is for
HousekeepingHousekeeping; reception and the managers see it tooThe board: every room, what it needs, and who is cleaning it. Clean, Inspected, Repair; Put back for a room out of service.
Work ordersHousekeeping, reception, the managersWhat needs fixing, who is fixing it, what it cost.
Guest requestsThe desk sees every request; housekeeping, the Inventory Manager, the kitchen manager, the chef and the waiter see their own team'sWhat guests in house have asked for: towels, a broken tap, a pot of tea.
Wake-up callsThe desk: the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager, receptionCalls to make, on the hotel's clock.
Lost propertyThe desk and housekeeping log items; only the desk returns or disposes of themWhat was found, kept until it goes back to its owner or is disposed of.

The housekeeper's menu also has Rooms, the house today (A1.7), and Store, Equipment and Purchasing (A9). Laundry is in A13.

The Start here card lists the housekeeper's three jobs: See what needs cleaning, Mark a room clean, Report something broken. Tap Got it to put it away; the account menu's Show Start here again brings it back (A0.2).

A6.2The Housekeeping board

The board says what it is for under its title: “Tap a room to move it on. Clean, then inspected.”

  • Empty rooms: the big figure is the rooms with no guest that are clean or inspected, of all rooms with no guest (“4/6 clean”). The two bars split it: Clean and Inspected. A room out of service is not counted.
  • The six counts: Needs cleaning, Clean, Inspected, In house, Due out, Out of service. A count with an arrow jumps to its group below. Due out has no group of its own, and a zero has nothing to jump to, so they stay flat.
  • Online means the board is connected. It refreshes by itself: it is told the moment a room changes anywhere, and reads again every 30 seconds (60 while it is live). Nobody needs to reload it.

The rooms are in groups, in this order:

GroupMeans
Needs cleaningNo guest, and not clean yet. Clean is ready.
CleanCleaned, not yet checked. Inspected is ready.
InspectedCleaned and checked: ready for the next guest.
In houseEvery room with a guest in it. The card shows the guest's name and a bed; a guest leaving today makes the card yellow, with “Due out”.
Out of serviceNot for sale (A6.7). The card has one button, Put back.

Watch out

  • No button sends a room for cleaning. A check-out does it by itself: the room the guest leaves goes to Needs cleaning. A room nobody slept in (a booking cancelled or a no-show) stays as housekeeping left it.
  • A room out of service cannot be marked clean: put it back first (A6.7).

Why it works this way

The words under the buttons, and a grey one saying why: D17-8. Each count jumps to its group, with an arrow; Due out and a zero stay flat: D27-95. The board refreshes itself: D17-39. The board uses the same words for a room as Rooms does, so the desk and housekeeping name a room the same way.

A6.3Giving rooms to a housekeeper

A supervisor gives each room to somebody before the shift. Everyone working at the hotel is in the list, housekeepers first.

  1. On the room's card, open the list that says Unassigned.
  2. Choose the person. It is saved at once; there is no Save button.
  3. The names along the top count the rooms on each person's sheet: Test Housekeeper 2. Unassigned, at the end, shows the rooms nobody has yet.

On a phone, a housekeeper taps their own name and sees only their rooms. All rooms shows every room again.

  • Rooms are given for the business day. When the night audit moves the date on (A7), the new day starts with every room unassigned.
  • Giving rooms out works with no signal too: it waits on the device and is sent when the line is back (A6.5).

Why it works this way

Everyone sees their own hotel's staff, names and roles only, so a hotel manager can give rooms out: D27-96. The list on each card stays as it is: D17-40.

A6.4Clean, then inspected

A room is cleaned, then inspected, in that order.

  1. When the room is clean, tap Clean on its card. The message “Room 210 is clean.” appears at once, and the room moves to the Clean group.
  2. When the room has been checked, tap Inspected. The message says “Room 210 is inspected.”, and the room moves to Inspected.

A grey button says why

A button that cannot be used yet is grey. Tap it anyway, and the card says why in one line, for example “Room 210 needs cleaning first.” or “Room 202 is already inspected.”. The line goes when the room moves on.

Why it works this way

The message at once, and the card moving straight away: D27-94. A grey button that says why when tapped: D17-8. The server refuses the same order: “A dirty room is cleaned before it is inspected.”

A6.5With no signal

The board is made for a phone on a stairwell. With no signal, carry on: each tap is kept on the phone and sent by itself when the connection is back.

  1. The pill at the top says Offline.
  2. Tap Clean as usual. The message says “Saved on this phone - Housekeeping is held and will be sent when the connection is back.”
  3. Under the title: “1 change waiting to sync”. The bar at the top of the page says the same (A0.8).
  4. The room's card turns yellow and says “Queued: mark clean”. The next button, Inspected, can be tapped too; it waits the same way.
  5. When the signal is back, the held taps are sent by themselves, and the lines go away.

Watch out

  • What waits on the phone: Clean and Inspected, giving rooms out, and a repair (A6.6). Taking a room out of service, putting it back, and a repair's cost need the connection.
  • The held taps stay on the phone even if it is locked or the page is reloaded. A private window cannot keep them: the bar says so (A0.8).
  • A grey button on a held room says so: “Room 209 is already marked clean on this phone, waiting to sync.”

A6.6Something broken: Report a repair

A dripping tap, a fused bulb, a broken chair. Most repairs do not stop a room being sold, so reporting one does not take the room out unless you say so.

  1. On the room's card, tap Repair. Report a repair · Room 209 opens.
  2. Type What needs fixing, in a few words.
  3. If it is a tagged piece of equipment, choose it under Equipment; the things in this room are listed first. Otherwise leave Not a piece of equipment.
  4. Choose the Kind (maintenance, housekeeping, electrical, plumbing, furniture, it, other) and the Priority (Urgent, High, Normal, Low). Add Anything else if it helps.
  5. Tap Raise it. The message says “Repair raised”, and it is on Work orders (A6.8).

When the room must come out too

  1. Tick Take room 209 out of service too.
  2. Choose Why is it coming out?, the From date (today to start) and, if known, Until. Leave Until empty if nobody knows.
  3. Tap Raise it. The message says the repair is raised and the room is out: “Room 209 is out of service, no return date set.” On Work orders the repair says “Room is out”.

Watch out

  • A room with a guest in it cannot be taken out: the window says “Somebody is in room 209, so it cannot be taken out of service now.” Report the repair; take the room out after the guest leaves.
  • A piece of equipment chosen here shows as Under repair until its last open repair is closed. Only a tagged item can be chosen; one waiting in the approvals inbox is listed, but cannot be.
  • With no signal, the repair waits on the phone (“Saved on this phone”), but taking the room out does not: the message says to do it when you are back online.

Why it works this way

Repair reports a repair for the room, and taking the room out is a second choice inside it, because a dripping tap does not cost a night's sale: D17-8. Opening a repair on an item makes it Under repair, closing it makes it In use: D17-7.

A6.7A room out of service, and back

A room that cannot be sold is taken out for a period: a refurbishment, a broken shower, a room kept for house use. A room out of service is not offered for sale anywhere. It is not given to a guest either, even when the period starts later: Assign room, Check in and Move room refuse it for any night it covers, with “Room 209 is out of order from 19 Oct to 20 Oct, so it cannot take this stay. Choose another room, or end the block first.”, and the room lists leave it out for those dates (D27-339).

To take a room out with no repair

  1. On the room's card, tap Repair, then Out of service without a repair at the foot of the window.
  2. Choose Why is it coming out?:
    • Out of order - something is broken
    • Maintenance / out of service - held back deliberately
    • Refurbishment
    • NC - not for sale (house use: staff, storage, an office)
    • Owner occupied
  3. Set From, and Until if it is known. The grey pill says the period, or “No end date”.
  4. Write in Note what is actually wrong.
  5. Tap Take out of service. The message says “Room 209 is out”, with “No return date set.” or the date it is back on sale.

To put a room back

  1. Find the room under Out of service (or tap that count at the top) and tap Put back.
  2. Under ALREADY OUT, each period the room is out is listed with its dates. Tap Put back beside the one that is over.
  3. The message says “Room 308 is back”. The room returns under Needs cleaning, so somebody looks at it before a guest sleeps in it.

Watch out

  • A room with a guest in it cannot be taken out: “Somebody is in this room. Move them out before taking it off sale.”
  • Closing the repair that took a room out does not put the room back. Put it back on the room itself, so somebody decides.
  • Taking a room out and putting it back need the connection.
  • A hotel can choose that a room back from a block returns as it was before, not as Needs cleaning: Settings, Front desk rules, Housekeeping, A room back from a block is sent for cleaning (on to start).

Why it works this way

Out of service is a period with dates, not a switch: a room can be out from Thursday for the plumber, and the hotel can still say what was for sale last Tuesday. Until is empty unless somebody knows it, so the room never comes back on sale on a day nobody chose. The housekeeping switches in Front desk rules: D27-260.

A6.8Work orders

Work orders is the list of what needs fixing: “What needs fixing. Most of it does not take a room out of service.” Open lists what is still to fix, most urgent first and the oldest first within that; Closed keeps what was done.

  • A repair that is not about a room (a lift, the lobby) shows a dash where the room would be.
  • The days open stand out once a repair has been open a week.
  • “Room is out” marks the few repairs that took their room out of service.
  • Cost is shown only to those who may see money (below). No cost recorded is a dash, never ₹0.

To raise one from Work orders

Raise one opens the same form as the room's Repair button (A6.6), called Raise a work order, with a Room box: “Leave empty for anything that is not a room - a lift, the lobby.” Raise it stays grey until What needs fixing is typed.

To start, and to close

  1. When somebody begins the work, tap Start. The repair says “Being fixed”. Put back makes it wait again.
  2. When the work is finished, tap Close.
  3. Write What was done: “The line somebody reads the next time this breaks.”
  4. Tap Fixed; or Not needed if it needed no fixing after all. Both need What was done.
  5. It moves to Closed, marked “Fixed” or “Not needed”, with who closed it and when, and what was done.

What it cost

A repair's cost is recorded with its proof. Tap Costs on the repair, open or closed.

  1. Under Record a cost, type the Amount, in rupees. The box is empty: the grey 1800 is only an example.
  2. Under Proof, choose the photo or screenshot of the bill, the payment or the transaction. “A cost is not recorded without it.”
  3. Add a Note if it helps: who was paid, for what.
  4. Tap Record the cost.
  • A repair may have several costs, each with its own proof. One bill proves one cost.
  • Each cost has See the proof. A wrong one is cancelled with Cancel this cost and a reason: it stays on the record, out of the total. Nothing is deleted.
  • A bill that arrives after the repair is closed is recorded under Closed, on the same Costs button.

Watch out

  • Start and Close are for the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager, the Inventory Manager and housekeeping. Anybody else sees one sentence saying so.
  • Costs are recorded by the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager or the Inventory Manager, with no approval but never without proof. The accountant sees them too. Everybody else sees the repair without the money.
  • A cost needs the connection: a photo cannot wait on the phone.
  • A repair already closed cannot be closed again: “This repair is already closed.”

Why it works this way

Who updates a repair: D22-34. Who records a cost: D17-5; no approval, but never without proof: D17-6. Closing the last repair on a piece of equipment puts it back in use: D17-7. Closed repairs are kept, because “how many times have we fixed this room” needs them.

A6.9Guest requests

A guest in house wants two more towels, or says the tap is broken. A request goes to the team it is for:

TeamWho receives it
HousekeepingHousekeeping
Something brokenWhoever updates a repair: the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager, the Inventory Manager, housekeeping. It is also a repair on Work orders.
Food and drinkThe kitchen manager, the chef, the waiter

The desk (the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager, reception) sees every team's requests and may take, close or cancel any. Anybody who sees the screen may raise one.

To raise a request

  1. Tap New request.
  2. Choose the Room. Only guests in house now are listed.
  3. Choose the team: Housekeeping, Something broken or Food and drink.
  4. Type What is wanted, and When only if the guest said.
  5. Tap Raise it. The message says “Raised”, with the team and the words.

To do a request

  1. Open Guest requests. If you receive more than one team, they are listed beside All; tap one to see only its requests.
  2. Tap Take it. It says “Being done” and, for everyone to see, “Test Housekeeper has it”.
  3. When it is done, tap Done. A Housekeeping or Food and drink request closes with that one tap. Something broken asks What was done first, like a repair.
  4. Done, last 24 h lists what was finished, with how long each took and who did it.

You may also tap Done straight away, without Take it. Cancel it asks Why it is cancelled, then Cancel the request.

Watch out

  • Somebody else has it: Take it on a request already taken is refused, naming who: “… has already taken it.”
  • Guests ask from their own page too, while they are checked in. Their requests arrive here saying “from the guest's page”, and the guest sees them as Open, Being done, Done or Declined.
  • The guest's name is shown only to those who may read guests' details: a housekeeper sees the room, not the name.
  • Food and drink carries no price. Anything to be paid for is still rung on the Till and charged to the room (A8).
  • A request needs the connection: it is not held on the phone.
  • While nobody has taken a request, the bell says so: “1 guest request waiting”.

Why it works this way

A request is a work order that carries the stay; three kinds, one per team; the desk sees and handles any; Something broken is also on Work orders and asks what was done; no time targets, so nothing turns red: D27-181.

A6.10Wake-up calls

Wake-up calls is for the desk: “Calls to make, on the hotel's clock. Due from fifteen minutes before.”

  1. Tap Set a call.
  2. Choose the Room (guests in house now), the Day (today to start) and the Time.
  3. Add a Note only if there is something to say on the call.
  4. Tap Set the call. It is listed under To make.
  5. From fifteen minutes before, it says “Due”, and the bell reminds the desk. Make the call, then tap Done.
  • A call stays Due until it is marked done: there is no “missed”.
  • Cancel it asks Why it is cancelled, then Cancel the call. The reason is kept.
  • A guest can ask for a call from their own page. It shows “Asked” and “asked from the guest's page”, with Confirm; once confirmed it is a call like any other.
  • A time already past is refused: “That time has passed.”

Why it works this way

Set by the desk and asked for from the guest's page; the bell from fifteen minutes before until done, with no missed state; in reception's menu: D27-241.

A6.11Lost property

Lost property is “What was found, kept until it goes back to its owner or is disposed of.” The desk and housekeeping log what they find; only the desk marks an item returned or disposed of.

To log an item

  1. Tap Log an item.
  2. Type What it is and Where it was found.
  3. Type the Room if it was in one, and Where it is kept now.
  4. Tap Log it. It is listed under Kept, with how many days it has been kept.

When it goes back to its owner (the desk)

  1. Tap Returned on the item.
  2. Type Who it went to.
  3. Tap Mark returned. It moves to Returned or disposed, saying to whom, by whom, and when.

When nobody claims it (the desk)

  1. Tap Disposed on the item.
  2. Type Why it was disposed of.
  3. Tap Mark disposed. It moves to Returned or disposed, marked “Disposed of”, with the reason, who and when.

Watch out

  • Nothing is disposed of by itself. The days kept are shown so the desk can decide.
  • A room number must be one of this hotel's rooms, in small letters or capitals (111a is room 111A): “There is no room 999 here.”
  • There is no photo of the item for now: describe it well in What it is.

Why it works this way

The desk and housekeeping log; only the desk returns (to whom) or disposes (with a reason); days kept shown; no automatic disposal; no photo for now; in reception's and housekeeping's menus: D27-241.

A6.12Your day in short

WhenDoSection
The start of the shiftHousekeeping. A supervisor gives each room to somebody on its card.A6.3
Your roomsTap your own name at the top.A6.3
A room is cleanClean.A6.4
A room is checkedInspected.A6.4
No signalCarry on: the taps wait on the phone.A6.5
Something brokenRepair, on the room's card.A6.6
A room cannot be soldTake it out of service with a reason; Put back when it is ready.A6.7
A repair begins, and endsWork orders: Start, then Close with what was done. Managers record the cost with its proof.A6.8
A guest asks for somethingGuest requests: Take it, then Done.A6.9
A guest wants a wake-up callWake-up calls (the desk): Set a call; Done once it is made.A6.10
Something left behindLost property: Log an item. The desk returns it or disposes of it.A6.11
Chapter A7

Night audit

For the manager or the desk who closes the hotel's day. What the night audit does, the checks it shows first, what stops it and how to clear it, running it, the closed days and how one is corrected, and the reports it can send by email.

A7.1What the night audit does

The night audit closes the hotel's day. Until it runs, the business date stays where it is, whatever the clock says (A1.1). A person runs it, late at night, from the Night audit screen. It is never run by itself: a hotel that forgets simply stays on yesterday, and every screen says so.

When it runs, in one go, it:

  • charges one night's room, with its tax, to every guest in house (not a complimentary room, a day-use stay, or a night already charged at check-in);
  • marks every arrival who never came as a no-show, and gives the room back. A no-show is charged only the retention its booking's terms set; a booking with no terms is charged nothing;
  • moves the business date on to the next day.

It never checks anybody out, and it never decides for a person. If something only a person can answer is still open, it refuses, and says what (A7.3).

WhoWhat they can do
Owner, Admin, General ManagerRead the screen, run the audit, correct a closed day (A7.5), set the report emails (A7.6).
Hotel Manager, Accountant, ReceptionRead the screen and run the audit.
Revenue Manager, ViewerRead the screen only. The Run card is shown to them without the Run night audit button.

Night audit is the first screen under Reports in the menu. If your menu does not show it, type “night audit” in Find a screen (A0.6). Its address is /h/5EL/night-audit.

A7.2The checks

The line under the heading names the day the audit is closing and the day it will open: “The night audit is closing Friday, 9 October 2026 and opening Saturday, 10 October 2026.” Below it, six checks, each with its count.

CheckWhat it countsOpen leads to
Arrivals still outstandingBookings due today, not checked in. When the day closes, each becomes a no-show. Check in the guests who came; the rest are the audit's job. The check says “An arrival left unchecked at roll-over becomes a no-show. A retention posts against it only if the booking has cancellation terms.”Arrivals (A1.3)
Departures not yet checked outGuests due out today, still checked in. This one stops the audit (A7.3).Due out (A1.6)
In-house folios carrying a balanceGuests in house whose bills are not at zero. “These roll forward. Nothing is wrong with that”.Folios
Room charges to postThe rooms the audit will charge tonight. A stay already charged for tonight (the first night is charged at check-in), a day-use stay and a complimentary room are not counted.-
Rooms still marked dirtyRooms waiting for cleaning. “Not a blocker.” The morning shift inherits them.Housekeeping (A6)
Postings reversed todayCharges and payments reversed today. Each one is somebody correcting something: worth reading before the day closes.Audit log

The badge beside the heading counts the checks with a yellow sign, for example “3 to look at”, or says “Nothing outstanding”. Open shows only on a check that has something in it.

Watch out

  • Yellow is not the same as stopped. Of the six checks, only Departures not yet checked out stops the audit. The other things that stop it are not checks at all: they are written on the Run card (A7.3).
  • An arrival is counted here only on the day it was due. The audit marks as no-shows every booking still waiting whose arrival day is today or earlier.

A7.3What stops the audit, and how to clear it

Below the checks, the Run card: Run the audit and roll to the next day. While anything stops the audit, the reason is written on the card and Run night audit stays grey. The Revenue Manager and the Viewer see the card and its reasons and no button: they may not run the audit (A7.1).

Four things stop it. Each has its own sentence on the card.

The card saysWhat to do
“The night audit for 16 Oct opens at 16:00, by the hotel's clock.”Wait until that time. Before it, nobody can close today's day. A day already behind (the business date is earlier than today) is never locked. The time is set in Settings → Times and rules, Night audit opens at, by the owner or an administrator (A17).
“4 rooms are still showing due out. Check them out, or extend the stay - the audit will not decide which.”Open the check Departures not yet checked out. For each guest: if they left, settle the bill and check them out (A1.6, A5); if they are staying on, open the guest and use Change dates or guests.
“A front-desk drawer is still open. Count the cash and close the shift …”On Cashiering, count the desk's cash and tap Close the shift.
“The till has not been closed for today. Run the day end on it first …”Close the restaurant's day: Close restaurant day (A8.9). Only a restaurant with orders today needs it.
“This property has no GST rule for rooms …”The card goes on: “Set it in the GST card, under Settings → Taxes and billing or Finance → Invoices. A missing rate is not zero - the audit will not invent one.” Ask whoever sets the hotel's taxes.

To clear the guests still due out

  1. On Night audit, tap Open on Departures not yet checked out. Due out opens (Figure A7-03).
  2. The red box says how many still owe, and how much in all. Tap a guest: the panel opens on the Bill tab.
  3. If the guest has left: take the payment, then check them out. Check-out unlocks when the bill reaches zero.
  4. If the guest is staying another night: Change dates or guests, and move the departure.
  5. Go back to Night audit. When nobody is left due out, the sentence goes from the card.

Why it works this way

Today's day closes only from the hotel's opening time, 16:00 to begin, so nobody closes it in the morning by mistake; catching up a day behind is never held back: D27-338. A guest still due out at night either left and nobody checked them out, or is staying another night. The two lead to opposite charges, and only a person at the desk knows which, so the audit refuses and names the rooms. The two drawers are counted first because the audit states the day's takings, and money not yet counted is not final. The button is shown grey, with its reason, to everybody who may run the audit, and not shown at all to the two roles who may never run it. The screen and the server ask the same question, so they cannot disagree: D27-305.

A7.4Running the audit

  1. Read the checks (A7.2) and clear what stops it (A7.3).
  2. When the card shows no reason, tap Run night audit.
  3. It asks first: “Close Friday, 9 October 2026?”, and shows three things to read: Closing (the day being closed), Today at the hotel (the date by the hotel's own clock) and Last audit (when the last one finished). Then “The property moves to Saturday, 10 October 2026. Tonight's room charges are posted to every guest in house and arrivals who did not come become no-shows. A closed day cannot be edited, only corrected afterwards.”
  4. Read them, and tick I have checked the day being closed, today's date and the last audit. Until it is ticked, the button stays grey.
  5. Tap Close 9 Oct 2026 (the day being closed), or Cancel. While it works, the button reads Closing the day….
  6. A green card says “Friday, 9 October 2026 is closed. The property is now operating in Saturday, 10 October 2026.”, with what it did: rooms posted and their revenue, rooms given free (“complimentary, not charged”), and no-shows.

When the restaurant sold something that day, the card also shows its day: orders, covers, the total with its tax, and each way it was paid. Under it, the two drawers side by side, never added together: Front desk (its shifts) and Till (its outlets), each with what it opened on, what was counted, and how many differences were explained. These are read from what the till and the desk already wrote; the audit adds none of it to a bill.

If the hotel has switched it on (Settings, Front desk rules, The night audit sends every room with a guest staying on for its daily clean), the audit also marks those rooms dirty for the new day. It starts off.

A day that has not begun, and 16 hours between audits

  • A day closes only once it has begun. If the hotel's business date is ahead of the hotel's own calendar, the card says, for example, “3 November has not begun at the hotel: it is 2 November there. A day closes only once it has begun.” and nobody can run it, the owner included.
  • Today's date, under 16 hours after the last audit: the window adds “The last audit finished at 23:36 on 1 Nov, 0.1 hours ago - less than 16. Say why this day closes so soon. The reason is kept with the audit.” and a box, Why now. The owner and an Admin type the reason and go on. The GM sees it as a Warning and must type a reason too. Everybody else is stopped: the card says “The last night audit finished at …, … hours ago. Another day closes only 16 hours after the last one - or sooner by the GM, the owner or an administrator, with a reason.”
  • Catching up on days already over is never held by the 16 hours: a hotel days behind closes them one after another.

Watch out

  • A closed day cannot be edited. It can be corrected, line by line, or - by the owner or an Admin, for an audit run by mistake - cancelled (A7.5).
  • Pressed twice, on two desks, or on a screen left open after the day was closed elsewhere? The day closes once. The second press changes nothing and says, for example, “9 Oct was already closed. Reload to see today.” and “Nothing was run again.”, with the record that was made: who ran it, when, rooms posted, room revenue, no-shows.
  • No connection, no audit. It closes the day for the whole property and needs the server. Wait for the line.
  • After the audit, other desks see the new business date the next time they open a screen (A1.1).

Why it works this way

The audit asks first, because a closed day cannot be edited: D27-117. The three facts, the tick box, a day that has not begun and the 16 hours came after an audit closed the next day one minute after the first: D27-389. A second press changes nothing and shows the record that was made: D17-12. The first night is charged at check-in, so the audit skips a night already charged: D27-204. The daily clean at the audit, off unless the hotel says so: D27-260. The audit is run by a person and never scheduled: the owner's rule.

A7.5Closed days, and correcting one

Under the Run card, Closed days lists every night audit run at this property, newest first: Day, Ran by, Closed, Rooms posted, Room revenue (the room charges the audit posted, before tax), No-shows and Why early. A figure the record does not hold is a dash. A day closed under 16 hours after the last is marked Under 16 hours, and Why early shows the reason and who gave it. Until the first audit, it says “No day closed yet” (Figure A7-02, arrow 4). Below it, Cancelled audits lists every cancel, with its reason (see below).

To correct a closed day (owner, Admin, GM)

  1. Under Closed days, tap Correct on the day. Days from the 1st of last month on can be corrected; older ones stay as they are, and their Correct is grey.
  2. Under Charge to correct, choose the charge that was wrong: a room charge, a no-show charge, a restaurant bill charged to a room, or another charge of that day.
  3. Type The right figure, before tax, or tick Take the charge off entirely.
  4. Type Why it was wrong. It is kept with your name and the time.
  5. Tap Save correction. “Correction saved”.
  • Nothing is rewritten: the wrong charge stays on the bill, and the reversal and the right charge sit beside it, on the same day. That day's reports show the corrected figure.
  • A corrected day is marked Corrected, and its Room revenue shows old → new. Anybody else who reads Closed days sees Corrections on that day: what was changed, why, by whom.
  • A payment, a refund or a discount is never corrected here. A bill with a tax invoice says “Issue a credit note instead.”; drinks with a VAT bill say “Cancel the VAT bill instead.”
  • A room charge's tax is worked out again, as the audit does; any other charge keeps the rate it was charged at.

To cancel an audit run by mistake (owner, Admin)

In the Admin section: Properties, the hotel, then the card Cancel a night audit. The hotel goes back to the day you choose: every audit from it on is undone, and what was billed since moves back to that day.

  1. How far back: To any earlier day (to start) or One audit at a time. This is the group's setting, for every hotel.
  2. Back to: the closed day the hotel should be on again. With One audit at a time, only the latest.
  3. Read what it does: the audits undone, with who closed them and when; how many room charges are reversed, and their total; the no-shows booked again; and what moves back, day by day.
  4. Type Why. It is kept with the cancel, as a mistake.
  5. Tick I have read what this undoes and moves., then tap Cancel 1 audit (or the number shown).
  6. The hotel is on that day again: “5EL is on Monday, 2 November 2026 again”. Run the night audit for it when the day is done.
  • Nothing is deleted. The audit stays on record as cancelled; its room charges stay on the bills, each with a reversal beside it on its own day. Run again, the day's audit charges the night again.
  • A no-show is booked again, and its room held again if nobody has taken it since. If somebody has, the message names the booking: give it another room.
  • Moved back to the chosen day: restaurant bills, charges and payments on room bills, the till's and the desk's drawers and their cash, stock movements and counts, deposits, laundry, and the bar's requests.
  • Tally. The card ends with the days the cancel reopens, for example “Tally: if 1 Nov 2026 to 2 Nov 2026 were already imported into Tally, delete those days there and export them again once each is closed again.” The Accountant sees the same on Accounting export (A11.8). The PMS does not record what was exported, so it says “if”.
  • Daily report emails. When a cancelled day is closed again, its reports go again to the same addresses, marked Corrected in the subject and at the top (A7.6).
  • It is refused, and nothing changes, when: a GST tax invoice or a VAT bill stands on those days (“… Issue a credit note first - and your CA should confirm it.”); a room was charged on a later day by a check-in or a correction; a later day was corrected; or the till was ended twice in those days.

Why it works this way

An audit run by mistake is cancelled by the owner or an Admin, from the Admin section, recorded as a mistake; back to any day by default, or one at a time by the group's setting; what was billed since moves back with it: D27-390. The history of closed days: D17-13. A closed day is corrected with a reason, the old and new figures both kept: D22-18. The owner, an Admin and the GM correct: D24-3; this month and the month before: D24-5. Every charge may be corrected, never money: D25-5.

A7.6The reports it sends by email

Right after the night audit closes the day, reports can go by email. Each address gets one email with every report switched on for it: the subject is the hotel's name, "daily reports" and the date ("5 Elements Akkalkot daily reports - 26 Oct 2026"); each report's key figures are in the email under its name, and each report is attached as its own PDF. If one of an address's reports cannot be made that night, its whole email waits and goes, complete, once every report is ready. The owner, an Admin or the GM sets them, for each hotel, in Settings, Messages, Daily report emails.

ReportWhat it holdsTo start
Night audit reportThe day the audit closed: rooms charged, check-outs, sales, receipts, room and guest counts, and the restaurant.On
Manager reportRevenue, payments, the ledgers, occupancy, ADR and RevPAR: the day, the month so far and the year so far.Off
Money owedThe guest ledger and the city ledger: what guests and companies owe at the end of the day.Off
Restaurant and stockThe restaurant's day, the closing stock in each store, and the day's wastage and breakage.Off
Bar stockThe bar's day: each drink's opening, purchases, sales, count and closing, the dishes sold and the bar bills (A11.9).Off

To send a report

  1. Switch the report on.
  2. Under Send to, type each address on its own line. At most 20 for one report.
  3. Tap Save at the foot.

Watch out

  • Nobody gets anything until an address is typed. A report switched on with no address says “On, but nobody gets it until an address is typed.”
  • A yellow box “Nothing is sent yet” means sending is not set up on the server. Nothing goes by email until it is.
  • A report switched on after an audit starts from the next audit.
  • A day whose audit was cancelled and run again sends its reports again, to the same addresses: the subject begins “Corrected:” and the email's first line says “Corrected: this day's night audit was cancelled and run again. These reports replace the ones sent before.” Each PDF says it too.

Why it works this way

Daily report emails, each report on or off with its own addresses, the night audit report on to start, nobody sent anything until an address is typed: D27-280. The key figures, at most 20 addresses, and a report switched on later starting from the next audit: D27-282. One email per address with a PDF for each report: D27-371. Sent again, marked Corrected, when a cancelled day is run again: D27-390.

A7.7Your night audit in short

WhenDoSection
Before the auditRestaurant: close the restaurant day. Desk: count the cash and close the shift.A7.3
Open Night auditRead the day being closed, and the checks.A7.2
A guest still due outLeft: settle and check out. Staying: change the dates.A7.3
An arrival still outstandingCheck in the guest who came. Leave the rest: they become no-shows.A7.2
The card shows no reasonRun night audit, then Close with the date.A7.4
After itRead the green card: rooms posted, no-shows, the restaurant, the two drawers.A7.4
A charge was wrong on a closed dayThe owner, an Admin or the GM: Closed days, Correct, with a reason.A7.5
Chapter A8

Restaurant

For waiters, cashiers, the kitchen and the restaurant manager. How an order goes from the table to the kitchen and onto the bill, how add-ons and custom add-ons are put on a dish, how the bill is printed and paid, how the cash drawer is opened, counted and closed, and how the restaurant and its KOT printers are set up.

A8.1The restaurant's screens

The restaurant has its own space. Click Restaurant in the switcher at the top (A0.4). Its menu, Point of sale, holds these screens. You see the ones your role uses.

ScreenWho uses itWhat it is for
TablesWaiters, the bar, Reception (if allowed)The room as it stands. Tap a table to take an order on a pad; print a table's bill; clear a table. New parcel, and the open parcels above the room.
TillWaiters, the bar, the cashierThe cash register: the bill line by line, sending to the kitchen, payment, the day's paid bills; discounts for the GM, the owner and an Admin.
TerminalWaiters, the barThe same work on a fixed tablet or screen, one outlet. Also where room-service orders from guests arrive.
KitchenChef, kitchen managerEvery dish the kitchen holds, oldest first: Start, then Ready.
Bar stockThe bar manager (the Bar role), GM, owner, AdminThe bar's day like the paper register - what came, what was sold (NIPs, 30, 60 and 90 ml), what is left - and the closing count; the bar's bills as printed; what each drink takes (A9.11).
Kitchen stockChef, kitchen manager (to read)The kitchen store's day - what came, what the KOTs used, what was wasted and why, what is left, the closing count - and each dish's recipe. The same as Inventory's Restaurant tab (A9.11).
MenuKitchen managerDishes, prices, variations, Sides, the numbered Add-ons, what is off today, promotions and coupons; for the owner, an Admin and the GM, Profit per dish.
Close restaurant dayCashier, waiters, the bar, kitchen managerThe cash drawer: open the day with a float, money in and out, the count, the close.
Table bookingsWhoever takes ordersHotel guests' requests for a table: confirm or decline. A table for somebody not staying. On the night: arrived, seated, a no-show, cancelled (A8.2).
Charges to roomsAccountsBills an outside till sent to guests' rooms.
Restaurant setupOwner, Admin, GM; the kitchen manager for the KOT section onlyThe restaurant's name, a parcel's packing charge, the voluntary service charge, sections and tables, which computer prints which KOT, table-booking hours.

At the top of Tables, the Till, the Terminal and the Kitchen, one line for each kind of KOT says whether it is printing, for example “Kitchen KOTs: Kitchen PC - online”. When it is not printing, the line is red and says why (A8.4).

In a test hotel (A0.5) the orange stripe “TEST HOTEL · practice only · nothing here is real” is across the top of the Kitchen screen and the Terminal as well, and every bill and KOT prints with “TEST · NOT VALID” at its head and foot. The bill carries no GSTIN.

A8.2Taking an order at a table

Open Tables. Each section of the room (A/C, Non A/C, the bar) shows its tables. A table's colour says where it stands.

ColourMeans
Free (white)Nobody is at it. Tap it to start an order.
Running (blue)An order is open; nothing has gone to the kitchen yet.
In the kitchen (orange)Dishes have gone to the kitchen.
Bill printed (green)The guest has the bill in front of them.
Paid - clear it (yellow)Paid. Tap Clear when the guests leave, so the table is free for the next ones.
Closed unpaid - clear it (grey)Closed without payment, with a reason (A8.7). Tap Clear too.

To take an order

  1. Tap a free table. The order pad opens over the room (Figure A8-02).
  2. Tap a dish to add it. Tap it again for two. To find a dish, type in Search the menu, or tap a section button (Starters, Main course…); tap it again to see all.
  3. A dish with a choice to make (a size, a crust, Sides) opens a small window first: choose, add a note for the kitchen if needed (“no chilli”), and tap Add.
  4. Check This round on the right. Use − and + for the number, the bin to take a dish off, Customise for add-ons (A8.3).
  5. Tap Send. The message “N4 sent · Kitchen docket 14.” means the kitchen has it and the KOTs are printing (A8.4).

To add a round to a table that already has an order, tap the table again. The pad says “Another round on this table's bill.” and lists the dishes Already sent at the top (A8.3), and under them the KOTs sent, each with Reprint (A8.4). The + beside a dish already sent puts one more of it on this round, with the same choices (size, sides, add-ons and note); it goes with Send on a new KOT, and the first is untouched (D27-349).

At the bar: the Bar role

Somebody given the Bar role works as a waiter does, on the same screens: Tables, the Till, the Terminal, Close restaurant day and Guest requests, with the waiter's Start here card, and has Bar stock too: the bar's sheet, its count and its bills (A9.11). Their pad, Till and Terminal hold only the bar's dishes: the dishes on the menu's Bar tab, the sections sold under Bar or Alcohol (A8.11), and the pad opens straight on them. Their KOTs print at the bar; if a manager has sent a Bar section's KOT to the kitchen (A8.10), its dishes are still the bar's and print where the manager chose. A dish from any other section is refused even if somebody tries it another way, and the message names it: “Paneer Tikka is not on the bar's menu. A waiter orders it.” They take payment, print the bill and close the restaurant day, as a waiter does; a discount is the GM's, the owner's or an Admin's (D27-352). The Bar role: D27-324; the Bar tab, Start here and Guest requests: D27-329; Bar stock: D27-356.

A parcel

A parcel is an order with no table, named by its customer. New parcel is on Tables, the Till and the Terminal.

  1. Tap New parcel.
  2. Type the Customer's name (it must be given, so two parcels can be told apart) and, if you like, a Phone to call when it is ready. Tap Open the parcel.
  3. On Tables the pad opens on it, titled “Parcel · Rahul”: add the dishes and Send, as for a table. On the Till and the Terminal the parcel opens there.

The KOT prints Parcel · Rahul in place of a table, and so does the bill. Tables shows each open parcel under Parcels, above the room: the customer's name, how long it has been open and what it comes to. Tap it to add a round; print its bill or open it on the Till from its buttons, as on a table. A parcel leaves the list once it is settled.

When the restaurant has a packing charge (Restaurant setup, A8.10), it goes on the parcel's bill once, with its first KOT, taxed as the food. It is on the bill, never on a KOT. Struck by a manager, with a reason, it does not come back.

Moving a table, or joining two

Guests change tables, and two tables become one party. Both are done on the table's open bill, on the Till or the Terminal (tap the eye on the table in Tables to open it on the Till), by anybody who takes orders. Nothing prints: the Kitchen screen shows the new table by itself (D27-370, D27-372).

To move the guests to a free table:

  1. On the open bill, tap Move to another table.
  2. The restaurant's free tables are listed, in every section (A/C to Non A/C is fine). Tap the one the guests are moving to.
  3. The bill, its dishes and its KOTs are now on that table, and the old table is free. The bill says “Moved from N4 to N6 by Ravi at 20:15.” and keeps it.

To join another table onto this bill, so the two pay one bill:

  1. On the open bill, tap Join another table.
  2. The restaurant's other tables with an open bill are listed, in every section. Tap the one that joins this one.
  3. The screen says what happens and that “This cannot be undone.” Tap Join.
  4. That table's dishes, KOTs and covers are now on this bill (this bill keeps its own waiter). Its own bill is closed as joined: it is not a sale, not a void and not closed unpaid, and no report counts it. On Tables, that table reads Joined to AC3 until this bill is settled, as the party may still be sitting there; then it is free.

A move or a join stays inside one restaurant. A bill that is held, on a function's bill, discounted or rounded off, or with something waiting at a printer or a request waiting for the GM, is refused with a sentence that says why. A table still showing a paid bill must be cleared first, and a table booked for today (by a hotel guest or anybody else, A8.2 below) is refused from two hours before the booking; earlier in the day it can be used.

A table booked: outside diners, and on the night

Table bookings lists the hotel guests' requests (they ask from their own page: confirm or decline each one) and every booking of the day. Somebody who is not staying is booked here, by whoever takes the call. Anybody who takes orders does it.

  1. Tap New booking.
  2. Type the Name, the Phone (so the restaurant can call them), how many People (1 to 20; more is a banquet function), the Day and the Time. If you know it, choose the Table; or the Area they would like (A/C, Non A/C). A Note if there is one.
  3. Tap Book the table. It is confirmed as you take it, and listed on its day.

On the night, each booking has its buttons:

  • Arrived: they are here, waiting for their table.
  • Seat: choose a free table. Its bill opens with the party as its covers and the diner's name on it, exactly as if a waiter had opened the table on Tables; take the order there. A table with a bill on it is refused.
  • No-show: only once the booked time has come; before it, it says “They are booked for 20:30: a no-show is marked once that time has come.” An arrived booking is never a no-show.
  • Cancel booking: with the reason if they gave one.

Day at the top shows another day's bookings; Back to today returns. A hotel guest's page keeps saying Confirmed for a table that is arrived, seated or a no-show.

Watch out

  • Nothing reaches the kitchen until you tap Send. The round is kept on your device while you build it. A round left on a pad shows on the table's tile as a dashed border with “not sent”.
  • No connection? Send says “N4 is held. The kitchen does not have it yet. It goes as soon as the connection is back.” The kitchen is not cooking it yet: tell them, or wait for the line.
  • A dish refused (off the menu today, a choice not made, the restaurant closed): nothing at all is sent, the round stays on the pad, and the message names the dish. Fix that dish and Send again.
  • The total at the foot of the pad is what the dishes cost before tax. The bill (A8.6) has the tax.
  • The same dish again is one more of it, but only until the kitchen has it. After that, more of it is a new line, so the kitchen gets a new KOT for it.

Why it works this way

The pad works with no network until Send, so a waiter at the table never waits on the internet; the whole round is sent at once, all of it or none, so the kitchen never cooks half an order. The same dish is one more of it: D27-189. The note after each tap: D27-290. Parcels, named by the customer, with a packing charge once per parcel taxed as the food: D27-359.

A8.3Add-ons: numbered, and custom

A guest wants something extra on a dish. There are two ways, both under Customise:

  • A numbered add-on, from the restaurant's list: “2 is Kebab, ₹120”. Staff remember the number.
  • A custom add-on, typed on the spot: something not on the list, with a name and a price, or Free.

A numbered add-on, before the dish is sent

  1. Tap Customise beside the dish (on the pad, the Till or the Terminal).
  2. Tap the add-on's number. Tap it again for two of it; × takes one off. An add-on that is off today shows, but cannot be tapped.
  3. The top of the window shows what the line will read, for example “Veg Biryani with add-on Kebab”, and the price moves as you tap.
  4. On a line of several of the dish, choose All 3 (the add-on on each) or Just 1 (one of them, as its own line). Done waits until you choose.
  5. Tap Done.

The dish stays one line, taxed at its own rate. The bill shows the breakdown under it (“Veg Biryani 310 · Kebab +120”), and the KOT prints “+ Kebab” under the dish so the cook does not miss it.

A custom add-on

  1. In Customise, tap Custom add-on.
  2. Type its Name, as the kitchen should read it: “Extra papad”.
  3. Type its Price in rupees (40, or 40.50), or tick Free. There is no default: a blank price, or 0 without Free, is not accepted.
  4. Set How many with − and +. It starts at 1 and is its own number: one papad for two thalis is one.
  5. Tap Add. It is listed under the add-ons as “+ Extra papad ×1” with its price. Add more if you need to; × takes one away.
  6. Tap Done.

A custom add-on is always its own line under its dish: “Paneer Tikka ₹320 / + Extra papad ₹40” on the bill. It is taxed at the dish's rate, and it goes to the kitchen with its dish.

On a dish the kitchen already has

The thali has reached the table, and the guest wants one more thing with it.

  1. On Tables: tap the table. The pad lists the dishes Already sent; tap Customise beside the dish.
    On the Till or the Terminal: tap Customise beside the dish.
  2. The window is called “Add to Paneer Tikka”. Tap numbered add-ons, or add a custom one, as above.
  3. Tap Done. Each add-on goes on as its own line under the dish.
  4. Send it, like any new dish: the pad's Send, or the Till's Send to the kitchen. Its KOT names the dish it is for: “+ Extra papad · for: Paneer Tikka (KOT 12)”.

Watch out

  • An add-on's number is set when it goes on. To change it, strike it (× on the Till) and add it again.
  • Taking off an add-on the kitchen already has is like taking off a dish: only the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager or the kitchen manager can, and they must say why (A8.7). Striking a dish strikes its add-ons, with the same reason.
  • Customise needs the connection on the Till and the Terminal: a change held offline could reach the dish after the kitchen has it.
  • Whoever takes orders can add a custom add-on. Each one records who added it and when.

Why it works this way

The numbered list, one line per dish, the breakdown on the bill and “+ Kebab” on the KOT: D27-289. “All 3 / Just 1”: D27-290. Custom add-ons, add-ons on a dish already sent, Free never a default, the dish's own tax, their own number: D27-291. The common custom add-ons can be given a number in the Menu (A8.11).

A8.4Sending to the kitchen: the KOTs

When you tap Send, the round gets one KOT number. The kitchen's dishes print at the kitchen's printer and the drinks at the bar's: one slip for each kind of KOT, each saying in big letters what it is.

  • What a KOT shows: the time, what it is (KITCHEN KOT 14), dine in or take away, the table, each dish with its number, its add-ons and Sides under it, and the kitchen note. Never a price.
  • Which kind a dish is depends on its menu section: Bar and Alcohol sections print at the bar, the rest in the kitchen, unless the manager chose otherwise (A8.10). It is decided when the dish is sent, so a reprint goes where the first slip went.
  • A dish taken off after it was sent prints, on a reprint of its KOT, under “STOP - TAKEN OFF”, with the reason.
  • A lost or torn KOT: the order's KOTs sent list one line for each KOT and kind (“KOT 3 · Bar”), each with Reprint: on Tables in the table's pad, and on the Till and the Terminal with the order open. Tap Reprint: it prints at the computer that printed that KOT, the kitchen's or the bar's, not on the device you are using, and the screen says where: “KOT 3 · Bar sent to Bar PC”. If that computer is off, the screen says “Bar PC is offline”: the reprint waits there and prints when it is back, or, if a manager moves that kind to another computer first (A8.10), it goes with the kind and prints there. If no computer prints that kind, it says so and nothing prints (a manager chooses one, A8.10). On the computer that printed it you can also open Restaurant setup, the KOT section, This computer's last 20 KOTs, and tap Reprint. Either way the slip says REPRINT. Waiters and the bar reprint: D27-324; at the station, and from the Till and the Terminal: D27-329; a waiting reprint follows its kind: D27-330.

The printing lines

The line saysWhat to do
“Kitchen KOTs: Kitchen PC - online” (grey)Nothing. It is printing.
“Bar KOTs wait: Bar PC not seen since 8:42” (red)The bar's computer is off, asleep, or its screen is closed. Its KOTs wait for it and print when it is back, oldest first, the same day. Turn it on and open a restaurant screen on it.
“No computer prints Bar KOTs - they are not printing” (red)Nobody has chosen a computer for that kind. A manager taps Set up on the line (A8.10).

Why it works this way

One computer prints each kind and no other device prints a KOT: D27-159, D27-161. A missed KOT prints when its computer is back, the same business day only: D27-167. Kinds, one number with a slip per kind, the heading in big letters, REPRINT, the red line only for a kind something is sent to: D27-292. A reprint prints at its kind's computer too, wherever Reprint is pressed: D27-329. The website cannot reach a printer by its address on the hotel's network, so a printer is always reached through the computer it is connected to.

A8.5The Kitchen screen

The Kitchen screen stays open on a screen in the kitchen (and one at the bar). Every dish the kitchen holds is a ticket, oldest first.

  1. When you begin a dish, tap Start. It moves to On the fire.
  2. When it goes out, tap Ready. It leaves the screen and is the waiters': the table's tile on Tables says “2 ready”.
  3. The waiter carries it out and taps “2 ready” on the tile (or Taken on the Terminal). It is served.
  • A ticket's edge turns yellow after 5 minutes and red after 10. Under the wait, “12 min est” is how long the dish should take; “- est” means nobody has timed it.
  • A dish taken off after it was sent turns into a red CANCELLED ticket with “stop cooking this” and the manager's reason.
  • By table shows one card per table, its dishes grouped by course, so you can see whether a whole table is ready.
  • All / Kitchen / Bar shows one kind's tickets. Each screen remembers its choice: set the bar's screen to Bar once.
  • LIVE in the header means new dishes arrive at once; RECONNECTING means it is checking every few seconds instead.

Why it works this way

Two buttons, Start and Ready; a Ready dish is the waiter's to carry out: D27-221, D27-222. The All / Kitchen / Bar filter in place of the old KOT printer button, and the two-row header on a phone: D27-292, D27-293.

A8.6Printing the bill

Each printed bill says at the top what it is:

HeadingWhen
BILLPrinted before payment, for the guest to check and pay; and the first print after payment, which also says how it was paid.
BILL · DUPLICATEA paid bill printed again.

Before payment, from Tables

  1. Tap the printer under the table.
  2. The message says where it went: “Bill sent to Bar PC”. The table turns green, Bill printed.

Where the bill prints

  • A bill printer is chosen (A8.10): it prints there by itself, and the screen says where it went.
  • The bill printer is off: the screen says “Bar PC is offline” and offers Print here. Print here opens the bill on your device; tap Print here on it. A bill printed here does not print again at the bill printer later. If you choose to wait instead, it prints there when it is back.
  • No bill printer is chosen: the bill opens on your device, as it always did. Tap Print here.

It is a plain restaurant bill. It shows the hotel and the restaurant, its GSTIN, FSSAI licence and HSN/SAC (the code of each kind its lines sell under, Settings › Taxes, A17; a dash until it is set: D27-344), the bill number and date, the table, the covers and the steward, and every line with its quantity, rate and amount (add-ons under their dish). The same dish ordered in two rounds - a beer, food, then a second beer - is one line, 2× (D27-353). Then the sub total, the discount, CGST and SGST for each rate (alcohol's VAT on its own line, and on its own VAT bill), any round off, and the GRAND TOTAL: the amount the Till asks for. A paid bill also says how it was paid. It ends “Thank you. Visit again.”

Why it works this way

The bill printer, Print here, and the bill opening as before when no bill printer is chosen: D27-292. A plain restaurant bill, BILL before payment, with the discount and the round off on it: D27-334. Alcohol's VAT apart from GST: D21-91.

A8.7The Till: the cash register

The Till is where a bill is checked and paid. The menu is on the left: tapping a dish adds it to the open order at once. The bill is on the right. Under it are Open orders, Settled today and An earlier day's bill. For bills of many days, see Bill history below.

To open an order on the Till

  1. From Tables, tap the eye under the table. Or on the Till, tap the order under Open orders.
  2. For a new order without Tables, type the table in Start an order and open it.

What each button does

ButtonWhat it does
Covers, waiter, customerOptional: people eating, who served, a customer's mobile, name and address (for take away and delivery). Hold keeps an order aside; Resume brings it back.
Customise (the sliders icon)Add-ons on the dish (A8.3).
−One fewer. For a dish the kitchen has, a manager and a reason (below).
+One more. Not yet sent: the count goes up. Already with the kitchen: one more of it, with the same choices, goes on a new line for the next Send, on its own KOT; the first is untouched (D27-349). On the bill and on the screens the two rounds still show as one line, 2× (D27-353); − and × act on the newest round.
×Strike the line. It stays on the record, struck through.
Send to the kitchenSends every dish not yet sent, as Send does on the pad.
KOTs sent: ReprintAt the foot of an open order: prints that KOT again at the computer that printed it, marked REPRINT (A8.4).
DiscountThe GM, the owner or an Admin only (D27-352): a percentage or a fixed amount, always with a reason, up to the whole bill: no 10% limit since D27-395. A promotion (Point of sale → Menu → Promotions) is the one the restaurant gives again and again, by name, at the top of the window. A coupon the guest brings is typed in Coupon code at the top, then Apply coupon (below). A waiter, the bar and the cashier do not see it: they Ask for a discount, and the GM approves.
Round offRounds the total to the rupee. Undo round off takes it back.
Service charge 5%, if the guest agreesOnly where the GM set a rate (A8.10). It asks first, and goes on only when you tap The guest agreed. The bill then has Service charge 5% (voluntary), with its GST. Take off the service charge removes it (below).
Tip for the staffType the tip, then tap Cash, Card or UPI: it is taken the same way as the bill, but it is not part of it (below).
Room and Charge to roomType the room number and tap Charge to room. It asks first, naming the guest: “Charge ₹441 to room 201?”. A room with two open bills asks whose.
Cash, Card, UPIPaid that way, at once. The bill moves to Settled today.
Part - pay two waysSplit the payment: each way with its amount. For cash, type the Cash given and the change is shown. Settle appears only when the parts add up.
No charge (NC)The owner, an Admin or the GM only: the bill is given free, with a reason, and prints at once with the dishes, their prices and the Bill total, and nothing to pay (below; D27-351, D27-394).
Close unpaidCloses the bill without payment. It always asks why. The table then reads “Closed unpaid - clear it”.

To take payment

  1. Check the lines and the Total with the guest. Print the bill if they want to see it (A8.6).
  2. Tap Cash, Card or UPI; or type the room and tap Charge to room; or Part - pay two ways.
  3. The bill closes and moves under Settled today. To print it, tap it there, then Print the bill.
  4. When the guests leave, tap Clear on the table in Tables.

The voluntary service charge, and tips

By law a restaurant may not add a service charge by itself or by default; a guest pays one only if they agree, and the bill must say it is voluntary (the Consumer Protection guidelines of 4 July 2022). So it is off unless the GM sets a rate on Restaurant setup (A8.10), and even then it goes on a bill only when you ask the guest and they say yes.

  1. Ask the guest. If they agree, tap Service charge 5%, if the guest agrees, then The guest agreed.
  2. The bill shows Service charge 5% (voluntary) under the net (after any discount or coupon), and the tax grows with it: GST is charged on a service charge as on the food. Alcohol under VAT takes none.
  3. Changed their mind? Tap Take off the service charge while the bill is open. A paid bill keeps it as it was paid.

A tip is money for the staff: not a sale and not taxed. Type it in Tip for the staff, then take the payment with Cash, Card or UPI: the tip is taken the same way. It is written on the paid bill and the printed bill as “Tip for the staff 100.00 by cash - not part of the bill”; the GRAND TOTAL and the payment are the bill alone. A bill charged to a room or a function, split two ways or on the owner's allowance takes no tip, and a tip of more than the bill is refused as a slip of the finger. A cash tip is in the drawer until it is handed out, so the count expects it (A8.9).

A coupon

A coupon is a promotion the guest brings as a code (Menu, Promotions, A8.11), good between two days, on so many bills, above a least bill. The GM, the owner or an Admin applies it, as a promotion.

  1. Tap Discount. Type the guest's code in Coupon code and tap Apply coupon. On the Terminal, tap Coupon.
  2. The bill shows Coupon DIWALI10 10% and the amount off, before tax. The use is the bill itself.

It is refused in a sentence before its first day (“Diwali coupon starts on 1 Dec 2026.”), after its last, once it has been used on its number of bills, under its least bill, and when it would take off more than the bill. A bill closed unpaid gives its use back. If a dish is struck so the bill falls under the coupon's least bill, payment is refused until the coupon is taken off (Discount, Remove) or more is added.

Printing a bill from an earlier day

Settled today lists today's bills only. To print an earlier paid bill again, for a guest or for the accounts:

  1. On the Till, under An earlier day's bill, pick the Day, or type the Bill number (a part of it is enough).
  2. Tap the bill in the list. Each says its day, its items and its total.
  3. Tap Print the bill. It prints at the bill printer (or here, as in A8.6), headed BILL · DUPLICATE, so it cannot pass as a new sale.

Only paid, voided and NC bills are listed: a bill closed unpaid has nothing to print. An earlier day's bill can only be printed; it is voided only on the day it was paid.

Why it works this way

The team asked to reprint a bill of an earlier day (18 October); the owner asked for it on 20 October. A bill printed again says DUPLICATE: D27-292. Who may print it is unchanged: whoever prints today's bills.

Bill history: any dates

The Till's card above finds one day, or one number, for everyone who uses the Till. For anything wider, the owner, an Admin, the GM, the Hotel Manager, the Accountant and Reception open Bill history in the restaurant's menu, under Till (D27-372). It lists every paid, VOID and NC bill of the dates you choose, and nothing else: an order still open is on the Till, and a bill closed unpaid has nothing to print.

  1. It opens on today's business day. Change From and To to any dates. Leave one empty to go on without an end.
  2. To narrow the list, fill any of these (all optional, and they work together): the Bill number (a part is enough), the Table, the Guest name or phone (a part of either; a phone is found however it was typed), Paid by, the Waiter and the Outlet. Tap Show bills. Clear empties the boxes.
  3. Each line says the bill number, its date and the time it was settled, outlet, table, guest (a bill charged to a room shows the stay's guest and room, and is found by them too), waiter, how it was paid, its total and its state: Paid, VOID (the total struck through) or NC (no value). A bill paid in two ways says both. A figure nobody holds shows a dash.
  4. Tap a bill to see the whole bill, as it is on paper. Print the bill prints it as in A8.6, headed BILL · DUPLICATE.
  5. Download to Excel saves the list on the screen as a file Excel opens (a CSV, named with the hotel and the dates). Totals are plain numbers so Excel can add them; an NC bill's total is left empty. A VOID bill keeps its total in the file, so filter its State column before adding up.

One ask shows at most 500 bills. If more matched, the screen says Showing the first 500 bills and the file holds those 500: narrow the dates or add a filter to see the rest.

Why it works this way

The owner asked for a full bill history on 27 October: D27-370. It answers the same question as the Till's earlier-bill card, so a reprint is the same DUPLICATE. It is in the menu for the people who see the Till.

Voiding a paid bill

A bill paid by mistake (the wrong table, paid twice) can be voided by the owner, an Admin or the GM, on the day it was paid and before Close restaurant day. Anyone else sees Ask the GM to void this bill and sends it (below).

  1. On the Till, tap the bill under Settled today.
  2. Tap Void this paid bill and type why.
  3. Paid by card or UPI: refund it on the card machine or the UPI app first, tap Next, and type the refund's reference (the UPI reference or the card approval).
  4. Tap Void the bill. Give the cash back to the guest out of the restaurant's tin.

The bill keeps its number and reads VOID, with the reason, who and when; Print the bill prints it headed Bill · VOID. The kitchen's KOTs stay as they were: the food was made. The day's sales, the reports and the Day book leave a voided bill out, and its alcohol's VAT bill is cancelled with it. Close restaurant day and the night audit list it under Paid bills voided. Its cash comes out of the restaurant's tin, so the tin's Expected leaves it out (A8.9); nobody's front-desk drawer is touched.

Giving a bill free: No charge (NC)

A bill the hotel gives free - the owner's guests, a staff meal - is closed as NC by the owner, an Admin or the GM. Their name on it is the approval. Anyone else sees Ask the GM for NC and sends it (below).

  1. On the Till (or the Terminal), open the bill. It must still be open.
  2. Tap No charge (NC) and type why.
  3. Tap Give NC. The bill prints at once at the bill printer (or here, as in A8.6).

The bill keeps every dish with its price and amount, and shows the Bill total at menu prices, then NC · No charge: ₹0 to pay, with the reason, who approved it and when. The paper is the same, headed NC · No charge, and has no tax lines: nothing was sold, so nothing was taxed. The kitchen's KOTs stay as they were: the food was made. An NC bill is no sale. Its value is shown, but always on its own as NC, never in the day's sales, the tax or the money taken. The stock counts it too: the Consumption report lists its dishes as given away, each at its MRP from the Menu (A8.11, A11.9). Close restaurant day lists each NC bill under No charge (NC): who approved it, when and why, and its value. A last line, NC (not in sales), gives the day's total. The Complimentary tile counts the NC bills and gives that value. The Night audit screen and its report list them the same way, with a Value (not in sales) column and a total, and Bill history shows NC ₹… for each. Its table is freed at once.

Sent to the GM: what a waiter or cashier may not do

Four things are the owner's, an Admin's or the GM's: taking off a dish the kitchen already has, a discount, giving a bill free (NC), and voiding a paid bill. A waiter or a cashier does not wait for the GM to come to their screen: they send it to the GM, with a reason, and carry on.

  1. On the Till (or the Terminal), tap what you need: the dish's X, Ask for a discount, Ask the GM for NC, or, on a paid bill, Ask the GM to void this bill.
  2. Type why. A discount: the percentage or amount, and why. A void paid by card or UPI: refund it on the card machine or the UPI app first, and type the refund's reference.
  3. Tap Send to the GM. The bill says “Sent to the GM, waiting: Strike 2 x Paneer Tikka (KOT 51) - Table 4 · bill …”.

The GM's bell counts it and Approvals, at the top of their menu, shows it (A12.3). When they Approve, it is done at once, as if they had pressed the button themselves: the dish comes off, the discount goes on, the bill is NC or void. The waiter's bill then says “Approved by …”. When they Refuse, with a reason, it says “Not approved by … (the reason)” and nothing changes.

Changing how a paid bill was paid

A bill paid by card but keyed as cash, or the other way round, is put right by the owner, an Admin or the GM, before the night audit closes its day. The amounts stay the same; only cash, card and UPI change into one another.

  1. On the Till, tap the bill under Settled today, then Change how it was paid.
  2. For each part of the payment (a split bill has more than one), pick Cash, Card or UPI.
  3. Type why, and tap Change it.
