The bill then reads, under “Paid by card”, “Payment mode changed: UPI to Card, ₹336.00, by … at 18:50 - the reason.” Close restaurant day lists it under Payment mode changed, marked “after the drawer was counted” where it was.

The owner's allowance

The hotel's owner takes up to a set amount a month from the restaurant free; above it, a set % off. Both are this hotel's settings, typed by the owner or an Admin in Restaurant setup, Owner's allowance: Free each month, ₹ and % off above it. Nothing is filled in to start with: until the amount is typed, no bill can go on the allowance. The month is the hotel's business month and starts again on the 1st; what is not used is not carried over. The card also lists this month's bills on the allowance: what was free, the % off given and what was paid.

  1. On the Till, open the owner's bill and tap Owner's allowance (the GM, the owner or an Admin; nobody else sees it).
  2. The window says this month's allowance, what is left, the bill, what is free, and, if the bill is more than what is left, what is to pay after the % off above it.
  3. Tap how the rest is paid: Cash, Card or UPI; or Settle it free when nothing is left to pay.

The bill then reads, for example, “₹164.00 free on the owner's allowance, ₹406.40 by UPI”, and its discount line names the % off: “Owner's allowance: 20% off above the ₹164.00 left of this month's ₹500.00”. GST is charged on the menu price, the free part included, as for any sale. Close restaurant day lists the free part as Owner's allowance in how the money arrived; it is not cash in the drawer, and the night audit report counts it with the room and function postings, the Manager report as Payment - Owner's allowance. A void gives the allowance back.

Watch out

  • Food the kitchen already has comes off only for the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager or the kitchen manager, and they type why: “The kitchen already has this. Why is it coming off?”. The reason prints on the KOT, shows on the Kitchen screen and in the day's list of dishes struck after the kitchen had them. The same goes for one fewer of a sent dish, and for closing unpaid a bill any of which was sent.
  • Cash before the first float is refused: “Count this outlet's first float once (Close restaurant day, Open the day): cash is taken after it.” Card, UPI and room charges go on. See A8.9.
  • A bill paid wholly in cash is rounded to the rupee.
  • Cash over ₹1,00,000 on one bill asks for the guest's PAN or another identity.
  • No connection: cash, card and UPI are refused until the line is back. A room charge can be made with no connection: it is held and sent when the line is back.
  • Once the day is closed (A8.9), new bills and payments wait for the night audit.
  • An order on a banquet function is paid on the function's bill only; cash, card, UPI and rooms are switched off for it, with the reason.
  • A bill charged to a room is never voided here: “This bill went to room 201 - reverse it on the guest's bill.” A bill on a banquet function is reversed on the function's bill.
  • The same day only: a void on a later day, or once the day is closed, is refused: “The restaurant's day is closed and its drawer counted. A bill of a closed day cannot be voided.”
  • NC is for an open bill, and cannot be undone. A paid bill is voided instead; a bill on a banquet function is paid on the function's bill and is never NC. An NC bill always says why: “Say why this bill is no charge. The reason prints on the bill.”
  • Sent to the GM, asked again when they approve: if the dish was struck meanwhile, or the bill paid, the GM is told why and it stays waiting: “That line is already struck, or is not here.” The same thing twice is refused: “This is already with the GM.” Nobody approves their own.
  • A payment mode changes only on a paid bill of the day the night audit has not closed, and never to or from a room or a function, which are changed on the guest's or the function's bill. Cash of ₹2,00,000 or more on one bill is refused; more than ₹1,00,000 in cash needs the PAN the bill has: void it and settle it again with the PAN.

Why it works this way

A manager and a reason for food the kitchen has: D27-119. Charge to room asks first, naming the guest: D27-117; two open bills in a room, one button each: D27-162. The Till sends to the kitchen like the Terminal: D27-166. Close unpaid frees its table with Clear: D27-288. Orders on a banquet function: D17-21. Voiding a paid bill: D27-324; its cash out of the tin: D27-327. No charge (NC), the GM's, owner's or Admin's approval with a reason: D27-351. Its prices and Bill total on the screen and the paper, ₹0 to pay and no tax lines, its value at menu prices shown as NC everywhere and never in sales, tax or the money taken: D27-394. A waiter or cashier sends the GM a strike of a sent dish, a discount, an NC or a void, approving does it; a paid bill's cash, card or UPI changed before the night audit by the GM, the owner or an Admin, with a reason: D27-363. Complimentary counting the NC bills: D27-365 (its screen without prices, until D27-394). The owner's allowance, its two figures the owner's or an Admin's to type, the rest paid at the till, GST as a sale, settled by the GM, the owner or an Admin: D27-355, D27-366. The taxes in Restaurant setup too, the same card as Settings: D27-368. A table for somebody not staying, the voluntary service charge and tips, coupons and profit per dish: D27-383, built under D27-396 (the service charge by the CCPA's guidelines of 4 July 2022, taxed as part of the supply; none on alcohol; a coupon applied by the same three as a promotion).

A8.8The Terminal

The Terminal is for a fixed tablet or screen in one outlet. The first time it is opened on a device it asks which outlet it is in, and remembers that on the device.

  • Open an order, tap dishes to add them (each with Customise, the sliders icon, and − and +), and send them to the kitchen.
  • A dish the kitchen made Ready shows Ready with Taken: tap it when you carry it out.
  • Under the dishes, the open order's KOTs sent, each with Reprint: it prints again at the computer that printed it (A8.4).
  • Room-service orders waiting: a checked-in guest's order from their own page. Accept makes it a room-service order for their room and sends it to the kitchen; Decline asks a reason, which the guest reads. It is charged to the room at delivery.
  • Payment and printing work as on the Till, No charge (NC) included.
  • One row above Cash, Card and UPI: Service charge 5%? (where the GM set a rate, only when the guest agrees), Coupon (the GM, the owner or an Admin) and Tip ₹, taken with the payment (A8.7).

A8.9The cash drawer: Close restaurant day

Close restaurant day is where the cashier opens the drawer with a float, records money that was not a sale, counts the drawer, and closes the day.

Once, before the first cash: open the day

  1. Open Close restaurant day. The card Open the day shows a row for each note and coin.
  2. Count the float in the tin and type how many of each: ₹500 × 4, ₹100 × 10. The total shows on the button.
  3. Tap Open the day - ₹3,000.

From then on each day opens by itself, on the float the last close kept.

During the day: money that was not a sale

  1. Open the Cash step. Under In and out of the drawer, tap Record.
  2. Choose What happened: Expense (paid out, such as milk), Cash in (a top-up), To the safe, or Due paid (money owed, collected).
  3. Type How much and What was it for. This line is what somebody asks about tomorrow, so say it plainly.
  4. For an Expense, choose its Category: Kitchen, Housekeeping, Maintenance, Office or Other. Record stays grey until one is chosen.
  5. For an Expense, add the Photo of the bill if you have it: take it with the phone's camera, or pick a file. It can be added later.
  6. Tap Record.

Each expense in the list shows its category after the word Expense; an expense recorded before 27 October 2026 shows a dash. Under it, Photo of the bill opens the photo, or Add photo adds one now - also after the day is closed. Every expense, with its category and photo, is in the Petty cash report (A11.6).

An expense may wait for a manager's yes: it shows “Waiting for a yes - not taken off the tin yet” and is not taken off what the drawer should hold until it is approved (A12).

At the end of the shift: count the drawer

  1. Open the Cash step. Under Count the drawer, type how many of each note and coin come out of the tin.
  2. Look at The sum: the opening float, plus the cash taken, plus the Cash tips, plus or minus the money in and out, is what the drawer is Expected to hold. Under it, Counted. A paid bill voided today is not in it: its cash went back to the guest out of the tin (A8.7). Cash tips handed to the staff from the tin are recorded as money out, with the reason.
  3. If they differ, a yellow box says “Short by ₹217” or over, and how much of it is a paid-out waiting for a yes.
  4. Tap Save the count - ₹3,140.

On the Overview, Service charge and tips shows the day's voluntary service charge (how many bills, and how much; it is already in the money above, with its GST) and the tips by cash, card and UPI, with their total: Tips for the staff (not in sales). The night audit (A7) and its report show the same two, the service charge under Charges and the tips under Tips.

Close the day

  1. Open the Finalize step. Before it closes lists what a person must decide first: bills still open (settle them, or close them unpaid with a reason), tables never cleared after payment.
  2. Under The drawer, if the count is short or over, type Why. It does not stop the close; it has to be written down.
  3. Type the Float kept for the next day. The rest is deposited.
  4. Tap Close with the date. “A closed day cannot be edited.”

Watch out

  • Close restaurant day refuses while any bill is still open. It will not decide for you whether a bill is paid or closed unpaid.
  • After the close, new bills and payments wait for the night audit (A7), which starts the next business day.
  • Close restaurant day needs the connection.

Why it works this way

The first float is counted once; after that each day opens on the float the last close kept, so nobody types it again every morning. A closed day is closed: the owner, 28 September. A paid-out is not taken off the drawer until somebody says yes: D27-242. A difference never stops the close but must have a sentence, because a manager needs the sentence, not the number.

A8.10Setting up the restaurant and its printers

Restaurant setup is for the owner, an Admin and the GM. The kitchen manager sees its KOT section only.

  • Sections and tables: add a section (A/C, Non A/C, the bar), then its tables, one or a numbered run, four to a row. Taking one away switches it off; it is refused while a bill sits on it. Nothing is deleted.
  • Table booking hours: when hotel guests may ask for a table from their own page.
  • Owner's allowance: the free amount a month and the % off above it (A8.7).
  • Taxes: the Serves alcohol (VAT) switch, then the same tax card as Settings, Taxes (A17): the GST rates, the VAT rate when alcohol is served, each menu section's tax and the HSN/SAC codes. Changed here or there, they are one setting. The owner or an Admin switches alcohol on or off; the rates, each section's tax and the codes are changed by whoever may change them in Settings, Taxes.

A parcel's packing charge

Under Parcels, type the Packing charge, ₹ and tap Save. It goes on each parcel's bill once, with its first KOT, taxed as the food (A8.2). Left blank, a parcel has no packing charge; nothing is put in for you. The owner, an Admin and the GM set it.

The voluntary service charge

Under Service charge, type the Service charge, % (above 0, at most 20) and tap Save. It never goes on a bill by itself: it lets the Till and the Terminal offer it, and the cashier puts it on a bill only when the guest agrees (A8.7). Left blank, the default, the restaurant has none and nothing is offered. A bill that has it keeps the rate it was ticked at. The owner, an Admin and the GM set it.

The KOT section

To make a computer print: the Fidato Printer app

Fidato Printer is a small Windows app that runs this website and prints each KOT and bill by itself: no window opens, no print screen flashes up. It sits by the clock and starts with Windows.

  1. On the Windows computer the printer is plugged into, open the website, sign in, open Restaurant setup, the KOT section, and under Set up this computer for printing tap Download Fidato Printer for Windows.
  2. Open the file (Fidato-Printer-Setup.exe). If Windows says “Windows protected your PC”, tap More info, then Run anyway. It installs and opens by itself, and puts Fidato Printer on the desktop.
  3. In its window, sign in and open Restaurant setup, the KOT section. Under This computer, type its name (“Bar PC”), tick what it prints, and tap Save.
  4. Click the Fidato Printer icon by the clock: Printer, then the receipt printer. (Left as Windows' default printer, it prints on whichever printer Windows uses.)
  5. Go to the Kitchen screen in that window and close the window: it keeps printing from the clock. The printing line on every till now reads “Bar KOTs: Bar PC - online”.
  • A slip the printer did not take (paper out, printer off) shows a Windows message, “Fidato Printer: not printed”; print it again from Reprint below.
  • It updates itself. When it starts and once a day it looks for a new version on the Fidato server; when there is one, it downloads it and installs it straight away, by itself. It is gone for a few seconds and comes back by the clock with no window; KOTs and bills sent meanwhile wait and print when it is back. If it cannot reach the server it keeps printing and looks again the next day.
  • Which version: rest the mouse on the icon: it says “Fidato Printer 1.1.0”, so you can see which computers have updated.
  • The icon's menu: Open Fidato Printer, Printer, Start with Windows, and Quit (stops printing).
  • The other way, with Chrome: download the setup file (KOT-station-setup-<code>.cmd). It lists the printers (type the receipt printer's number), makes it the default printer, puts a Fidato Printer shortcut that opens Chrome on the desktop and in Startup, stops the computer sleeping, and opens this section. Chrome prints without asking but shows its print screen for a moment.

By hand instead, step by step: src/modules/pos/KOT-STATION-SETUP.md. If slips come out too wide, set the printer's paper to 80 mm once in its Printing preferences.

Printing on this computer: the shortest slip, and a test

On a computer that prints, the KOT section shows Printing on and its name. Each slip is as long as it needs, and never shorter than its Shortest slip: 160 mm unless you change it. A receipt printer turns a slip it takes for a landscape page, so a short KOT can come out sideways while the longer bills come out upright.

  1. On the printing computer, open Restaurant setup, the KOT section.
  2. Tap Print a test KOT, and Print a test bill. They print exactly as the real ones do, marked as tests.
  3. If the test KOT comes out sideways, type a longer Shortest slip, mm (180, 200), tap Save, and print the test KOT again. Blank puts it back to 160 mm.
  • One computer per kind. Ticking a kind on another computer moves it there; the old one stops printing it by itself. A reprint still waiting for the old one moves with the kind and prints on the new one, marked REPRINT (D27-330); a new KOT sent before the move does not print there.
  • One computer can print everything: tick every kind and the bills on it. Each slip still says what it is.
  • KOT kinds: Kitchen and Bar can be renamed (“Restaurant”) but never switched off; add a kind (Tandoor, Desserts) with Add a KOT. Its name heads its slip: TANDOOR KOT 14.
  • Which section prints where: each menu section starts with its tax heading's KOT (Bar and Alcohol to the Bar, the rest to the Kitchen); change the odd one, such as Mocktails to the Bar. This moves only the printing: who may order a dish follows its tax heading, so the Bar role orders Mocktails only if the section is sold under Bar (A8.2, D27-329).
  • A computer replaced: tick its kinds on the new one. The old one then prints nothing and can be Removed from the list.
  • Every computer that prints keeps its last 20 KOTs here, with Reprint.

The KOT's design

How every KOT at this hotel prints: one design for the hotel, set by the GM, the owner or an Admin. Anyone else who opens the KOT section sees it but cannot change it. The KOT beside the choices is the preview, drawn as it will print.

  1. Open Restaurant setup, the KOT section, The KOT's design.
  2. Choose the size of The dishes, and of The KOT number and table: Small, Normal or Large.
  3. Under What it prints, tick each line the kitchen needs: Waiter, Covers, Time sent, The KOT kind (KITCHEN, BAR), Notes, The order number.
  4. Type a heading line if you want one (“Fidato Kitchen”), at most 40 letters. Blank prints none.
  5. Choose The paper: 80 mm or 58 mm, the width of the roll in the printer.
  6. Tap Save the design. The next KOT prints this way on every computer that prints KOTs. Print a test KOT shows it on paper.
  • As it was puts back the KOT every hotel printed before: Normal sizes; the time, the kind, the notes and the order number; no waiter, covers or heading; 80 mm. Tap Save the design to keep it.
  • With the KOT kind off, the slip is headed KOT - 14 instead of KITCHEN KOT 14. Each computer still prints only its own kinds.
  • If a 58 mm slip comes out too wide, set the printer's paper to 58 mm once in its Printing preferences.
  • The design is for KOTs only. The bill does not change.

Why it works this way

Restaurant setup without a developer: D22-6. The KOT section, its kinds, one computer per kind, the routing by section and the bill printer: D27-292. The kitchen manager may open the KOT section: D27-292. The one-click setup file, and signing in coming back to the page asked for: D27-299. The Fidato Printer app, printing with no window, and the shortcut's new name: D27-360. The app updating itself, straight away: D27-365, D27-366. The KOT's design, one for each hotel, with a preview: D27-368.

A8.11The menu and the add-ons list

  • Prices are yours. Nothing was shipped with the system. A price changed today applies to the next order; bills already printed keep the price they were sold at.
  • Each section has a tax heading (Restaurant, Bar, Alcohol, Banquet). A dish is taxed by its section's rule unless it has its own rate.
  • Variations (a size, a crust): the first type's prices are the dish's; a further type's add to it, or are Free.
  • MRP: beside a dish's price, tap MRP -, type the dish's MRP and press Enter; empty the box to clear it. It is used for one thing: a bill given free (NC) is valued at it in the stock (the Consumption report, A11.9), never in sales or tax. A dish with none shows a dash, never a zero, and the price is never put in for you. A dish sold by variation has an MRP for each choice of its first type, typed on the variations form beside its price; a further type has none. The owner, an Admin, the GM and the kitchen manager set it, as they set prices (D27-373).
  • Sides: groups of options linked dish by dish, with how many a guest may choose.
  • Take off a dish until a time (“out of paneer”): the pad shows it, and refuses it, until then.
  • Recipes (what each dish, size, side and add-on takes from the kitchen store) are not kept here: they are in Inventory, Restaurant, Recipes (A9.11). A dish with no recipe sells as before and takes nothing.
  • Promotions and coupons: Add a promotion: a code, a name, a percentage or an amount off. Tick A coupon the guest brings to give it From and Until days, how many Bills it may go on and a Least bill, ₹ (blank: no limit, any bill). A coupon is never a button on the Till: it is typed from the guest's code (A8.7). The list shows each coupon's days and how many of its uses are gone. A coupon cannot take off more than its least bill.

Profit per dish

The owner, an Admin and the GM have a third tab, Profit per dish. A dish's cost is its recipe (A9.11) at each Store item's average cost today; its margin is the menu price less that cost, and the margin %. A dish sold by size is a row for each size. A dish with no recipe, or with an ingredient nobody has priced yet (an ingredient has no cost), shows a dash, never a zero: it has no cost yet. Under it, What was sold: for the days chosen, the dishes on paid bills, how many, their sales at the price sold (before the bill's discount), their cost and margin, with the total margin of the dishes that have a cost and what was sold of those that have none. NC, voided and unpaid bills are not sales.

The Add-ons tab

  • The numbered list: number, name, what it is, price or Free. Change (never the number), Off for a while, Switch off / Bring back. A number is never given to a second add-on while the first is in use.
  • Custom add-ons used: what staff typed in the last 30 days, most used first, with who. Number it opens a new numbered add-on with its name and price filled in.

A8.12Your shift in short

WhenDoSection
The first day onlyCount the first float: Close restaurant day, Open the day.A8.9
Before serviceCheck the printing lines are grey. Open the Kitchen screen on the kitchen's and the bar's computers.A8.4
A table sits downTables, tap the table, tap the dishes, Send.A8.2
Something extraCustomise: a number, or a Custom add-on.A8.3
A dish is readyCarry it out; tap “ready” on the table's tile.A8.5
The guest asks for the billThe printer under the table: INTERIM BILL.A8.6
The guest paysThe Till: Cash, Card, UPI, Charge to room, or two ways. Print the bill if asked.A8.7
The guests leaveTables: Clear.A8.2
Money that was not a saleClose restaurant day, Cash, Record.A8.9
End of the shiftSettle or close every bill, clear the tables, count the drawer, write why if it differs, keep the float, Close.A8.9

A8.13Trying it without a KOT printer

On the test computer only, two virtual printers stand in for real ones, so everything in this chapter can be tried with no printer: “Virtual Kitchen” prints Kitchen KOTs, and “Virtual Bar” prints Bar KOTs and the bills, onto a page instead of paper (Figures A8-09, A8-14 and A8-19 were printed this way). They are a testing tool kept on that computer only: they are never part of the live system, and they cannot reach it. How to start them is in .local/virtual-printer/README.md on that computer.

Chapter A9

Stores and purchasing

For the Inventory Manager, the kitchen manager and the managers who approve. How the stores and suppliers are set up, how a thing is added to the Store, received, issued, moved and counted, how something is asked for, approved, ordered and delivered, and how equipment is registered and taken out of the store.

A9.1The Store and equipment screens

These screens sit in the menu's Store and equipment section. You see the ones your role uses.

ScreenWho uses itWhat it is for
StoreThe Inventory Manager, the kitchen manager; managers; others look onlyWhat the property keeps (rice, gas, linen, soap) and where it is: deliveries, issues, moves, counts. Two views: Shelf and Days.
EquipmentThe Inventory Manager; anybody who can see it may askThe register of durable things: an AC, a TV, a fridge, a kettle. Where each one is, its repairs, and taking it out of the store.
Places and suppliersThe Inventory Manager and managersThe stores and the other places things stand, and who the property buys from.
PurchasingWhoever may ask to buy; the GM approves. Bar bills: the owner, an Admin, the GM, the Inventory Manager, the bar managerRestaurant and hotel: ask for something, get it approved, order it, record the delivery into a store; Who may ask to buy is its setting. Bar: record a bar bill as printed, with its photo (A9.11). Supplier dues: what is owed to suppliers, and paying it - the Accountant, the GM, the owner and an Admin only (A9.11).
InventoryThe Inventory Manager; whoever sees the Store reads itBar: the bar's day - today's sheet and its count, the bills, the set up; the same as Bar stock in the Restaurant menu (A9.11). Restaurant: the kitchen store's day - today's sheet and its count - and the recipes every KOT takes (A9.11).

The Inventory Manager's menu is Store, Equipment and Purchasing, and they land on the Store after signing in. Places and suppliers is not on that short menu: type “supplier” or “places” in Find a screen (A0).

Who may do what in the Store

ToWho
See the StoreThe owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager, the Inventory Manager, the kitchen manager, the chef, housekeeping, the accountant, a viewer.
Add an item, receive, issue, record waste or a return, move to another storeThe owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager, the Inventory Manager, the kitchen manager.
Correct the count, count a store, set levels, undoThe owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager, the Inventory Manager.

Somebody who may only look sees one line, “You can see the store. Receiving, issuing and adding items is for the Inventory Manager, hotel manager or GM.”, and a History button on each item.

A9.2Places and suppliers

Before anything can be received, the property needs its stores; before anything can be ordered, a supplier. Both are set up once, here.

To add a place

  1. Tap Add a place.
  2. Type its Name (“Main store”) and choose its Kind: Store - stock is kept here, Kitchen, Bar, Restaurant, Public area, Office or Other.
  3. Tap Add.

Rooms are already known; they are not added here. Tap a place to rename it, or to Switch off one no longer used.

To add a supplier

  1. Tap Add a supplier. “Only the name is needed now.”
  2. Type the Name. Add the Person to call, Phone, Email, GSTIN, Address and a Note if you have them.
  3. Tap Add.

Watch out

  • Adding and changing places and suppliers is for the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager and the Inventory Manager. Everybody else reads them.
  • Two suppliers, or two places, cannot have the same name: “There is already a supplier called … here.”
  • Nothing is deleted. Switch it off: stock was kept there, and deliveries came from them.

Why it works this way

Who may add places and suppliers: D17-1. The Store, Equipment and Purchasing all read the same places and suppliers, so a supplier is typed once.

A9.3Adding something to the Store

An item is a thing the property keeps and counts. It has no price: a delivery has a price (A9.4).

  1. On the Store, tap Add an item.
  2. Type What is it (“Basmati rice”) and what it is Counted in: kg, litre, piece, cylinder.
  3. Choose Where it belongs: Kitchen, Bar, Housekeeping, Maintenance or Everything else. Nothing is chosen for you.
  4. For cups, plates and cutlery, tick Crockery or cutlery - in use at an outlet until it breaks (A9.8).
  5. If you want a warning when it runs low, type Warn me below, in the Main store. Leave it blank for no warning.
  6. Tap Add. The message says “Receiving a delivery is what gives it a quantity and a value.”

Watch out

  • A name already in the Store is not added twice. Adding it again changes that item: its unit, where it belongs and its Main store level. Only those who may correct counts can do that.
  • Zero is not “no warning”. Zero means warn me when it has run out, which is too late.
  • The kitchen manager adds items without a level. Levels are set by those who correct counts (A9.7).
  • Import adds a list of items from a file.

A9.4Receiving a delivery

A delivery is where the quantity and the cost come from. Record it when the goods arrive, with the bill in your hand.

  1. On the item, tap Receive.
  2. Choose Which store it went into, and type How many.
  3. Type What it cost, per kg, before GST. If it was free, tick Free - it cost nothing. If the bill has not come, leave the cost blank.
  4. From the bill, choose the GST rate, %. The GST amount is worked out for you; change it to what the bill says. Say whether Can this GST be claimed? is Yes or No.
  5. Add the Use by date if it has one, Who from, and the Delivery note or bill number.
  6. Tap Receive.

Watch out

  • A cost cannot be added later. A delivery received with no cost can only be priced by undoing it (A9.7) and receiving it again. A blank is better than a guess.
  • The GST is all three or none: the rate, the amount and claimable. With only one or two, Receive stays grey.
  • Only a store that is switched on takes a delivery.
  • An item held with no cost at all is counted on the Not valued tile (A9.5).

Why it works this way

An item has no price because the same rice costs differently in June and October; what the shelf is worth is the running average of what was actually paid, and a blank cost is a dash, never a zero. The cost before GST, then the bill's rate, amount and claimable: D27-238, D27-242.

A9.5Reading the Shelf

Shelf is the Store as it stands: each item, what is on hand, and what it is worth. Under the heading, the number of items and what the shelf is worth in all.

The tiles

TileCounts the items that
Below levelAre at or below their level in a store (A9.7).
Run outHad some, and hold none now.
Received today, Issued todayCame in, or went out, today.
Wasted todayWere wasted, or broken (crockery), today.
Awaiting deliveryAre on an order sent to a supplier and not delivered (A9.11).
Not valuedAre held, but no delivery of them had a cost.
Not counted in 30 daysAre held in a place where they were never counted, or not for 30 days (A9.9).

A tile with a job in it (Below level, Run out, Not valued, Not counted) turns yellow.

Choose one store in the Store picker and each card shows only what is in that store.

A9.6Issuing

Stock given out of a store, to the kitchen, the bar or a floor, is an issue. It needs nobody's approval.

  1. On the item, tap Issue.
  2. Check Which store it comes from. Each store shows what it holds.
  3. Type How many.
  4. Choose Which outlet it went to, or Not an outlet for housekeeping or a floor.
  5. Type the Department if you use one (“Kitchen”, “Banquets”), and Why: where it went.
  6. Tap Issue.

Watch out

  • The outlet is chosen every time. Issue stays grey until you choose one, or Not an outlet.
  • An issue cannot take more than that store holds. With nothing on hand, Issue is grey: “Nothing on hand to issue - receive a delivery first.”
  • The Store needs the connection. With none, it says so and records nothing.

Why it works this way

Every issue says which outlet it went to: D22-20. That is what the Days view adds up per outlet (A9.10). The department is free text: D27-242. Stock going out of a store needs no approval; equipment does (A9.13): S12.

A9.7More: waste, returns, moves, levels and history

In MoreWhat it does
WasteTakes spoiled stock off a store, with why. Somebody will ask at the end of the month.
Return to supplierTakes stock off that went back: Who it goes back to and why (damaged, the wrong thing, more than was ordered).
Move to another storeFrom one store to another, such as the Main store to the Kitchen store. Needs nobody's approval.
Correct the countFor one store: type what the shelf holds now. The difference is recorded. To count a whole store, use Count a store (A9.9).
Set levelsThe level for each store at which to warn.
HistoryEvery movement of the item, newest first, with Undo.

To move stock to another store

  1. In More, tap Move to another store.
  2. Choose From and To, type How many and, if you like, Why.
  3. Tap Move.

History, and undoing a mistake

Nothing in the Store is edited. A wrong entry is undone: a new row takes it back, and both rows stay on the history.

  1. In More, tap History.
  2. Find the wrong row and tap its undo arrow.
  3. It asks first, for example “Undo this issue of 10 kg?”. Tap Undo issue, or Cancel.
  4. Then record it again, correctly.

To set the levels

  1. In More, tap Set levels.
  2. For each store, type the figure at which to warn. “Warn when a store holds this many kg or fewer. Blank is no warning, not zero.”
  3. Tap Save. The card then reads “Warn at Main 20 · Kitchen 4”.

When a store is at or below its level, the item is on the Below level tile and its card says so in yellow, for example “Kitchen store: 4 kg, level 4” (Figure A9-20). It only warns: buying is done in Purchasing (A9.11).

Watch out

  • Correct the count, Set levels and Undo are for the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager and the Inventory Manager. Others see who may.
  • An undo that would leave less than nothing in that store is refused: some of it has already gone out. Correct the count instead.
  • Undoing a move takes back both halves, in both stores.
  • A delivery's Use by date shows in History.

Why it works this way

On hand is added up from the movements every time, so nobody can type over it; a mistake is undone by its own row, and the store's past stays as it was. Levels per store, set by those who correct counts; the warning only shows: D25-12, D25-13, D25-14.

A9.8Gas cylinders, crockery and cutlery

Gas cylinders

An item counted in “cylinder” is kept as Full and Empty, because the supplier swaps empties for full ones and holds a deposit on each.

  • Receive also asks Empties the supplier took back.
  • Issue also asks Empties back from the kitchen.
  • Both are typed every time. 0 is an answer: “0 if none came back.”
  • In More, Set levels and deposit also holds Cylinders on deposit with the supplier and the Deposit per cylinder, as on the supplier's receipt. A dash until typed.

In use at the kitchen is the cylinders on deposit less the full and empty ones in the stores. If the stores hold more than is on deposit, the line says to check the count or the deposit.

Crockery and cutlery

An item ticked Crockery or cutlery can be moved into use at a restaurant, bar or kitchen place (set up in Places and suppliers): its More menu says Move into use, or to another store. It has a level there, and it is counted there. When it breaks, record it:

  1. In More, tap Broken.
  2. Choose Where it broke, type How many.
  3. Choose Who broke it: a person working here, or Not known. Nothing is chosen for you.
  4. Type Why (dropped, chipped, cracked in the wash) and tap Record breakage.

Watch out

  • Breakage is for crockery and cutlery only. Anything else that is lost is Waste.
  • Undoing an issue of cylinders does not undo the empties that came back with it: each is undone on its own line in History.
  • Empties stay in the store the full cylinder left from. The count corrects them (A9.9).

Why it works this way

Full and empty, empties typed each time, the deposit typed on the item: D17-4, D25-18, D25-19. Crockery in use at an outlet, breakage with who or Not known, and a reminder when a place goes 30 days uncounted: D27-238, D27-242.

A9.9Counting a store

A count compares what is really on the shelves with what the system says (the book), store by store.

  1. On the Store, tap Count a store, and choose the Store.
  2. Tap Print the sheet. The paper has each item, its unit and an empty box. It has no book figure: you write what is there.
  3. Count the shelves. Then type the counts in straight away.
  4. When you type a count, the line shows the book and the difference, such as “Book 4 kg · 1 fewer”. Where it differs, type Why, if known.
  5. Tap Save the count.

A drink with a bottle size (the bar's, A9.11) has two boxes: the full bottles, and the ml in the open one. Five full and 400 ml of a 750 ml bottle is one figure; the book shows in the same words, such as “Book 5 bottles + 630 ml · 0 bottles + 230 ml fewer”. The Store's cards show a drink the same way: “Bar 5 + 630 ml”.

  • Each difference is saved as a correction with your name and “Count of Kitchen store”, plus the reason typed on its line.
  • A line left blank is not counted. It is never taken as zero.
  • A cylinder item has a second line, “- empty”, for its empties.
  • At a place where crockery is in use, the sheet lists the crockery only.

Watch out

  • The store is not locked while you count. If an item moved in that store after the sheet opened, the save is refused and names it. That line takes the new book with its count cleared: count it again and save.
  • Count a store is for the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager and the Inventory Manager.

Why it works this way

No lock, a blank sheet, the book shown only after the count is typed, whoever saves it, a blank line never zero: D25-15, D25-16, D25-17. A blank sheet makes the counter look at the shelf, not at the figure the system expects.

A9.10The Days view

Days shows fourteen business days of the Store, ending today: one row per item, one column per day.

  • A cell is what came in (green, +) over what went out, in the item's unit. Blank: nothing moved.
  • With All stores, a move between stores is left out: it is not in or out of the property.
  • The footer's rupees are at the running average. Wasted ₹ is waste only, not breakage.
  • Tap an item's cell in today's column to Receive or Issue it.
  • The tiles and the Store picker work as on the Shelf.

By Outlet, each outlet's cell shows what was issued to it; for those who may read reports, also what the outlet sold and the food cost %, both before GST. For anybody else those two are a dash: “Issued to each outlet. What it sold is for those who read reports.”

Why it works this way

The tiles, the fourteen days, Receive and Issue from today, the outlet view: D27-238. Sales only for those who read reports, and the food cost % as costs before GST over sales before GST: D27-242.

A9.11Buying something: Purchasing

Purchasing has two tabs: Restaurant and hotel, described first, and Bar, for the bar's bills (below). On Restaurant and hotel, a purchase goes through five stages, each shown on the order as its state:

StateWhat happens next
Waiting for approvalThe general manager approves, refuses or sends it back.
Ready to orderApproved. Every line needs an agreed price, then Send the order.
OrderedSent to the supplier. When the goods come, Record the delivery.
DeliveredReceived into the store. Done.
Refused, Sent back, CancelledIt stops here, on the record. To go ahead, raise a new request.

To ask to buy something

  1. Open Purchasing and tap Ask to buy.
  2. Choose Which store is it for: where the goods will go.
  3. Type What is it for. The general manager reads this before approving.
  4. Under What is needed, pick the item and type how much. Type the price only if one has been agreed; tick Free if it costs nothing. Add another item for more lines.
  5. Tap Send for approval. The message says it is with the general manager to approve.

The general manager decides

  1. Open the order (from Purchasing, or the Approvals inbox, A12).
  2. Read what it is for, the lines and the Total.
  3. Tap Approve this purchase. Or Refuse, or Send back for something to be cleared up: both ask you to say why, for the person who asked.

Sending the order

  1. Open the approved order. It says Ready to order.
  2. If a line has no agreed price, type it on the line. Send the order appears only when every line has one.
  3. Tap Send the order, choose Order it from, and tap Send the order.
  4. Tap Download the order: a PDF. Print it, or attach it to a message to the supplier. Nothing is sent automatically.

When the goods come

  1. Open the order. It says Ordered. Tap Record the delivery.
  2. For each line, type what Came and what it cost each, before GST. Then the bill's GST %, the GST amount, Claimable, and the Use by date if it has one.
  3. Type Anything to note: a short delivery, a damaged case, a different brand.
  4. If the goods came on credit - the supplier is paid later - tick On credit - the supplier's bill is paid later and type the supplier's Bill number, the Bill date, the Amount, as printed and the date it is Due on (filled with the bill date + 30 days; change it to what the bill says). The bill goes on Supplier dues (below).
  5. Tap Record the delivery. The goods land in the order's store, as a delivery in the Store (A9.4).

The delivered order then says, under the note, “On credit: bill … due …” and whether it is paid yet.

Watch out

  • No price is invented. A line with no agreed price reads “-”, never 0, and the order cannot be sent to a supplier until every line has one. An order with an unpriced line has no total.
  • Only items already in the Store can be asked for. Add the item first (A9.3).
  • The price can be typed until the order is sent; after that it is fixed.
  • One delivery per order. If less came, type what came: both the order and what came stay on the record.
  • A gas cylinder's delivery here does not ask for empties. Correct them on the Store's count.
  • Cancel works until it is delivered, and asks why.
  • A bill on credit needs all four: its number, its date (not in the future), its amount (more than zero, as printed) and its due date (on its own date or later). A missing one is refused and nothing is received.
  • The Inventory Manager records the supplier's bill on the delivery, but does not see Supplier dues or pay it.

The bar's bills

A bill for the bar is recorded as printed, with no approval: the bill has already come. Its bottles go into the Bar store at once, so the bar's stock is right from the moment the bill is saved. The owner, an Admin, the GM, the Inventory Manager and the bar manager (the Bar role) record them; whoever sees Purchasing or Bar stock can read them.

  1. Open Bar stock in the Restaurant menu, tap Bills, then Record a bar bill. (Or Purchasing, Bar.)
  2. Pick the Supplier from the hotel's list (a new one is added first in Places and suppliers, so one supplier never becomes two by spelling), type the Bill number as printed, the Bill date and the T.P. number (the transport permit, if the bill has one).
  3. Photo of the bill: take it with the phone's camera, or pick a file.
  4. For each line of the bill, pick the drink from the bar's list. A drink the list does not have yet: Add another drink…, then its brand as on the bill, its size in ml (a NIP is 180) and what it is counted in (bottle, can, packet, piece). It joins the bar's list.
  5. Type the line as printed: Bottles a case (48 NIPs, 12 beers of 650 ml; filled in from the drink's last bill), the Cases, any Loose bottles, the MRP and the Rate a case. The Amount works itself out: the rate for each case, and a case's share of it for each loose bottle. Add a drink for the next line.
  6. Type the Handling charges, the TCS and the Total, as printed. The line under them says what the lines, handling and TCS make, and “matches the bill”, or how much more or less it is.
  7. If the bill is on credit, tick On credit - the bill is paid later and check the date it is Due on (filled with the bill date + 30 days). Its number, date and total go on Supplier dues (below).
  8. Tap Save the bill.

The bill shows under Bills as printed: the supplier, its number, date and T.P. number, its total; each line's drink and MRP, cases and loose bottles at the rate a case, and the amount; the handling and the TCS; who recorded it. Photo of the bill opens the photo. The bottles are in the Store, in the Bar store, each at the line's amount over its bottles, each delivery's line naming the bill.

Watch out

  • A bill the lines do not make is refused, saying both figures: “The lines, handling and TCS make ₹8,000.00; the bill says ₹9,000.00. Check the cases, the rates and the charges against the bill.” Up to ₹1 apart is the bill's round-off, and saves.
  • The same bill twice is refused: “Bill A-1021 from Amit Traders is already recorded.”
  • A drink already on the Store's list is picked, not added again: “"Romanov Vodka 180 ml" is already on the store's list. Pick it instead.”
  • Every line needs its rate a case as on the bill; zero is an answer, a blank is not. A bill is not dated in the future.
  • A wrong line is undone in the Store, from the drink's History (A9.7), as any delivery is.
  • A bill on credit shows “On credit, due …” under its lines, and “not paid yet” or the day it was paid.

Supplier dues: what we owe suppliers

The Supplier dues tab of Purchasing, and Supplier dues in the Finance menu, list every bill taken on credit - from a delivery or a bar bill - with something still to pay. Each supplier has its bills (number, the order or "bar bill" it came from, bill date, due date, amount and what is Left, marked Part-paid once something is paid), its total and a link to its Statement (A11.6); the total owed to all of them is at the top. A bill past its due date is in red, with “overdue”. The Accountant, the GM, the owner and an Admin see it and use it; nobody else sees it (D27-370, D27-372).

To pay all or part of a bill:

  1. On the bill, tap Record payment.
  2. The Amount paid is filled with what is left; type less to pay a part.
  3. Pick How: Cash, Cheque, Bank transfer or UPI. For a cheque, a bank transfer or UPI the Reference (cheque, UTR or UPI number) is needed; for cash it may be left empty. Check Paid on, and type who Handed over the money or cheque.
  4. If TDS was deducted, tick TDS deducted and type its Section (194C, 194Q, 194J or 194I), Rate, % and TDS amount. The Accountant decides whether TDS applies; the system works nothing out. The supplier is paid the rest, and the payment and its TDS together come off the bill.
  5. Tap Record payment. When nothing is left, the bill leaves the list.

A credit note lowers what is owed, money only: Credit note on a bill, or beside the supplier's name for one not against a bill. Say whose note it is (the supplier's, or ours), its number, date, amount and what it is for. Goods sent back leave the store as a store movement, separately.

A mistake is never changed or deleted: Reverse a bill, a payment or a credit note and say why. Both stay on the record, with who did it. Reversing a wrong bill can carry the right one (its number, date, amount and due date), which then replaces it.

Watch out

  • A payment is never more than what is left on the bill, nor dated in the future or before the bill.
  • Nothing changes in a cash drawer or a shift: the payment is a record of what was paid.
  • A bill, payment or credit note is put right only by Reverse, with a reason.
  • What was owed on a date and the payments made are in the Supplier dues report; one supplier's ledger in the Supplier statement; TDS by section in TDS on suppliers (A11.6).

The bar's day: Bar stock

Bar stock, in the Restaurant menu after Kitchen, is the bar's one place. It has four parts: Today's sheet, Requests, Bills (above) and Set up. It is the bar manager's (the Bar role), the GM's, the owner's and an Admin's. The same parts are the Bar tab of Inventory, in Store and equipment, for the Inventory Manager; whoever sees the Store can read them.

The bar has two places, as on paper:

  • The Bar store, the godown: the supplier's bills go in here, and only sealed NIPs, bottles and packets are kept, counted whole.
  • The Bar counter: what is being sold. Every KOT sent takes from here, and the open bottle is counted in ml.

The counter asks the store for stock, and the GM or the Inventory Manager approves; approving moves it.

Bar stock is a switch for each property, in Admin, Properties (A17.14): on at every hotel open before release 14 unless the owner or an Admin turns it off; a hotel added since starts with it off until they turn it on. Off, none of this part is offered, KOTs take nothing off the bar's stock and the night audit does not wait for a bar count.

Set up: the bar's drinks

Each drink is on the bar's list once for each bottle size: Blenders Pride 180 ml and Blenders Pride 750 ml are two. The GM, the Inventory Manager, the owner and an Admin keep the list; the bar manager reads it.

  1. Open Bar stock, tap Set up, then Add a drink (or Change on one).
  2. Type its Name, and pick Counted as:
    • NIPs or bottles, poured in pegs: hard liquor and wine. Whole in the store; at the counter, the sealed ones and the open one's ml.
    • Whole bottles (beer): counted in bottles everywhere.
    • Packets, and loose ones (cigarettes): whole packets in the store; at the counter, packets and the open packet's sticks. Type How many in a packet.
  3. For liquor: its Bottle size, ml, its Kind of liquor (Whisky, Rum, Vodka, Gin, Brandy, Wine, Beer strong or mild...), the Brand, as the register names it, and Imported if it is not Indian made. These place it in the excise registers. Cigarettes and soft drinks are Not liquor, and stay out of them.
  4. Tap Save. A drink on a bar bill that is not on the list yet joins it the same way (above).

Set up: what each drink takes

Each bar dish, and each of its sizes, says what it takes from the Bar counter: a 30, 60 or 90 ml peg takes that many ml of the brand's NIP, a NIP one whole NIP, a beer one bottle. Once that is saved, every KOT sent takes it off the counter, from whichever screen sent it: the Till, the Terminal, a waiter's phone, or a guest's order accepted.

  1. Under What each drink takes from the bar, every dish in a section taxed as bar or alcohol is listed, with each size.
  2. Where the names match, a suggestion is ready: tap Use the … suggestions to fill them all, and check them.
  3. For the rest, pick the NIP or bottle each is poured from, type how much, and choose ml of it or whole.
  4. Tap Save. A dish left on Nothing set takes nothing, and the Bar stock report lists it.

How the daily sheet looks, at the top of Set up, is the owner's, an Admin's or the GM's choice: Like the paper register or Simple. It changes only how the counter's sheet is laid out.

The counter asks the store: Requests

When the counter runs low, the bar manager asks the store for whole NIPs, bottles or packets. The GM or the Inventory Manager (the owner or an Admin too) approves; approving moves them from the Bar store to the Bar counter. Nobody approves their own request.

  1. Open Bar stock, tap Requests.
  2. Under Ask the store, pick a drink (the list says what the store has) and type how many; Another drink for the next. A note if you like.
  3. Tap Ask the store. It waits, marked Waiting, with what the store holds of each.
  4. The GM or the Inventory Manager taps Approve and move, or Reject with a reason the counter reads.

Every day: the sheet, the closing count and the morning count

Today's sheet is the bar register: one line for each drink, under its menu section, for the hotel's business day. Pick the place at the top: Bar counter or Bar store.

ColumnWhat it says
Opening (Nip, ML)What the place held when the day began: full NIPs, and the ml of the open one. A beer or a packet shows its count.
RecdThe counter: what came from the store. The store: what came on the day's bar bills.
Total (Nip, ML)Opening and received together.
Sell (Nip, 30, 60, 90, ML)The counter: what each KOT sent took, the NIPs sold whole, how many 30, 60 and 90 ml pegs, and the ml of all the pegs. The store's sheet shows what it sent to the counter instead.
Other movesThe store's sheet, and the Simple one: breakages, wastage, count corrections and anything else that left or came, so every row adds up: opening + received - sold or sent to the counter + other moves = closing. The paper layout has no such column, as the paper has none; the Bar stock report shows them for both places.
Closing (Nip, ML)What the place holds by the book at the end of the day.
Rate, AmountThe counter: the menu price of the dish that takes one whole bottle, and what the day's lines of the drink were billed.
Counted, DifferenceThe closing count, and how far it is from the book.
MorningThe morning count's difference from the book: anything but “matches” moved overnight, in red.

Before the night audit, the bar manager counts both places:

  1. Open Bar stock. Today's sheet opens on the business day, on the Bar counter, with Closing count chosen.
  2. For each drink counted, type the full NIPs and the ml in the open one under Counted; a beer, its bottles; cigarettes, the packets and the loose sticks. A line left blank is not counted, never taken as zero.
  3. The Difference shows as you type. Tap Save the closing count; a difference is saved as a count correction against your name.
  4. Tap Bar store and count it the same way, in whole NIPs, bottles and packets.

The night audit waits for it: a day with bar drinks cannot be closed until the counter and the store are counted, each drink that holds stock or moved that day, after its last move. If the bar did not open, the GM taps The bar did not open today on the sheet, types why, and taps Mark the bar closed today; The bar opened takes it back.

In the morning, before the first KOT, the bar manager taps Morning count, counts the counter (and the store, if its key is with them) and taps Save the morning count. Nothing should have moved since the night's count: a difference shows in red in Morning, and on the day's Bar stock report for the GM.

The excise registers

The GM and the Inventory Manager print the registers the excise department asks for, laid out like the paper books, from the sheet's buttons for its day (FLR-1A/2A/3A for the day, FLR-3 for its month), or from Reports (A11.9):

  • FORM F.L.R.-1A / 2A / 3A, the day: one row per brand under its kind, with Opening Balance, Receipts, Sales and Closing Balance for each bottle size, and the T.P. No. of the day's bills.
  • FORM F.L.R.-3, the month: a row per day of Received (with the Permit No.), Sold and Closing Balance, by spirits imported and Indian made, wines, fermented and mild liquor, and each size; at the foot Opening, Received, Grand total, Less sold, Less breakages and Closing balance.

Both count whole bottles, the store and the counter together. A NIP poured as pegs counts as sold the day it is opened: the counter's open bottle is not in the closing balance. Sales are what the paper writes: opening + receipts - breakages - closing.

The day's figures are also the Bar stock report (A11.9). It can be emailed after each night audit (A17.12).

Watch out

  • A drink is taken off when its KOT is sent, not when the bill is paid, and from the counter. Struck after the bar had it, it stays off, as poured, and the report lists it.
  • A counter with nothing moved to it goes below zero as KOTs are sent: ask the store in time.
  • The store short of a drink: “The store is short: Blenders Pride 180 ml (the store has 2, 5 asked). Nothing was moved.” Reject it, and ask again for what is there.
  • The open one's ml is under its size: “Imperial Blue 180 ml: whole NIPs, and the open one's ml under 180.”
  • If a drink moved after the sheet was opened (a KOT sent), the count is refused and names it: count it again.
  • A drink with no kind of liquor set is not in the registers; one with no bottle size goes under “size not set”.

Why it works this way

The GM approves every purchase, at any amount: D18-4, D17-35. The order is a PDF sent by hand: D18-3. One Approvals inbox, with the screens keeping their own buttons: D18-19. The bar's bills, recorded directly with a photo; the bar in bottles and ml, the stock off when the KOT is sent, a daily count, the Bar stock report and its email: D27-354. The bar like the paper register: all spirits as NIPs, both sheet layouts as a setting, bills as printed, one Bar stock page in the Restaurant menu for the bar manager, the GM, the owner and an Admin: D27-356. The Rate column, the ₹1 round-off, Set up read by the bar manager: D27-357. Two places, the store and the counter; the counter asks and the GM or the Inventory Manager approves; counted three ways; the night audit waits for the closing count, the GM may mark the bar closed; the morning count; FLR-1A/2A/3A and FLR-3 like the paper, a NIP sold the day it is opened: D27-361. Bar stock as a switch for each property, fully off when off: D27-367. Other moves on the store's sheet and the Simple one, so each row adds up: D27-364. GST and use-by at delivery: D27-238.

The kitchen's day: Inventory, Restaurant

The Restaurant tab of Inventory is the kitchen's stock, the way Bar stock is the bar's. It has two parts: Today's sheet and Recipes. The owner, an Admin, the GM and the Inventory Manager keep it: they set the recipes, count, and change which store is the kitchen's. Whoever sees the Store reads it. The kitchen manager and the chef open the same two parts as Kitchen stock in their Restaurant menu, after Kitchen, to read.

Which store is the kitchen's. Each hotel's Kitchen store is the kitchen's from this release, and a new hotel's from the day it is added. Its name is beside Change on the sheet; Change picks another store, and Mark it the kitchen's saves it. A hotel with no store called Kitchen store picks one the same way; until one is picked, a KOT takes nothing. The Bar store and the Bar counter are never the kitchen's.

Recipes: what each dish takes

A recipe says what one of a dish takes from the kitchen store, in each Store item's own unit: Paneer Tikka takes Paneer 0.1 kg and Butter 0.01 kg. Once it is saved, every KOT sent takes it off the kitchen store, from whichever screen sent it.

  • A size (a variation), a side and a numbered add-on have lines of their own, taken on top of the dish's. Left empty, they take nothing extra: Paneer Tikka (Full) may add another 0.1 kg of paneer, and (Half) nothing.
  • A dish with no recipe sells as before and takes nothing. The Recipes part lists every such dish at the top, so none is forgotten.
  • A custom add-on typed at the table has no recipe and takes nothing.
  1. Open Inventory, tap Restaurant, then Recipes. The food on the menu is listed by section, each size under its dish, then the sides and the add-ons. Find a dish narrows it.
  2. Tap Edit beside one. Tap Add an ingredient, pick the Store item and type how much one takes, in the unit shown beside it. Add as many lines as it needs; the cross takes one off.
  3. Tap Save. Saved with no line, it takes nothing.

Every day: the kitchen's sheet and its closing count

Today's sheet shows the kitchen store's business day, one line for each item it holds, moved or is in a recipe. Pick another Day to read an earlier one.

ColumnWhat it says
OpeningWhat the kitchen store held when the day began.
ReceivedDeliveries straight into it.
Moved in, Moved outMoves from and to the other stores, and issues, returns and breakages recorded in the Store.
Used by KOTsWhat the recipes of the dishes sent took.
WastageWaste recorded in the Store, and every dish struck after its KOT. The reasons are listed under the sheet.
CorrectedWhat the day's counts put right.
ClosingWhat it holds by the book: opening + received + moved in - moved out - used - wastage + corrected. Below zero, it is red.
Counted, DifferenceThe closing count, and how far it was from the book.
  1. At the end of the day, open Inventory, Restaurant. Today's sheet opens on the business day.
  2. Type the count of each item counted under Counted, in its unit. A line left blank is not counted, never taken as zero. The Difference shows as you type.
  3. Tap Save the closing count. A difference is saved as a count correction against your name.

Watch out

  • A recipe is taken off when its KOT is sent, not when the bill is paid. A KOT always goes: an item the store does not have goes below zero and shows red, until a delivery or a count puts it right.
  • A dish struck before its KOT took nothing, so nothing comes back. Struck after (or made fewer), what it took stays used and shows as wastage, with the strike's reason: “Struck after the KOT: guest left”.
  • A bill voided after it was paid does not give its ingredients back: the food was made.
  • Bar stock switched off (A17.14) does not switch the kitchen off.
  • If an item moved after the sheet was opened (a KOT sent), the count is refused and names it: count it again.

Why it works this way

Inventory's Restaurant tab, the kitchen store's daily sheet and recipes taken by every KOT: D27-373. No recipe takes nothing and is listed; sizes and add-ons have their own lines; a KOT always goes, below zero in red; struck before the kitchen had it gives back, after counts as wastage with the reason: D27-374. Each hotel's Kitchen store marked the kitchen's, as the Bar store was; Kitchen stock in the kitchen manager's and the chef's Restaurant menu; recipes and the count the owner's, an Admin's, the GM's and the Inventory Manager's; the night audit does not wait for the kitchen's count; a voided paid bill's ingredients stay used: D27-378.

A9.12Who may ask to buy

Who may ask to buy is a setting for each property, by role. The owner or an Admin changes it: Who may ask on Purchasing. It takes effect at once. Everybody else who opens it can read it.

It starts as the Inventory Manager, the general manager, the owner and an Admin. The general manager still approves every purchase, whoever asked.

Why it works this way

A setting per property, changed without a developer, with the kitchen or housekeeping switched on when the owner wants them: D18-2, D22-11. A role, not a person, because staff leave; switched off, never deleted.

A9.13Equipment

Equipment is the register of everything durable in the hotel, the restaurant and the rooms. Things used up (rice, gas, soap) are the Store's.

To add a piece of equipment

  1. Open Equipment and tap Add an item.
  2. Type What is it (“Split AC 1.5 ton”) and its Category: pick one this property already uses, or type a new one.
  3. Choose How is it kept track of: One by one, with a tag, or A count in one place (twelve kettles in one room is one line of 12).
  4. For a tagged item, the next free Tag is offered. If it already carries a printed label, type that instead.
  5. Choose Where is it: A room, or Another place such as the Main store.
  6. Add the Status, Supplier, Bought on, Cost, in rupees, Warranty ends and Service contract (AMC) ends if you know them. Blank if nobody knows.
  7. Tap Add. Its page opens.

Report a repair raises a repair, as Work orders does (A6): the item shows as under repair until the repair is closed. Under repair, at the top, marks it by hand. Only a tagged item is repaired; a counted line is retired or replaced.

Taking equipment out of the store

A piece of equipment that leaves a store waits for the Inventory Manager's yes. Anybody who can see it may ask.

  1. Open the item. Somebody who may not move equipment sees Ask to take out; tap it. (The Inventory Manager and managers tap Move: out of a store, it is asked for in the same way.)
  2. Choose To a room and the room, or To another place.
  3. Type Why. The person deciding reads it.
  4. Tap Ask. The message says “Asked - it moves when the Inventory Manager approves it”.

The Inventory Manager decides

  1. Open Equipment. At the top: “One request waits in the approvals inbox”, with the item, where it is going, who asked and why. In the list it says Waiting to leave the store.
  2. Tap Approve; or Refuse, which asks why. (The item's own page has the same buttons.)
  3. Approved, it is in its new place. Refused, it stays in the store, with the reason beside it.

Under repair, and retiring

  • Under repair asks What is wrong, or what was done (optional). Back in use undoes it later.
  • Retire asks why (broken beyond repair, lost, sold, given away). It stays in the register as retired, with who, when and why. A tagged item retired by somebody who may not approve, such as the hotel manager, waits in the approvals inbox for the Inventory Manager.

Watch out

  • Changing, moving and retiring equipment is for the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager and the Inventory Manager. Anybody else sees those buttons grey, and may only ask for something to leave the store.
  • While a request waits, the item cannot be changed, moved or retired: it is decided first.
  • A move between rooms, or back into a store, needs nobody's yes.
  • Who did what in an item's history is shown to the owner, an Admin, the GM and the Inventory Manager. Others see a dash, except their own name.
  • A retired item is kept exactly as it was retired. Nothing is deleted.

Why it works this way

Equipment leaving the store waits for the Inventory Manager, with the owner, an Admin or the GM as backup; anybody who can see it may ask; stock goes out with no approval: S12, S15. Retiring a tagged item, in the same inbox: S16. Where a thing is comes from its approved moves, so a refused request leaves it where it was and nothing has to be undone.

A9.14Your week in short

WhenDoSection
OncePlaces and suppliers: the stores, the other places, the suppliers.A9.2
Something new to keepStore, Add an item. A level if you want a warning.A9.3
A delivery arrivesReceive: the store, how many, the cost before GST, the bill's GST, the bill number. Through an order: Record the delivery.A9.4, A9.11
The kitchen or a floor needs stockIssue: the store, how many, the outlet or Not an outlet.A9.6
From the main store to the kitchen'sMore, Move to another store.A9.7
Something spoiled, sent back, brokenMore: Waste, Return to supplier, Broken.A9.7, A9.8
A mistakeMore, History, undo it; then record it again.A9.7
Running lowThe Below level tile. Purchasing, Ask to buy.A9.5, A9.11
ApprovedAgreed prices, Send the order, Download the order, send it by hand.A9.11
Every store, regularlyCount a store: print, count, type, Save the count. Watch the Not counted in 30 days tile.A9.9
Equipment asked out of the storeEquipment: Approve or Refuse.A9.13
Chapter A10

Guests and guest messages

For reception, managers and the owner. Who has stayed, the companies and agents bookings come through, correcting a guest's record, one guest across the whole group (Guest 360) and the same person entered twice, what the system sends to guests by itself, the Guest messages screen and what to do when a message did not go, and asking a guest for a review.

A10.1The Guests & CRM screens

In the Front office menu, the part called Guests & CRM holds everything the system knows about a person rather than a booking. You see the screens your role may open.

ScreenWho sees itWhat it is for
GuestsOwner, Admin, General Manager, Hotel Manager, Reception, Accountant, ViewerEveryone booked at this hotel, grouped by name, with their stays, nights, spend and what they owe (A10.2).
Companies and agentsThe same peopleWhere the bookings came from - booking sites, direct, companies - and what each was worth. Add company, and Edit on each company (A10.4).
Guest messagesThe same peopleWhat the system sent guests and whether it went, the bookings no message can reach, and messages guests wrote to the desk (A10.8).
ReviewsThe same people (only the owner, an Admin, the GM, the Hotel Manager and Reception may ask)Ask a guest who has left for a review; the hotel's review link (A10.10).
Guest 360Owner, Admin, General ManagerOne guest across every hotel of the group: every stay, what they were charged, what was sent to them, the blacklist, offers, loyalty (A10.5).
Possible same personOwner, Admin, General ManagerGuest records that share a phone number or an email: join two that are one person, or say they are not (A10.6).

Reception's own menu shows Guests and Guest messages. Companies and agents and Reviews are reached with Find a screen (Ctrl K, A0), where they read “Not in your menu”. Which messages go out by themselves is set in Settings, under Messages, Guest messages on/off (A10.7).

Why it works this way

One part of the menu for what is known about a person - the guest list, companies and agents, what was sent to them, the reviews asked for - and the CRM's screens joining it as they were built: D21-79. Guest 360 and the same-person list are for the owner, an Admin and the GM only, because a person's whole history across the group is more than any one desk needs: D21-4.

A10.2Guests

Open Guests. Every guest booked at this hotel is one line, put together from their bookings by the name on the booking. Repeat guests come first. The pill beside the heading counts them.

ColumnWhat it shows
GuestThe name. “overlapping stays” under it means two of its stays share a night (see Watch out). A cancelled, voided or no-show booking does not count: a booking entered twice and voided is not a second person: D27-329.
Stays, NightsHow many bookings under the name, future ones included, and how many nights they cover. A cancelled, voided or no-show booking is not a stay and its nights are not counted, as for the overlapping mark: D27-330.
Last stayWhen the last stay ended; “first visit” when none has. “back 14 Dec 2026” under it: they are booked to come again.
Booked viaEvery source their stays came through: Agoda, Walk-in, the hotel's own site…
Total spendWhat their stays were charged. It is worked out as Charged on Guest 360 is, for this hotel only.
BalanceWhat they still owe, in red; what they are owed, in blue; a dash for nothing.

On a narrower screen Booked via is hidden first, then Last stay, then Nights. A row does not open: to correct a guest, use Edit guest (A10.3).

Watch out

  • The list goes by the name typed on the booking. Two people called “Rohan Mehta” are one line; one person typed two ways is two lines. A name with “overlapping stays” is either two people sharing a name or something entered twice: “Shown, not merged - a wrong merge is far harder to undo than a visible duplicate.” To tell one person from another the system uses their phone and email instead (Guest 360 and Possible same person, A10.5 and A10.6).
  • The search finds names only. Nothing found: “No guest by that name”, “Try part of the surname.”
  • A guest appears here the first time they are booked. A guest record is never deleted.

A10.3A guest's record: the marks on a booking, and Edit guest

A guest's own record - name, phone, email, address, nationality, VIP - belongs to the person, not to one booking. It is changed from a booking's panel (open the booking from Arrivals, In house or All bookings), on the line under the guest's name.

  • Mark VIP. Tap it. Where the group has VIP levels, choose which. The message says “Marked VIP”, “… - this holds for their next visit too.” Remove VIP takes it off.
  • Stayed before. A guest who has stayed with the group before carries a blue mark, “Stayed with the group 3 times”. That is all the desk is shown: no hotels, dates or amounts.
  • Agreed to WhatsApp. The voucher goes on WhatsApp only when this is ticked and the booking has a phone number (A10.7). You may tick or untick it at any time; the audit log keeps who did.

To correct a guest

  1. On the booking's panel, tap Edit guest. (The owner, an Admin and the GM also have it on Guest 360, A10.5.)
  2. The window says “The guest's own record: it is the same on every booking of theirs, at every hotel.”
  3. Change what is wrong: Salutation, Full name, Phone, Email, Address, City, State, PIN code, Country, Nationality.
  4. On the booking's panel, under them, are this booking's Company name, GSTIN and Company address (A2.2): “This booking's company. With a GSTIN, its tax invoice is made out to the company; the guest still pays.” Change them here before the tax invoice is issued. They are not on Guest 360: they belong to the booking, not the guest. Only the people who may change a booking see them, and nobody does when the hotel has switched off the Company section in Settings.
  5. Tap Save. It stays grey until something has changed and everything typed is right. The message says “Guest updated”, “A10 Test Ravi Kumar: the change is on every booking of theirs.”

What stops Save, in red under the form: “A guest has a name.”; “"12345" is not a phone number. Type 10 to 15 digits, e.g. +91 98765 43210.”; “"ravi@" is not an email address, e.g. name@example.com.”; “Nationality is a two-letter country code, e.g. IN.”; “"XX" is not a country code. Type the two letters, e.g. IN, GB or US.”; “That GSTIN is not right - a character is mistyped. Check it against the company's GST certificate.”

The booking's panel shows the company under Booked through as Guest's company, with its GSTIN. An invoice already issued keeps the name it printed.

Watch out

  • You are changing the person, not this booking. The new phone or email is on every booking of theirs, at every hotel of the group, and messages go to it from then on. Every change is kept in the audit log.
  • A box emptied is cleared on the record - except Name and Nationality, which a guest always has.
  • A nationality other than IN puts the guest on the Form III register (chapter A3).
  • Only the people who may edit guests see Edit guest, Mark VIP and the WhatsApp tick: the owner, an Admin, the GM, the Hotel Manager and Reception.

Why it works this way

No screen could correct a guest's record until the owner asked for this one, from the booking panel and Guest 360: the owner, 28 September. WhatsApp goes only to a guest who agreed, ticked on each booking: D21-72; the desk may change the tick at any time: the owner, 21 September. The desk sees “stayed with the group before” and nothing more: D21-13.

A10.4Companies and agents

Companies and agents answers “where did the business come from, and what was each worth?”. Three tiles at the top, then one table for each kind of source.

KindWhat it says
Travel agents“Booked through a channel, and charged a commission for it.” Agoda, Booking.com, Expedia and go-MMT.
Direct“Straight to the property. No commission on any of it.” Walk-in and Fidato Hotels.
Corporate accounts“A firm booking for its own people, settled on the city ledger.” Every other source is listed here too - a travel agent added with Add company among them, and a company with no booking at this hotel yet, with 0 bookings and a dash for its revenue.

Each table: Source, Bookings, Room nights, Revenue, Commission, Owed, and Edit on a company for the owner, an Admin and the GM. The heading line of each kind adds up its revenue and bookings. Under the tables: “Commission is charged outside this system today and prints as a dash rather than a zero. It fills once a channel manager is connected.”

To add a company

  1. Tap Add company. The window says “One record for the group: the same company at every hotel.”
  2. Type its Name. Choose its Kind: Corporate or Travel agent.
  3. Type its GSTIN from the company's GST certificate - it prints on the company's tax invoices - and its Billing address, City, State, PIN code.
  4. Optionally the Contact person, Phone, Email.
  5. If the company may pay later, switch on Credit allowed (“A bill may be sent to the company to pay later (Bill to company).”) and type Credit days and Credit limit (₹).
  6. Tap Add company at the foot. The message says “Company added”.

Reception gets a shorter window: Name, GSTIN, Billing address, City, State and PIN code, and the line “Its name, GSTIN and address, for the tax invoice. Credit and contracts are set by the owner, an administrator or the GM.”

To change a company

For the owner, an Admin and the GM; nobody else sees the button. The same window opens from Edit company on a company's Contracts page (A15).

  1. Find the company in its table and tap Edit at the end of its row. A booking site or a source that is not a company, such as Walk-in, has no Edit: those are on Booking sources.
  2. The window is headed Edit company, with the company's details in it. Change what is wrong.
  3. Tap Save. The message says “Company updated”.

A company is one record for the group, so the change is at every hotel at once, on every booking of that company. A tax invoice already issued stays made out to the name, GSTIN and address it was issued to, and a credit note against it repeats them; the next invoice takes the new details. Only the Source line in the stay's details follows the new name when an old invoice is opened or reprinted: it says where the booking came from, not who the invoice is made out to.

What stops it: “A company has a name.”; “A GSTIN is 15 characters: 2 digits, the 10-character PAN, then 3 more, e.g. 27AAPFU0939F1ZV.”; “That GSTIN is not right - a character is mistyped. Check it against the company's GST certificate.”; “A PIN code is 6 digits, e.g. 413216.”; “Credit days is a whole number from 1 to 365.”; “A credit limit is an amount above 0, in rupees.”

Watch out

  • A company is one record for the whole group. The same name or GSTIN twice is refused: “… is already on the list. Edit that company instead.”, “… already has GSTIN …. Edit that company instead.”
  • Credit days and the limit are “Shown, not enforced, until the company's payments are recorded. Blank is not set.”
  • The Hotel Manager, the Accountant and a Viewer see the list but not Add company. Reception adds a company but does not see Edit.
  • This is not Booking sources under Property setup, which is the list a booking's source is picked from, with each one's commission.

Why it works this way

The heading says what the menu says, “Companies and agents”, because it once said “Booking sources” - the name of a different screen: D17-22. Add company here as well as on Contracts, with Reception limited to the name, GSTIN and address and never credit: D27-184. Edit on every company here, the existing window, and who may stays the owner, an Admin and the GM because a company is one record for the group: D27-382.

A10.5Guest 360: one guest, every hotel

For the owner, an Admin and the GM. Guest 360 shows one person across every hotel of the group.

To find a guest

  1. Open Guest 360.
  2. Type two letters of a name, or a whole phone number or email, in Name, phone or email.
  3. Each guest record found is a row: the name, “Blacklisted” if so, the phone and email, and how many times they stayed. Tap the row.

Nobody found: “Nobody found”, “No guest record has that name, phone or email.” The booking panel's Guest 360 link (Figure A10-02) opens the guest's page directly.

To blacklist a guest

  1. On the guest's Guest 360, under Blacklist, type the Reason. “The desk is shown this when they book again. It warns; it never refuses.”
  2. Tap Blacklist. The message says “Blacklisted”, and the guest carries the red “Blacklisted” mark.
  3. To take it off: Clear the blacklist. The message says “Blacklist cleared”.

From then on, typing this guest's phone or email on New booking or a walk-in shows a red line: “Ravi Kumar is blacklisted. Reason: …. The booking is not refused - you decide.” A booking site's guest whose phone or email is a blacklisted guest's is named on Arrivals and in the check-in the same way (chapter A1).

Offers

The Offers card says either “Agreed to offers. They may be sent to this guest's phone and email, at every hotel.” or “No offers are sent: this guest has not said yes.”

  • Record their yes: the guest has said yes to offers.
  • Record "no offers": the guest does not want them. It is listed as “No offers to phone 98765 43210” (or email) with Clear.
  • Both buttons show only when the guest's record has a phone or an email. Rekha Gaikwad's has neither, so Figure A10-08 shows none.
  • The desk asks too, with Guest agreed to offers on New booking (the walk-in too) and at check-in. A later answer replaces an earlier one.

Watch out

  • An ID document is never shown here - only “an ID is on file” or “no ID on file”.
  • The blacklist warns; it never stops a booking or a check-in. A person decides.
  • “Offers” and “no offers” are kept against the phone number and the email themselves, for every hotel of the group - not against one booking.
  • Visits counts the times they checked in, at any hotel; several rooms booked together count once; cancelled, no-show and future bookings do not count. Charged is worked out as Total spend on Guests is, over every hotel.
  • A guest who was joined from two records shows “Joined into this record: …” with Undo a join (A10.6).

Why it works this way
