Guest 360 now, on the PMS's own data: D21-3; for the owner, an Admin and the GM: D21-4. The blacklist is set with a reason by those three and warns the clerk, never blocks: D21-21; a booking site's guest who matches is warned of on Arrivals and at check-in: D22-8. “No offers” is recorded against the phone and email for the whole group: D21-22. Offers only to a guest who said yes: D25-39, D26-6; asked at booking, the walk-in, check-in, the guest's own page and on Guest 360: D26-7.

A10.6The same person twice

A guest is one record for the whole group. The system recognises a returning guest by an exact phone number or email, never by a name, and never joins anyone by itself: a person always confirms.

At booking: “same person?”

On New booking (and the walk-in), as soon as a phone or email matches a guest on file, a grey box appears under them: “A10 Test Ravi Kumar · Has not stayed with the group yet - same person?” (or “Stayed with the group 3 times”). Nothing is offered when something typed disagrees with the guest on file - a different email, say; the two then wait on Possible same person for a manager.

  1. Ask the guest. If it is them, tap Same person. The box then says “- this booking is theirs.” and the booking goes on their record.
  2. Not them? Do nothing, or tap Not them to undo your choice: the booking makes a new guest record, as before.
  3. Typing the phone or email again clears the choice.

The desk sees a name and how many stays, nothing more. A blacklisted match also shows the red line of A10.5.

Possible same person: the old duplicates

Bookings made before this existed made a new record each time, so a returning guest may be two or ten records. Possible same person (owner, Admin, GM) lists every two records that share a phone number or an email, across every hotel. The pill says how many are “to look at”.

To join two records

  1. Open Possible same person. Each card is two records: the name (it opens their Guest 360), VIP or Blacklisted, phone and email, how many stays, the last stay, and “ID on file” or “no ID on file”.
  2. Decide whether they are one person. A family on one mobile, or an agent's number, is two people: see below.
  3. On the record whose name, phone and email should stand, tap Keep this record. It now reads This record stands. If only one of the two has an ID on file, it is chosen already: “Only … has an ID on file, so that record stands and the ID stays with the guest.”
  4. Read the strip: “A10 Test R. Kumar's stays move to A10 Test Ravi Kumar. Nothing is deleted, and it can be undone.” Tap Join into one.
  5. The message says “Joined”, “A10 Test R. Kumar's stays are now A10 Test Ravi Kumar's. It can be undone below.” The join is listed under Joined: “A10 Test R. Kumar joined into A10 Test Ravi Kumar · 1 stay moved · by … · 9 Oct 2026”.

Two people, not one

  1. On the card, tap Not the same person.
  2. The message says “Kept apart”, “… will not be listed again. It can be undone below.” The pair is listed under Not the same person: “A10 Test Ravi Kumar and A10 Test R. Kumar are two people · by … · 9 Oct 2026”.

To undo

Under Joined or Not the same person, tap Undo on the line. The message says “Undone” with “Every stay is back on the record it came from.” or “The two records are listed again.”

Watch out

  • Nothing reads a name. Two records with the same name and different phones are never listed; two different names on one phone are.
  • A join moves the stays; nothing is deleted. A blacklist or VIP on either record stays on the joined guest, and comes off again on undo.
  • An ID document never moves. When both records have one, the one on the record that does not stand stays where it is, for an undo.
  • When unsure, do not join. A wrong join is worse than a missed one.

Why it works this way

Suggested on an exact phone or exact email, a person confirms, every join can be undone, never automatic: D21-2. The same rule at booking - “stayed 3 times - same person?” - and a list of the old duplicates for a manager: D21-20. “Not the same person”, undoable like a join: D22-8.

A10.7What goes out to guests

The system sends a guest only a few messages, each through one sending service. Today:

MessageWhenHow
Booking voucherOnce, when a booking is confirmed. A booking waiting for the hotel sends nothing until it is confirmed.By email where the guest has an email, with the voucher PDF; and on WhatsApp where the booking is ticked Agreed to WhatsApp and has a phone, with the same PDF. Each way is its own message.
The sign-in codeWhen the guest opens their own check-in pageOn WhatsApp to the booking's own phone, or by email to the booking's email: the guest chooses. No switch: it is how a guest gets in.
Tax invoiceWhen an invoice is issued, if the hotel's switch is on and the invoice is made out to the guest. One made out to a company, an agent or a booking site goes only with Send invoice (chapter A4)By email only, with the invoice PDF. Never a credit note.
Review requestWhen a clerk asks, after check-out (A10.10), if the hotel's switch is onWhatsApp or email, as the clerk chooses.

The voucher is the booking's confirmation. Its PDF shows the guest and who booked; under the stay, the guest's arrival time, their special request (A2.3) and the room promotion, each where there is one; each room with its guests, nights and rate; the booking's extras, each priced or “Included”; the room charges, GST, the extras with their GST and the grand total (a dash where no GST rule is set), and under it Paid and Due at check-in; what was paid in advance and what is left to pay at the hotel (or “Pay at the hotel”, or “Bill to company”), the booking's cancellation terms, the check-in and check-out times, the hotel's house policies, the bank details where they are set, and “Confirmed by the hotel” with the reference and the clerk. While online check-in is on, it also prints the guest's own check-in link and a QR code, “Check in online”.

  • A group of rooms gets one voucher, about its lead room, to that room's guest. It covers every room of the group.
  • Bookings made before sending was first switched on are confirmed only between 09:00 and 21:00, the hotel's time. A booking made after that goes at once, any hour.
  • There is no day-before reminder and no separate confirmation.
  • The booking's Notes are never on the voucher: they are the hotel's own. The guest's own wish is its Special request (D27-347). The lines the hotel's old confirmation printed: D27-344.

The desk's buttons

After a booking is made, its Booked card (chapter A2) has:

  • Send voucher: sends the voucher now, instead of waiting for it to go by itself. Once the voucher has gone by email, the button is replaced by “Voucher sent 9 Oct 2026, 14:05 by …”. It goes once: “The voucher for this booking has gone already, or three tries to send it failed. It is sent once, and not again from here.”
  • View voucher: opens the PDF to look at, print or save. It sends nothing. It is also under More options on a booking's panel, for a confirmed booking still to arrive.
  • Send check-in link: sends the voucher again, with the guest's check-in link, every way the guest can be reached: “Voucher sent again, with the check-in link”. Hidden where the hotel has switched online check-in off.

While sending is not set up, both send buttons are grey and the sentence under them says why (A10.8). Other refusals: “This booking is waiting for the hotel, so nothing is sent to the guest. Confirm it first.”; “There is nowhere to send it: no email address, and no telephone number the guest agreed to WhatsApp on.”; “No voucher could be made for this booking, so nothing went on WhatsApp.” (tell the manager).

Which messages are switched on

Settings, Messages, Guest messages on/off (the owner, an Admin and the GM). One switch per message, for this hotel only. Nothing here sends anything. The Tax invoice row says when it goes: “When the invoice is issued, by email, if it is made out to the guest. Only invoices issued after it is switched on; one made out to a company, an agent or a booking site goes by Send invoice.”

Watch out

  • The voucher goes on WhatsApp only with the guest's yes. New booking says it: “Ask them. Unticked, messages go by email if there is one, else not at all.” Bookings from the central reservation system arrive ticked; bookings from booking sites do not.
  • Nothing goes until sending is set up on the server: the sending workflow's address, its secret and the WhatsApp number. The vouchers that go by themselves also wait for the owner's pace, how many a minute. Until then, every screen that could send says so, and nothing is recorded.
  • The wording a guest reads is kept in the sending workflow, not in the PMS. Messages are in English.
  • A message goes to the phone and email on the guest's record when it is sent. Correct them first (Edit guest, A10.3).

Why it works this way

Fewer messages: the voucher is the confirmation, sent once, with the check-in link printed in its PDF; no day-before reminder; the desk's button stays to send it again: D27-264. The voucher both ways, email and WhatsApp: D27-235. WhatsApp through the central system's already-approved voucher template for now: D27-266; online check-in on for every hotel, a hotel may switch it off: D27-281. The tax invoice by email only: D27-284; by itself only when it is made out to the guest, never when it is made out to a booking site, an agent or a company: D27-313. One voucher per group, to its lead guest: D22-41, D22-52. Every future booking confirmed on switch-on day, soonest arrival first, at the owner's pace: D21-33, D21-34; the catch-up only from 09:00 to 21:00: D22-42. English only: D21-73.

A10.8The Guest messages screen

Guest messages answers “did the guest get their voucher?”. It is a record: nothing on it sends. It shows, from the top:

  1. Messages from guests, when there are any (see below).
  2. A yellow notice while sending is not set up.
  3. The bookings no message can reach, with what to add to each.
  4. The record of every message sent at this hotel, newest first (the last 200).

The record

ColumnWhat it shows
WhenThe day it was sent, the hotel's own clock.
What“Booking confirmation” is the voucher by email; “Booking voucher” is the voucher on WhatsApp; “Their sign-in code”; “invoice”; “review”. Older records may read “Before arrival” or “Check-in link”. The list is of messages to guests: the daily report emails and the system's health alerts go to the hotel's own people and are not listed here (A17.12).
BookingThe booking's reference; a dash where it was not about a booking.
ToThe phone or email it went to, as it was then.
State“Delivered to the sender” (green): the sending service took it. “Did not go” (red): see A10.9.
Sent byThe person who pressed the button; “A member of staff” when it was a colleague you may not see; “The system” when it went by itself.
What came backThe sending service's answer, in a sentence (A10.9).

When the list is empty it says which of two things is true: “Nothing has been sent yet” (sending works, nothing has gone), or “Nothing has been sent, because nothing can be yet” with “This is not a fault and nothing has failed. No message has been attempted, so there is nothing to show.”

One booking's messages

The same screen for one booking reads “What this system sent about this booking”. For a room of a group it shows the group's messages, because the group's one voucher covers every room. It is opened from Reply on a guest's message (below).

Messages from guests

A guest can write to the desk from their own page (Message the front desk). For the owner, an Admin, the GM, the Hotel Manager and Reception, Guest messages then starts with a card, Messages from guests, and a yellow “2 unread”.

  1. Read the message: the guest's words, their name, the booking and when.
  2. To answer, tap Reply. The booking's own Guest messages opens, with Reply to the guest: “They see it on their own page as “Front desk”. It is not sent on WhatsApp.” Type and tap Send reply. A reply marks the booking's unread messages handled.
  3. Done with it without a reply? Tap Mark handled. It then reads “Handled by …” with the time.

Once the guest has checked out: “This guest has checked out. Replies stop at check-out.”

Watch out

  • “Delivered to the sender” is not “read by the guest”. It means the sending service accepted the message for WhatsApp or email.
  • A booking listed as one no message can reach is not recorded anywhere else: nothing was attempted, so nothing failed. Fix it on the booking (A10.9).
  • The booking panel has no button for one booking's messages. Look for its reference in the Booking column.
  • The Revenue Manager, Housekeeping, the kitchen and the till do not see Guest messages: “What was sent to a guest is part of their guest record, and your role cannot open guests at this property.”
  • No connection: “This device is offline, so what was sent cannot load. It loads by itself as soon as the connection is back.”

Why it works this way

The system sends the voucher by itself, and the screen records every attempt so the desk can answer the guest's question the next day: D18-12, as changed by D27-264. Guest messages follow the Guests permission, so the Revenue Manager, Housekeeping, the kitchen manager and the till no longer read them: D27-144. One “Message the front desk” box on the guest's page, landing here with an unread count: D23-14; the desk replies, the guest sees “Front desk”, no WhatsApp, no replies after check-out: D27-224.

A10.9When a message did not go

A message that did not go shows “Did not go” in red, with the reason under What came back. The system tries the voucher - and a tax invoice - again by itself, a minute later, up to three tries for each way (email and WhatsApp count apart). After three, it stops.

What came backMeansWhat to do
“The receiver took it (200).”Gone to the sending service.Nothing.
“Could not reach the receiver. …”The sending service could not be reached.Nothing at once: it tries again. If it says this three times, tell the manager - the sending service needs looking at. Give the guest the voucher yourself meanwhile (View voucher, print or save it).
“The receiver did not answer within twenty seconds.”It was slow. It may in fact have gone.As above. A try again after a slow answer is never sent twice: the sending service remembers what it sent.
“The receiver refused it (400). …” (or another number), with its own wordsThe sending service said no.Check the guest's phone and email (Edit guest, A10.3). Tell the manager, with the words shown.

A booking no message can reach

The reason saysWhat to do
“No telephone number and no email address”Ask the guest. Add their email with Edit guest; or add their phone and, if they agree, tick Agreed to WhatsApp on the booking's panel.
“Not agreed to WhatsApp, and no email address”Ask the guest whether WhatsApp is all right. If yes, tick Agreed to WhatsApp; if not, add an email.

Once the booking can be reached, the voucher goes by itself and the booking leaves the list. The list does not depend on whether sending is set up: a booking fixed now is a guest reached on the day sending begins.

Watch out

  • After three failed tries, Send voucher refuses too. Hand the guest the PDF from View voucher, and tell the manager.
  • Never tick Agreed to WhatsApp to “make it go”. The tick is the guest's yes.

A10.10Reviews

Reviews asks a guest who has left for a review, and shows who was asked. Nothing is read in from Google, TripAdvisor or the booking sites: “Open the site itself to read them.”

To set the hotel's review link (owner or Admin)

  1. Under The review link, paste the hotel's own Google review link in Paste the link. It must start with https://.
  2. Tap Save the link. The message says “The review link is saved.”, and under it: “Set by … on …”.
  3. A wrong link: correct it, or tap Clear it: “The review link is cleared. Nothing will be sent until there is one.”

Not a web address: “A review link has to be a full web address beginning with https://. Paste the one the guest should open.” Anyone else reads “Setting this is for the owner or an administrator. Ask one of them.”

To ask a guest

  1. Find the guest under Departures: Guest (with the reference), Left, Stay, Review asked.
  2. Tap WhatsApp or Email on their row. WhatsApp is grey when the guest has no phone, Email when there is no email address.
  3. The message says “Ravi Kumar has been asked for a review.” The row then reads “Asked” with the time; or “Did not go” with the reason.

The buttons appear only when the hotel has a review link, sending is set up, and your role may ask (the owner, an Admin, the GM, the Hotel Manager, Reception). A dash under Review asked means not asked yet.

Watch out

  • After check-out only: “A guest is asked for a review after they have left, never before. This stay has not been checked out.”
  • A group is asked once, at its lead guest's room. The other rooms read “The group is asked once, at FH-….”
  • The hotel's Review request switch (A10.7) is off until switched on. While it is off, asking is refused: “Review requests are switched off for this hotel (Settings, Messages).”
  • No link: “This property has no review link yet, so there is nowhere to send the guest. The owner or an administrator can add it on this screen. The group's own review link has not been given yet.”
  • The Accountant and a Viewer read the list and send nothing.

Why it works this way

Ask after check-out and record who was asked; reviews are not pulled in from anywhere: D18-14. Each hotel's own Google link: D21-30. A group asked once, at its lead guest's room: D22-10. The review request was left for later, so its switch starts off: D27-266. No link is invented: a link nobody has set is a dash, and nothing is sent without one.

A10.11In short

WhenDoSection
Taking a bookingType the phone and email; if “same person?” appears, ask, and tap Same person if so. Ask about WhatsApp and offers.A10.6
A guest's name, phone or email is wrongThe booking's panel, Edit guest, Save.A10.3
“Did my voucher come?”Guest messages: find the booking's reference; read State and What came back.A10.8
A booking no message can reachAdd an email, or tick WhatsApp with the guest's yes.A10.9
A message from a guestGuest messages, Messages from guests: Reply, or Mark handled.A10.8
A new company at the deskCompanies and agents, Add company.A10.4
A guest has leftReviews: WhatsApp or Email on their row.A10.10
Managers, now and thenPossible same person: join or keep apart. Guest 360: blacklist, offers.A10.5, A10.6
Chapter A11

Reports

For managers, the accountant and the owner; reception and the store for their own reports. Where the reports are, what every report has in common, and which report answers which question: the day, the month and the year, money owed, the statutory registers, the accountant's export, and the Store's reports. Reports only read: opening one changes nothing.

A11.1Finding a report

In the Front office menu, the part called Reports lists three screens: Night audit, the screen that runs the audit (see A7), All reports, and Manager report. Every other report is one click away in All reports (/reports), or one search away with Find a screen (Ctrl K, A0.6).

All reports puts the reports in four groups, each with one line saying what the report is for. You see only the reports your role may open.

GroupReportsWho opens them
The dayManager report, Night audit report, Monthly occupancy, Voids, Monthly statistics, Yearly statistics (A11.3 to A11.5)Owner, Admin, General Manager, Hotel Manager, Revenue Manager, Reception, Accountant, Viewer
Money owedCity ledger, No show, Guest ledger, Cashier shift, Supplier dues, Petty cash (A11.6)The same, except that the Revenue Manager does not open City ledger, Guest ledger, Cashier shift or Petty cash; Supplier dues only the Owner, Admin, General Manager and Accountant
StatutoryLodging tax, GST sales register, Form III register (A11.7)The same as The day; the Form III register only for the Owner, Admin, General Manager, Hotel Manager and Reception
Store and equipmentClosing stock, Stock movement by day, Consumption, Wastage and breakage, Count differences, Dead stock, Days of cover, Supplier spend, Equipment report, Bar stock, FLR-1A/2A/3A register, FLR-3 register (A11.9)Owner, Admin, General Manager, Hotel Manager, Inventory Manager, Accountant, Viewer

One more screen sits in the Reports part of the menu: Accounting export, the month as a file for the accountant (A11.8). The Kitchen Manager, Chef, Waiter, Bar, Housekeeping and the Inventory Manager do not open All reports; the Inventory Manager reaches the Store's reports from the Store (A11.9).

To keep a report at the top

  1. Open All reports.
  2. Tap the star on the report's card. It fills in yellow.
  3. The report now also shows under Starred, above the groups. Tap the star again to take it off.

To find a report that is not in your menu

  1. Press Ctrl K, or click Find a screen at the top or at the foot of the menu.
  2. Type a word: the report's name, or a word such as “gst”, “tally” or “frro”.
  3. Click the report, or press Enter. “Not in your menu” beside it only means it is not listed in your menu: you may open it.

Watch out

  • A star is kept in this browser only. On another computer, or in another browser, your stars are not there.
  • While you type in Find a report, the Starred group is hidden. No match says “No report matches that”: try a word from a description instead.
  • The Night audit menu screen closes the day. The Night audit report only reads it (A11.4).

Why it works this way

The reports in the format of the owner's own eZee exports: D17-62. A shorter menu, with everything reachable by search: Reports lists only Night audit, All reports and Manager report (the owner, 15 September). The printed night audit is a report in All reports, apart from the screen that runs the audit: D17-78. No reports for housekeeping, the kitchen manager and the Inventory Manager, because they carry revenue: D27-141. The money-owed reports are not the revenue manager's: D27-147. Passports stay with the people who check guests in: D25-38, D27-122. The Store's readers: D27-240.

A11.2Every report works the same way

A report is laid out like a printed page: the hotel's name, the report's name and its date behind an orange bar, then one line of facts (the date or the period it covers), then the figures in bands, then the notes, then who printed it and when.

The buttons at the top

  • Print: prints the report alone, without the menu or the buttons.
  • PDF, Excel, CSV: save the report as a file (Figure A11-04). The file is made on the server from the same figures as the screen. They wait until the report has loaded. The message “PDF saved” names the file; if it fails, “The PDF was not made” says why.
  • Guest ledger, Cashier shift, GST sales register and the Form III register have Print and CSV only.

Reading the figures

  • A dash (-) is not a zero. It means the system does not hold that figure. The report's notes say which ones.
  • A figure in red is below zero. It is real: for example a guest who paid more than the bill came to.
  • An empty report still prints its date, and says in words that there was nothing (Figure A11-22).
  • Most reports print dates as 09/10/2026: day, month, year.

Which day a report is for

Except Voids, which has a From and a To, the reports have no date to choose. Each is for the hotel's business date (A1.1), or that date's month or year:

CoversReports
The business dateManager report (with the month and the year so far), Night audit report, City ledger, No show, Cashier shift, Closing stock, Dead stock, Days of cover, Equipment report
The 1st of the month to the business dateGuest ledger, GST sales register, Form III register, Stock movement by day, Consumption, Wastage and breakage, Count differences, Supplier spend, Supplier dues (owed on the business date; paid in the month so far)
The whole monthMonthly occupancy, Monthly statistics, Lodging tax
The calendar year, January to DecemberYearly statistics
Any days you chooseVoids (A11.4), Accounting export (A11.8); Petty cash, which opens on the 1st of the month to the business date (A11.6)

Watch out

  • Until the night audit has run, the day's figures can still change. A report opened at noon is the day so far.
  • Downloading a file is not for everyone. Reception and a Viewer may read the reports; a PDF, Excel or CSV from the server is for the owner, an administrator, the general manager, the hotel manager, the revenue manager or the accountant. Anyone else is told “Downloading reports is for the owner, an administrator, the general manager, the hotel manager, the revenue manager or the accountant. Ask one of them.”
  • A wide report scrolls sideways inside its card. Click Collapse at the foot of the menu to give it more room.

Why it works this way

The layout of the owner's eZee exports: D17-62. A real Excel file and a CSV: D17-31. PDFs made on the server: D17-32. Dates as 25/08/2026: D17-77. A figure the system does not hold is a dash, never a zero, because a zero would be read as a fact.

A11.3The Manager report

Open Manager report in the menu (/reports/manager). It is the day in three columns: Today, PTD (period to date: from the 1st of this month) and YTD (year to date: from 1 April, the start of the financial year). It is read afresh each time it opens.

Its bands, top to bottom: Room Charges, Extra Charges (late check-out, early check-in, no-show retention, food, beverage, laundry, spa, minibar and the rest), Tax, Revenue, Payment, City Ledger, Advance Deposit Ledger, Guest Ledger, Room Summary, Statistics, POS Summary and POS Payment Summary (the restaurant), and Revenue Summary (without tax).

LineMeans
Sold RoomRooms sold. Two switches on Front desk rules (A17.11) decide what counts: A complimentary room counts as sold (on to begin with) and A day use counts as half a room sold (off to begin with). The note under the report says how this hotel counts: “Sold Room, occupancy and the average rate count rooms as this hotel says (Settings, Front desk: complimentary rooms, day use).”
Occupancy Rate (%)Rooms sold, as a share of the rooms that could be sold.
Average Daily Rate (ADR)Room charges divided by rooms sold: what a sold room earned, on average. Extras, food and tax are not in it.
Revenue Per Available RoomRoom charges divided by every room that could be sold. Unlike ADR, it falls when rooms stay empty.

Watch out

  • While A complimentary room counts as sold is on, a complimentary room lifts the occupancy and lowers the average rate, because it is sold and earns nothing. Switch it off and it does neither.
  • Tonight's room charge is in Today even before it is posted, at the booking's rate.
  • Some City Ledger and Guest Ledger lines show “-”: the system does not hold them yet. The notes under the report say which.

Why it works this way

The owner's eZee Manager report, line for line: D17-62. A complimentary room counts as sold, as in eZee: D17-72. One rule for occupancy on every screen, this report's, and the report read afresh when opened: D27-151. What counts as sold follows the hotel's two switches, in this report and in the statistics (A11.5): D27-307.

A11.4The Night audit report

Open All reports, Night audit report (/reports/night-audit). It is one day, to the paisa: every room charged and every room given free, who checked out, the day's sales, every receipt, the rooms and guests, and the restaurant. It is wider than the screen: it scrolls sideways.

  • Booking is the booking's reference. Nrml. Tariff is the room's normal price that night; Ofrd. Tariff is what this guest is charged. A room type with no normal price shows “-” in Var %.
  • Checkin By is a dash when the system holds no record of who checked the guest in.
  • In Checked Out, a Balance may be below zero: the guest paid more than the bill came to.

Between them are Misc. Charges (everything charged that day apart from the rooms) and, at the end, POS Payment Summary (how the restaurant's bills were paid).

Watch out

  • Occupied means checked in. A booking for tonight whose guest has not arrived is under Reserve.
  • Before the audit runs, a guest who has not arrived is still in Room Charges. They go when the night audit marks the no-show.
  • A night's room charge is shown on the night it pays for, whatever day it was posted.
  • A bill sent to a company is not a receipt: it is on the Manager report as Charges Raised.
  • Charges, item discounts and tips are not recorded in this system: in the POS Summary they show “-”.

Why it works this way

A report in All reports, not part of the screen that runs the audit: D17-78. The Booking column prints the booking reference: D17-76. The guest not yet arrived stays in Room Charges until the audit marks the no-show, so this report agrees with the Manager report: D17-94.

Voids: what was voided, closed unpaid or struck in the restaurant

Voids (/reports/voids) lists every restaurant bill that was voided after it was paid, every order closed unpaid and every dish struck, for the days you choose, by outlet and day. It opens on the month so far; change From and To to look at other days.

  • Voided bill: a paid bill the owner, an administrator or the general manager voided. Its amount is what the guest had paid. Asked by names the waiter, when the general manager voided it on a waiter's request.
  • Closed unpaid: an order closed without payment, with the reason typed. Its amount is what the guest would have paid.
  • Struck dish: a dish taken off an order. Its amount is its price times its quantity, before GST. Kitchen had it says Yes when it was struck after its kitchen ticket was sent, No when it was struck before.

Watch out

  • An order closed unpaid shows who closed it and when from 28 October 2026 (D27-372); one closed before that shows “-” for both, as only its reason was kept.
  • A dish struck before the kitchen had it may have no reason: the reason column then shows “-”.
  • The three kinds are never added together: a bill's amount has GST, a struck dish's does not.
  • A bill given free (NC) and a discount are not voids and are not on this report.
  • The people who can open it are those who open the other reports (A11.1). A waiter, the bar, the kitchen manager and the chef cannot. A PDF, Excel or CSV is for the owner, an administrator, the general manager, the hotel manager, the revenue manager or the accountant.

Why it works this way

The restaurant's voids as one report, on screen and as a PDF: D27-370. Voiding a paid bill: D27-324. Striking a dish the kitchen has: D27-119.

A11.5Occupancy and statistics: the month and the year

  • Monthly occupancy (/reports/monthly-occupancy): the business date's month as a chart, one bar per day. Full houses and empty days both stand out.
  • Monthly statistics (/reports/monthly-stats): the same month as a grid, one row per day.
  • Yearly statistics (/reports/yearly-stats): the same columns, one row per month from January to December, then a Grand Total worked out again from the year's figures, not an average of the months.
  • All three count rooms sold the way the Manager report does, by the hotel's two switches (A11.3, A17.11): Occ %, ADR and the bars follow them. Night Sold (the paying rooms) and Complimentary stay columns of their own.

Watch out

  • Days after today have figures too. Nights already booked are counted at the booking's rate. They change if the booking changes.
  • Occ % and ADR count rooms sold as the hotel's two switches say: with A complimentary room counts as sold on, complimentary rooms are counted with the rooms sold; with A day use counts as half a room sold on, each day use is half a room. The first note under the report says which: “Occupancy and ADR count rooms sold as this hotel's switches say (Settings, Front desk rules): a complimentary room counts as sold; a day use is not counted.”
  • Rooms are counted from the day the hotel first traded (the note under the report gives the date). Days before it show nothing.

Why it works this way

A stay's room charge is spread over its nights, and nights booked ahead show at the booking's rate, as in eZee: D17-71. Complimentary rooms count as sold unless the hotel switches that off: D17-72, D27-307. Available rooms start on the first trading day: D17-93.

A11.6Money owed: City ledger, No show, Guest ledger, Cashier shift, Supplier dues, Petty cash

City ledger

City ledger (/reports/city-ledger) is the bills sent to a company or a booking site, account by account, for the business date: Opening Balance, Debit (bills sent to the account), Credit (what the account paid, recorded on Company accounts), Closing Balance.

The switch is on when the report opens. Turn it off to see every account, even those with nothing on them. The switch itself is never printed.

Money owed by age

Money owed by age (/reports/dues-by-age, or the link under the table on Company accounts) is what each company, travel agent and booking site owed on a date, by how old each bill is: 0-30 days, 31-60 days, 61-90 days and Over 90 days since the bill was sent to the account (settled Bill to company). Each kind of account has its own band - Companies, Travel agents, Booking sites - with its total, and Total owed is at the foot. Change the date above it to see another day.

An account's payment is recorded against the account, not one bill, so it pays the oldest bill first. Credit days are the company's own, from its record; a dash where none is set.

Statement of account

Statement of account (/reports/company-statement, or Statement beside an account on Company accounts, A4.8) is one company's, agent's or booking site's account for the days chosen, to send to them: the Opening balance, then each bill sent (the booking, the guest and the bill's tax invoice), each payment received and each payment reversed, by date, with the Balance after it, and the Closing balance. Pick the account and the From and To dates. PDF and Excel make the file to send.

A credit note cancels a tax invoice; it does not change what the account owes. What it owes changes when the bill sent to it is corrected (its Bill to company reversed and settled again), so the statement lists a credit note in its own part, with the invoice it cancels, and the balance does not move.

No show

No show (/reports/no-show) lists the bookings marked no-show that were due to arrive on the business date: booking, guest, room type, arrival, departure, pax, source and rate. On a day when everybody came, it still prints and says “Nobody failed to arrive on this day.” (Figure A11-22).

Guest ledger

Guest ledger (/reports/guest-ledger) is every guest's bill that moved from the 1st of the month to the business date: Opening, Charges, Received, Closing.

Opening is the balance before the window; Closing includes the last day. A charge that was reversed, and its reversal, are both left out.

Cashier shift

Cashier shift (/reports/cashier-shift) is what each cashier took on the business date, by method: how many receipts, and how much.

Petty cash

Petty cash (/reports/petty-cash) is every expense paid out of a restaurant's tin (A8.9) and the front desk's drawer (A4.10), together. It opens on the 1st of the month to the business date; change the two dates above it to see other days.

  • Expenses, by day: one line per expense - the date, where (the outlet, or Front desk), its category, what it was for, the amount, who recorded it, its approval (Approved, Waiting, Asked for more, Refused, or Not asked for one from before approvals began) and Yes under Photo when the bill's photo is on it. Each day ends with its total, and the report with the total of all.
  • By category: Kitchen, Housekeeping, Maintenance, Office and Other - how many expenses, and how much is Counted, Waiting for a yes and Refused.

Watch out

  • Petty cash totals count an expense once it is approved, as the drawer and the tin count it. One waiting for a yes or refused is listed but not added; By category shows it in its own column.
  • In Petty cash the restaurant's expenses fall on their business day; the front desk's on the business day its drawer was opened.
  • A dash for a category is an expense recorded before categories began (27 October 2026).
  • A receipt that was reversed is not money the cashier holds, so it is not counted - the same rule as the Manager report.
  • “not on record” is never filled in with a name: naming somebody would be worse than the gap.
  • The Revenue Manager does not see City ledger, Money owed by age, Statement of account, Guest ledger, Cashier shift or Petty cash.
  • Commission is counted on the room revenue before GST because no booking source or contract names another amount; the group's CA confirms that, and the booking sites' GST on their commission and the TCS or TDS they keep are not on it.

Supplier dues

The Supplier dues report (/reports/supplier-dues) is what the hotel owes, not what it is owed: the suppliers' bills taken on credit (A9.11). Owed to each supplier lists, under each supplier, every bill dated by the business date and not paid by it - its date, its due date, the days it is overdue and its amount - with the supplier's total, and the total owed at the foot. Payments made lists the bills paid from the 1st of the month to the business date: the day, the supplier, the bill, how it was paid, its reference, who recorded it and the amount, with the total paid. It is the Owner's, an Admin's, the General Manager's and the Accountant's only; it has PDF, Excel and CSV like the others.

Supplier statement, and TDS on suppliers

The Supplier statement (/reports/supplier-statement, or Statement beside a supplier on Supplier dues) is one supplier's ledger for the days chosen: the opening balance, then each bill, payment, TDS, credit note and reversal by date with the balance after it, and the closing balance. Pick the supplier and the From and To dates.

TDS on suppliers (/reports/tds) lists the TDS deducted on supplier payments for the days chosen, by section (194C, 194Q, 194J, 194I) and supplier: the figures for the quarterly TDS return (26Q). Both are read by the Accountant, the GM, the owner and an Admin, and download as PDF, Excel and CSV (D27-372).

Commission owed

Commission owed (/reports/commission) is the commission on the stays from booking sites and agents that checked out in the days chosen (from the 1st of the month to the business date when it opens), booking by booking, under each site or agent with its total. For each booking: the arrival and departure, the Room revenue before GST, the Rate % on record when the booking was taken (the source's on Settings, Money, Commission, or the agent's contract), the Site's figure when the booking site sent its own, and the Commission.

The commission is the site's own figure when it sent one; otherwise the rate times the room revenue; otherwise a dash - never a zero and never a rate made up. A stay counts in the days it checked out in, whole. Nothing here is a payment: paying a booking site is not recorded in this system, so the Manager report's Outstanding Commission still shows "-". The Owner, an Admin, the GM, the Revenue Manager, the Accountant and the Viewer read it; not Reception or the Hotel Manager.

Why it works this way

The city ledger's Debit is the bills transferred to the account: D17-74. Company payments are recorded on Company accounts and counted by the day they reached the hotel: D27-242. Money owed and money taken are not the revenue manager's: D27-147. One figure for a company everywhere, so Money owed by age and the Statement of account are the City ledger's own: D27-127. Commission is the site's figure, else the rate on record, else a dash: D17-84; Outstanding Commission stays "-" while no payout is recorded: D17-75, D27-259. All three were asked for in D27-383.

A11.7Statutory: Lodging tax, GST sales register, GSTR-1, Input tax credit, GST on advances, Form III register

These are filed with the government, not just read. This system files nothing: they are what the accountant, or whoever files, works from.

Lodging tax

Lodging tax (/reports/lodging-tax) is the month's check-out bills, one row for each day a bill was issued, with that day's first and last bill number, the room rent, and CGST and SGST.

The tax columns carry the room rent less its discount. Everything else on those bills is in Other Bills, except alcohol and its VAT, which are not on this sheet.

GST sales register

GST sales register (/reports/gst-sales) is every invoice and credit note issued from the 1st of the month to the business date, as GSTR-1 wants them: invoice, date, recipient, GSTIN, type (B2B or B2C), place, taxable value, CGST, SGST, total.

An invoice is listed on the business day it belongs to, not the moment it was printed. A credit note says which invoice it credits.

An invoice made out to a registered business - a company billed, or the guest's own company with the GSTIN typed on the booking (A2.2) - has its name under Recipient and its GSTIN in the GSTIN column, and Type says B2B. A dash under GSTIN is an unregistered recipient, and Type says B2C. A credit note has the type of the invoice it credits. The CSV carries the same Type column: D27-372.

GSTR-1, and its file for the GST portal

GSTR-1 (/reports/gstr-1) is the month's GSTR-1 for this property's GSTIN, table by table, from the tax invoices and credit notes issued in the month (by their business date) and the restaurant's bills paid at the outlet. Choose the Month above it.

  • 4A - B2B: each invoice to a registered recipient (a GSTIN on it), one line for each rate on it: the taxable value, CGST and SGST.
  • 5 - B2C large: always empty for a hotel, and it says why: B2C large is an invoice to another state over ₹1,00,000, and a hotel's supply is always in its own state.
  • 7 - B2C small: by rate, everything sold to an unregistered guest - invoices without a GSTIN, less their credit notes, and the restaurant's bills.
  • 9B - Credit notes: each credit note to a registered recipient, with the invoice it cancels.
  • 12 - HSN/SAC summary, B2B and B2C apart, by code and rate.
  • 13 - Documents issued: the first and last number, how many, how many cancelled, of the tax invoices, the credit notes and the restaurant's bills.

To make the GSTR-1 file

  1. Open GSTR-1 and choose the Month.
  2. Read the tables. If a part headed To put right before the file is made is at the top, put each line right first - an HSN/SAC not set for a kind (Settings, Taxes), or an invoice whose bill no longer adds up to it.
  3. Click GSTR-1 file (JSON). The file is saved: “GSTR-1 file saved”, named for the property, the GSTIN and the month.
  4. Give it to whoever files: they open it in the GST offline tool (or upload it on the portal), check it there, and file.

If anything still needs putting right, the file is not made and the message says what: “The GSTR-1 file was not made.” and the reasons. The file is for those who may download reports: the Owner, an Admin, the GM, the Hotel Manager, the Revenue Manager and the Accountant.

Input tax credit

Input tax credit (/reports/input-tax-credit) is the GST on the month's deliveries to the Store (A9), as it was recorded when each was received: GST marked claimable, then GST marked not claimable, each delivery with its supplier, the supplier's GSTIN when it is on the supplier's record (Places and suppliers), the item, its reference, the value before GST, the rate and the GST. CGST and SGST when the supplier's GSTIN is in this state, IGST when it is in another, a dash when no GSTIN is on record. Deliveries that recorded no GST are counted in the notes, not listed. It is read by the Owner, an Admin, the GM and the Accountant.

GST on advances

GST on advances (/reports/gst-advances) is the GST on money taken on a bill before its tax invoice - an advance, on which GST falls due in the month it is received. For the month chosen:

  • By rate, for GSTR-1 Table 11: 11A - Advances received, Given back before an invoice, and 11B - Advances adjusted, each by rate: the taxable value, CGST and SGST.
  • Advances received this month, no tax invoice by its end: each booking, the amount, and the tax inside it.
  • Given back this month before an invoice: a refund of an advance.
  • Advances of earlier months, adjusted against invoices issued this month: each with its invoice.

Money received and invoiced in the same month is not an advance in GSTR-1 and is not here. An advance includes its tax. "Bill to company" is not money received. The rate is the room's GST rule at the booking's rate; where no rate is known when the money is paid (a function, a group's bill, a free room) it is 18%. It is read by the people who read Company accounts. This report changes nothing about how a tax invoice is made.

Form III register

Form III register (/reports/c-form) is every foreign guest who arrived from the 1st of the month to the business date, each foreign adult in a room on a row of their own: passport and visa, arrival, departure, and the FRRO portal's numbers.

A guest not yet filed shows “not filed” in red; one who has left without the departure filed, “departure not filed”. A passport not captured at check-in shows “not on record”. The CSV carries every Form III field.

Watch out

  • Nothing here is filed by itself. The Form III register is the record of what was filed on the portal; the portal numbers are typed on the Form III screen (Finance part of the menu).
  • The Form III register is for the Owner, Admin, General Manager, Hotel Manager and Reception only: it shows passports. The Accountant does not see it.
  • Lodging tax counts the bills issued. A stay still in house is not on it yet (compare the Accounting export, A11.8).
  • For the group's CA to confirm before the first GSTR-1 is filed from this system: that credit notes share the tax invoice numbers (so Table 13's ranges overlap); that a cancelled invoice is not counted as cancelled in Table 13; whether a deposit is an advance, and how money given back before an invoice is reported; and that input tax credit is claimed only as GSTR-2B shows it. The marked-claimable column is what the person receiving chose, not a ruling.

Why it works this way

Lodging tax reads the room rent less its discount, and the group's accountant confirms before anything is filed: D17-99. No rate in the CGST and SGST headings: D24-23. GSTR-1, input tax credit and GST on advances: D27-383; the file follows the GST offline tool's JSON (version 3.2.2), and an advance for a service is taxed when received (CGST Act section 13(2); the exemption of Notification 66/2017 is for goods). Alcohol and its VAT kept off the sheet: D22-45. Passports only for the people who check guests in: D25-38; not the Accountant: D27-122.

A11.8Accounting export: the month for the accountant

Accounting export (/reports/accounting) hands the accountant the hotel's days as a file. It reads the same figures the reports print, and changes nothing. It is for the Owner, Admin, General Manager and Accountant; find it with Find a screen (“tally”, “day book”, “export”).

To export the month

  1. Open Accounting export. From is the 1st of the month and To is the business date. Change them if you need to. Both days are included.
  2. Under Format, choose Day book (CSV) or Day book (Excel), whichever your accountant asks for.
  3. Check the table below: it is the file, drawn on the screen.
  4. Tap Export. The file is saved on this computer.

The day book has one row a day: room revenue and its tax, food charged to a room, the other extras, the tax on those two, the restaurant and its tax, discount, alcohol and its VAT, sales, GST, receipts, what companies paid, and whether the night audit has run.

Food charged to a room is food on a bill: charged at the desk, or a restaurant bill charged to a room or a function. Other extras are laundry, the spa, drinks that are not alcohol, late check-out and the rest. What the restaurant took itself, in cash, by card or UPI, is under Restaurant. Together the two columns are the old Extra charges figure, to the paisa.

Under the table, four totals for the range: Sales, Tax, Receipts and Received from companies, then each company payment on its own line.

After a night audit is cancelled

When the owner or an Admin cancels a night audit (A7.5), the days it reopens were closed, so they may already be in Tally. For 60 days, a yellow card at the top, Night audits cancelled, names them, for example “Cancelled on 2 Nov 2026: Tally: if 1 Nov 2026 to 2 Nov 2026 were already imported into Tally, delete those days there and export them again once each is closed again.”

  1. If those days are in Tally, delete their vouchers there.
  2. Wait until each day is closed again: the day book's Night audit column says Closed.
  3. Export those days again and import them.

Watch out

  • A day not closed is still exported, and says so (Not run). Tell the accountant before sending a month that is not closed.
  • Tally Prime (XML) and Tally ERP 9 (XML) stay off until every ledger name is typed. Each says which are missing: “Type these ledger names first: Room rent, CGST.” Export stays grey while one of them is chosen.
  • A range where nothing happened says “Nothing was charged or received in this range. The file will have a row for each day, all of them nil.”
  • This and the Lodging tax report will differ in a month with a stay still in house. Both are right.

Why it works this way

All three kinds of export offered, whoever exports picks: D18-16. Both a CSV and a real Excel file: D22-37. The Accountant opens it: D27-122. Company payments in the day book as receipts of their own: D27-242. Food as its own line: D27-382. Each hotel's ledger names are typed by its Accountant and none is ever made up: D27-382. The days a cancelled night audit reopened are named, to delete in Tally and export again; the PMS keeps no record of exports, so it says “if”: D27-390.

To type the Tally ledger names

Each hotel has its own list, on the same screen, under Tally ledger names. The Accountant, General Manager, Owner and Admin may change it. There is one box for each ledger this hotel needs: alcohol and VAT only where the hotel serves alcohol, the restaurant's only where it has one, and one for each way of paying it uses.

  1. Open Accounting export and find Tally ledger names.
  2. In each box, type the name exactly as it is in this hotel's Tally. Spaces at the two ends are taken off; the spelling and the capitals stay as you typed them.
  3. Two boxes may hold the same name: if one bank account takes bank transfers and cheques, type its name in both.
  4. Tap Save ledger names.

Watch out

  • No name is suggested, and none is ever made up here. A box left blank stays blank. Clearing a box and saving takes its name away.
  • The words beside each box, such as Room rent, say what the ledger is for. They are not ledger names and never go into a file.

To make a Tally file

  1. Type every ledger name first (above). Each name must already be a ledger in the hotel's Tally: the file creates none.
  2. Choose From and To. Every day in the range must be closed by the night audit.
  3. Under Format, choose Tally Prime (XML) or Tally ERP 9 (XML), and tap Export.
  4. In TallyPrime, open the company, press Alt+O (Import), choose Transactions and pick the file. In Tally.ERP 9: Gateway of Tally, Import Data, Vouchers. The file names no company, so it goes into the company open in Tally.
  5. Read what Tally reports. Every voucher should be created, with no exceptions.

There is one Sales voucher a day, not one per bill. The day book counts each day's charges, and a bill is counted differently (see the Lodging tax report), so only a day's voucher holds the same figures. A voucher per bill would also need a ledger for every guest.

In the day bookIn Tally
Room revenue, food charged to a room, other extras, restaurant, alcohol, GST, VAT, discountThe day's Sales voucher, each on its own ledger. GST is split evenly into CGST and SGST; VAT is never split
What the restaurant took in cash, by card or UPIThe same Sales voucher, on the Cash, Card and UPI ledgers. A rounded bill's difference goes on Round off
Charges on billsThe same Sales voucher, on What guests owe
Money paid on billsThe day's Receipt voucher, by way of paying
A refundThe day's Payment voucher
A bill moved to a companyThe day's Journal voucher, from What guests owe to What companies owe
A company's paymentA Receipt voucher of its own, with the company and the reference in its narration
The owner's allowance, its free partThe Sales voucher, on Owner's allowance: it is a sale, with its GST
A reversed charge, a struck lineIn no voucher: the day book does not count them
An NC bill, a voided billIn no voucher: neither is a sale (an NC bill's value is shown only as NC, D27-394)

Not in the file, and not in the day book: credit notes and cancelled VAT bills; supplier bills; cash expenses; cash banked. A day's voucher does not list each bill.

Watch out

  • A range holding a day not closed is refused, naming the day. The day book files still carry it; a Tally file does not, because tonight's room is only an estimate until it is posted.
  • A day that cannot balance is refused, naming the day and the difference, for example a restaurant bill settled with no payment recorded. No line is added to make it balance.
  • A ledger name that does not match stops that one voucher, and Tally takes the rest of the file. Tally says “Ledger 'Round Of' does not exist!”. The day is then only part-way in. Put the name right under Tally ledger names, export the day again and import it again.
  • If a closed day is corrected, export it and import it again. Its vouchers are replaced, not doubled. A voucher the corrected day no longer has stays in Tally until it is deleted there: if the day's only bill to a company was reversed, its Journal voucher stays, and What companies owe reads too high. In TallyPrime, check that replacing vouchers is switched on under Alt+O, Configuration.
  • Tally gives each voucher its own number. The day and the kind are in the narration, for example 5EL day book 2026-08-02: sales.
  • Tally's free Educational Mode takes vouchers dated only the 1st, 2nd and 31st, and says “Voucher date is missing” for any other day.

What has been proved, and what has not

Proved on 31 October 2026, on TallyPrime 7.2 in Educational Mode, in a practice company, with demo figures and the file sent to Tally's XML port on the same computer. Five vouchers for one day: all created, no exceptions, every voucher balanced in Tally, and Tally's own Day Book matched the day book to the paisa on room, food, other extras, restaurant, alcohol, GST, VAT, discount, receipts and company receipts. Ledger names holding & and an apostrophe went in exactly as typed. Reversed and struck lines stayed out. A corrected day imported again replaced its vouchers. A misspelt ledger was refused and no ledger was created.

Not proved: Tally ERP 9 is not installed here, so only that file's shape has been tested. Importing the file through Alt+O has not been tried, nor a licensed copy of Tally, nor Tally's GST reports on these vouchers.

The first real proof is the Accountant importing one day into a copy of the company in Tally. Do that before the hotel's real books.

A11.9The Store and equipment reports

Ten reports on what the stores hold and use, and where the equipment is. Costs are as recorded: delivery prices before GST, each item at its running average at the time.

To open one

  • From the Store (A9): tap Reports at the top of the Store, and choose the report.
  • All ten on one page: Find a screen, Store reports (/reports/store); or the Store and equipment group in All reports.
ReportWhat it shows
Closing stockEach store's stock on the business date, at the average cost as recorded.
Stock movement by dayReceived, issued, wasted and counted, one row a day.
ConsumptionWhat was issued, per item and per outlet. Then Given free (NC), at MRP: each dish on the bills given free in the window, per outlet, with how many, its MRP from the Menu (A8.11) and the value at it. A dish with no MRP shows a dash, is left out of the total, and the line under it says how many lacked one. This is the only place an NC bill has a value: it is no sale and no tax (D27-373).
Wastage and breakageEvery wastage, and every breakage with who broke it.
Count differencesWhat each count corrected, and why.
Dead stockStock that has not gone out for 30, 60 or 90 days.
Days of coverHow long each item lasts at the last 7 days' use.
Supplier spendDeliveries per supplier, and each item's first and last price.
Equipment reportWhat is out of the store, under repair, and when warranties and AMCs end.
Bar stockThe bar's day, in full bottles and ml, for the Bar counter and the Bar store each: opening, what came (from the store, or the bills), what was sold or sent to the counter, other moves, count corrections, closing, the closing count and the morning count's difference; the counter's requests decided; then each dish sold and what it took, dishes sold with nothing set up, drinks struck after the bar had them, and the day's bar bills (A9.11).
FLR-1A/2A/3A registerThe excise department's daily register, as the bar keeps it on paper: one row per brand under its kind (Whisky, Rum, Wine, Beer...), and for Opening Balance, Receipts, Sales and Closing Balance a column for each bottle size, with the T.P. No. of the day's bills. Whole bottles, the store and the counter together (A9.11).
FLR-3 registerThe excise department's monthly register: a row per day for Received (with the Permit No.), Sold and Closing Balance, by spirits imported and Indian made, wines, fermented and mild liquor and each size; at the foot Opening, Received, Grand total, Less sold, Less breakages and Closing balance (A9.11).

Below them: each dish sold and what it took, dishes sold with nothing set up, drinks struck after the bar had them, and the day's bar bills.

The register is wider than the screen: scroll it sideways. Print and PDF lay it out landscape, as the paper is.

Watch out

  • The Inventory Manager does not open All reports: use the Store's Reports, or Find a screen, Store reports.
  • Downloading a store report is for the owner, an administrator, the general manager, the Inventory Manager or the accountant.
  • A price nobody recorded is a dash, never a zero.

Why it works this way

The Store's reports: D27-238. Who reads them, costs as recorded, dead stock as nothing gone out for 30, 60 or 90 days, and days of cover from the last 7 days: D27-240. The Inventory Manager has no All reports, because the other reports carry revenue: D27-141.

A11.10In short: which report answers which question

The questionThe reportSection
How did today go, against the month and the year?Manager reportA11.3
Every room, receipt and restaurant bill of one dayNight audit reportA11.4
Which restaurant bills were voided, orders closed unpaid and dishes struck, by whom and why?VoidsA11.4
How full were we, day by day?Monthly occupancy; Monthly statisticsA11.5
The year, month by monthYearly statisticsA11.5
What do companies and booking sites owe?City ledgerA11.6
How old is what they owe?Money owed by ageA11.6

What commission do the booking sites and agents get for this month's stays?Commission owedA11.6
Who did not come?No showA11.6
