Chapter A12

Approvals, cash expenses, notifications

For the general manager and the owner, who decide; for the Inventory Manager and anyone who asks for something; and for everyone who reads the bell. Who approves what, how to approve or refuse, what a cash expense waits for, what the person who asked sees, and what the bell and the Notifications screen tell you. Also the other screens in the System part of the menu.

A12.1The System part of the menu

System is the last section of the Front office menu. You see the screens your role uses. Approvals is not here: it is at the top of the menu, after the Dashboard (A12.3).

ScreenWho sees itWhat it is for
ApprovalsOwner, Admin, GM, Hotel Manager in the menu; the Inventory Manager by Find a screenEverything waiting at this hotel, from every part of the system: Approve or Refuse it there (A12.3).
NotificationsMost rolesThe same list as the bell, on a page (A12.9).
System healthOwner, AdminWhat the server is doing, from its own records: how long it has been up, the database, disk space, the last backup, requests, each hotel's business date and last night audit, the slowest routes, errors. No guest is named on it.
Room systemsOwner, Admin, GMMarked “Not built yet”. Door locks, room phones, minibars and TVs. Key cards are built and switched off until the hotel's lock system is connected.
Design system, ConsoleOnly on the test computerTools for the people who build the system. They are not in the live system.
Users, IntegrationsUsers: Owner, Admin, GM, Hotel Manager. Integrations: Owner, AdminNot in the menu: open them with Find a screen (A0.6). Users: who can reach what. Integrations: what the server has set up (sign-in, the channel manager, WhatsApp and email). The owner's book explains them (B2, B5).
SettingsOwner, Admin, GMThe Settings space, from the switcher at the top (A0.4).

Why it works this way

One Approvals screen for everything waiting on a person: D18-19. System health inside the system, for the owner and administrators, from the server's own records: D27-91. A service not built yet sits in its own section, marked “Not built yet”, for the owner, admins and GMs: D27-87.

A12.2Who approves what

Some things wait for a second person's yes before they count. Each one is a request: somebody asks, with a reason, and somebody else decides. Every request, whatever it is, goes to the same Approvals screen.

RequestRaised whenDecided by
Purchase requestSomebody asks to buy something on Purchasing (Ask to buy, A9). By default the Inventory Manager, the GM, the owner and an administrator may ask.The general manager, every purchase, whatever the amount.
Cash expenseMoney is paid out of a drawer: the front desk's (Cashiering) or a restaurant's tin (Close restaurant day). See A12.7.The general manager or the owner. Never an administrator.
Equipment leaving the storeEquipment goes out of a store to a room, the kitchen or the restaurant.The Inventory Manager; when they are away, the owner, an administrator or the GM.
Equipment being retiredA tagged item is retired by somebody who may not approve it, such as the Hotel Manager.The same as above.
Restaurant: sent to youA waiter or cashier sends what only the GM may do: take off a dish the kitchen has, a discount, an NC bill, or void a paid bill (A8.7). Approving does it.The general manager, the owner or an administrator.
Front desk: sent to youReception asks, after check-in, what only the GM may do: undo the check-in, cancel or void the booking, change the arrival date or the rate, or how a payment was taken (A2.9). Approving does it.The general manager, the owner or an administrator.
  • Nobody approves their own request. A GM's own cash expense waits for the owner (Figure A12-04).
  • The group owner may decide any request.
  • A decision stays. An approved or refused request cannot be decided again. To go ahead after a refusal, raise a new request.
  • A refusal always has a note, so the person who asked knows what to do next. Approving needs none.

Why it works this way

The GM approves every purchase, with no amount above which the owner must: D18-4, confirming D17-35. Who may ask is a setting per hotel, changed without a new release: D18-2. Every cash expense needs a yes from the GM or the owner, never an administrator, never one's own: D27-239, D27-242. Equipment waits for the Inventory Manager, with the owner, an administrator or the GM instead: the owner, 16 September. A waiter's or cashier's strike, discount, NC or void sent to the GM, the owner or an administrator, approving does it, with the bell and Approvals at the top of the menu: D27-363. The front desk's, after check-in, the same way: D27-397. Who decides is kept as a rule for each hotel, and a request keeps the rule it was raised under: a rule changed later never moves a request already waiting.

A12.3Approving or refusing

Approvals is at the top of the menu, after the Dashboard, and the bell counts what waits for you: “2 requests waiting for your approval”, with a link here. The list refreshes by itself every few seconds.

Open Approvals. The line under the title says “Everything waiting at this hotel, from every part of the system.” Waiting lists every request still waiting, newest first. Each card says what kind of request it is, what it is for in the asker's own words, the amount, who asked and when.

A request from the restaurant says exactly what it is in a line of its own, such as “NC, the bill free: ₹672.00 - Table 7 · bill 20261011-128”, and the waiter's reason under it. Approve does it at once; the waiter's bill says so.

A request from the front desk is the same: Front desk: sent to you, what exactly and for whom, such as “Change the rate to ₹3,000.00 a night - Omkar Shinde, room 203, FH-2608-4859”, and the clerk's reason. Approve does it as you, with every check of the guest's menu asked again: if one refuses (a day closed since, a charge put on the bill), the message says why and the request goes on waiting.

To decide a request

  1. Read the card. To see the whole request first (each line, the store it goes to), click its orange name, such as Purchase request.
  2. To approve: tap Approve. The message “Approved.” shows and the card leaves the Waiting list.
  3. To refuse: type why in A note (required to refuse), in one sentence, then tap Refuse. The message is “Refused, and they have been told why.”

What happens next belongs to the request. An approved purchase can be ordered from a supplier (A9). Approved equipment leaves the store. An approved cash expense is taken off what its drawer should hold (A12.7).

Watch out

  • Refuse with no note is not accepted: “Say why it is refused, so the person who asked knows what to do next.”
  • Approve and Refuse cannot be undone. Read the card before you tap.
  • A purchase request can also be decided on its own page, which has a third button, Send back, to ask for something to be cleared up. Approvals shows such a request as Asked for more.
  • A request from the restaurant that can no longer be done (the dish struck meanwhile, the bill paid) is not approved: Approvals says why, and it stays waiting until it is refused.
  • The bell does not tell you a request is waiting. Open Approvals to see what waits on you.

Why it works this way

A GM with a purchase, two equipment requests and a cash expense waiting had to know to open four screens; now one screen shows them all, decided in place, while each service's own screen keeps its buttons: D18-19. Both make the same decision, so they never disagree. A refusal needs a reason because the person who asked has to know whether to buy it elsewhere, buy it cheaper, or not buy it.

A12.4A request that is not yours to decide

Approvals lists every request waiting at the hotel. Where you may not decide one, the card has no buttons, and a sentence says why.

A request that belongs to another role says whose it is instead, and waits for them. The GM's own cash expense in Figure A12-04 waits for the owner.

A12.5What was decided, and by whom

Tap Everything at the top right. Requests still waiting come first, then the decided ones, newest first. Each decided card says Approved or Refused, who decided it, and the note.

The person who decides sees who asked, and the person who asked sees who decided. Where a name is not yours to see, it shows a dash.

A12.6When you asked: reading the answer

The person who asked finds the answer on the request itself. For a purchase: open Purchasing and click the request.

A request still waiting says Waiting for the general manager. A cash expense shows its answer on its drawer's line (A12.7).

The Inventory Manager may decide equipment requests, but their menu is short and leaves Approvals out. It is still theirs: press Ctrl K or click Find a screen, type approv, and press Enter.

A12.7Cash expenses

A cash expense is hotel money paid out of a drawer for something the hotel needs: milk for the kitchen, a taxi, a courier, a repair. Every one waits for a yes.

To record one

  1. At the front desk, open Cashiering; in a restaurant, open Close restaurant day and its Cash step (A8.9).
  2. Under In and out of the drawer, tap Record.
  3. Choose What happened: Paid out at the desk, Expense in a restaurant.
  4. Type How much and What was it for, choose its Category, add the Photo of the bill if you have it (A8.9, A4.10), then tap Record.

The expense goes to Approvals as a Cash expense, named by its drawer and your words: “Fidato Restaurant tin: Milk for the kitchen”, or “Front desk drawer: …”. The GM or the owner decides it (A12.3). Not the person who paid it out.

While it is…The drawer's line saysAnd the drawer
Waiting“Waiting for a yes - not taken off the drawer yet” (in a restaurant, “… the tin yet”)Is expected to hold that money still. At the count, Paid out, waiting for a yes shows how much; if the count is short, the yellow box says how much of it is paid out and waiting.
ApprovedNothing more: it is a paid-out like any other.The money is taken off what the drawer should hold, even if the drawer has been closed since.
Refused“Not approved: the note - not taken off the drawer”The money is a shortage on that drawer, and nothing more.

Watch out

  • Record an expense as soon as the money leaves the drawer, with plain words. What was it for is the line somebody asks about tomorrow.
  • A waiting expense does not stop the drawer closing. The part of a shortage it explains needs no reason at the close; only the rest does.

Why it works this way

Every cash expense needs a yes, from the GM or the owner, never an administrator, never one's own; while waiting it is not counted and explains its part of a difference; both the desk's drawer and the restaurant tins; a refused expense is a shortage only: D27-242, following D27-239.

A12.8The bell

The bell at the top of every screen shows how many notices you have not read (9+ when there are more than nine). Click it: the list opens on the right.

  • Click a notice to go to its screen (Arrivals, Folios, the Store…). It is then marked read.
  • A notice goes by itself when the thing is done: check the guest in and the arrival notice is gone. Nothing needs clearing by hand.
  • When every notice is read, the bell's list says “You are all caught up”.

A12.9The Notifications screen

Notifications, in the System part of the menu, is the same list on a page, each notice with Open. Its first line says why the list is always right: “Derived, never stored - so nothing here can go stale while the thing it describes changes.”

KindNotices of this kind
reservationArrivals not yet checked in; table bookings guests asked for, waiting for an answer.
paymentA balance outstanding on a room due out today; money to refund to a guest who paid more than their charges.
customerGuest messages and guest requests waiting; room-service orders waiting; wake-up calls due, or asked for by guests.
approvalSomething for a manager to look at: a store's crockery and cutlery not counted for 30 days, or never; postings reversed today. It is not a request in Approvals.
systemRooms out of service. For the group owner: a hotel's bank details set, changed or removed.

Watch out

  • You see what your role may see. A guest's name only if you may read guests; an amount only if you may read bills. The Inventory Manager in Figure A12-09 reads “A balance is outstanding on room 204” where the owner reads “₹5,715 outstanding on room 204” and the guest's name.
  • Mark all as read lasts until the page is reloaded. It is kept in that browser window only; reload the page, or open the system on another computer, and the notices still standing are unread again.
  • The time on a notice is not when it arose. Most say nine in the morning of the hotel's business day.
  • Requests waiting in Approvals are not on the bell (A12.3).

Why it works this way

Each notice is worked out afresh from the same records every other screen reads, so the bell never disagrees with the folio or the report, and never has to be tidied. The bell follows the screens' own rules: names only for roles that read guests, amounts only for roles that read bills, the alert for everyone: D27-153.

A12.10In short

WhenDoSection
You need something boughtPurchasing, Ask to buy, say what it is for, Send for approval.A9
You pay cash out of a drawerRecord it: Paid out (desk) or Expense (restaurant), with what it was for.A12.7
Something waits on youApprovals, Waiting. Approve, or type a note and Refuse.A12.3
You asked for itYou cannot decide it. Read the answer on the request, or on the drawer's line.A12.6
Who decided that?Approvals, Everything.A12.5
Refused, and still neededRaise a new request. The first decision stays.A12.2
The bell shows a numberClick it, click a notice, do the work. The notice goes by itself.A12.8
Chapter A13

Banquets, spa and laundry

For the general manager, reception and housekeeping, at a hotel that runs a banquet hall, a spa or a laundry. How each is switched on, how a function is booked, fed and billed, how a spa treatment is booked and put on the room bill, and how a laundry bag goes out, comes back and is charged.

A13.1The three parts, and their switches

Not every hotel has a banquet hall, a spa or a laundry. Each is switched on hotel by hotel. Where it is on, the Front office menu has a part for it: Banquet, Laundry and Spa. Where it is off, that part of the menu is not there at all.

ScreenWho uses itWhat it is for
DiaryThe GM; the owner, an Admin, the hotel manager. Reception may also register and confirm a function (open it with Find a screen)Each hall and the functions in it: register, confirm, feed, bill (A13.3, A13.4).
Halls and packagesOwner, Admin, GMThe hotel's halls, and its catering packages (A13.2).
Spa diaryReception; the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel manager. Housekeeping sees it and does not bookOne day, therapist by therapist: book, charge to the room, cancel (A13.5).
TreatmentsOwner, Admin, GMWhat the spa sells, how long each takes, its price, and the therapists (A13.5).
DocketsReception and housekeeping (in their menus); the owner, an Admin, the GM, the hotel managerEvery laundry bag, a guest's and the hotel's own: collect, record what came back, charge to the room (A13.6).
Price listThe same people, one search awayWhat the hotel charges for each thing it launders (A13.6).

To switch one on

Only the owner or an Admin can. Other roles do not see the page.

  1. Choose the hotel. Click Settings in the switcher at the top (A0.4).
  2. In the menu, under Modules and connections, open Modules (/settings/connections/modules). The card Modules says “What this property runs.”
  3. Tap the switch beside Banquet hall, Laundry or Spa. The message “Turned on” names it, and the menu shows its part at once.

Each switch says what it runs, in the screen's words:

  • Banquet hall: “The diary, the halls and their packages. A hall cannot be sold twice for the same session.”
  • Laundry: “A guest's laundry, charged to their room, and the hotel's own linen going out and coming back.”
  • Spa: “Treatments, the day's diary, and each one charged to the guest's room.” Settling at the spa is not built: a treatment is always put on the room bill (A13.5).

What staff see while one is off

The menu has no part for it. A screen opened by its address, or from an old link, says it is not available, with the reason (Figure A13-x2). Nothing can be booked or changed, even by typing the address: the server refuses it as well.

Watch out

  • The message says “Turn it on in the property's settings if that is wrong.” Only the owner or an Admin can. Anyone else: ask one of them. The server's answer to anyone else is “Switching a module on or off is for the owner or an administrator. Ask one of them.”
  • Each part starts off at a hotel until somebody turns it on. Nothing is set up for you when it is: no hall, no treatment, no price (A13.2, A13.5, A13.6).

Why it works this way

The module switches are the owner's and an Admin's; the GM may open Settings: D17-36. Laundry and the spa, each behind its own switch, shown only where it is on: D17-54. A part of the menu that is off is absent, not greyed out, and the server refuses its work on its own, because a hidden screen is still an address anybody can type.

A13.2Banquets: halls and packages

Before the first function, enter the hotel's halls. Open Halls and packages (or the button of that name on the Diary). The screen says “Nothing here is created for you, and no price is ever assumed.” Only the owner, an Admin or the GM can add or change anything on it. For anybody else, Reception for one, Add a hall, Edit, Add a package and the packages' switches are grey, and each card says who may: “The owner, an administrator or the GM adds and edits them.”

To add a hall

  1. Tap Add a hall.
  2. Type its Name (“Emerald Hall”). Seated capacity and Standing capacity are optional: leave them blank if they have not been measured.
  3. Usual rate is optional too. It is only ever offered on the booking form; what is billed is what is agreed for each function. Tick Free only if the hall really is free.
  4. Tap Save. Change a hall later with Edit.

To add a package

A package is food sold by the head, such as a dinner buffet. Packages are optional: a function can be fed off-menu, from the restaurant, or not at all.

  1. Tap Add a package.
  2. Type its Name, and if you wish its Rate a head (or Free), its Kind (“Veg, non-veg, jain…”) and What is in it.
  3. Tap Add. A package with no rate reads “no rate - agreed per function”.

To take a package off offer

A package is never changed once it is added: “Never changed once added. Switch one off to stop offering it; functions keep what they were sold.” For a new rate or a new menu, switch it off and add another.

  1. Under Packages, tap the switch at the right of the package's line. The line shows Off, and the message says “Dinner buffet is off: not offered for functions now”.
  2. Tap it again to offer it again: “Dinner buffet is offered again”.

A package that is off is not in the list when a course is added (A13.4), and the server refuses it for any function. A function that already has it keeps its line as it was sold: its name, plates and rate.

Watch out

  • A package is never changed once it is added, only switched off. Name it carefully, and add a new one for a new rate or menu.
  • Changing a hall's usual rate never changes a function already booked: each function keeps the figures agreed for it. A package is never changed at all.

Why it works this way

A package can be taken off offer but not changed, so a function sold on it, and its bill, never move: D27-305. Halls and packages are set up by the owner, an Admin and the GM; every button is grey, with a sentence saying who may, for anybody else: D27-307.

A13.3Banquets: the Diary, and booking a function

The Diary answers one question: is the hall free on that day? Each hall is a row, with its functions under it, over 30 days from the hotel's business date. ← Earlier and Later → move 30 days; From today comes back. A hall with nothing booked says “Free for the whole window.”

Each function shows its name, its state, its reference, when it runs, the host, the guests expected, who registered it, and the agreed amount, or a dash if none is agreed yet. Tap it to open it.

StateMeans
EnquiryWritten down. It holds nothing: two families may ask about the same Saturday.
ConfirmedIt holds the hall for that time, and its bill is open.
CompletedBilled: the hall and food are on its bill (A13.4).
CancelledCancelled, with the reason. The hall is free again.

To register a function

  1. On the Diary, tap Register a function. The window says “This holds nothing yet. Confirming it takes the hall.”
  2. Choose the Hall. Type What is the function? (“Sharma sangeet”), From and Until (a date and a time each), and the Host. Telephone, Expected guests and Notes are optional.
  3. Agreed amount is the hall's price. Leave it blank if it is not agreed yet: it stays unpriced, not free. Use usual fills in the hall's usual rate; Free means no charge.
  4. Tap Register. The message gives its reference and says it is “an enquiry until it is confirmed.” The function opens.

If the guests expected are more than the hall holds, the form warns “More than this hall holds”; it is a warning, not a refusal.

To confirm it

  1. Open the function and tap Confirm and hold the hall.
  2. The message “The hall is held, and a bill is open.” means it is done.
  3. If another confirmed function has the hall at that time, it is refused, and the message names it: “The hall is taken: …” with its name, reference and times.

The function's page

  • What and when: from, until, the host and telephone, guests expected and guaranteed, the hall, who registered it.
  • The money: Hall, Catering, Restaurant orders and the Total. If anything is unpriced the total is a dash, and a line says what is missing. Set the hall price (or Change the hall price) sets the agreed amount; an empty box makes it unpriced again.
  • Catering: the courses (A13.4). With none, it says “Nothing is being served. That is a complete booking - add a course only if food is part of it.”
  • Restaurant orders: what the restaurant charged to this function (A13.4).
  • The bill: once confirmed (A13.4).

To cancel a function

  1. Tap Cancel. Type Why?: it is required, and it stays on the record.
  2. Tap Cancel the function (or Keep it). The message says “The hall is free again.”

A function with an advance may be cancelled; the advance stays as the host's credit. A billed (Completed) function cannot be cancelled.

Why it works this way

A hall is booked from a time until a time, and only a confirmed function holds it, so it cannot be sold twice; an enquiry holds nothing. No default prices: a blank amount is unpriced and shows a dash, and a price of 0 is kept only when ticked Free: D27-120. Cancelling a function with an advance, and never a billed one: D27-135.

A13.4Banquets: food, and the function's bill

To add a course

  1. On the function, under Catering, tap Add a course.
  2. Choose a Package, or Off-menu. A package fills in its name and offers its rate. Only packages that are on are listed (A13.2).
  3. Check What is being served?, type Plates (at least one) and Rate a head. Leave the rate blank if it is not agreed yet; the total says so until it is.
  4. Tap Add. The bin beside a course takes it off.

Food from the restaurant

A confirmed function running today can take food from the restaurant. When taking the order on Tables, the Till or the Terminal (A8), choose it under Banquet function. That order is then paid on the function's bill, not at the till. It shows under Restaurant orders; an open order is not in the total until it is settled.

The bill

Confirming opens the function's bill. Its card, The bill, shows what is charged, the GST, what is paid and the balance. Only the owner, an Admin and the GM take money and bill; the Accountant may also issue the tax invoice.

  1. An advance: tap Take an advance, choose the Method, type the Amount, tap Take payment. No GST receipt voucher is issued for an advance yet.
  2. Bill it: tap Bill the function. The hall and every course go on the bill under the Banquet GST rate. After this the price, the courses and the restaurant orders are fixed, and the function is Completed.
  3. Settle: tap Settle and take the balance the same way.
  4. Invoice: tap Issue tax invoice. It takes the next number of the series, and a number once taken cannot be taken back. The invoice then shows on the card.

Bill the function is refused while anything is unpriced, while a restaurant order on the function is still open, or while the hotel's banquet tax is not set: “Banquet tax is not set: ask the GM to set it before the bill.” While it is not set, the function's page says so at the top.

More than ₹1,00,000 in cash at once asks for the payer's PAN, or Form 97. Paying more than the balance after the bill is kept only if you tick Hold it as the host's credit.

To correct a billed function

Before the tax invoice: Reopen the bill, type Why, and tap Reopen the bill. The hall and every course come off the bill, with the reason on each line; advances, payments and restaurant orders stay. Change what is wrong, then bill the function again. A bill posted on a day the night audit has closed is refused: “correct it on Closed days.” After the tax invoice, only a credit note corrects it.

Why it works this way

Restaurant food on a function's bill: D17-21, posted like a room charge so it is on the invoice: D27-133. Who takes the money, and the Accountant's invoice: D27-132. The warning while banquet tax is unset: D27-124. Billing any time after Confirm, its refusals, and the advance with no receipt voucher: D27-138. The invoice's SAC, 996334 with food and 997212 for a hall alone, for the CA to confirm: D27-134. Reopening: D27-154. A function's bill lives on its own page, not on Folios: D27-137.

A13.5The spa

The spa has two screens: the Spa diary, and Treatments (its heading is Treatments and therapists). Reception books, charges and cancels. Housekeeping sees the diary and does not book; the diary tells them so.

Setting it up (owner, Admin, GM)

  • Treatments: Add a treatment with its Name, How long, in minutes, and Price. Leave the price empty if none is set; it reads a dash, and a price added later applies to new bookings only. Change it later; Take off the list and Put back on the list.
  • Therapists: Add a therapist with a Name. It is a name, not an account: nobody signs in as a therapist. Take off the list when someone leaves; past bookings stay as they were.

The diary

One day at a time, opening on the hotel's business date: ← Day before, Today, Day after →. Each therapist is a row with their treatments: the time, the treatment, the guest and room, and the price, or a dash. A therapist with nothing booked says “Free all day.”

To book a treatment

  1. Move the diary to the day of the treatment. Tap Book a treatment.
  2. Choose Which guest: guests in the house, or arriving (with their arrival date).
  3. Choose Which treatment. Its length places it in the day, so nothing asks when it ends.
  4. Choose Which therapist, type What time, and tap Book it. The message says “The treatment is in the diary.”
  • Every treatment is for a guest's stay, on a day from their arrival to their departure. Otherwise: “The guest is not staying on that day.” A guest who is not staying cannot be booked.
  • One therapist is never in two places at once. If the time is taken, the message names who is in the way: the therapist, the guest, the treatment and the time.

When the treatment is given: Charge to room

  1. On the treatment, tap Charge to room.
  2. The window says the price “goes on their bill as its own line, taxed at this property's spa rate.” Tap Charge to room (or Not yet).
  3. The message names the room. The treatment now shows On the room.
  • The guest must be checked in: “The guest has not checked in yet, so it cannot go on their room bill.”
  • If the hotel has not set its spa GST rule, the charge is refused, and the message says where GST is set.
  • To undo a charge, reverse the line on the guest's bill (A4). A charged treatment can no longer be cancelled.

To cancel a treatment

Tap Cancel, type Why, and tap Cancel the treatment (or Keep it). The message says “The hour is free again.”

Watch out

  • Price the treatment before you book it. The price is copied onto the booking when it is taken. A booking taken while the treatment had no price shows a dash and “Unpriced”, has no Charge to room, and pricing the treatment afterwards does not change that booking: “Unpriced - it cannot be closed for money. A price added to the treatment later applies to new bookings only: cancel this one and book it again.” Cancel it and book it again.
  • Settling at the spa (cash at the spa) is not built yet: every treatment goes on the room bill.

Why it works this way

Booked by telephone to the desk: D18-6. Run by reception and housekeeping, with no new roles and no therapist sign-ins: D18-8. Reception books and closes, housekeeping only sees, and the spa's own GST rule per hotel: D18-21. On the room bill as its own line: D18-7; settling at the spa set aside for later: D18-22. Booked only on a day of the stay, charged only once checked in: D27-136.

A13.6The laundry

One place for everything that goes to the laundry: a guest's bag, and the hotel's own linen. A docket is one bag: whose it is, what is in it, and what has come back. Reception and housekeeping run it; Dockets is in their menus.

The price list

Open Price list (or the button on Dockets). Its heading is Laundry price list. One line is one thing and one service: a shirt washed, a saree dry-cleaned.

  1. Tap Add an item. Type What is it, choose What is done to it (Wash, Press or Dry-clean), and the Price if the hotel has decided one.
  2. A price can be typed later in the list itself; it is saved when you leave the box, and it applies to new bags only: a bag already collected keeps its dash. Free means free. Retire takes a line off the list; dockets already written keep their own copy.

The hotel's own linen goes on the list with no price: it is counted, never charged.

To collect a bag

  1. On Dockets, tap Collect a bag.
  2. Answer Whose is this first: A guest's bag or The hotel's own linen. Nothing is filled in for you.
  3. For a guest, choose Which stay. Only guests in the house are listed: a bag is collected only from a checked-in guest.
  4. Under What is in the bag, pick each thing from the price list and type How many. Add another thing for the next.
  5. Anything to note is optional (“Ink on the left cuff”). Tap Collect it. The message gives the docket's number, and the docket opens.

The list of dockets

Everything, Guests' bags or The hotel's linen. Every row says whose it is, its state (Out, Back or Cancelled), the pieces, how many are still out, the total, and when it was collected. What is still out is listed first.

One docket

  • When it comes back: tap Record what came back and type how many of each have come back in total, not how many arrived this time. Tap Record it. When nothing is still out, the docket marks itself Back.
  • A guest's bag: tap Charge to the room. It goes on the guest's bill as its own line, with the docket number and what was in the bag, under the hotel's laundry GST rate. The message says it “is on the room's bill as its own line.”
  • The hotel's own linen has no charge button: it is never charged to anybody. The docket says it, in a card headed The hotel's own linen: “Counted out and back, never charged to anybody.”
  • Print prints the docket. Cancel works until it is on a bill; after that the charge is reversed on the bill instead. A docket already on a bill carries a card, Already on the bill: “It is its own line on the room's folio. A charge is reversed on the folio, never by cancelling the docket under it.”

Watch out

  • Price the list before you collect. The description and price are copied onto the docket when the bag is collected. A bag holding an item with no price has no total and cannot be charged, and pricing the item afterwards does not change a bag already collected: “A price added to the price list later applies to new bags only: cancel this one and take it again.” Cancel the bag and take it again.
  • If the hotel has not set its laundry GST rule, the charge is refused: “This property has no GST rule for laundry.”
  • Not in this version: linen par levels per room type, an outside laundry's bills, express surcharges, and a guest sending a bag from their own page.

Why it works this way

A guest's laundry and the hotel's own linen in one place, every docket saying whose it is: D18-5. Straight onto the room bill as its own line: D18-7. Run by reception and housekeeping: D18-8; Dockets in their menus where the hotel has laundry on: D22-22. Collected only from a checked-in guest: D27-136. Laundry's own GST heading, refused until set: D27-194. The docket's own words, with no decision codes on a staff screen: D27-316.

A13.7In short

WhenDoSection
The hotel starts a hall, spa or laundryThe owner or an Admin: Settings, Modules, the switch. Then enter the halls, treatments or price list.A13.1
A call about a functionDiary, Register a function. It is an enquiry.A13.3
The host says yesThe function, Confirm and hold the hall. Take an advance.A13.3, A13.4
The food is agreedCatering, Add a course. Restaurant food: choose the function under Banquet function.A13.4
After the functionBill the function, Settle, Issue tax invoice.A13.4
A guest wants a treatmentSpa diary, the day, Book a treatment.A13.5
The treatment is givenCharge to room.A13.5
A guest hands in laundryDockets, Collect a bag, A guest's bag.A13.6
Linen goes outDockets, Collect a bag, The hotel's own linen.A13.6

Chapter A14

Sales, marketing and loyalty

For the owner, managers and reception. The leads app's enquiries inside the PMS and how a lead becomes a booking, the month's marketing figures, and the loyalty programme: switching it on, its rules, joining a guest, points earned at check-out and taken off the room charges.

A14.1The Sales and marketing screens

In the Front office menu, the part called Sales and marketing sits under Guests & CRM: both are about people. It holds three screens.

ScreenWho sees itWhat it is for
Leads and WhatsAppEveryone who sees guests: Owner, Admin, General Manager, Hotel Manager, Reception, Accountant, ViewerThe leads app's enquiries for this hotel, read as you open the page; Book this lead (A14.2).
MarketingOwner, Admin, General ManagerOne month: each campaign's spend beside the bookings and revenue it brought, and every booking source's (A14.3).
LoyaltyEveryone who sees guests (Points by hotel and The rules: owner, Admin, GM)Who is in house and their points: join, use points, leave; the programme's rules; points by hotel (A14.4).

Where each one works

None of the three is hidden by a hotel's module switch: the menu shows them wherever your role allows. What each needs before it does its work:

  • Leads and WhatsApp and Marketing's spend: the leads app connected on the server (the owner's read-only login), and this hotel matched to one of the leads app's hotels. Without them the screen says so; Marketing still shows its bookings and revenue.
  • Loyalty: the hotel's own Loyalty switch (A14.4), plus a programme name and an earn rate for the group. Without the switch the screen says “Loyalty is off at this hotel: nobody joins, earns or uses points here. The owner or an administrator turns it on in Settings, under Modules.”

Reception's own menu has none of the three. Reception opens Leads and WhatsApp and Loyalty with Find a screen (Ctrl K): type “loyalty” or “leads”, and tap the screen, marked “Not in your menu”.

Why it works this way

A Sales and marketing part of the menu, for Leads and WhatsApp, Marketing and Loyalty: D27-87. Everyone who sees guests sees leads; marketing's numbers only the owner, an Admin and the GM: D27-170. A shorter menu for each role, with every other screen they may open one search away: the owner, 15 September.

A14.2Leads and WhatsApp

The hotel's enquiries - from WhatsApp, the website and ads - live in the leads app, where staff reply to them. Leads and WhatsApp shows them inside the PMS: “Enquiries from the leads app, read as you open this page. Staff reply in the leads app.” The PMS sends nothing to a guest from here and writes nothing into the leads app. The one thing done here is Book this lead.

What the screen can say

It saysMeans
“Not connected yet” (Figure A14-01)“The leads app is read with a read-only login the owner sets up on the server. Until then nothing is read and nothing is shown here.”
“This property is not in the leads app”“The leads app has no hotel matched to this property, so it has no enquiries to show here.”
“The leads app was not read”With the reason: “Today's reads of the leads app are used up. They come back after midnight Pacific time.”, or “The leads app could not be reached. Nothing was changed there. Try again in a few minutes.”
“No enquiries yet”“Enquiries arrive in the leads app from WhatsApp, the website and ads, and show here.”

When it is connected

  • Along the top, one button per status with its count: All, Open (New, Assigned, Claimed, Overdue, Contacted, Follow-up and Quoted together), then each status there is - New, Assigned, Claimed, Contacted, Follow-up, Quoted, Booked, Lost, Long term, Dead, Overdue, Closed. These are the leads app's own words.
  • Enquiries, “Newest message first”: the name (or the phone), the status, the last message, the channel - “Meta Ads”, “Google Ads”, “Website organic”, “Direct WhatsApp”, “Referral”, “Walk-in or phone”, “Manual entry”, “Other” - and when. Fifty at a time; Show older enquiries for more.
  • Tap an enquiry to read it beside the list: the name, phone, channel and status; Came in; for a booked one, Booking in the leads app and Value typed there; then the conversation, the guest's messages on the left and the hotel's on the right. On a phone the conversation takes the screen; Back to the enquiries returns.
  • Reply in the leads app opens the enquiry in the leads app, where you answer.

To book a lead

  1. Open the enquiry and tap Book this lead.
  2. New booking opens with the guest's name and phone filled in, the booking source by the lead's channel - Meta Ads, Google Ads, WhatsApp or Website, when this hotel has a booking source by that name; any other channel, you choose - and the lead's campaign kept on the booking.
  3. Finish the booking as usual (chapter A2). Its campaign is what Marketing counts (A14.3).

An enquiry opened too long ago, or erased in the leads app: “This enquiry is no longer in the leads app, or its link has expired. Open it again from Leads and WhatsApp.”

Watch out

  • Every look costs. The leads app is read live and its free allowance is shared with the app itself, so the PMS reads at most 5,000 times a day. The list comes 50 at a time; a conversation is read only when you open it; a screen opened twice within a minute is read once.
  • Nothing is copied into the PMS. A guest erased in the leads app is gone from here the next time the list loads. Their stays and bills stay.
  • Staff's internal notes in the leads app are not shown here.
  • “The guest asked not to be messaged. The leads app refuses replies to them.” on an enquiry means exactly that.

Why it works this way

The leads app keeps running; the PMS shows its leads, conversations and spend read-only, with a link to reply there: D27-100; its conversations are linked, never copied: D21-5. Read live every time, no copy kept, a cap of 5,000 reads a day, staff notes not shown, a lead's booking taking its source by channel and keeping its campaign: D27-170. A guest erased there is erased from this view too, and their stays and bills stay as tax law requires: D27-108. The app is kept separate, and the PMS only shows its leads: D27-186.

A14.3Marketing

For the owner, an Admin and the GM. Marketing shows one month, by the stays' arrival date: what each campaign cost, beside the bookings and revenue it brought here, and the same for every booking source.

To read a month

  1. Open Marketing. It opens on this month.
  2. Choose another in Month.
  3. Read Campaigns: Campaign, Where (“Meta Ads”, “Google Ads”, “Other ads”), Spend, Bookings, Revenue.
  4. Read By booking source: Booking source, Bookings, Revenue.
  • Spend comes from the leads app; bookings and revenue from this system's own stays. A booking carries its campaign only when it was made with Book this lead (“A booking carries its campaign when it is made from a lead.”).
  • Revenue is the stays' room charges before tax: the nights already charged, plus the nights still to come at the booking's rate. Cancelled and no-show stays are left out.
  • A dash under Spend means nobody has the figure - never a zero. The line under the campaigns says why: “Spend is read from the leads app, which is not connected yet.”, “This property is not one of the leads app's hotels, so it has no spend.”, or the leads app's own reason.
  • Nothing that month: “No campaigns this month”, “No spend was recorded in the leads app, and no stay arriving this month came from a campaign.”; “No stays arrive this month”.

Watch out

  • The month is by arrival: a stay booked in September for October counts in October.
  • Opening Marketing reads the leads app twice; it counts against the same daily allowance as Leads and WhatsApp.
  • The guest lists for sending offers (stayed twice, not back in a year, came from which site) have no screen yet. Offers will go only to guests who said yes (A10.5).

Why it works this way

Spend beside the bookings and revenue of this system's own stays, never a figure typed in the leads app; marketing numbers for the owner, an Admin and the GM only: D27-170. Revenue is booked value - nights charged plus nights to come at the booked rate, before tax, cancelled and no-shows out, by arrival date: D27-173. The first version of marketing asked for guest lists that can be acted on: D18-17, for the owner, an Admin and the GM: D22-17; offers only to a guest who said yes: D25-39.

A14.4Loyalty

A member earns points on their stays at every hotel of the group, and uses them on their room charges: 1 point is ₹1 off. The heading line says the programme's name and its earn rate, for example “… · 5 points per ₹100 before GST; 1 point is ₹1 off room charges” - or, until they are set, “No programme name yet · no earn rate set: stays earn nothing”.

Once: switch it on and set the rules

  1. The owner or an Admin opens Settings, Modules and connections, Modules, and switches on Loyalty for the hotel: “Members earn points on their stays here and use them on their room charges. Off means nobody joins, earns or uses points at this property.”
  2. The owner, an Admin or the GM opens Loyalty. Under The rules (“For every hotel of the group.”) they type the Programme name - “The words a guest agrees to use it.” - and Points per ₹100 - “Before GST. Empty: stays earn nothing.”
  3. Tap Save the rules. The message says “Rules saved”.

What stops the rules: “The name is 40 letters at most.”; “Points per ₹100 is a number above 0 and at most 100, or empty for none.”

To join a guest

In house lists every guest checked in: Room, Guest, Points (or “Not a member”). Join, Use points and Leave are shown only to a role that may use them, and the heading of the list says who may: “Guests join and leave through reception, the hotel manager, the general manager, an administrator or the owner.” and “Points are used by reception, the hotel manager, the general manager, an administrator or the owner.”

  1. Ask the guest. Tap Join on their line.
  2. The window says “Read this to the guest. Joining is not a yes to offers.” Read them the words shown: “Join programme name: we keep your stays and points to give you rewards. I am 18 or over.”
  3. If they agree, tick The guest agrees.
  4. Tap Join. The message says “… joined”.

What stops a join: “Loyalty is off at this hotel. The owner or an administrator turns it on in Settings.”; with no programme name, the window itself says “The programme has no name yet, so there is nothing to agree to. The owner, an administrator or the GM names it on this Loyalty screen, under The rules.” and The guest agrees and Join stay grey; “A member needs a mobile number. Add it to the guest first.” (Edit guest, A10.3); “This guest is already a member.”; “Tick that the guest agrees, in their own words, before they join.”

Earning: by itself, at check-out

When a member checks out, the stay earns points by itself, usable at once, at the earn rate: everything on the stay's bills before GST and after discounts - room, restaurant charged to the room, and the rest - except GST, alcohol, refunds and payments. On a booking from a booking site or an agent, the room earns nothing; the extras do. Whole points, rounded down, once per stay.

To use points

  1. On the member's line, tap Use points (shown on direct bookings only, and only to Reception, the Hotel Manager, the General Manager, an Admin and the owner).
  2. The window, Use points for …, says their balance: “They come off the room charges as a discount line, from 500 at a time.”
  3. Type the Points - “1 point is ₹1 off. The guest signs the bill.” The button reads Use ₹500.
  4. Tap it. The message says “₹500 off the room charges”. The bill shows a discount line under the nights; each night keeps its price.

What stops it: “Points are used while the guest is checked in.”; “Points are used on direct bookings only, not on a booking from a booking site or an agent.”; “Points are used from 500 at a time.”; “The guest has 320 points.”; “Points come off room charges only, and this bill has … of them left.”; “This stay has a tax invoice. Points cannot be taken off it now.”

To leave

  1. On the member's line, tap Leave.
  2. The window asks … leaves loyalty?: “Their 320 points lapse. Their history stays with the bills.” and “They can join again later, with no points.”
  3. Tap Leave. The message says “… left”.

The member card on Guest 360 (owner, Admin, GM)

Guest 360 (A10.5) shows a Loyalty card: “Member since …, joined at …”, the points, and every line of the statement at every hotel - “Earned”, “Used”, “Adjusted”, “Lapsed” - with the booking, the hotel and any reason. A guest who is not a member reads “Not a member. The desk joins a guest on the Loyalty screen, with their yes.” (Figure A10-08).

  1. To add or take points by hand: type Points (“Minus to take”) and the Reason (“Stays on the statement”); tap Adjust. The message says “Points adjusted”.
  2. To take a member out: Leave, then Leave loyalty: “Left the programme”.

What stops an adjustment: “Say why. The reason stays on the statement.”; “The guest has 320 points; a balance cannot go below 0.”

Points by hotel

For the owner, an Admin and the GM (Figure A14-05): for the month chosen, each hotel's Points earned and Points used, in rupees, so the hotels can settle between themselves. Points earned at one hotel may be used at another; the hotel that gives the discount carries it on its own invoice.

Watch out

  • Joining is not a yes to offers. Offers are a separate question (A10.5).
  • A member is one person across the group. Two guest records joined as one (A10.6) share one balance; an undo splits it back.
  • A discount line of points taken off the bill again (reversed) gives the points back by themselves.
  • No tiers. Points do not lapse yet: the 24-month expiry is not built, and no point could lapse before October 2028.
  • Reception, the Hotel Manager, the GM, an Admin and the owner join a guest, use points and take guests out. The Accountant and a Viewer only look: they are shown no Join, no Leave and no Use points.

Why it works this way

Build loyalty now: D27-178. The earn rate is a setting with no default - unset, nothing earns; no tiers at the start; a per-hotel switch; 18 or over with a mobile; its own consent tick; one membership per person; booking-site and agent rooms earn on extras only; points used from 500 on the member's own room charges as a discount line; the giving hotel carries the discount: D27-179, with the rules L1 to L18 in the loyalty service's notes. Using points is a right of its own, held by Reception and above (the owner, an Admin, the GM, the Hotel Manager, Reception) and not by the Accountant, who looks: D27-305. Join and Leave follow the right to change a guest, and are not shown to anybody without it: D27-307.

Answering an enquiryReply in the leads app.A14.2
