Chapter A15

Rates, revenue and distribution

For the owner, the GM, the Revenue Manager and whoever reads prices. How to read the Rates calendar, change a price for a day or a run of days, set the add-ons every price is built from, close a date or set a minimum stay, read the Revenue outlook, set up the Channel manager to the booking sites through SU, and keep the companies and agents with their contracts.

A15.1The screens

Two parts of the Front office menu hold this chapter: Rooms and rates (what this hotel is selling) and Distribution (who sells it). You see the screens your role uses.

ScreenWho sees itWhat it is for
RatesEveryone who reads prices: Owner, Admin, General Manager, Revenue Manager, Hotel Manager, Reception, Viewer. Only the Owner, an Admin, the GM and the Revenue Manager change anything on it.Each day's price for every room type, and how the day sold; Rooms left and the restrictions; how rates are built; prices set before (A15.2 to A15.5).
Revenue outlookOwner, Admin, General Manager, Revenue ManagerThe coming ninety nights: this month on the books, what to consider, the dates worth a look. It never changes a price (A15.6).
Channel managerOwner, Admin, General Manager. The SU setup: the Owner and an Admin only.The connection to the booking sites through SU: what it sends and takes, what it still needs, the bookings the sites sent (A15.7, A15.8).
ContractsOwner, Admin, General Manager, Hotel Manager, Reception, Accountant, Viewer. Contracts are kept by the Owner, an Admin and the GM.The group's companies and travel agents, and the rates each has agreed with this hotel (A15.9).

Reception's menu is its working menu, which leaves out Rates and Contracts: Reception opens them with Find a screen (Ctrl K, A0).

Two screens these depend on sit under Property setup: Booking sources, where each booking site gets its SU code, and Cancellation terms. The same company records also open from Companies and agents in Guests & CRM.

A15.2Reading the Rates calendar

Open Rates. It says “Each day's price, and how the day sold. The add-ons follow the base.” It opens on two weeks from the hotel's own business date.

  • The base is the grey line of each room type: what one guest pays for the room alone (room only, EP) that day. Under the price, “3 left” is the rooms of that type still to sell that day.
  • The rows under it are what the room really sells for that day: for two guests on room only, then CP, MAP, AP and AI. Where the room sleeps more, + per extra adult and + per extra child say what one more guest adds; where it sleeps no more, those rows are left out.
  • The arrows move two weeks at a time. Away from the business date, Today brings you back. Weekends and the hotel's holidays are shaded grey.

The key

On the calendarMeans
4,000 (bold)A base typed for this room type.
4,000 (grey)From the base room type: the base room type's base plus this type's difference (A15.4).
4,000 (grey italics)A price set before, covering two guests (A15.4).
-Not priced. Nothing that needs it is sold. Never read a dash as zero.
3 leftRooms of the type still to sell that day.

Paying rooms sold, ADR and Revenue are the paying rooms only, at the booked rate before tax: complimentary rooms and day use are left out. The occupancy under Paying rooms sold counts complimentary rooms, as the reports do, so it can be a little higher than the paying rooms alone. ADR is a dash on a day nothing was sold.

Under the calendar, links open the reports: Manager report, Monthly occupancy, Monthly statistics and Revenue outlook (Figure A15-05).

Watch out

  • On the demo hotel every price is still the old rack rate, so every base shows in grey italics and every meal plan shows the room-only figure. A hotel priced only by its old rack keeps selling every plan at that figure until a base and the add-ons are set (A15.4).
  • Everyone who reads prices sees the calendar; only the Owner, an Admin, the GM and the Revenue Manager can tap a price. The server asks the same question on every price it is sent.

Why it works this way

One screen for the price and how the day sold, in place of the old Pricing, Rate plans, Rate calendar and Rate performance: D27-188. The break-up rows under each room type and Set prices: D27-206; every room type always open: D27-237. Paying rooms sold beside one occupancy rule everywhere: D27-151.

A15.3Changing a price

Only the base is typed: what one guest pays for the room alone. Every plan and guest count on that day follows it, through the add-ons (A15.4). The line under the calendar says so: “Tap any price to change it, for that day or through a later day.”

One day, or from that day: tap the price

  1. Tap the room type's base on the day. The window is named after it: “Deluxe · base”.
  2. Type the Base per night in rupees. Or tick Free if it really is free.
  3. Leave Through on the same day for that day only, or choose a later day. The line under it says what it covers: “12 Oct 2026 only.” or “5 days, 12 Oct 2026 through 16 Oct 2026.”
  4. Tap Set base. The message says “Base set” with the room type and the days.

A run of days: Set prices

  1. Tap Set prices at the top of Rates.
  2. Choose the Room type.
  3. Choose From, the first day, and Through, the last day.
  4. Type the Base per night, or tick Free.
  5. Tap Set base. It stays grey until a price is typed or Free is ticked.

Watch out

  • No default price. A blank is not priced, and 0 is kept only when it is ticked Free: “0 is kept only when it is ticked Free. Leave it blank if nobody has priced it yet.”
  • A day that already has a base of its own also offers Clear, which takes that base away (“Base cleared”).
  • On a date that has a base, the old rack rate is no longer used there. Each plan is then the base plus its add-on, and a plan or a second guest whose add-on is a dash is not sold that day. Set the add-ons (A15.4) before the first base.
  • Where the rooms are derived from one base room type (A15.4), only that room type's base can be tapped; the others follow it.

A15.4How rates are built, and prices set before

Under the calendar, How rates are built shows the add-ons that ride on every base. Each is set once for the hotel, in rupees, with no dates:

  • Breakfast (CP), per guest, MAP, per guest, AP, per guest, All inclusive (AI), per guest: every guest pays the meal plan's add-on, children too.
  • Double occupancy (the second guest): what the second guest adds, adult or child.
  • Extra adult (from the third guest) and Extra child (from the third guest).

The card says: “A base covers one guest, room only. A dash is not set: nothing that needs it is sold.”

To set the add-ons, or derive the room types from one

  1. Tap Edit on How rates are built.
  2. Under Room types, choose Each room type has its own base, or Derived from one room type: “Derived: the others are the base room type plus a difference.”
  3. Derived: for each other room type, type how much it is more than the base, and choose ₹ or %. A percentage is rounded to the whole rupee.
  4. Type each add-on in rupees, or tick Free. Leave it blank where nobody has priced it.
  5. Tap Save. The message says “Every price follows the base and the add-ons.”

Prices set before

Prices typed before this way of pricing began are kept, under Prices set before: “Kept exactly as they were: each covers the guests it always did, and wins over the base on its dates.” A room type's old rack rate is listed there too, “Used only on dates no base covers.”

  1. Tap Remove beside the price.
  2. It asks first, naming the price. Tap Remove, or Cancel.

Why it works this way

A base plus add-ons set once, each room type its own base or derived from one by rupees or a percentage, and the calendar changing only the base: D27-188. The base covers one guest; the second guest is double occupancy; from the third, extra adult or child; meals per guest, children too; a percentage rounded to the rupee; a part nobody set is a dash and is not sold: D27-194. A hotel still on its old rack sells every plan at the room-only rack until a base and the meal add-on are set: D27-196. Zero only when ticked Free: D27-120.

A15.5Rooms left and the restrictions

Tap Rooms left at the top of Rates. Each room type, each day: the rooms still to sell in large figures, and under them “paying rooms sold / sellable”.

  • A day with nothing left shows yellow; a day on stop sell, red.
  • Complimentary and tentative rooms hold a room but are left out of the small figure; occupancy on the reports counts complimentary rooms.
  • A minimum or maximum stay shows on the day as its figures, such as “2–5”.

To close a date or set a minimum stay

  1. On Rooms left, tap the room type's day. The window is named “Deluxe · 17 Oct 2026”.
  2. Tap what applies: Stop sell (“Nothing may be booked at all”), Closed to arrival (“A stay may not begin here - protects a long weekend”), Closed to departure (“A stay may not end here”).
  3. Type Minimum nights or Maximum nights if needed.
  4. For a run of days, choose Through: “Apply the same rules to every day up to here.”
  5. Tap Apply. The message says “Applied” with the room type and the days.

Watch out

  • To take a rule off, clear everything and tap Apply: “Clearing everything removes the rule rather than storing a row that says nothing.”
  • Apply with Through sets the same rules on every day of the run, in place of what each day had.
  • A minimum above the maximum is refused: “A minimum of 3 nights and a maximum of 2 accepts no booking at all.”
  • A restriction is per room type, not per plan: a room not for sale is not for sale on any plan.
  • Restrictions go to the booking sites through SU (A15.8). A booking made at the desk is not checked against them: the desk decides.
  • Only the Owner, an Admin, the GM and the Revenue Manager can tap a day.

A15.6The Revenue outlook

Open Revenue outlook (under Rooms and rates, or the link under the Rates calendar). “What the coming ninety nights look like, and what they suggest. Nothing here changes a price - Rates does that.” A line at the foot says the same: “A suggestion never names a price, and nothing here sets one. Rates is where a rate is changed.”

What it suggests, and when

A night that isReads
14 days out or nearer, and 50% sold or less: Soft“Consider a lower rate for Sunday, 11 October 2026.”
85% sold or more: Filling well“Consider holding or raising the rate for …”
Anything else: On trackNothing.

Each suggestion's reason gives the figures, for example “2 days out, 47.06% sold, 9 of 17 rooms left.” The sold figures are the reports' own: complimentary rooms count, over the rooms that can be sold.

Nearby shows the lowest and middle price of the hotels nearby that night, and when they were checked, where Rivals' prices is switched on in Settings (Modules and connections). Tap it for the list. They are other hotels' public prices, never a price this hotel sells at.

  • Dates worth a look lists the soft nights, emptiest first, then the nearest. With none soft, it lists the coming nights.
  • New 1 day, New 7 days, New 30 days: how many of the rooms sold for that night were booked in that long, counted back from the property's own day. A dash where the records do not reach back that far, as on the demo.

Why it works this way

It shows and it suggests; a person sets every price: D17-56, D18-15. Soft is 14 days out and 50% sold or less, filling well 85% or more, as built, to be reviewed after a month of real bookings: D22-14. The nearby hotels' lowest public price per night, 30 nights ahead, checked twice a week: D27-270.

A15.7The Channel manager

Open Channel manager, under Distribution. “The connection between this system and the booking sites, through SU. Nothing is sent or taken until SU is set up and this hotel is switched on.” The GM sees what it does, what it still needs, and the bookings the sites sent; the Owner and an Admin also see the SU setup (A15.8).

What it doesIn the screen's words
Rooms left, sent outSell a room here and SU tells the booking sites, so the same room is not sold twice.
Prices and closures, sent outThe prices and closures on Rates go to SU as they change. A date with no price goes to SU closed.
Bookings, taken inA booking site's booking arrives as a booking, and its cancellation cancels it. Anything it cannot read waits for a person, with the reason.
  • What it still needs before it goes live, as the screen lists it: SU's test account and its keys in the server's settings; SU's certification; the room types and meal plans matched to SU's ids; each booking site's SU code, picked on Booking sources; this hotel switched on in Settings; and one rate everywhere or a rate per channel, still to be decided.
  • Booking sites and their SU codes: each booking site recorded on Booking sources, with its code. “No SU code: its bookings wait for a person” or “…not one of SU's codes: its bookings wait for a person” means the code is to be picked on Booking sources.

Bookings from the booking sites

Every booking SU has sent is listed as it arrived, with the guest, the site, the dates, the rooms, the total and what became of it: Booked, Changed, Cancelled, Refused: no room free, Needs somebody. Until the first arrives it says “SU has not sent a booking yet.”

  1. A booking Refused: no room free was for a room no longer free: it was not made here, and the site was told there is nothing left. Settle it with the site and the guest.
  2. A booking that Needs somebody says why underneath. Deal with it.
  3. Tap I have dealt with this. It is marked Dealt with.

Why it works this way

The channel manager is SU: D17-66, built D27-178. A booking for a room no longer free is not made, and listed for the GM to settle: D17-80. Each booking site's SU code is chosen on Booking sources, nothing hard-wired: D27-183. A date with no price goes to SU closed: D17-81.

A15.8Setting up SU (the Owner and an Admin)

The SU setup is on the Channel manager, in the order it is needed. Nothing is suggested or filled in from a name: each id is typed, each SU type is picked. Saving sends nothing: sending is its own button.

  1. SU login. Until the owner adds SU's keys to the server's settings, it reads Not set up. Then tap Check the login: “SU accepted the login.”
  2. This hotel on SU. The address, phone and email come from the hotel record (the Properties screen); the PIN code and map point from Settings, on the Property tab. Type the SU hotel id (up to 20 letters, digits and hyphens), the Country (its two-letter code), the contact's first and last name and the Description. Tap Save hotel details.
  3. Room types. For each room type, type its SU room id, pick its SU room type, type Children, at most, tick Send to SU, and tap Save with its name.
  4. Meal plans. The same for each meal plan: SU rate plan id, SU meal plan, Send to SU, Save.
  5. Send to SU. It lists what SU still needs first. When nothing is missing, tap Send to SU: it sends the hotel, its room types and meal plans marked Send to SU, and no prices or rooms left.
  6. Rooms left, prices and closures. Tap Send a year when the hotel first goes on SU. After that only what changed is sent, on its own every minute once the hotel is switched on; Send what changed sends it now.

Watch out

  • A room type with no rack rate cannot be listed on SU.
  • A wrong match oversells the wrong room type: check each SU id against SU's own.
  • Where a meal plan has no price of its own, the room type's rack rate goes to SU, so the room keeps selling; where there is no price at all, the date goes to SU closed. The card then says how many nights are selling at the rack rate, and from when.
  • On a server using SU's live account, nothing is sent for a hotel that is not switched on.

Why it works this way

The Owner and an Admin set SU up; the GM sees the status page: D17-85. The rack rate goes where a meal plan has no price of its own, instead of closing the date: D17-92; a date with no price at all goes closed: D17-81.

A15.9Contracts: companies and their rates

Open Contracts, under Distribution: “Companies and agents, and the rates each has agreed with this hotel.” Each row is a company: its GSTIN, city, credit, and its contract here. A travel agent shows Travel agent beside its name. Tap a row to open the company.

To add a company

  1. Tap Add company. “One record for the group: the same company at every hotel.”
  2. Type the Name, choose the Kind: Corporate or Travel agent.
  3. Type the GSTIN from the company's GST certificate (it prints on the company's tax invoices), the Billing address, City, State and PIN code.
  4. Type the Contact person, Phone and Email.
  5. Switch on Credit allowed only if the company may pay later: “A bill may be sent to the company to pay later (Bill to company).” Then type Credit days and Credit limit (₹), or leave them blank.
  6. Tap Add company. The company opens.

Reception adds a company with its name, GSTIN and address only, for the tax invoice: “Credit and contracts are set by the owner, an administrator or the GM.”

To add a contract (the Owner, an Admin or the GM)

  1. Open the company and tap Add contract. “The contract in force on the arrival date prices the booking.”
  2. Type a Name (the company and the year), and choose Valid from and Valid to.
  3. Under Priced by, choose:
    • Fixed rates: for each room type and meal plan, the Single (₹) and Double (₹) rate. “Per room per night, before tax. Single is one guest, double two; a third guest pays the extra-person price on Rates. Blank is not agreed: the booking takes the day's price.”
    • Or Discount off the day's rate: the Discount (%), taken off the price on Rates for the arrival date.
  4. For a travel agent, type the Commission (%). Add Notes if needed.
  5. Tap Add contract. “The next booking for this company is priced by it. Bookings already made keep their rate.”
  • A contract shows on the company with its dates, In force while it runs, and Edit.
  • When a booking names the company, its contract in force on the arrival date prices every night; the booking line says “Contract: …”. A rate typed on the booking stays as typed.

Watch out

  • A contract rate is an amount above 0: “A contract rate is an amount above 0. Leave it blank where none is agreed.” A discount is above 0 and at most 100.
  • A contract rate is always before GST: the booking's “Rate includes GST” tick does not apply to it (“Contract rates are before GST”).
  • Credit days and the credit limit are shown, not enforced, until the company's payments are recorded.

Why it works this way

Fixed rates per room type and meal plan, single and double, or a percentage off the day's rate; the contract in force on arrival prices every night; no contract figure is the day's price; the Owner, an Admin and the GM keep contracts: D27-184. A contract rate is never split for GST: D27-233.

A15.10Rate work in short

WhenDoSection
Checking the fortnightRates: each day's price, rooms left, how it sold.A15.2
A price changesTap the base on the day; Set prices for a run of days.A15.3
A plan or a second guest shows a dashHow rates are built, Edit: set its add-on.A15.4
A date to close, or a minimum stayRates, Rooms left, tap the day, Apply.A15.5
Which nights are softRevenue outlook: What to consider, Dates worth a look. Change the price on Rates.A15.6
A booking site's booking refused or waitingChannel manager: settle it, then I have dealt with this.A15.7
A booking site's bookings wait for a personBooking sources: pick its SU code.A15.7
A company agrees a rateContracts: open the company, Add contract.A15.9
Chapter A16

Across properties

For the owner, an Admin and the general manager. How to see every property on one page, read and edit a property's details, add a property, and run the people who work in each one: adding them, giving them a property and a role, setting their password, and switching them off.

A16.1The screens across properties

The Across properties section of the menu holds the screens that sit above any one hotel. The property switcher at the top does not change them. You see the ones your role uses.

ScreenWho uses itWhat it is for
All propertiesThe owner, AdminThe group today: every property added up, what needs you at each one, and a row per property.
PropertiesThe owner and Admin; the GM, hotel manager, revenue manager, Reception, accountant and viewer see their ownA card per property: its rooms and tax. For the owner also Edit, Close, adding a property, and each hotel's test hotel.
PeopleThe owner, Admin, the GM; the hotel manager can lookEverybody who can sign in, where they work and as what. Add somebody, give a property, set a password, switch somebody off.

One more screen is not in the menu: one property's page, /properties/5EL, with its figures and the people who work there (A16.5). It opens from Open on a property's card: the owner's, and for a GM or an Admin the card of a property they run.

A16.2All properties: the group today

Open All properties. The line under the title says how many properties there are, “each on its own business date”: a property that has run its night audit and one that has not are each shown on their own day.

  • The group today shows Occupancy, Average rate (ARR), RevPAR and Room revenue for today, with the Month so far under each, and the same month last year (Month last year; for room revenue, vs last year, the change in percent).
  • The rates are worked out from the group's totals, never averaged from each property's rate.
  • Last year counts only the properties that sold a room in that month a year back. “Last year: 0 of 1 properties” means none did yet, so the last-year figures are a dash. A new property never pulls the comparison down.
  • The (i) beside it says the same in one line.

Needs you

A property whose business date is behind comes first: “business date 9 Oct, 1 day behind today (10 Oct)”, with “Close the days in Night audit”. Then everything each property's bell asks somebody to act on: an arrival not yet checked in, money outstanding on a room due out, money to refund, a store never counted. Each line starts with the property's name. A line with › opens the screen that deals with it. When there is nothing, it says “Nothing waiting at any property”.

A row per property

Watch out

  • A figure that did not come back is a dash, never a zero. If the figures fail to load, the page says so and offers to try again.
  • Test hotels are never counted or shown here, and never in Needs you.

Why it works this way

All properties replaced the table at the foot of the Dashboard; last year compares only the properties that had one, and says how many: D27-243. Test hotels kept out of everything real: D27-296.

A16.3Properties: a card per property

Open Properties. What you see depends on who you are.

The owner and a group administrator

The line under the title counts them: “1 open”, or “2 open · 1 closed”. Each open property has a card; closed ones are under Closed, faded.

  • The card shows All rooms (every active room, blocked or not), room Types, the GSTIN, and the GST in use: GST on rooms, GST on restaurant, bar, banquet, spa, laundry and everything else. A dash means none is set.
  • Calendar switches to that property and opens its Calendar.
  • Close takes the property out of every picker. Nothing is deleted: its bookings, bills and invoices stay. It is off while guests are checked in, and the card says why: “15 bookings checked in - it cannot be closed until they check out.” Reopen, on a closed card, brings it back.

The test hotel

Under each open property's card, the owner and a group administrator see Test hotel: “A practice copy of this hotel's whole setup, with no guests or money.”

  • Make a test hotel makes it, once per hotel. Then the card shows its name with TEST, and three buttons.
  • Open switches to the test hotel and opens its Rooms. Every screen there carries an orange stripe: “TEST HOTEL · practice only · nothing here is real”.
  • Reset deletes every booking, bill, invoice, restaurant order, guest, company, cash entry, stock move and night audit made in the test hotel. Its setup and the people testing in it stay. Type RESET to confirm.
  • Re-copy setup deletes the test activity, then brings the real hotel's rooms, rates, menu and settings again. Type RE-COPY to confirm.

Clear this hotel and start today

For one account only: the one the server's settings name, which is the owner's own. Nobody else sees it, whatever their role, and the server refuses anybody else who asks. It is on every real hotel's card, under Start afresh: “Deletes every booking, bill and order here, after a backup. The setup stays.” Use it to start a hotel afresh once its practice is over.

  1. On the hotel's card, click Clear this hotel and start today. The window says what would be deleted, in numbers: bookings, guests, bills, invoices, payments, restaurant orders, functions, night audits, cash shifts, stock movements, and how many other records. When guests' ID photos are kept for the hotel, it says how many go too: “Also deleted, for good: 3 ID photos of guests, from Google Drive. The backup keeps the records, not the photos.”
  2. Read what is kept: the hotel, its rooms, rates, menu, tables, staff, sign-ins and settings. Invoice numbers carry on from where they are.
  3. Type the hotel's code (for example AMR) in the box. Clear and start today stays off until the code is typed exactly.
  4. Click Clear and start today. A backup of the whole system is taken first, then the hotel is cleared in one go: all of it or none of it.
  5. The window says how many records went, the backup's file name and whether it was copied off the server, and the new business date: today. Then, once the hotel is cleared, the guests' ID photos are deleted from Google Drive, and it says how many: “3 ID photos deleted from Google Drive.”

If Google Drive does not answer, the hotel is still cleared, and the window says how many photos are left: “1 ID photo could not be deleted from Google Drive now: written down, and tried again every hour until Drive deletes them.” The window never shows a guest's name or where a photo is kept, only how many.

It is refused, and nothing is deleted, while a guest is checked in at the hotel. The card names them: “A guest is still checked in at Hotel Amrapali: Ravi Kumar. Check them out before the hotel is cleared.” It is refused too when the backup fails, on a test hotel, which keeps its own Reset, and when the hotel has ID photos in Google Drive but the server's settings have no way to reach them, since the photos would stay.

Everyone else

A GM, Reception or an accountant sees only the properties they work at, and cannot change anything here. A test hotel they also work in shows TEST beside its name. Their card says Rooms sellable today: the rooms less the ones blocked today, so it can differ from the owner's All rooms. A GM or an Admin of a property also gets Open on its card, to its own page (A16.5), beside Open the Calendar.

Watch out

  • Close does not ask first. The property leaves the pickers at once. Reopen undoes it.
  • Reset and Re-copy setup cannot be undone. They touch the test hotel only, never the real one.
  • Clear this hotel and start today cannot be undone from the screen. What it deleted is only in the backup it names; getting it back is a job on the server. The guests' ID photos are not in the backup: they are gone for good.

Why it works this way

A property that has taken a booking must never disappear: its folios and invoices may have to be produced years later, so it is closed, not deleted, and never with a guest still in it. “Stay view” became “Calendar”: D27-82. Test hotels, one per real hotel, made, reset and re-copied by the owner and group administrators only: D27-296. The card's Calendar opens the Calendar, not Rooms; a GM or an Admin gets Open on a property they run; the two room counts have two labels: D27-308. A full reset for the owner's own account only, one hotel at a time, never while a guest is in, a backup first, the test hotels keeping their own Reset: D27-342, D27-365.

A16.4Editing and adding a property

To edit a property's details

  1. On the property's card, click Edit. The window says “These print on this property's invoices.”
  2. Change the Name, City, State, Address, GSTIN, Phone or Email.
  3. Click Save. If something is wrong (a GSTIN that is not fifteen characters, for example), it says “Not saved” and why.

The rest of a property's profile (PIN code, PAN, website, property type, stars, the map point) is in Settings. There a GM or Admin edits their own hotel's details; the name is a group administrator's to change (A17.2).

To add a property

  1. Under the cards, find Add a property.
  2. Type its Code: 2 to 8 letters or digits, such as NSK. Think twice: “It appears in every URL and every invoice number, and it cannot be changed later.”
  3. Type its Name and City; its State and GSTIN if you have them.
  4. Type the Provisioning key, the key for this system. The box says “Creating a property makes the hotel and its invoice series; its room types and rooms are added in Set up this hotel. Being signed in as an administrator is not enough on its own.” Your browser is told not to fill a saved password into it.
  5. Click Create the property. It stays off until the code, name, city and key are typed.

The message names the new code and says what comes next: “No room types yet - add them in Set up this hotel.” The new property starts with its own invoice series and no room types or rooms (D27-263, D27-322). The key box is emptied after each property. Under the cards a grey line says the same: “Creating a property makes the hotel and its invoice series; add its room types and rooms in Set up this hotel. The code appears in every URL and every invoice number and cannot be changed afterwards.” To go on, choose the new property in the top bar and walk through Set up this hotel (A17.2).

Why it works this way

Creating a property makes a whole new hotel in the system, so it takes the provisioning key as well as the owner's sign-in. The code is in every address and every invoice number ever issued, so it is fixed. The hotel's code, currency and time zone are the group owner's, and its name a group administrator's to change: D27-214, D27-308.

A16.5One property and its team

On a property's card, click Open (the owner's card; a GM or an Admin has it on the card of a property they run). The page shows that property's own figures, on its own business date, not the date of the hotel chosen at the top, and the people who work there. A group administrator can open it for any property, and a GM or Admin for their own; anybody else reads “This property is not yours to manage”.

  • A figure not measured yet is a dash. A property in its first week often has no month figures yet, and Average rate and RevPAR are a dash while nothing is sold, never ₹0.
  • FSSAI licence number: the owner, an Admin or the GM clicks Change, types the 14 digits from the licence (blank for none) and clicks Save. It prints on food bills from then on.
  • Starts on is Dashboard, Rooms or Calendar. Choosing one saves it at once, from the person's next sign-in. They can change it themselves.
  • A person with no password yet shows “No password yet” in red: they cannot sign in until one is set (the key).
  • Remove asks first, as on People (A16.6).

To add somebody at this property

  1. Click Add somebody here. The window says “They can sign in straight away, and they see this property only.”
  2. Type Their name and The email they sign in with. “A typo here means they cannot sign in at all.”
  3. Type A password for them: at least 8 characters (10 for an Owner, Admin or GM). It is hidden as you type; Show lets you read it back to them.
  4. Choose What they do here. It starts on Reception, as on People.
  5. Click Add. Tell them the password and the address yourself: nothing is emailed.

Why it works this way

The person, their password and their role are one act: split into three, somebody stopped halfway can sign in and see nothing. The page answers only a property you run, because it carries the property's GSTIN and contact details.

A16.6People: everyone, where they work, and as what

Open People. The line under the title counts them: “14 active · 3 can reach every property”. The owner and the other group administrators see everybody; anybody else sees themselves and the people they share a property with.

  • Every property: “A group administrator reaches every property, including ones added later. Property grants do not apply to them.” This screen cannot make one.
  • Each property chip reads the code and the role there: “5EL · Reception”. A test hotel's chip carries TEST.
  • “No password yet” in red: “No sign-in account yet - they cannot get in at all. Set a password and they can.”
  • Two-step on in green: they sign in with a code from their phone as well (A0.1). Only the owner, and an Admin for the people at their hotel, see it, with Two-step off beside it for a lost phone: it asks why, the reason goes into the audit log, and they set it up again (A17.13).
  • You see a button only where you may use it. A GM leaves the hotel's Owner and Admin alone, and nobody takes away their own access or switches themselves off.

To take a property away from somebody

  1. Click the ✕ on the chip.
  2. It asks “Remove Agra Clerk from 5EL?”: “They can no longer work at 5EL. Their account stays, and their name stays on everything they did there.”
  3. Click Remove, or Cancel.

To switch somebody off

Click Deactivate on their card. They can no longer sign in, and their name stays on everything they did. Their card fades and reads Switched off; Bring them back lets them sign in again. Once somebody is switched off, Everybody / Switched off at the top shows them on their own.

Watch out

  • Deactivate does not ask first. It works at once. Bring them back undoes it.
  • Nobody is ever deleted. A person who has left is switched off.
  • Somebody added with no property signs in to an empty system. The yellow note at the top names them until they have one.

Why it works this way

The activity log names people, so deleting one would leave entries nobody can read: they are switched off instead. Removing a person's access asks first: D27-117. Nobody switches their own access off: D24-19. Nobody runs somebody above them: the owner, 24 September. The Switched off filter: D27-243.

A16.7Adding somebody, and giving them a property

Access is per property. That is what stops one hotel seeing another's guests.

The owner: add, then give a property

  1. On People, click Add somebody.
  2. Type Their name and The email they will sign in with. “This is the link between the person and the account. A typo here means they cannot sign in at all.”
  3. Type A password for them, at least 8 characters. It is hidden; Show lets you read it back to them.
  4. Click Add. The message says “They can sign in now. Give them a property next - until then the app opens empty for them.”
  5. On their card, click Give a property. Choose Which property and Doing what. The line under it says what that role does.
  6. Click Give access. The message says “Pune Clerk can now work at 5EL”, and as what.
  • Only properties they do not already have are offered. Somebody can work at more than one property, with a role at each.
  • Test (the owner and a group administrator): in Add somebody, switch on Test, “For practising in a test hotel, never a real one.” The window then asks where they work, from the test hotels only, and as what. They work only in the test hotel, never the real one. With no test hotel yet, it says “There is no test hotel yet. Make one on Properties first.” (A16.3).

The GM, or a hotel's Admin: add somebody at your hotel

  1. On People, click Add somebody.
  2. Type their name, email and password, as above. The window says “Set them a password, where they work and what they do, and they can sign in straight away.”
  3. Choose Where they work (your own hotel) and Doing what.
  4. Click Add. They can sign in at once, at that property, in that role.

The roles, as the picker describes them

RoleWhat the screen says it does
OwnerEvery property, and the settings that govern them
AdminRuns the system day to day, including accounts
General ManagerEverything at this property, and the night audit
Hotel ManagerThe property day to day, without the money decisions
Revenue ManagerThe picker has no sentence for it yet. Its job: prices, restrictions and what the booking sites sell; no bills, guests or staff.
ReceptionBookings, check-in, bills, the cash drawer
HousekeepingRoom status and work orders
Kitchen ManagerThe pass and the menu
ChefThe pass - moves dishes along, touches no money
WaiterOrders, KOTs, bills and payment; the restaurant's day end
BarThe waiter's work, on the bar's menu only
Inventory ManagerStock, receiving and issues. Raises purchases
AccountantInvoices, the city ledger and the reports
ViewerCan look, cannot change anything

Watch out

  • The email is the whole sign-in. Type the address they actually use. It cannot be changed afterwards on this screen.
  • Nothing is emailed. Tell them the password and the address yourself.
  • A password for an Owner, Admin or GM role is at least 10 characters; for anybody else, 8.
  • A GM's picker never holds Owner or Admin. Only the owner makes somebody an Admin.

Why it works this way

People works for the GM, for their own hotel only: D22-3. Only the owner makes an Admin; the GM and a hotel's Admin make none: D22-2, D27-140. Somebody who reaches every property is a group administrator, and making one takes the provisioning key. The Test switch: D27-296. Password lengths: D27-243.

A16.8A new password, and a person's details

To set somebody's password

  1. On their card, click Password (Set a password if they have none yet).
  2. The window is “New password for Agra Clerk”: “Their old one stops working immediately.”
  3. Type the Password: at least 8 characters, 10 for the owner, an Admin or a GM. They type it at a terminal in front of guests, so choose something they can remember. Show lets you read it back.
  4. Click Set it. Then tell them: “Nothing is emailed - tell them yourself.”

The owner and a group administrator can set anybody's password; a GM or a hotel's Admin, the people at their hotel, never a group administrator's. If it is refused, the message says why.

To change a person's name, phone or first screen

  1. On their card, click Edit.
  2. Change the Name or Phone.
  3. Choose where they Starts on: Dashboard, Rooms or Calendar, the first screen after they sign in. They can change it themselves.
  4. Click Save.
  • “Their name is on everything they have done. The email is how they sign in and cannot be changed here.” The window shows it as “Signs in as agra@fidato.in.”
  • A group administrator's Edit has no Starts on: they set their own from their account menu.

Why it works this way

The password is typed, not emailed, because many of a hotel's staff have no address they read. A misspelt name is on every folio and every line of the activity log, so it is corrected here, not left.

A16.9In short

WhenDoSection

Chapter A17

Settings

For the owner, an Admin and the GM. How the hotel is set up: its profile, the step-by-step walk-through that takes a new hotel to its first booking, logo and pictures, policies, rooms, rate plans and taxes, the money lists, the lists the desk picks from, the front desk's times and rules, guest messages and report emails, people and security, and the modules and outside connections. Every other screen reads what is set here.

A17.1The Settings space and its menu

Settings is a space of its own (A0.4). Click Settings in the switcher at the top. Its menu has nine groups. A group is drawn only when it holds something you may open, and a page shows only what can be changed there.

GroupPages (↗ opens a Front office screen)Section
PropertyProfile, Set up this hotel, Logo and photos, Highlights, Cancellation terms ↗ (A2), Amenities, Group, Policies, DocumentsA17.2 to A17.4
RoomsRoom typesA17.5
Rates and taxRates ↗ (A15), Rate plans, Meal plans, TaxesA17.6, A17.7
MoneyBank details, Payment methods, Extra charges, Room discounts, Commission, Pickup and dropA17.8, A17.9
ListsBooking sources ↗ (A2), Market segments, Reservation types, Ready reasons, Holidays, ID types, VIP levelsA17.10
Front deskTimes and rules, Front desk rulesA17.11
MessagesGuest messages ↗, Reviews ↗, Online check-in ↗ (A10), Guest messages on/off, Daily report emailsA17.12
People and securityPeople ↗ (A16), Roles and permissions, Audit log, Activity, Sign-ins and devices, Signing inA17.13
Modules and connectionsModules, Channel manager ↗ (A15), CRS bookings ↗ (A2), Rivals' prices, Integrations ↗ (A12), Connection healthA17.14

Who sees what

  • The owner and an Admin see every page.
  • The GM sees the same, except Roles and permissions, Sign-ins and devices, Modules and Integrations (Figure A17-50).
  • Nobody else has the Settings space.

Watch out

  • Many switches save the moment they are tapped, with no Save button: an amenity's switch, a payment method's or a list's On/Off, the choices on Front desk rules, the guest messages' switches, the modules and Rivals' prices. Change them only when you mean to.
  • The hotel a page changes is the one chosen in the top bar (A0.5). Check it before you change anything.

Why it works this way

Settings as its own space, with its own menu, for the owner, Admin and GM: D27-249. Settings shows only what somebody can change: D27-220. The GM opens Settings; the module switches stay the owner's and an Admin's: D17-36.

A17.2Profile: what the hotel still needs, its details and its numbers

Profile is the first page. It holds three things: the checklist of what the hotel still needs, the hotel's details that print on its invoices, and its registration numbers.

The checklist

The yellow card “Before 5 Elements Akkalkot can take a guest” lists only what is still missing, each line with why it matters. Tap a line to open the screen that settles it. Nothing on it is ticked by hand: each line asks the system the same question the work it guards asks. When everything is settled, the card goes; it comes back by itself if something stops being true. Above the list, a link, Set up this hotel, step by step, opens the walk-through below.

A line that blocks means “until then a booking, a bill or the night audit will refuse and say so.”

The checkBlocks?
A real GSTIN (not missing, and not the standard dummy number)Yes
A GST rule for roomsYes
Room typesYes
A tariff on every room typeYes
RoomsYes
An invoice seriesYes
Address, phone and emailNo
Somebody who works hereNo
Cancellation termsNo
A tax heading on every menu sectionNo

Set up this hotel, step by step

The checklist says what is missing. Set up this hotel walks a new hotel from nothing to its first booking in 18 steps. It is second in the Property group of the Settings menu, under Profile; the checklist links to it, and so does the Dashboard's Still to do card (below). It is one page for the hotel chosen in the top bar. The owner, an Admin and the GM have it; for anybody else the server says “A hotel is set up by its owner, general manager or Admin, or by a group administrator. Ask one of them.”

The steps come in three groups, each with a count such as “2 of 5 done”: Must be done before the first booking, steps 1 to 5 (“These five are what the hotel needs before it can sell a room and bill it correctly.”); Before opening, steps 6 to 13 (“The hotel can take a booking without these, but should not open its doors until they are done.”); and Optional, steps 14 to 17 (“Worth doing, and nothing waits on them.”). Step 18, Ready to go live, is the summary.

Each step is a row: its number (a tick once it is done), its name, one line on what it is, and its state: Done, To do, Later or Remind me with the day. Tap a row to open it. It says What it is and Why it matters, and, while the step is not done and the system can tell, What is missing: “Still missing: the GSTIN, the phone.” Under them is one button for each real screen the step needs (Open Taxes, Open Room types) and the choices. A screen your role cannot open is grey, and a line says so: “Your role cannot open … Ask the owner or an Admin.”

#StepIt opensIt ticks itself when
1Hotel profileProfilethe GSTIN is a real one (not the dummy number), and the address, phone and email are set. A test hotel needs no GSTIN, because its paper carries none (A0.5): only the address, phone and email count
2TaxesTaxesthere is a GST rule for rooms
3Room typesRoom typesthere is a room type
4RoomsRoom types: Add a room, which can add several at once (A17.5)there is a room
5PricesRates, a Front office screen (A15)every room type has a price
6Payment methods and bank detailsPayment methods, Bank detailsa way of paying is switched on and the bank details are set
7Front desk times and rulesTimes and rules, Front desk rulesnever: the times start filled in, so only a person can say they are right
8Cancellation termsCancellation terms (A2)the hotel has cancellation terms; or you mark it Completed yourself, because charging nothing for a cancellation is a valid choice
9Charges, discounts and commissionExtra charges, Discounts, Commissionsomething is set: an extra charge, a discount, a booking source's commission, or an early or late fee. A hotel may rightly have none
10Booking sourcesBooking sources (A2)never
11People and rolesPeople (A16)somebody works at the hotel
12Guest messages and daily reportsGuest messages on/off, Daily report emails, Guest messagesa daily report is switched on, with an address
13ModulesModulesnever
14Logo, photos and highlightsLogo and photos, Highlightsa logo, a photo and a highlight are all there
15Group and house policiesPolicies, Groupnever
16The listsMarket segments, Reservation types, Ready reasons, Holidays, ID types, VIP levelsnever
17ConnectionsChannel manager, CRS bookings, Integrations, Connection healththe hotel is connected to the channel manager or the CRS, or Rivals' prices is on
18Ready to go liveno screen: a summarysteps 1 to 5 are done

Where a step never ticks itself, or the hotel has nothing to set, you say so yourself. The four choices:

  • Completed: shown only on a step the system cannot see for itself. The row then reads Marked done by your name and the day. On a step the system can see it is not offered, and the system's word wins over anything chosen.
  • Next: goes to the next step. It changes nothing.
  • Later: puts the step aside. It waits on this page, and on the Dashboard: for the owner, an Admin and the GM, a card Still to do (“Steps of setting up this hotel that you put off.”) lists up to four, then “and 3 more”, and links back here. It shows only while something waits.
  • Remind me: Tomorrow, In 3 days, In a week, or a date after today (“Pick a day after today.”). On that day the bell shows “Setup: Taxes” and “You asked to be reminded today.” to every owner, Admin and GM of the hotel, and opens that step. The bell and the Ready to go live lines name a step as this page does: step 5 is Prices in all three.
  • Undo: takes back a Later, a Remind me or a tick by hand.

Back to setup. A screen opened from a step carries a slim orange bar under the top bar: “Setting up this hotel: step 2 of 18, Taxes”, with Back to setup and a ✕. It stays on every screen you visit in that browser tab until you press Back to setup, which returns to that step, or close it with the ✕. It is not drawn on the Set up this hotel page itself, where you can already see the step, and opening that page makes the bar forget its step: the next screen you open by hand has no bar until you open one from a step again.

Ready to go live changes nothing. Once steps 1 to 5 are done it says “Ready to go live. The five things a first booking needs are done. Nothing is locked: change anything, at any time.” Until then, “Not ready yet. Still needed before the first booking: Taxes, Rooms.” Under it are two lists: Still to do, with the steps you put off first, each opening its step, and Done.

Watch out

  • A step's state is worked out each time the page opens. It is never stored, so it can go back: delete the last room type and step 3 is to do again.
  • Ready to go live switches nothing on and locks nothing. It is a summary. Every setting can be changed at any time.
  • The invoice series is not a step. It stays on the Profile checklist, above.
  • The GM cannot open Modules or Integrations (A17.1), so on steps 13 and 17 those buttons are grey for them, with the line about the role. The GM may still mark step 13 Completed.

To change the hotel's details

  1. On the Profile card, tap Edit. The window Edit 5 Elements Akkalkot opens: “These print on this property's invoices.”
  2. Change what is wrong: City, State, Address, Address line 2, PIN code (six digits), GSTIN, Phone, Email, and further down Property type, Stars, Latitude and Longitude (the map point: both, or neither), Reservations contact, Reservations phone, Website and PAN.
  3. Tap Save.
  • The hotel's name is a group administrator's to change (the owner, or another person who reaches every property). For anybody else the Name box is locked and says “A group administrator changes the name.”
  • Reservations contact prints on the booking voucher as “Contact”. Reservations phone, Website and PAN are kept here and print on no document.

The FSSAI number and more registration numbers

  • FSSAI licence number: tap Change, type the 14 digits from the licence (blank for none) and save. It prints on food bills.
  • More registration numbers: tap Add, type a name (a trade licence, say) and the number, then Save. Up to four.
  • Under them, Open on map once the profile has a latitude and longitude; until then “No map point yet: it is set with the profile's latitude and longitude.”

Why it works this way

The checklist derives itself and is a yes or a no with the reasons, never a percentage: a hotel opening on “80% ready” is usually missing the tax number that prints on every bill. The name is a group administrator's to change: D27-214, D27-308. The walk-through, 18 steps in the owner's order, each ticking itself where the system can see it done, with Completed, Next, Later and Remind me and a summary that locks nothing: D27-311. Back to setup stays until pressed or closed, a reminder shows to every owner, Admin and GM of the hotel, and step 15 opens both Group and Policies: D27-312. A test hotel's Profile step needs no GSTIN, Cancellation terms may be marked Completed by hand, the bar is not drawn on the setup page, and the bell and the summary use the page's step names: D27-316. More registration numbers in Settings only, never printed: D27-257.

A17.3Logo and photos, Highlights, Amenities

These three pages are what the hotel shows: its logo on its documents, and its photos, texts and amenities on the guest's own page, after the guest's code.

  • With no logo of its own, the hotel prints the group's (A17.4). The voucher PDF prints a PNG logo; an SVG logo shows on the bills, and the group's logo on the voucher.
  • Up to 20 photos. “Never a guest in one.” Until one is added, guests' pages show none.

A text left blank is not shown. Saved blank, it is removed.

  • Each hotel switches on what it has. The switch saves at once.
  • The list itself is the owner's and an Admin's: they add, rename, move up or down, turn off and delete. Everybody else sees only the switches.
  • Each room type picks its amenities from the same list (A17.5).

Why it works this way

One amenities list for the whole group, each hotel switching on its own; highlights and amenities shown to guests after the code, not on the voucher; plain text with paragraphs: D27-257.

A17.4The group, and the policies

  • The group's name prints on every bill after the hotel's name, as “by” the group. Blank for none.
  • The group's logo prints at every hotel that has no logo of its own.
  • Office details (Office address, Phone, Email, Website, GSTIN, Instagram) are the footer of every booking voucher and every tax invoice (printed and e-mailed, A4.11). Until one is typed, the footer is the hotel's own. The tax invoice also prints the group's logo beside the hotel's own (A17.3).
  • They are typed once, for every hotel. The owner, an Admin or the GM may change them.
  • House policies: tap Edit. One policy a line, in the order they print; at most 8, each up to 200 characters. With none, the voucher prints the booking's terms and the times only. The registration card prints them over the guest's signature (A3.9).
  • Policy texts: Parking and arrival, Family and extra guests, Reservation terms. Each has its own box (2000 characters) and its own Save.
  • The child ages are words only. Prices do not change with them: the desk types the number of children as today, and a child costs the room type's extra-child rate once the room's own places are taken. Not set: “the desk decides, as today.”
  • Cancellation terms opens the Front office screen where they are written (A2).

Why it works this way

The group's office details on every voucher's footer, the bank details and the house policies per hotel: D27-215. One Policies page; the child ages as words only, for now: D27-257.

Documents

Documents, last in the Property group, shows what the hotel prints and sends, one tab each: Tax invoice, Proforma bill, Registration card, Booking voucher and Restaurant bill. Each tab says when the document is printed, links to where that is set, and shows a sample: the real document with this hotel's name and address and a made-up guest, “SAMPLE · NOT VALID” across it and no GSTIN. Nothing on the page is saved or sent.

  1. Open Settings › Documents and pick the tab.
  2. Click Print a sample. The print window opens: pick the printer to test it, or Save as PDF to keep a file. The tax invoice prints in the hotel's copies (A5.9). The booking voucher opens as its PDF in a new tab; print it from there.

Why it works this way

The documents as the hotel's old system printed them, in Fidato's design, with a page to see and test each: D27-344. A sample is printed, or saved as a PDF from the print window: D27-348. The sample's figures are a sample's; nothing reads them.

A17.5Room types and rooms

Room types is what the hotel sells and what it sells it in. The heading says how many: “2 room types · 18 rooms, 18 sellable”. No price is asked here: a new room type is unpriced until its price is set on Rates (A15).

To add a room type

  1. Tap Add a room type. The window says “What the property sells. The rate is set separately, on Rates.”
  2. Type its Code (two to ten letters or digits; it prints on the tape chart) and its Name.
  3. Type Adults the rate covers (before an extra-person charge), Children it covers and Sleeps at most. If you need them: Adults at most (empty: only the total), Children at most (fewer than the total), Size (sq ft), Beds, View, Colour (on the Calendar and the rate plans).
  4. Tap Save.

A room type in use is not removed: untick Sold at this property at the foot of Basic instead. That is refused while rooms are still of this type; off keeps its bookings and prices.

To add a room

  1. Tap Add a room.
  2. Type its Number (at most 10 letters, digits and -; a letter is saved as a capital, so 111a is room 111A) and choose its Type.
  3. Floor: 0 (the ground floor) to 99; leave it blank if the property has one floor. Tick Smoking room if it is one.
  4. Tap Save.

Tap a room's tile to change it. Unticking Sellable takes it out of the sellable house; for a fault with an end date, use a block instead. A room with somebody in it cannot be retired.

To remove a room added by mistake

  1. Tap the room's tile, then Remove at the foot of its window.
  2. The window asks first. Tap Remove room 309 to remove it, or Keep it. It then says “Room 309 removed”.

Only a room nothing has used can be removed: no booking, stay, housekeeping, key card, block, work order, lost item, wake-up call, equipment or guest link, and nobody in it. A used room is refused and says what used it: “Room 101 has been used (a booking or stay), so it cannot be removed. Switch Sellable off instead.” Untick Sellable instead, so old bills and Form C keep it. A room type whose rooms are all removed can then be removed too. A room with a connecting door is removed with its door: the other room is no longer connected, and the window says so: “Room 309 removed. Its connecting door to room 310 was taken off.”

To add several rooms at once

  1. Tap Add a room and switch on Several rooms. Number becomes From and To.
  2. Type the first and the last number, each as the hotel numbers its rooms: letters, digits and -, at most 10, shown in capitals. The two are the same except one number that counts up, or the last letter: From 101, To 109 adds 101 to 109; A101 to A110, G01 to G12, VIL1 to VIL8 and A-101 to A-110 work the same way; From 101A, To 109A adds 101A, 102A and on to 109A; From 111A, To 111D adds 111A, 111B, 111C and 111D. Zeros typed in From are kept: G01 to G12 adds G01, G02 and on to G12. Anything else is refused with its reason under To: a To below From, “To is below From.”; two parts changing, 101A to 109B or A101 to B101, “Only one number (or the last letter) may change between From and To.”; more than 100, “At most 100 rooms at a time.”
  3. Choose the Type, type the Floor if there is one, and tick Smoking room if they are. These are the same for every room.
  4. The button counts them: Add 9 rooms. Tap it. The window then says what was added: “Added 8 rooms: 101, 102, 103, 104, 106, 107, 108, 109”. A number the hotel already has is skipped and named, “105 already exists, skipped”, and the rest are added. Tap Done.
  • The floor is the one you type, for all the rooms: it is never worked out from the number, and left blank it stays blank. For rooms on several floors, add one range for each floor.
  • With Several rooms off, Add a room adds one room exactly as above.

Why it works this way

Nothing in use is deleted: reservations, rates and a year of bills point at a room type, and every stay at its room. A new hotel starts with no room types, and a room type nothing uses can be removed: D27-263. Room types in Settings, with their amenities, photos and the rooms in order: D27-258. Several rooms at once: one range, one floor typed for all, a number that exists skipped and named, the rest added: D27-309. Room numbers with letters, both kinds of range, and always in capitals, so 111a can never be a second room beside 111A: D27-335. A range as loose as each hotel's numbering, at most 100 rooms at a time, and a room nothing has used removed (a used one only switched off, so old bills and Form C keep it): D27-336; a connecting door removed with its room: D27-365.

A17.6Rate plans and meal plans

Prices are set on Rates ↗, the Front office screen (A15). Rate plans and meal plans set how those prices are offered; they never hold a second price.

KindMeans
MasterThe base room on room only. Changing it moves every derived plan.
DerivedFollows the master or its own room only, by a difference or the meal add-on.
IndependentIts own base, typed on Rates.

A plan is named by itself: “Superior · Room only (EP)”. Switched off, its prices and bookings stay. Drag a plan by its handle to change the order.

To change a plan

  1. Tap Edit. The editor has three steps; the Summary on the right follows your choices.
  2. Step 1, What it is: the room type, the meal plan, the name and the meals. Tap Next.
  3. Step 2, Its price: choose how it is priced. A derived room-only plan asks how much more than the master, in ₹ or %. Tap Next.
  4. Step 3, Who sells it: tick the booking sources that sell it. None chosen: every source sells it. Tap Update.

Meal plans

For each plan, tick which meals are served on the Check-in day, the Stay-over days and the Check-out day, then Save. Until then the plan says “Not said yet.” The days show on the rate plan's summary and on the guest's voucher. The price of a meal is its add-on, on Rates.

Why it works this way

Rate plans as a tree over the one pricing, so there is one price to change: D27-251. Independent, a plan switched Off, meal days on the summary and the voucher: D27-258.

A17.7Taxes

Taxes holds the GST rules, “One set of rules, for the front desk and the till”. Each heading (Rooms, Restaurant, Bar, Banquet, Spa, Laundry, Everything else, and Alcohol where the hotel serves it) has its rates and its HSN/SAC code.

To set or change a heading's rates

  1. Tap Edit (or Set it). The window says what the heading covers.
  2. One row is one rate. In the first row, leave On everything from at zero and type the GST %.
  3. To charge more above a figure, add a second row: Above the figure, and its GST %.
  4. If a rate starts or ends on a day, type From and Last day (empty: always, and current). Write a Note: why this band exists. It shows on the card.
  5. Type the HSN/SAC code your accountant gives you: a SAC is six digits; for goods sold under the heading (bottled water in the minibar, say), its HSN, of 4, 6 or 8 digits.
  6. Tap Save.

The till's half

Watch out

  • Not set is not zero. A heading with no rate shows a dash and Not set, and nothing under it can be billed until a rate is set: the bill or the till refuses and names it. A laundry charge, for one, is refused until Laundry has its rate.
  • A menu section under a heading with no rate is named in a yellow line at the top of the card: “The till will refuse those items rather than bill them at nothing.”
  • There are no rates built in. Every rate here is the hotel's own, confirmed by its accountant.
  • Alcohol is VAT, not GST: one rate, one VAT line on the bill, kept off the GST invoice. Its heading opens only where Serves alcohol is on (A17.14).

Why it works this way

One set of rules for the desk and the till, so a bar's whisky is never billed at the restaurant's rate by a default nobody chose. A SAC code for each heading: D27-258; an HSN in the same box for goods, printed on the proforma bill and the restaurant bill too: D27-344. Alcohol as VAT: D21-91.

A17.8Bank details and payment methods

Bank details

The hotel's bank details print on its booking voucher. With none set, the voucher prints no bank details. The group's owner is told whenever they change.

  1. Open Bank details and tap Set bank details (or Change).
  2. Type the Account name, the Account number (digits only, 9 to 18), the Bank, the Branch and the IFSC (eleven characters, the fifth a zero). Add a UPI ID if guests may pay to one.
  3. Tap Save. The card then says who changed them last, and when. Remove takes them off the voucher.

Payment methods

“How guests pay here: what the bill, New booking and a function's bill offer.”

  1. Tap Add a method.
  2. Type its Name: what the bill and the receipt print (“Paytm”).
  3. Choose In the books: where the reports count it. A booking site that collected the money is Bill to company: “Agoda” prints as Agoda and is owed by Agoda in the City ledger.
  4. Tap Save.
  • To change the default, open a method with its pencil and tap Make default. The default stays On. Times and rules shows it as Way of paying (A17.11).
  • Drag a method by its handle to change the order.

Why it works this way

Bank details per hotel, changed by the owner, the GM or an Admin, every change told to the group's owner: D27-215. The default way of paying set on Payment methods; a booking site's payment counted as Bill to company: D27-259.

A17.9Extra charges, discounts, commission, pickup and drop

Extra charges

What a booking may add, and the early check-in and late check-out fees. The bill's Add charge picks from this list.

  • A fee left blank is no fee, never ₹0.
  1. Tap Add a charge.
  2. Type its Name and its Price. Leave the price blank when the rate includes it at no charge (a welcome drink).
  3. Choose the Bill's column: where the money lands in the reports (a cake under Food, a pickup under Other charges).
  4. Switch on A pickup or a drop if it is one.
  5. Tap Save.

Room discounts

Named discounts on rooms for New booking: a percentage or rupees off each night. By hand the desk may give up to 10% of a night, with a reason. A bigger discount is given only by picking one of these. They are for rooms only: the restaurant's discounts are Promotions, in Point of sale → Menu (A8), and a restaurant bill can also be discounted by hand by any amount, with a reason. The page was called Discounts until D27-395.

Commission

What each booking source and agent takes. A change applies to bookings made after it.

An agent's commission is set on the company's contract; Agent contracts, below the sources, lists them.

Pickup and drop

Airport, station and bus stand runs a booking may add. Each is an extra charge marked A pickup or a drop, added the same way. The time goes in the booking's note.

On all these lists: the switch turns one On or Off at once, the pencil edits it, and the bin shows only for one never used.

Why it works this way

Extra charges as the inclusions list plus the early and late fees, picked from the bill's Add charge; rupees off each night; free-hand discounts capped at 10% with a reason; commission per source on Money and a contract's on the contract; pickup and drop as extra charges marked so: D27-259.

A17.10The lists

The lists are what the desk picks from instead of typing. Booking sources ↗ opens its Front office screen (A2).

The list pattern

  • Market segments: who the guest is, for the reports, offered on New booking. A booking keeps its segment's words even if the segment is renamed or switched Off later.
  • Delete is refused for one something uses: switch it Off instead.

Reservation types

The colour of each kind of booking on the Calendar: Confirmed, Tentative (waiting for the hotel), In house, Due out, Checked out, No-show. Colours only: these are the states a booking can be in today.

Ready reasons

One tapped fills the reason box. Typing your own still works, and the reason is kept exactly as it was written.

Holidays, ID types, VIP levels

Holidays are shaded on the Calendar and Rates like a weekend, with the holiday's name on the Calendar. No price reads them. The bin beside one deletes it.

One switched Off leaves the check-in, New booking and the guest's online form. A document already recorded stays as it was.

A guest is one record at every hotel: marking a guest VIP asks which level, and the level travels with them. Each level has a colour.

Why it works this way

Reservation types as colours only for today's states; VIP levels one group list; ID types Off also leave the guest's online form; holidays shaded, with no effect on a price: D27-260.

A17.11The front desk's times and rules

Times and rules

A guest arriving before the first time, or leaving after the second, needs a reason. The charge reaches their folio unless the owner, the GM or a group administrator waives it, and the reason is kept either way. A late departure counts only on or after the departure date, and is recorded once (A1.6).

Night audit opens at (16:00 to begin) is the time, on the hotel's own clock, before which nobody can run today's night audit; a day already behind can always be closed (A7.3). Only the owner or an administrator can change it; the GM still saves the other hours.

  • An advance is never asked of a company's booking, a room the group's host pays for, or a booking prepaid on a booking site.
  • With The desk may overbook off, a booking (or a group) past a full house is refused.
  • Nationality: two letters, IN for India. Title: what a new guest's title starts on.
  • The GM may undo a check-in (on at every hotel to begin with): the GM may undo a check-in and cancel or void a guest in the house, and reception asks the GM to (A2.9). Off, a guest who has arrived is checked out instead, for the GM and reception alike. The owner and an Admin always may. The card above reads GM may undo a check-in: Yes or No.

Front desk rules

This page repeats the rules card at the top, then the rest of what the desk's screens start on and allow. Each choice here saves the moment it is made.

  • A new booking starts as: the desk can still change both on each booking.
  • A booking must carry: Phone, Email, Nationality, Address, Expected arrival time, Market segment, Business source, Sales person. A booking from a booking site is never held for them. Business source ticked is asked of a company guest only, and starts on their company; a normal guest, a walk-in for one, is never held for it (A2.2, D27-392).
  • Housekeeping: a room a guest leaves at check-out is always sent for cleaning. The switches decide the rest: a room a guest moved out of; a room back from a block (off: it comes back as it was before the block); and whether the night audit sends every room with a guest staying on for its daily clean.
  • The tax invoice at check-out (A5.9): Issue it and print it, by itself (the hotel starts on this), Offer an Issue tax invoice button, or Nothing at check-out: issue it on Invoices. And 2 copies (the hotel starts on this) or 1 copy: two print as “ORIGINAL FOR RECIPIENT” and “DUPLICATE FOR SUPPLIER”, wherever the invoice is printed. Who may issue an invoice does not change.
  • The restaurant's round-off: Manual: the Round off button, Automatic: every bill paid there, to ₹1, or Off: no Round off button. A restaurant bill paid in cash is always taken to the rupee. Room bills and invoices are never rounded.
  • How the figures count: occupancy = rooms sold ÷ rooms available; ADR = room revenue ÷ rooms sold; RevPAR = room revenue ÷ rooms available. Rooms blocked that night are not available. Two switches: A complimentary room counts as sold and A day use counts as half a room sold. The Manager report and the statistics reports (Monthly occupancy, Monthly statistics, Yearly statistics) follow them (A11).

Why it works this way

The default guarantee and bill-to, the fields a booking must carry (never refusing a channel's booking), the housekeeping switches, the round-off for restaurant bills only, and the figures in plain words: D27-260. The tax invoice issued and printed at check-out by default, in two copies, each hotel's choice: D27-344. The fees live on Extra charges, and the way of paying on Payment methods: D27-259.

Guest messages ↗, Reviews ↗ and Online check-in ↗ open their Front office screens (A10). The two pages here say what goes out by itself.

MessageWhen it goes
Booking voucherOnce, when a booking is confirmed: the voucher PDF, on WhatsApp and by email. It carries the check-in link only while Online check-in is on.

Review requestWhen a clerk presses Ask for a review, after check-out.
  • A switch saves at once and changes only this hotel. The wording stays in the sending workflow.
  • The tax invoice goes by itself only for an invoice made out to the guest, and only for invoices issued after the switch is turned on. One made out to a company, an agent or a booking site is not sent by itself: the desk sends it with Send invoice (A10).
  • Nothing here sends anything by itself: sending needs the server's connection settings (Connection health, A17.14).

Right after the night audit closes the day, each address gets one email with every report switched on for it: the subject is the hotel's name, "daily reports" and the date ("5 Elements Akkalkot daily reports - 26 Oct 2026"); each report's key figures are in the email under its name, and each report is attached as its own PDF. If one of an address's reports cannot be made that night, its whole email waits and goes, complete, once every report is ready. An address typed under one report only gets that report. There are five: Night audit report (on to start), Manager report, Money owed, Restaurant and stock and Bar stock (off to start; D27-354). Type the addresses, set the switches, and tap Save at the foot. Nobody gets anything until an address is typed.

Why it works this way

Fewer guest messages, the voucher being the confirmation: D27-264; the switches: D27-261. The tax invoice by itself only to the guest it is made out to: D27-313; the switch says so in its own words: D27-316. Each report its own switch and addresses, no address filled in for you: D27-280. One email per address, a PDF for each report: D27-371.

A17.13People and security

People ↗ opens the Front office's People screen, where people are added, given a place and a role, and switched off (A16). For the owner and a group administrator, Add somebody there has a Test switch: a person added with it works only in test hotels, never the real one. A test hotel is made, reset and copied again from its real hotel's card on Properties (A16).

“The live matrix. The menus, every disabled button and the server read this same source, so it cannot drift from what the product enforces.” Nothing is changed here. The owner and an Admin see it.

Append-only. “Nothing here is edited or deleted - a wrong posting is reversed, and the reversal is its own entry.” Each entry: when, the business date, the action (such as “Posted a charge”), what it was on, the detail, and who.

A guest's details read “changed”: the values are never shown. The GM sees their own hotel's changes.

  • When each person signed in, and on what device. Kept 90 days.
  • Sign out this device: that device must sign in again; the password still works.
  • The owner sees everybody; an Admin sees the people at a hotel where they are Admin.
  • A password is at least 10 characters for the owner, an Admin and a GM, and at least 8 for everybody else.
  • Somebody given the owner's, an Admin's or a GM's role with a shorter password sets a new one at their next sign-in.
  • Each sign-in is kept for 90 days: when, and on what device. The owner and an Admin see it under Sign-ins and devices.
  • Two-step sign-in (a code from a phone app as well as the password, A0.1): anybody may set it up from their account menu.

To require two-step sign-in

  1. Set up your own first: your name at the top right, Two-step sign-in (A0.1). The switch refuses until yours is on, so it cannot lock you out.
  2. Open Settings, Signing in.
  3. Switch on Required for the owner, Admins, GMs and Accountants.

From then on, each of them sets it up the next time they open the system, before anything else; everybody else is not asked. It starts off. Only the owner or an Admin may change it; the GM sees it greyed, with “The owner or an Admin changes this.” Every change is in the audit log.

A lost phone: on People (A16.6) the person shows Two-step on; the owner, or an Admin at their hotel, clicks Two-step off, types why, and clicks Switch it off. The reason goes into the audit log, and the person sets it up again on their new phone.

Why it works this way

Across the group for the owner and Admin only; who sees whose sign-ins: D27-245. One page, Sign-ins and devices, with Sign out this device: D27-255; the Signing in page names it so: D27-308. Test hotels, and the Test switch on Add somebody: D27-296. Two-step sign-in, off until required, the four roles, and the owner or an Admin switching somebody's off with a reason: D27-384, D27-396.

Channel manager ↗ (A15), CRS bookings ↗ (A2) and Integrations ↗ (A12) open their Front office screens.

  • The owner and an Admin only. A switch saves at once: “Turned on” or “Turned off”.
  • The modules: Point of sale, Banquet hall, Reception can use the POS, Channel manager, Laundry, Spa, Serves alcohol, Loyalty, Bar stock. Each says under it what Off does. For most, the screens go and the server refuses them: not just a hidden menu entry. Point of sale off also stops an outside till posting bills to this property.
  • Reception can use the POS off hides the point of sale from Reception only; every other role is unaffected.
  • Bar stock is on at every property open before release 14 until it is turned off; a property added since starts with it off (D27-369). Off, the Bar stock screen, Inventory's Bar tab, the bar bills, the Bar stock report and the FLR registers go and the server refuses them, KOTs take nothing off the bar's stock, and the night audit does not wait for a bar count. Bar KOTs still print at the bar (A9.11).
  • A second card, New booking, holds the sections that fold open on New booking (Company section, Notes section). Off hides one at this property; nothing already booked changes.

Switched on, each nearby hotel's lowest price on Google Hotels is checked for the next 30 nights, on Mondays and Thursdays from 06:00, the hotel's time (about 260 searches a month). What is found shows beside each suggestion on Revenue outlook (A15). Nothing here changes a price.

Every outside connection, for the hotel in the top bar: Emails (n8n), WhatsApp (Meta), CRS bridge, Firebase sign-in, Backups, Disk and Rivals' prices. Backups, the disk and Firebase are the server's own. The line under the list says whether the owner is emailed when a connection turns red. Nothing is changed here: a connection is set up on the server.

  • Disk says how full the server's disk is and how much is free. Needs a look from 80% used; Not working from 90%, because the database stops when the disk is full. Tell whoever looks after the server at once.
  • Backups turns Not working when last night's backup failed, when none has run for 26 hours, or, once copies have been going to the off-site bucket, when none has gone for 26 hours. Once restore to any minute is switched on, also when the database's change journal or its weekly base copy is not reaching the bucket. Also when the nightly copy of the uploaded files (bill photos, receipts) or n8n's own nightly copy failed or has not run for 26 hours; Needs a look while either has no bucket link, and the line says which stays on the server's disk only.

Why it works this way

The module switches are the owner's and an Admin's: D17-36. Rivals' prices, 30 nights twice a week, the lowest public price: D27-270. One page for every outside connection: D27-276. The disk and the off-site copies watched there too: D27-373 (plan A, A2).
