Chapter B1

The system at a glance

For the owner. What runs where, what talks to what and why it was built that way, one booking's journey through all of it, what watches it, and the risks that come with the shape it has. The rest of Part B goes into each part.

B1.1The parts, in one picture

Fidato PMS is three things you own and run, and a handful of outside services it talks to. Staff use it in a web browser; nothing is installed on their computers. The website is only the screens. Every figure, every rule and every check lives on one server, in the API and the database behind it.

B1.2What each part is, and why it is there

PartWhere it runsWhat it does
The websiteGoogle's Firebase Hosting, pms.fidatohotels.comThe screens only. It reads the API's address from a small file beside it when it opens, so the server can move without rebuilding the website.
Sign-inGoogle's Firebase AuthenticationAnswers "who are you": an email and a password. It does not know anybody's role or hotel.
The APIThe Oracle server, api.fidatohotels.com, behind nginx with its certificateAnswers "what may you do": every write and every read asks your role at the hotel in the address (B2.3). It is the only thing that talks to the database. It also has three doors with no person behind them: the guest's page, outside tills and SU.
The databasePostgreSQL 16 on the same serverThe record: bookings, guests, bills, payments, prices, the menu, the stock, every setting. Money is kept to the paisa; nothing on a bill is ever overwritten (B3).
n8nThe same server, in a container of its own, n8n.fidatohotels.comThe messages. The PMS decides what goes and when; n8n holds the wording, the mailbox login and the WhatsApp login, and sends. It also holds the workflow that keeps guests' ID photos in Google Drive, encrypted.
BackupsThe same serverAt 03:00 the database is backed up, restored into a scratch copy and compared figure by figure. The last 14 are kept on the server's disk.

Whose accounts they are: the Oracle server, the Firebase project, the code's repository on GitHub and the domain fidatohotels.com are all Fidato Hotels' own D26-4. When the system is sold, Influvate hosts each buyer on its own accounts, and Fidato's copy stays where it is D25-30 D26-1.

Why it works this way

  • The PMS is the record for rooms, availability, prices and bookings; the CRS and the other apps show copies D17-28. One record means one answer to "is the room free?".
  • A real database, not Firestore. Chosen at the start (docs/MASTER-ARCHITECTURE.md, 26 August): a hotel's day needs changes that succeed or fail together (a check-in touches the room, the booking and the bill), and sums over thousands of rows. Firestore, which the CRS uses, can do neither well and charges for every row a report reads.
  • Sign-in kept apart from permission. Firebase only says who you are; your role and your hotels live in the database, where the rules are. Roles never live in Firebase, so nothing kept there can make anybody an owner.
  • The website apart from the API. Several clients talk to the same API (the screens, the guest's page, outside tills, SU), so the API is the contract. The website needs no server of its own and is the same for every hotel.
  • n8n on the PMS's server, holding the words D17-29 D17-87: a message's wording, the mailbox and the WhatsApp login are changed in n8n, without a new release. The PMS sends the figures and the exact A4 PDF the desk prints D17-91 D18-20. Since 30 September every guest message goes through one workflow D27-98 D27-186.
  • Separate apps, joined by bridges, for good: the CRS stays the sales team's app and the leads app stays separate; the PMS reads them D27-27 D27-276 (7). That replaced the plan of 15 September for one combined system.
  • One server, for now D27-276 (1): the backups must reach storage off the server and a full restore is rehearsed monthly; a standby server comes once five or more hotels pay.
  • What the server records about itself stays on it: each request's time and result, errors and slow queries, kept 180 days, shown on System health; no guest data leaves India for it D27-91 D27-92.
  • When it is sold, each customer gets its own database on one shared server D27-278: there is never a "which customer" column, so one customer's rows cannot show up in another's screens D21-12.

Said differently in the documents

The documents call the n8n that sends guest messages "the CRS's n8n", because the CRS's own voucher workflow and its mailbox and WhatsApp logins live there (deploy/n8n/IMPORT.md). The release steps of 5 October open that workflow at n8n.fidatohotels.com, the n8n on this server (docs/go-live/RELEASE-5OCT.md, step A9). This book takes them to be the same n8n; no single document says so in one sentence.

B1.3The addresses

AddressWhat answers there
pms.fidatohotels.comThe website, for staff. A guest's own page is pms.fidatohotels.com/g/…, the same website D21-60.
api.fidatohotels.comThe API. /health says whether it is up. /api/guest is the guest's door, /api/pos an outside till's, /api/channel SU's.
n8n.fidatohotels.comn8n's own screen, open to the internet and protected by n8n's own sign-in; two-step sign-in is recommended for everybody who uses it D21-96.

B1.4One booking's journey

A guest phones the hotel, books two nights, stays, eats in the restaurant and leaves. This is everything that happens, and where.

#WhenWhere it happensWhat happens
1The desk takes the bookingWebsite → API → databaseNew booking saves the guest, the booking, its bill and the room held, in one step that succeeds or fails whole. The booking gets its reference, such as FH-5EL-2610-5033: the hotel, the year and month of the hotel's business date, a number D27-123. The desk ticks "guest agreed to WhatsApp" if the guest says yes D21-72.
2Within about a minuteThe server, then n8n, Meta and the mailboxA job on the server that looks every minute finds a confirmed booking owed its voucher. It draws the voucher PDF and hands it, with the figures, to n8n. n8n emails it, and sends it on WhatsApp if the guest agreed. The voucher is the confirmation, sent once D27-264. What was sent, or why it failed, is on the Guest messages screen (B5.2).
3Before arrival, if the guest wantsThe guest's phone → the website → the API's guest doorThe voucher carries the guest's own link and a QR code. The guest proves who they are with a code to the booking's phone or email, or with Google D27-207, fills in their details and may add a photo of their ID. The photo is encrypted and kept in Google Drive through n8n; the server keeps none D27-209. All of it waits for the desk D21-8.
4ArrivalWebsite → API → databaseThe desk checks the guest in, confirming the online details against the real ID. The first night's room charge and its GST go on the bill at check-in, on that business date D27-204.
5During the stayThe restaurant's Till, or an outside tillDinner is charged to the room from the Till (A8.7), or by an outside till through its own door. Laundry and spa charges go straight onto the room bill D18-7. Every line carries the hotel's business date, not the clock's.
6Each nightWebsite → API → databaseA person runs the night audit; at 5 Elements the GM, every night D21-77. It posts the next night's room charge, closes the day and moves the hotel to the next business date. The daily report emails go to the addresses the hotel typed D27-280.
7Check-outWebsite → API → database; n8n for the emailThe desk takes payment (the money rules are B3), and checks the guest out. On Invoices, the departed stay's bill is given its tax invoice number with Issue, with a VAT bill beside it if there were drinks D22-44. Where the hotel has switched it on, the tax invoice is emailed to the guest D27-284.
803:00The serverThe night's backup is taken, restored into a scratch copy and checked.

Two other ways a booking arrives

  • From the CRS. A salesperson books one of the group's own hotels in the CRS. Every five minutes the PMS reads the CRS's new bookings with a read-only login of its own, and each becomes a booking Waiting for the hotel, its room held. The hotel confirms it; then the one voucher goes D27-35 D27-171. Details in B5.5.
  • From a booking site, through SU. SU will push each booking to the API's own door the moment the site takes it D17-79; a booking for a room no longer free is not made, and SU is told at once D17-80. Built, not connected yet (B5.6).

Why it works this way

  • The message follows the booking, it is not part of it. A job sends it within a minute, outside the booking itself, so a slow or broken WhatsApp can never stop a clerk saving a booking. The cost: the voucher leaves up to a minute after Save, not the instant it is pressed (src/modules/guest-messaging/MODULE.md).
  • One door for every booking. The desk, the CRS and the booking sites all end at the same place on the server, so every rule (the room held, the reference, the voucher) applies to all of them, including a way in added next year.
  • The business date, not the clock, dates every line (B3.2): a bill settled at 00:40 belongs to the day the hotel has not yet closed.

B1.5What watches it

WhatWho sees itWhat it shows or does
System healthThe owner and AdminsThe server itself: its version, how long it has run, the database's size, the disk, each hour's traffic, the slowest requests, errors, each hotel's business date (amber a day behind, red two or more) and the last backup D27-91 D27-113 D27-114.
Connection healthThe owner, Admins and GMsEvery outside connection green, amber, red or "Not set up", with its last success and last error D27-276 (3). Figure B5-01.
The alert emailOne address in the server's settingsWhen a connection turns red, one email, at most once an hour per connection, by email only D27-276 (3).
n8n's alerts workflowThe owner, on WhatsAppA failed or missing nightly backup, and the API not answering D27-20.
UptimeRobotThe owner, by emailA free outside check that the API and n8n answer, for the one case n8n cannot report: the server itself down D27-20.
The logsKept on the serverA year of the API's, the web server's and the database's logs D27-21.

B1.6The risks that come with this shape

Watch out

  • One server holds everything: the API, the database, n8n and the backups. If it is lost, everything stops until it is rebuilt. There is no standby yet D27-276 (1).
  • The backups are on that same server. Copies off it, to Oracle Object Storage in Fidato's own account, were chosen D27-18 D27-19, then put on hold D27-285 (5). A read-only check of the live server on 4 October found the upload setting empty: every night's backup says "this copy is on this disk only" (MEMORY 385). Until the copies go off the server, losing the server loses the backups with it.
  • The Oracle account stays on its free tier D27-285 (4). Oracle may take back a free server that looks idle; the owner chose this knowing it.
  • n8n watches the box it runs on. If the server goes down, n8n cannot say so; UptimeRobot is the outside backstop D27-20. Whether it has been set up is not recorded in the documents. And the same check of 4 October found the backup's alert address empty too, so a failed backup on live tells nobody until it is filled in (MEMORY 385; deploy/README.md, Backups).
  • If n8n stops, nothing is sent, but nothing else stops: bookings, bills and check-ins go on, and each message is tried again, up to three times (B5.2).
  • If Firebase sign-in stops answering, nobody can sign in. Connection health shows it red.

Left out, and why

  • A standby server: once five or more hotels pay D27-276 (1).
  • Online payments: guests pay at the desk for now D17-57 D25-36; planned for after the release of early October D27-239.
  • Our own booking engine: SU's booking engine is used instead D27-180.
  • Desktop and phone apps: the web version first; the apps later D21-98.
  • Electronic invoicing (IRN): required only above ₹5 crore turnover; the group is under it (deploy/README.md).
  • One merged system with the CRS and the leads app: they stay separate apps D27-276 (7).

This book describes the system as it is on the development computer (branch cp6). What is on the live server, and how a release gets there, is chapter B9.

Chapter B2

People and security

For the owner. The roles and who sees what, how a person signs in and on which devices, the three locks every request passes, how each hotel's data is kept apart, the record of who did what, and why the test sign-ins can never reach the live system.

B2.1The roles

Every person has a role at each hotel they work at. The list of roles is one list for the whole group, not one per hotel D22-24. A person can hold different roles at two hotels, for example GM at one and Reception at another; the screens and the server both use the role at the hotel in the address D26-13. A group administrator is the owner at every hotel.

RoleWhat it is forDecided
OwnerEverything, everywhere.-
AdminRuns the system day to day, including people's accounts. An Admin at one hotel runs that hotel's people.Only the owner makes an Admin D27-140; a hotel's Admin D23-2

A fifteenth role, Automation, is for machines and is never offered when a person is added. The CRS reader and an outside till each work as such an account, at one hotel only (B2.4).

The restaurant has no row in the matrix, so the Waiter's and the Bar's columns show little more than View on bookings and rooms. A line under the matrix names the rest: “The restaurant is not in the matrix: the server lets the Waiter and the Bar in by name, for ringing up an order, printing the kitchen's KOTs, answering a table booking and closing the restaurant's day, …”, and that ringing up an order includes sending the KOT, printing the bill and taking payment D27-329; a discount is the GM's, the owner's and an administrator's D27-352.

B2.2Who sees what

The system has three spaces, Front office, Restaurant and Settings (A0.4) D27-249. The owner, an Admin and a GM have all three. The roles that work in one place have a short working menu of their own, chosen by the owner on 15 September; everything else they may open is still reached with Find a screen (A0.6).

In the Restaurant: Tables, Till, Terminal, Close restaurant day, only where "Reception can use the POS" is on.

Kitchen ManagerRestaurant onlyKitchen, Kitchen stock (to read), Menu, Close restaurant day, Guest requests, the Store, Notifications. Starts on Kitchen D27-378.
ChefRestaurant onlyKitchen, Kitchen stock (to read), Guest requests, Notifications D27-378.

BarRestaurant onlyTables, Till, Terminal, Close restaurant day, Guest requests, as the waiter. Starts on Tables, with the waiter's Start here card; sees only the dishes on the menu's Bar tab D27-329.
Inventory ManagerFront officeStore, Equipment, Purchasing, Notifications.
  • Restaurant, Banquet, Laundry and Spa are there only at a hotel that has them switched on; a section a hotel does not have is simply absent.
  • No Dashboard for housekeeping, the kitchen, the Inventory Manager, the waiter or the bar, because it carries revenue D27-141. The roles that read bookings but not bills see no balances, and a guest's phone and email come back blank to them D27-143.
  • Guests' ID and Form III details: the owner, Admin, GM, Hotel Manager and Reception only, the people who check guests in D25-38.
  • Where each person starts: the GM sets it per person (Dashboard, Rooms or Calendar) and the person can change their own (the owner, 14 September).

Who may do the acts that matter

Why it works this way

  • A shorter menu, nothing lost (the owner, 15 September): a new receptionist faced 47 menu entries and asked what to do. Their own work is in their menu; the rest is one search away.
  • One matrix, read by the screens and the server (Figure B2-01). Until 22 September it lived only in the website, and the server let any rostered person write anything at their hotel; the owner had it fixed before the first real day D21-88. Since then a menu and the server cannot disagree.
  • A control the server would refuse is hidden, not left as a button that fails D24-18 D24-27. And a screen the role cannot open names its menu entry: “You are signed in as Reception, which does not include Guest 360.” D27-5
  • Nobody runs somebody above them: a GM cannot change, switch off or reset the password of the hotel's Admin or the owner, and nobody can switch off or change their own access D24-19 D24-28.

B2.3Three locks on every request

  • Sign-in is Firebase's: it gives the browser a pass, and the API checks the pass on every request. Firebase knows nothing about roles or hotels.
  • The role gate is the API's. Every write, and since 28 September every read, finds its rule and asks the person's role at the hotel in the address. A route with no rule is refused for everybody, and a test lists every route the server has and fails on one without a rule.
  • Row security is the database's. Every table that belongs to a hotel carries the hotel, and the database itself shows a person only the rows of hotels they work at (B2.4).

Three doors have no person behind them and do not use the role gate: the guest's page (its link is the credential, B2.7), an outside till (its outlet key, B5.7) and SU (its own key, B5.6). Each of them still works inside row security, as an account at one hotel.

B2.4Each hotel's data kept apart

  • Every hotel's table carries the hotel, and the database applies the rule to every question asked of it, by anyone. The API connects as an account (pms_app) that can read and write rows and nothing else; it cannot switch the rule off. So a forgotten filter in the code still returns only the asker's hotels.
  • Guests are kept once for the whole group, on purpose: one person across seven hotels keeps their history, and a blacklist cannot be walked round by booking elsewhere. Their name and phone are shared. Their ID documents are not: they live in a table of their own, readable only at a hotel that holds a booking for that guest (migration 013), and only by the roles that check guests in D25-38.
  • Machines are scoped like people. An outside till, SU and the CRS reader each work as a service account at one hotel, so a misconfigured till cannot even see another hotel's guests. The CRS reader works as a Viewer at its one hotel, with no sign-in D27-286 (4).
  • When the system is sold, each customer gets its own database on the shared server D27-278, so no customer's rows ever sit beside another's.

Watch out

  • Customers' databases share one login (pms_app), by the owner's choice, with a check at start-up that the database belongs to the customer the API is set for D27-279 (1). The owner chose this knowing that a break-in at one customer's API could reach every customer's data (deploy/README.md, Add a customer).
  • A test of who sees what must run as pms_app: the database's superuser skips row security entirely and would pass any check. The isolation tests run as pms_app for that reason (MEMORY 47).

Why it works this way

One database, one set of tables, the hotel on every row and the rule in the database was chosen at the start over a database or a set of tables per hotel: those make the group's own reports hard and multiply every change by seven (docs/MASTER-ARCHITECTURE.md § 5). Adding a hotel is then a matter of data, never of building anything. One gap was found by use rather than by a test: the list of hotels itself was not scoped, so any member of staff could list every property and its GSTIN. It was closed, and no guest data or money had crossed between hotels (MEMORY 59).

B2.5Signing in, passwords and devices

  • An email and a password, kept by Firebase. The GM (or an Admin) adds the person on People, types their first password and tells them; nothing is emailed (src/modules/admin/MODULE.md). A forgotten password is reset by the GM on People (A0.1).
  • At least 10 characters for the owner, an Admin and a GM, 8 for everybody else D27-243. Somebody given one of those three roles while their password is shorter sets a longer one at their next sign-in D27-245.
  • Every sign-in is kept 90 days: when, and on what device. The owner sees everybody's; an Admin sees the people at their own hotel D27-245.
  • Sign out this device: the owner or an Admin can make the server refuse one device's sign-in from its next request D27-255.
  • Switching a person off on People also switches off their Firebase sign-in; switching them back on turns it back on D27-275 (4). A GM removes a person who also works at another hotel from their own hotel only; only the group administrator switches them off everywhere D23-4.

Why it works this way

  • No "sign out everywhere" and no "block a device": switching the person off already does both D27-255.
  • Adding somebody can never take over an existing account. From 9 to 15 September a GM could "add" the owner's email with a password of their choosing, and the sign-in service changed the owner's password before the database refused; the GM could then sign in as the owner. Closed on 15 September (migration 088): the address is checked before the sign-in service is touched. The lesson kept: something that cannot be undone happens after every check, never between them (MEMORY 263).

B2.6Who did what: the audit trail

WhereWhat it showsWho sees it
Audit logThe money: every line ever posted to a bill and every reversal, with who posted it, by name D17-14. Nothing on a bill is overwritten, so this is the whole record.Owner, Admin, GM
ActivityEvery change to every record: who, when, which record, what changed, before and after. A guest's own details read only "changed" D27-243.Owner, Admin, GM for their hotel; changes that belong to no hotel (a guest, a person, a company, the group's settings) under Across the group, for the owner and an Admin D27-245
Sign-ins and devicesB2.5.Owner; an Admin for their hotel's people
The server's logsEvery request, the database's sign-ins, kept a year D27-21.Read on the server

B2.7The guest's own doors

  • The guest's link is the only credential their page has. The server keeps only a fingerprint of it, and it stops working at 11:00 the morning after check-out (src/modules/guest-messaging/MODULE.md).
  • Before a code, the page shows only what a clerk would say across a counter, never the bill. The code goes to the booking's own phone or email, or the guest uses Google with the booking's email D18-13 D27-207. A phone that answered it stays unlocked for a day D27-169; a forwarded link asks again D21-6.
  • The QR card in a room shows the hotel and the room number only D21-14; reprinting a card stops the old one at once D21-16.
  • ID photos are encrypted with the hotel's own password and kept in Google Drive; the server keeps none D27-208 D27-209. Online, an Aadhaar photo must be masked D27-207. Once confirmed, a kept photo is seen only by the owner, Admin and GM, every view is recorded, and only they delete one, with a reason D27-210.
  • A typed Aadhaar number is accepted in full D21-17; screens show its last four digits and only the printed registration card shows it all D21-18. Whether the hotel may keep the full number is with the lawyer D25-37.

B2.8The test sign-ins never reach the live system

On the development computer the sign-in page has buttons that sign in as a test owner, GM or receptionist with no password. They exist for testing only (the owner, 14 September: "keep it simple for the local system; for production remove it"). Three separate locks keep them off the live system:

  1. The build refuses. Building the website for release fails if any trace of the test sign-ins is in the result.
  2. The live API refuses to start if the test sign-in is switched on with the production setting. It does not warn; it stops.
  3. The tests cannot reach the live sign-in service. The test runs blank the Firebase key, and a test fails if it ever comes back. On 15 September a proof run reached the live sign-in service and created two junk accounts before this lock existed (MEMORY 264).

The developers' Console, which can create properties and people, exists only in development builds.

Watch out

  • The server's secrets live only in its settings file: the Firebase Admin key, the sending workflow's secret, the CRS login, the ID photo passwords. Never in the code, a screen, a chat or this book. The Firebase Admin key passed through a chat once and is on the owner's list to replace (HANDOVER.md § 8).
  • n8n's encryption key is a master password for every login n8n holds: never pasted anywhere (HANDOVER.md § 5). n8n is open to the internet behind its own sign-in, so two-step sign-in there matters D21-96.
  • The two spare database logins (for migrations and read-only use) could still sign in on 4 October; they lose their sign-in with migration 202, in the next release D27-279 (4).

Left out, and why

  • Two-step sign-in for the owner, Admins and GMs: after this release, once the owner upgrades Firebase D27-243.
  • Roles per hotel: one list for the group D22-24.
  • A person's own "my devices": later D27-255.
  • The address a sign-in came from is kept, not shown D27-243.
Chapter B3

Money rules

For the owner. The rules every rupee follows: no price the hotel did not type, the business date, the taxes, the documents and their numbers, why an issued invoice never changes, rounding, discounts, and cash. What each rule protects, and what was deliberately left for later.

B3.1No default prices: a dash, never a zero

The system ships with no prices at all: no room rate, no dish, no add-on, no hall, no laundry item, and no tax rate. Every figure is typed by somebody at the hotel. Where nothing has been typed, every screen shows a dash (-), never ₹0 D17-16 D17-49.

  • A zero must be said. A price of 0 is refused unless somebody ticks Free; a blank is "not priced yet" D27-120 D27-192. A booking at ₹0 must be ticked complimentary, by the owner, an Admin or the GM D27-59.
  • No tax rate is invented either. A new hotel has no GST rate until somebody sets one (migration 136); asked for a rate that has not been set, the database refuses rather than charging 0% (migration 067). So a dish in a section with no tax rate cannot be sold, and the till says why.
  • Unpriced means not sold. A night or a meal plan with no price is not sold, and is sent to the booking sites as closed D17-81 D27-194. A new hotel starts with no room types at all D27-263.
  • Never a figure the database has not agreed to (HANDOVER.md § 5): the screens show what the server worked out, not a sum of their own.

Why it works this way

A zero is a claim that something is free; a dash is an honest "nobody has set this". A missing tax rate that quietly became 0% would not look like a fault, it would look like a bill (the comment in migration 067). The system once shipped prices nobody at the hotel had chosen, from its templates; they were taken out (migration 032; MEMORY 63, 65), and a "Rack rate ₹0" for an unpriced room type was found and removed later (MEMORY 246). The owner's rule since: prices are the hotel's, never the system's.

B3.2The business date

Every line on every bill, every payment and every invoice carries the hotel's business date: the day the hotel is still trading in, which ends when the night audit closes it, not at midnight (A1.1).

  • Everything before the night audit belongs to that business date: a check-in, a charge, a payment, even at 5 a.m. the next morning D27-200. A guest who arrives after the audit is on the next date.
  • A person runs the night audit; it is not scheduled. At 5 Elements the GM runs it every night D21-77. A hotel that forgets stays on yesterday, which is safe and visible: every screen shows one warning line while the date is behind D27-237 (4.2). Pressing it twice changes nothing D17-12.
  • Each hotel has its own date, and two hotels are often on different days.
  • A booking's reference takes the business date's month, not the clock's D27-123.
  • A time belongs to its hotel. The server runs on GMT; a time a person types is stored and read in the hotel's own zone (migration 113; MEMORY 297).
  • Dates print as 25/08/2026 on screens, PDFs and spreadsheets D17-77.

Why it works this way

A bill settled at 00:40, before the night audit, filed under the clock's date would land on a day the hotel has not reached; the night audit would close the day without it, and the day's cash would never balance (MEMORY 19). With one date for all money, the night audit, the Manager report and the bank deposit always agree.

B3.3Taxes

Tax is a set of rules per hotel, typed in Settings, one set for the front desk and the restaurant alike (migration 067). Each kind of sale has its own rule, and a rule may have bands by value.

KindRuleDecided
RoomGST by the value of each night: 5 Elements' rules are 5% up to ₹7,500 a night and 18% above. Worked out night by night, on each night's own price D27-162.The accountant confirms before the first real bill D21-65
RestaurantGST, 5% at 5 Elements. A dish shows the rate its section charges, or a dash where none is set D21-94.D21-65
BarGST at a rate the hotel sets; soft drinks and snacks at a bar are GST by their menu section D22-43.-
AlcoholVAT, not GST: one "VAT 10%" line, never split into CGST and SGST, kept out of the GST sales register, on a VAT bill of its own. Only at a hotel switched on for alcohol, off by default.D21-90 D21-91 D22-44
Banquet, spa, laundryEach its own GST rule; the spa's per hotel D18-21; laundry's refused until set, the CA to give the rate D27-194. A banquet function cannot be billed while its tax is not set D27-124.
  • Who sets the rates: the owner, an Admin, the GM and the accountant D22-32, in Settings or on the accountant's Invoices screen D23-1.
  • A rate change has a start date: a rule applies by the charge's business date, so a GST change on a date in the future is typed ahead D27-258.
  • The tax on a line is fixed when the line is made. A rate changed today never reaches a bill already printed (migration 067). One line carries one tax rate (migration 015).
  • Always CGST and SGST, never IGST: a hotel's supply happens at the hotel, whoever the guest is and wherever they come from (migration 025).
  • SAC codes print per kind of line: rooms 996311; the others a dash until the CA gives them D27-258; a banquet function 996334 with food, 997212 for the hall only, the CA to confirm D27-134.
  • The FSSAI licence number is a per-hotel setting printed on every restaurant bill and on a tax invoice carrying food, and frozen on the invoice when it is issued D26-11 D27-3.

Said differently in the documents

A room at exactly ₹7,500 a night: the decision list and the go-live plan say "5% below ₹7,500, 18% from ₹7,500" D21-65; the tax-rules migration (067), its tests and the "includes GST" split (D27-195) treat ₹7,500 itself as 5% and ₹7,500.01 as 18%. The system charges what the hotel's rule says, so the accountant's confirmation of the rule settles it.

B3.4The documents and their numbers

DocumentWhat it isDecided
Proforma billWhat the desk prints, and what the guest's own page shows, before the tax invoice, laid out as the tax invoice: the stay, every line with its HSN/SAC and its taxes (drinks with VAT), the payments, its exact total with no round-off, Paid, any night still to be posted marked "to be posted tonight" (on the desk's print only), and the balance due. No number: the booking's reference. The interim bill until 19 October.D22-7 D24-25 D27-126 D27-200 D27-204 D27-205 D27-344 D27-365
Tax invoiceFor one bill of a departed, settled stay: issued and printed at check-out, two copies (ORIGINAL FOR RECIPIENT, DUPLICATE FOR SUPPLIER), unless the hotel chose a button or Invoices' Issue (A5.9). Numbered from the hotel's series for the financial year: 5EL/2026-27/00001. The year's series opens itself with its first invoice. A company's invoice carries its name and GSTIN.D24-22 D27-344
VAT billFor alcohol, issued in the same moment as the tax invoice (or the restaurant's settlement), from its own series restarting each 1 April: VAT/5EL/2026-27/0001. Each names the other.D22-44
Credit noteThe only way to correct an issued invoice: its own number from the same series, a reason, one per invoice. Then a corrected invoice can be issued. A VAT bill is cancelled the same way, from the VAT series.D22-33 D22-44
Restaurant billINTERIM BILL before payment, BILL after, BILL · DUPLICATE when printed again (A8.6). It carries the GST lines but says it is not a tax invoice; the GST invoice is issued against the guest's room bill.D27-292
Booking voucherThe booking's confirmation, with its figures: each night's price, GST by the night's band, a dash where no GST rule is set, and the advance and balance D27-172 D27-215.

Why an issued invoice never changes

An invoice is a legal document the guest and the tax office both hold. The database itself refuses to change or delete one, whoever asks, even its most powerful account (migration 025: a trigger, because a permission could be bypassed). A wrong invoice is answered by a credit note with its own number, so both stay on record, exactly as a wrong charge on a bill is answered by a reversal line and never rubbed out. The invoice also states the tax that was charged; it never works it out again from today's rules (MEMORY 31). The place of supply, the hotel's state and its GSTIN are stored on each invoice, so a later correction to the hotel's details never alters an invoice already issued.

Not answered in the documents

A diner who is not staying at the hotel gets the restaurant bill, which says it is not a tax invoice, and has no room bill for a GST invoice to be issued against. The documents do not say how such a guest gets a numbered GST invoice if they ask for one. Worth putting to the CA.

B3.5Correcting money: nothing is rubbed out

A line on a bill is never edited or deleted. Every correction is a new line, with who made it and why.

The mistakeHow it is put rightDecided
A wrong charge, todayReversed, once, with a reason that stays on the reversal line. A payment is reversed only by the owner, an Admin, the GM or the accountant.D27-117 D27-125
A charge at the wrong price or wordsEdit (owner, Admin, GM): the old line reversed and the right one posted in one step, with a reason. Change rate for the whole stay corrects every night already charged.D27-157 D27-162
A charge on a day the night audit has closedOn the Night audit screen's Closed days: the owner, an Admin or the GM, this month and last month only, with a reason; the old and new figures are both kept, and the day's reports show the corrected figure.D22-18 D24-1 to D24-5 D25-5 D25-8
Anything on a bill that has its tax invoiceRefused: “This bill has tax invoice X. Issue a credit note instead.” Drinks with a VAT bill: cancel the VAT bill instead.D24-4 D25-7
A payment, refund or discount on a closed dayNot changed: “Its payments, refunds and discounts are not changed - put the difference right today.”D25-11

B3.6Rounding

  • Money is kept to the paisa, and the tax on each line is worked out on that line. Room bills, proforma bills and invoices are exact, with no round-off D27-126 D27-260.
  • The restaurant: a bill paid wholly in cash is always rounded to the rupee, with a "Round off" line, so the drawer never expects paise nobody took D27-129. Otherwise each hotel chooses its restaurant round-off: Off, Manual (the Till's button) or Automatic D27-260. A restaurant bill charged to a room or to a function stays exact.
  • A room type priced as a percentage of the base is rounded to the whole rupee D27-194.
  • A rate typed "Includes GST" is split into the price before tax and the GST, so the bill and the voucher add up exactly to the typed figure. A figure that cannot split exactly to the paisa splits to the nearest total not above it, and the line says so; a typed rate the bands cannot split (₹7,875.01 to ₹8,850) is refused, in words D27-187 D27-195 D27-199. A company's contract rate is always before GST D27-233.

B3.7Discounts, promotions and complimentary

  • Rooms: up to 10% by hand, always with a reason; more only by a named discount (Settings → Room discounts) D27-36. The restaurant: any amount by hand, with a reason, since D27-395. On a room it is rupees off each night, or a percentage D27-259. A typed room rate is not a discount and stays as it is D27-62.
  • Promotions start empty; the hotel names its own D27-57.
  • Complimentary: ticked by the owner, an Admin or the GM only D27-59. A complimentary room counts as sold on every report, as eZee counted it D17-72.
  • Loyalty points, where the hotel has loyalty on, come off the member's own room charges as a discount line; the earn rate is a setting with no default D27-179.

B3.8Cash

  • Every rupee belongs to a drawer D27-118. A receptionist's drawer opens by itself with their first cash after the night audit; the restaurant's opens on the float the last close kept, and only its very first day counts a float once D27-200 D27-201.
  • Every close is counted: expected against counted, a sentence for any difference, the float kept typed (above ₹0, with the next person's name), the rest to deposit. "What comes is what goes" D27-202.
  • Deposits: the GM records each day's bank deposit with the slip's photo; the owner or the accountant verifies it; a difference stays red until explained D27-190 D27-191.
  • Cash paid out (an expense from the drawer) needs a yes from the GM or the owner, never one's own; until then it is not taken off what the drawer should hold D27-242.
  • The legal limits: ₹2 lakh or more in cash from one guest for one stay or event is refused, counting the whole stay, a group as one event, and the guest's cash that day; above ₹1 lakh at one time the desk records the PAN or ticks No PAN: Form 97 taken; a foreign guest is not asked D25-40 D26-8 D26-9 D26-10.
  • Company payments are never cash: bank transfer, cheque, UPI or card D27-242.
  • More than the bill is taken only with the tick Hold it as the guest's credit, and is refunded at check-out; no money is held for a guest who has left D27-4 D27-11 D27-12.

Why it works this way

A drawer that opens by itself means nobody types a float every morning and nobody can take cash outside a shift. A difference never blocks a close, but it must have a sentence, because a manager needs the sentence, not the number. The cash limits are the law's (the Income-tax Act 2025, s.186, and Rule 159 for the PAN), applied the way the owner chose: by stay, group and day, so one large payment cannot be split to slip under them.

Left out, and why

  • GST on advances: an advance is a payment on the booking, with no receipt voucher and no tax on it, until the CA answers (docs/SELLING-IN-INDIA.md C2) D27-138.
  • Online payments: guests pay at the desk D25-36.
  • Other currencies: every figure is in rupees. A booking-site booking not in rupees waits for a person and is never converted D27-183.
  • Electronic invoicing (IRN): needed only above ₹5 crore turnover; the group is under it.
Chapter B4

Rooms and rates

For the owner. What a hotel sells and how its price is built: room types and rooms, the base price and its add-ons, rate plans and meal plans, the restrictions, and how the CRS's and the booking sites' room types are matched to the hotel's own. Why it was built this way, and what was left out.

B4.1Room types and rooms

A room type is what is sold: Deluxe, Superior. A room is where the guest sleeps: 201, 202. A booking is for a room type; the room is given at check-in or before.

  • A room type says who it sleeps: the adults and children its price covers, the most it sleeps, and the most adults and children; and its beds, view, size, colour on the Calendar, amenities and photos (Settings, Rooms, Room types). New bookings are held to its limits D27-258.
  • A new hotel starts with no room types: the owner or GM adds their own, as with prices. A type nothing has used can be removed; one that has been used is switched Off, hidden from new bookings, its history kept D27-263.
  • The GM sets up their own hotel: room types, rooms, their imports D21-47 D22-30.
  • Out of service is a dated block, from a date with a reason; the Rooms screen, the room count and every occupancy figure follow it D17-11. A room lived in by staff is blocked with the reason house use and no end date, which the owner calls "NC": at 5 Elements the GM's room, so 18 rooms, 17 sellable (the owner, 16 September; D21-64).
  • Occupancy has one rule everywhere, the Manager report's: rooms sold on the night (complimentary in; no-shows, waiting bookings and day use out) over the sellable rooms D27-151.
  • The desk may overbook where the hotel allows it (a switch, on by default) D27-243; a machine never may: a booking from the CRS or a booking site for a room no longer free is refused D17-43 D17-80.

B4.2How a price is built: a base and add-ons

Since 30 September a room's price is a base plus add-ons D27-188 D27-194. The base is what one guest pays for the room alone (room only, EP) on a date. Everything else is added to it, and the add-ons are set once for the hotel. So the daily work is only the base: change it on a date, and every plan on that date moves with it.

  • Two ways per hotel: each room type carries its own base; or one room type is the base and the others are derived from it by a difference, in rupees or a percentage (rounded to the whole rupee) D27-188 D27-194.
  • Counting guests: the base covers one guest; two guests (adult or child) add the double occupancy figure; from the third, each adds the extra adult or extra child figure, adults first. Every guest, children too, pays the meal plan's add-on D27-194.
  • A part nobody set is a dash, and anything that needs it is not sold, and goes to the booking sites as closed D27-194.
  • Nothing already typed moved. A price typed before 30 September is kept exactly as it was, and prices exactly as it did, with a Remove beside it D27-194. A hotel still priced only by the older rack rate keeps selling every meal plan at its room-only rack until a base and the meal add-on are set on Rates D27-196. (The local demo is priced that older way, which is why every meal plan in Figure B4-01 shows the room-only figure.)
  • Prices are typed as rupees, never invented: everything on Rates starts as a dash (B3.1).

The Rates screen

  • Everyone who may read prices sees Rates; only the owner, an Admin, the GM and the Revenue Manager can change anything on it, and the server asks the same question on every price it is sent (B2.2).
  • Each day's price sits above how that day sold: rooms sold, occupancy, average rate, revenue D27-188 D27-151. Every room type is always open with all its rows D27-237 (5.1).
  • The Calendar shows each night's base price, else the standard price, else a dash D27-274.

Why it works this way

  • One figure moves everything: the owner, 16 September, wanted the cheapest room to be the base and everything else "connected by a difference", so a change reflects all through the system. The first build (16 September, migration 090) took that literally: one base for the hotel and dated differences in rupees. On 30 September the owner simplified it to a base per day and add-ons set once: the calendar changes only the base D27-188.
  • Rupees, not percentages, was the owner's rule of 16 September for every difference. Since 30 September a room type derived from the base may also be a percentage; the add-ons stay rupees (migration 162) D27-188.
  • The base is not the default. The base is priced for one guest; how many guests a room is sold for by default is a separate setting on the room type, which the pricing does not change (the owner, 16 September, HANDOVER.md § 4).

B4.3Rate plans and meal plans

A rate plan is a room type on a meal plan, named by itself: "Deluxe · Room only (EP)". It is not a second price list: it is a view over the one pricing, drawn as a tree D27-251.

  • Master, Derived, Independent: the master is the base room type on room only; a derived plan follows it by a difference or a meal add-on; an independent room type has its own base D27-258.
  • Who sells a plan: each plan names the booking sources that sell it, none named meaning all; New booking offers only the plans the chosen source sells. The booking sites keep their own mapping in SU D27-258.
  • Meal plans: EP (room only), CP (with breakfast), MAP (one more meal), AP (all meals) and AI (all inclusive, everything charged to the room) D17-50 D17-68. RO is no longer offered; every picker shows the code with its words, "CP · Room + breakfast" D27-164. Each plan says on which days of the stay its meals are served, and the voucher says so too D27-258.
  • On reports, the "Rate Type" is the booking's meal plan; no separate plan names to keep up D17-95.

Prices that are not the day's rate

  • A typed rate on a booking stays as typed; the 10% discount rule binds only the Discount box D27-62. A rate may be typed "Includes GST" and is split exactly (B3.6) D27-187.
  • Company contracts: fixed rates per room type and meal plan, or a percentage off the day's rate; the contract in force on the day of arrival prices every night; a contract rate is always before GST D27-184 D27-233.
  • Day use: its price is typed on every day-use booking, never taken from the night's price, and a day use never turns into a night stay or back D27-229 D27-230.
  • Changing a confirmed booking's rate before check-in: the owner, an Admin or the GM, with a reason kept in the booking's notes D27-187 D27-195.

B4.4Restrictions

Beside the price, a rate setter can say a room type may not be sold, or not sold that way, on a date: stop sell, closed to arrival, closed to departure, and minimum and maximum nights (migration 044). They are set per room type per date, not per plan: a room not for sale is not for sale on any plan. They show on Rates' Rooms left, and go to the booking sites through SU.

Why it works this way

The owner's answer of 16 September: bookings from SU and every outside system are held to stop sell and minimum nights, and a price of 0 is refused unless complimentary; the desk keeps its own judgement, because a person at the desk can see the whole picture (HANDOVER.md § 4, "D10").

Not found in the code

The booking sites are held to the restrictions by SU, which receives them. The CRS bridge, the other outside system, refuses a booking at ₹0 as that answer says, but the code reviewed for this chapter does not check a CRS booking against stop sell or minimum nights. Worth confirming before the CRS sells into a restricted date.

B4.5Matching the CRS's and the booking sites' room types

The CRS and SU each have their own names and ids for the hotel's rooms. Nothing is matched by guessing: a person matches each one, once.

The CRS

  • On CRS bookings, the card Connection to the CRS (owner and Admin): the hotel's id in the CRS, the source CRS bookings are filed under ("Fidato CRS", made once in Settings D27-286), and each CRS room type's id with the room type it is here (Figure B5-02). The CRS room type ids come from the CRS's Firebase console D27-275 (1).
  • A CRS room type with no match is never booked by itself: the booking waits under "Needs attention" with the reason, as does one with no rate, or whose price per room does not split exactly D27-171.
  • The price is the CRS's quote, before tax, per room per night D27-171; the PMS adds the tax and bills it D17-46.

The booking sites, through SU

  • In the channel manager's SU setup (owner and Admin) D17-85: the hotel's SU id, each room type's SU room id and type, each meal plan's SU rate plan id. Nothing is suggested or filled in from a name.
  • On Booking sources, each booking site carries its SU channel code, picked from SU's list; nothing is hard-wired D27-183.
  • What goes to SU: rooms left, each price for each number of guests, and the restrictions, for a year ahead, then only what changed. A date with no price goes closed D17-81.

Two answers, depending on how the hotel is priced

A meal plan with no price of its own: on 18 September the owner chose to send the room-only rack rate rather than close the date D17-92; on 30 September, for a hotel priced the new way, an unset plan is not sold and is closed on SU D27-194, while a hotel priced only by the old rack keeps selling every plan at the room-only rack D27-196. The SU setup page says how many nights are selling at the rack rate, and from when.

B4.6Revenue management: suggestions only

  • Revenue outlook shows and suggests; it never changes a price by itself D17-56 D18-15. A night 14 or fewer days out and 50% sold or less is "Soft"; 85% or more is "Filling well" D22-14.
  • Rivals' prices: where the hotel switches it on, each nearby hotel's lowest public price per night, 30 nights ahead, checked twice a week, beside each suggestion D27-269 D27-270 D27-272. It needs the owner's data key in the server's settings.

Left out, and why

  • A price that changes by itself: never; a person sets every price D18-15.
  • Room categories (Deluxe and Deluxe valley view grouped under Deluxe), asked for on 16 September: a field for it exists in the database (migration 090), but no screen sets it.
  • Contract allotments: later D27-184.
  • Our own booking engine: SU's is used instead D27-180.
Chapter B5

Connections

For the owner. Every way the PMS talks to something outside it: the sending workflow in n8n, WhatsApp and its templates, email, the CRS bridge, the booking sites through SU, outside tills, the guest's ways of proving who they are, the leads app, and the provisioning key. What each does, what it needs from you, and what happens when it fails.

B5.1The connections at a glance

A connection is switched on by its settings on the server, which only the owner types in (they are secrets, and never go in the code, a screen or a chat). Until they are there, the connection does nothing, and the screens say so in plain words rather than offering a button that would fail.

ConnectionWhat it doesStateIf it fails
Sending (n8n)Every email and WhatsApp to a guest, and the alert and report emailsBuilt; on once its three settings and the pace are inNothing is sent; nothing else stops. Each message is tried again, up to three times
WhatsApp (Meta)The voucher and the check-in code, from one Fidato numberThrough the CRS's Meta account and its approved templatesMeta's refusal is shown on Guest messages; the email still goes
The CRS bridgeThe CRS's bookings for the group's own hotels, read every five minutesBuilt; per hotel, on its cardNothing is booked; Connection health turns red after 30 minutes
