The provisioning keyThe lock on creating a hotel or a group administratorMade once by the ownerWithout it, no hotel can be created

B5.2The one door out: the sending workflow

Every message the hotel sends a guest leaves through one part of the API, and from there through one workflow in n8n, PMS send · email and WhatsApp (CRS). The PMS decides what goes, to whom and when; it sends the figures as data with the exact PDF the desk prints, and n8n writes the message and sends it D17-87 D17-91 D18-20. Since 30 September that one workflow sends everything; the PMS runs no n8n workflow of its own for guests D27-186.

What it needs

  • Three settings on the server: the workflow's address, its secret, and the WhatsApp number's Meta id. All three, or nothing sends (deploy/n8n/IMPORT.md, part C).
  • The pace: how many messages a minute. It is the owner's number, from what the WhatsApp account allows; until it is given, the job that sends vouchers sends nothing at all, rather than everything at once D21-34.
  • In n8n: the mailbox the guest sees (until it is filled, every email is refused with a sentence the desk sees), and the template names (B5.3).

What goes

MessageWhen, and howDecided
The booking voucherOnce, when a booking is confirmed: by email with the PDF, and on WhatsApp with the PDF where the guest agreed. It is the confirmation; there is no separate one and no day-before reminder. Its PDF prints the guest's check-in link and QR code where the hotel has online check-in on. One per group, to the lead guest.D27-264 D27-235 D27-281 D22-41
The check-in codeWhen the guest asks for it on their page: on WhatsApp or by emailD27-207
The tax invoiceBy email only, when issued, where the hotel has switched it on and the invoice is made out to the guest; one made out to a company, an agent or a booking site only by the desk's Send invoice; never a credit noteD27-261 D27-284 D27-313
Daily report emailsAfter each night audit, each report switched on, to the addresses the hotel typed: one email per address, a PDF for each report; nobody gets anything until an address is typedD27-280, D27-371
The health alertWhen a connection turns red (B5.10)D27-276
The review requestLaterD27-266
  • Bookings made before sending was first switched on get their voucher too, soonest arrival first, but only between 09:00 and 21:00 hotel time; a new booking's goes at once, any hour D21-33 D22-42.
  • The desk's Send check-in link sends the voucher again D27-264.

When it fails

  • A message that fails is written down with the reason ("The receiver did not answer within twenty seconds", or the refusal itself) and shown on Guest messages, which the desk reads. A message never attempted is not written down at all.
  • It is tried again, the next minute, up to three times. Each try carries the same message id, and the workflow remembers what it has sent for 30 days, so a try after a lost answer never reaches the guest twice.
  • A booking never fails because of a message: the message is sent by a separate job, after the booking is saved.
  • n8n down, or the server's n8n unreachable: every message fails the same way and Connection health turns Emails red after three failures in a row. On 16 September it was found that every deploy had been cutting n8n off from the network without anybody noticing; the service that puts its network back after a deploy was switched on then (MEMORY 279).

B5.3WhatsApp and its templates

  • One real Fidato number on Meta's Cloud API talks to guests D27-101. For now it sends through the CRS's Meta account and its already approved templates; nothing new is submitted to Meta D27-266.
  • Only to a guest who agreed. WhatsApp lets a business start a conversation only with somebody who said yes, so each booking has the tick "guest agreed to WhatsApp"; without it the guest gets email if there is an address D21-72. A CRS booking arrives ticked (its guest agreed when booking); a booking site's does not D27-235 (2.3). The code a guest asks for goes to the booking's own phone, tick or not: asking is their own request D21-75.
  • A guest's reply is not read by the PMS: it arrives in the leads app's inbox, where the number is routed D27-186. The step that would tell that inbox the guest is already booked is built and not used for now, so a reply can be taken there as a new enquiry (deploy/n8n/IMPORT.md).
TemplateForState
The CRS's reservation_confirmationThe voucher, with its PDFApproved; in use D27-266
The owner's booking_confirmationThe voucher with a "Check in online" buttonWith Meta for review; switched on in n8n once Meta shows it Active D27-281
guest_page_codeThe six-digit check-in code (Meta writes its words)With Meta for review D27-285 (5)
review_requestAsking for a review after check-outLater D27-266
booking_voucherOur own voucher templateOn hold D27-265 D27-266
stay_reminder, checkin_link, tax_invoice-Not used D27-264 D27-284

When it fails: a template Meta has not approved is refused by WhatsApp; the refusal is shown on Guest messages, and the other messages still go. Connection health judges WhatsApp apart from email, so a Meta fault turns WhatsApp red while the alert email about it still goes.

B5.4Email

Email goes from the mailbox the sending workflow names, the CRS's crs@fidatohotels.com, through the mail login already in n8n D27-266. The PMS sends only the guest's address and the figures; the wording of each email is in the workflow, changed there without a release D17-88 D17-87. An email kind the workflow has no wording for is refused with a sentence on Guest messages ("No email for … in this workflow"): the alert, report and invoice emails needed the workflow updated on 5 October (deploy/n8n/IMPORT.md, part C).

B5.5The CRS bridge

The CRS is the sales team's app, for the partner hotels Fidato does not own. When a salesperson books one of the group's own hotels there, the PMS must hold the room and the hotel must confirm D27-35.

  1. Every five minutes the PMS signs in to the CRS with a read-only login of its own and reads the bookings changed since its last read. The CRS's document id is the key, so a booking read twice is one booking.
  2. A new confirmed CRS booking for a connected hotel becomes a booking Waiting for the hotel, its room held, the salesperson as its sales person, its rate the CRS's quote before tax D27-171. If the hotel is full, nothing is booked.
  3. A booking that cannot be made by itself waits under Needs attention with the reason: a CRS room type with no match, no rate, a price that does not split exactly, a date before the hotel's business date.
  4. The hotel confirms; then the one voucher goes, in the PMS's own design, sent once D27-171.
  5. A later change in the CRS, a cancellation included, is a note for the desk with Done; nothing is changed by itself D27-171.
  6. Later, with a workflow in the CRS's n8n: the hotel's answer (Confirmed with the PMS reference, Cancelled, or "Partly confirmed: N of M rooms") is written into the CRS's booking register, where the salesperson sees it D27-106 D27-174. Until then, answers wait.
  • Setting it up, once per hotel, is the owner's (deploy/README.md, "Connect the CRS"): a read-only login in the CRS's Firebase, its four settings on the server, the card filled and saved switched off, a script run on the server that makes the account the reader works as (a Viewer at that one hotel, with no sign-in), then the switch on, then one test booking. Only bookings made after the switch is on are read; earlier ones are typed by hand.
  • Until the CRS's n8n is changed, the CRS still sends its own voucher at once when "Send the confirmation to the guest" is ticked, before the hotel confirms. So the sales team unticks it for the group's hotels, and types "PMS" as "Confirmed by" D27-286.

When it fails

  • The card says why in words: the login not in the settings, a wrong password, a missing permission in the CRS, the CRS's key refusing the server.
  • Nothing is booked while the read fails; the salesperson must phone the hotel. Connection health turns the CRS bridge red when a read fails or nothing has been read for 30 minutes.
  • Switching the card off stops the reading at the next turn; bookings already made stay.

Why it works this way

  • The PMS reads; it never trusts a push from the CRS. The plan of 27 September had the CRS's webhook call n8n. But the CRS is a browser app with no server, and its webhook key is readable by every CRS user, so a call could not prove it came from the CRS. Reading with the PMS's own read-only login proves it (src/modules/crs/MODULE.md).
  • Waiting, not confirmed: the CRS has no availability of its own, so the hotel's yes is what makes it real; the room is held meanwhile so nobody else sells it D27-35.
  • One voucher, once, whoever made the booking, so a guest is never sent two D27-35 D27-99.

B5.6The booking sites, through SU

SU (Su channel manager) is the wire to Agoda, Booking.com, Expedia, Goibibo and the rest D17-30 D17-66. Built in four parts, all done: SU's login, the hotel's content, rooms left and prices out, bookings in D27-178. It is not connected: nothing reaches SU or any site until the owner has SU's keys in the server's settings, the hotel is switched on, and the owner says yes to the first live send.

  • Bookings come in by push: SU sends each one to the API's own door the moment the site takes it D17-79.
  • No room free: the booking is not made, SU is told it was received, 0 rooms left goes at once for that night, and the GM sees it as "Refused: no room free" to cancel on the site and call the guest D17-80.
  • Waits for a person: nights at different prices, a change to a booking, a request to book, a booking not in rupees D27-183. A cancellation cancels by itself under the site's policy, unless the guest has arrived D27-183 D17-44.
  • Card numbers are never kept: dropped on arrival, never stored, logged or shown D17-83.
  • Commission: SU's figure when it sends one, else the source's percentage, else a dash D17-84.
  • Who: the SU setup is the owner's and an Admin's; the GM sees the bookings and deals with the refused ones D17-85 D27-183. Each hotel is switched on separately D17-45.

B5.7Outside tills

A restaurant that runs its own till can charge a guest's meal to their room through four calls to the API (docs/POS-INTEGRATION.md): which rooms may be charged, charge this bill, did my bill land, and void it. The hotel's own restaurant does not need this: it is part of the PMS (A8).

  • A key per outlet, made on the server (npm run pos:outlet) and shown once. Only its fingerprint is kept, so it cannot be read back from the database or a backup; a lost key is replaced and the old one stops at once. The key belongs to one outlet at one hotel, and is refused where the hotel's restaurant module is off.
  • The till's own bill number makes a retry safe: the same number sent again returns the first charge, never a second.
  • The PMS dates every charge with the hotel's business date; the till never sends a date.
  • A void is a cancelling line, never a deletion; refusals are recorded with their reason. Charges to rooms (A8.1) shows everything an outside till sent, refusals included.
  • Two guests in one room on a changeover day: the PMS will not guess; it asks the till which guest.

When it fails: a till that timed out asks "did my last request land?" instead of sending again; the answer "not received" means send it, "posted" means it is on the bill.

Said differently in the documents

The worked example in docs/POS-INTEGRATION.md sends the till's calls to https://pms.fidatohotels.com/api/pos. That address is the website, which answers every path with its own page; the API, and the till's door, is api.fidatohotels.com. A till set up from the example would get a web page back.

B5.8The guest's ways in: codes, Google, DigiLocker, ID photos

  • A code to the booking's phone on WhatsApp or to its email, or Continue with Google, where the Google account's verified email must be the booking's D27-207. Nothing is sent until the guest presses a button D27-210. During the stay a guest may type the room and phone number (a room's letter in small letters or capitals, the keyboard a text one D27-335); the code goes only to the booking's own number, and only when both match D27-235 (2.4).
  • DigiLocker, through API Setu as a DigiLocker partner: prepared and switched off until the partner keys and the lawyer's answers arrive D27-235 (2.5). When on, the DigiLocker account's mobile must be the booking's own number; only the masked Aadhaar number and the name are kept; the ID waits for the desk like any other submission. A fuller ID number already on file is kept D27-247.
  • ID photos go through a second workflow in n8n, with its own secret, into Google Drive: one encrypted file per upload, opened only with that hotel's password; the server keeps nothing D27-208 D27-209 D27-211. A hotel with no password set is not offered the upload. A failed delete is shown to the owner, Admin and GM with "Try again".

Watch out

  • A hotel's ID photo password cannot be recovered. A changed password does not open earlier files, and a lost one means those photos can never be opened. The owner accepted this: no master password, no rotation D27-211. Keep each hotel's password in the password manager.

B5.9What the PMS only reads: the leads app and rivals' prices

  • The leads app (the market-to-revenue app) keeps running on its own; the PMS shows its enquiries, conversations and spend, read live every time and never copied, with a link to reply there D27-100 D27-170. It reads with the server's own Google credential, borrowing a short-lived token, because the organisation allows no keys D27-186. At most 5,000 reads a day, since the app's free plan is shared with the app itself; at the cap the screen says so and reads nothing. A guest erased in the app disappears from the PMS's view too; their stays and bills stay D27-108.
  • Rivals' prices: a search service (SerpApi) reads Google Hotels' lowest public price per night for nearby hotels, 30 nights ahead, twice a week, for a hotel switched on D27-270. With the switch off, the prices already checked stay visible with their date D27-272.

B5.10Watching the connections

ConnectionRed when
Emails, WhatsAppThe last three tries all failed.
CRS bridgeThe last read failed, or nothing has been read for 30 minutes (the reader runs every five).
Firebase sign-inIt did not answer.
BackupsThe last backup failed, or there has been none for 26 hours; or, once copies have gone to the off-site bucket, none has for 26 hours D27-373; or, with restore to any minute on, the change journal or the weekly base copy is not reaching the bucket; or the nightly copy of the uploaded files, or n8n's own nightly copy, failed or has not run for 26 hours D27-377. Amber when backed up but on the server's disk only, all of it or the uploaded files or n8n's copy.
DiskThe server's disk is 90% used or more: the database stops when it is full. Amber from 80% D27-373.
Rivals' pricesNever red; amber when switched on and nothing kept yet.

When a connection turns red, one email goes to the address in the server's settings, at most once an hour per connection; none while Emails itself is red, because that email could not go D27-276 (3). The owner, an Admin and the GM see the page. The thresholds (three failures, 30 minutes, 26 hours) are the ones built; the owner has been asked to confirm them (src/modules/connections-health/MODULE.md).

B5.11The provisioning key

Creating a hotel makes its invoice series and the home of all its bills, and its code appears in every address and every invoice number it will ever issue; the code cannot be changed afterwards (deploy/README.md). So it needs more than an owner's sign-in: it needs the provisioning key, and so does making somebody a group administrator.

  • The key is never in the database. Only its fingerprint is, so a copy of the database or a backup cannot be used to create anything (migration 029). It is not in the server's settings either: the person creating the hotel types it on the screen, so no ordinary session can create a hotel.
  • The owner makes it once on their own computer and stores its fingerprint on the server; the key itself goes straight into the owner's password manager and is never sent to anyone (docs/go-live/RELEASE-3OCT.md, steps F5 and F6) D21-54.
  • Without it, the database refuses to create a hotel, whatever the screen shows. A server with no key at all cannot have a hotel created on it by anyone.

Risks, and what was left out

Watch out

  • n8n carries every message, the mailbox login and the WhatsApp login. It is open to the internet behind its own sign-in D21-96; two-step sign-in there matters, and its encryption key is a master password (HANDOVER.md § 5).
  • Selling the system with n8n inside: n8n's licence allows "your own internal business purposes"; a copy Influvate sells may need n8n's commercial licence. A question for the lawyer (docs/PLATFORM-PLAN.md, R8).
  • A guest's WhatsApp reply reaches the leads app's inbox as a new enquiry until the "booked guest" step is used (B5.3).
  • Our own WhatsApp templates: on hold while the CRS's approved ones are used D27-266.
  • Online check-in is on for every hotel by default; a hotel can switch it off D27-281.
  • The leads app moved into the PMS: withdrawn; it keeps running on its own D27-100.
  • A payment gateway: excluded for now D17-57 D25-36.
Chapter B6

Each module in depth

For the owner. The system is divided into services, one per job of the hotel. For each: what it is and holds, the decisions that shaped it and why, what was left out and why, and what is still open. Taken from each service's own brief (src/modules/<service>/MODULE.md), its list of faults (DEFECTS.md), the code and your decisions, as they stand on 9 October.

B6.1How the system is divided

Since 15 September the code is sorted by service, at your request, so that several helpers can work at once, each in one service, without breaking another. A service lives in three places: its screens in src/modules/<service>/, its server routes in api/src/modules/<service>/, and its database checks in db/tests/modules/<service>.sql. Each keeps three notes:

FileWhat it holds
MODULE.mdThe service's brief: its screens, routes and tables, the decisions that bind it, what is open, and requests to other services.
DEFECTS.mdEvery fault found in it, numbered with the service's prefix (FD-1, POS-1, FIN-1 …), what was done about it, and the fix waiting for the open ones.
CHANGELOG.mdWhat each working session did in it, and what it proved.
  • One front door each. A service uses another only through that service's index.ts. A test refuses any reach past it (B8.6), so a change inside the restaurant cannot quietly break finance.
  • The shared core (the design system, the frame of every screen, the data seam, the server's wiring and the one sequence of migrations) is changed only by the main chat.
  • Switches per hotel. Some services are switched on per hotel in Settings: the restaurant, banquets, laundry, spa, alcohol (VAT), the channel manager, loyalty and "Reception can use the POS", among others. A switched-off service is not in that hotel's menu.
  • Not built yet. On 16 September every missing service got a folder and a "Coming soon" page; on 28 September each moved to where it will belong, marked "Not built yet", seen by the owner, admins and GMs only (D27-87). On 30 September you asked for every one to be built (D27-178), and the booking engine was dropped in favour of the channel manager's (D27-180). Today only Online payments and Room systems still carry the mark.
  • Nothing is decided by a helper. Each service's choices are your decisions, asked one by one with a recommendation (HANDOVER § 5). Where your answer went against the recommendation, the decision says so.

In each section below, Open lists the faults still open in that service's DEFECTS.md on 9 October; a fault that is fixed is not listed.

Why it works this way

On 27 August two helpers changed the same folder at the same time for two hours, and a day's work was lost beyond recovery (AGENTS.md). One service per helper, one front door per service, and a claim taken before the first change (npm run claim) are what stop that happening again.

B6.2Front desk

Check-in, check-out, and everything the desk does to a stay in between. Built, always on.

ScreensRooms, Calendar, Arrivals (Today, Upcoming), In house (In house now, Due out), Walk-ins (a record: a walk-in is now New booking opened from an empty room), the stay panel; in Settings: Front desk rules, Market segments, Reservation types, Ready reasons, Holidays, ID types, VIP levels.
HoldsEach stay's state (arriving, in house, checked out), which room it is in, its inclusions, the hotel's desk lists and holidays.
Decided
  • One meaning for "In house" and "Empty" everywhere: In house is checked in and not checked out, whatever the departure date says; Empty is nobody in it and sellable tonight (D21-36, D21-37, D23-9). Two screens once disagreed about who was in a room.
  • Nobody is put into a room somebody is still in; a room given ahead of time to a booking not yet here is allowed (D23-12, D24-15, D24-26; B7.2).
  • One page, three buttons: Save booking, Save and assign room, Check in now. Your standing rule: nothing takes more than two pages or three clicks (D27-158, D27-163, D27-236).
  • The first night is charged at check-in, with its GST, dated the business date; the night audit posts each later night and never the first one twice, so a bill printed after check-in never misses the room (D27-204, D27-205).
  • Express check-in counts only this stay's own confirmed online ID, never a document from an earlier visit, and never applies to a foreign guest (D27-236, D27-242).
  • A late departure is asked only on or after the departure date, and once: a guest leaving before it is leaving early, whatever the hour, and is never asked or charged a late fee; one already recorded is not asked or charged again (D27-314; A1.6, B7.11). The date is the hotel's business date, not the clock's.
  • The desk's lists read only their own days: Arrivals, In house, Due out and the check-in's room list ask the server for the day's bookings, not every booking ever made (793 on the demo hotel, about three seconds each time); Rooms, the Calendar and the Dashboard read only the dates on screen; after a payment only that stay's bill and the open list are read again. Nothing a person reads changed: D27-313, D27-316.
  • A check-in days early is allowed, warned and confirmed (D27-193). A day use is charged at check-in and stays a day use (D27-225, D27-230). A returning foreign guest's nationality is never overwritten by "India" typed at check-in; a stay is capped at 90 nights (D27-197).
  • Per-hotel desk rules: the desk may overbook (on), an advance before check-in (none to start), weekend days, the default ID type, nationality and title (D27-243, D27-246).
  • Controls a person cannot use are hidden (D24-18, D24-27). When a hotel's business date is behind the real day, one warning line in the top bar of every screen (D27-237).
Left outCheck-out, moves and other changes to a stay are refused offline; a check-in is held, with a warning (A0.8). The full list of bookings is deliberately not kept on a shared desk computer. The plan's own test, somebody new doing a stay alone, waits for you to arrange it (D21-48, D21-57).
OpenNothing.

B6.3Reservations (bookings)

Taking a booking, for one room or many, and groups with their master bill. Built, always on.

ScreensAll bookings, Groups, New booking (one page), and one group's own page.
HoldsBookings, groups, the sales people list. The same booking door serves the desk, the CRS and the channel manager.
Decided
  • New booking takes every field of your Add Reservation screenshot, in this system's layout (D27-33).
  • Overbooking: a machine (a booking site, the CRS) is never allowed to (D17-43, D17-80); the desk may, unless the hotel switches that off (D27-243; B7.1).
  • "Rate includes GST" is a tick per room line, off by default, and also covers the list price (D27-187, D27-199); a contract's rate is always before GST (D27-233).
  • Discounts: up to 10% by hand with a reason, more only by a named room discount (D27-36, D27-62; the restaurant has no limit since D27-395); a ₹ discount comes off each night (D27-259).
  • A waiting booking (from the CRS) is confirmed with one button, or cancelled directly with a reason and no charge, freeing the room at once (D27-60, D27-64, D27-69, D27-71).
  • A day use is booked from New booking with its price typed every time; nothing is filled in for it (D27-227, D27-229).
  • A booking reference's month is the hotel's business date, not the wall clock (D27-123); who made each booking is recorded (D27-239).
  • A group's lead guest is the room booked first that still stands, unless the desk picks another (D22-52).
  • A company over its credit limit is refused with the amount; a GM or above may allow it with a reason; the limit counts what the company owes across the whole group (D27-275, D27-279).
  • A booking from a booking site carries "Prepaid on the booking site", on by default, so the guest is not asked for an advance twice (D27-246).
Left outPrices that differ night by night inside one booking (D17-82): a stay has one agreed rate, and the channel manager makes such a booking wait for the desk (D27-183). Changes to a channel's booking stay at the desk. Commission is stamped on each booking, but nothing totals it yet. New bookings are refused offline.
OpenRES-6: a group's lead can be a waiting room, which holds back the group's voucher. Not reachable from the desk today.

B6.4Housekeeping

Which rooms need cleaning and whose they are, repairs, and rooms out of service. Built, always on, and works offline.

ScreensHousekeeping (the board) and Work orders; Repairs on an equipment item's page.
HoldsEach room's cleaning state, who is assigned, out-of-service blocks, work orders and their costs.
Decided
  • A room card's three buttons have words, Clean, Inspected, Repair, and a greyed one says why when tapped (D17-8). No separate "Needs cleaning" section (D17-9).
  • The board refreshes itself (D17-39); after Clean or Inspected a message says so at once and the card moves (D27-94).
  • A repair cost needs proof, a photo of the bill or payment, but no approval (D17-5, D17-6). Opening a repair sets the item Under repair and closing it sets In use (D17-7).
  • Out of service is a dated block with a reason (D17-11). The GM's own room at 5 Elements is "NC": not for sale, house use, never deleted (HANDOVER § 4).
  • Everyone sees their own hotel's staff, by name and role only (D27-96). No Dashboard or reports for housekeeping (D27-141).
  • Per-hotel switches: a room left by a move turns dirty (on), a room back from a block turns dirty (on), stay-over rooms turn dirty at the night audit (off) (D27-260).
Left outPutting a room out of service is refused offline. A repair cost is never held offline, so a proof photo is never separated from its cost.
OpenNothing.

B6.5Night audit

A person closes the hotel's day: later room nights are posted, no-shows marked, and the business date moves on. Built, always on, never scheduled.

ScreensNight audit: its checklist, Run, Closed days, and the correction drawer.
HoldsOne record per closed day, and every correction to a closed day.
Decided
  • Run by a person, never by a clock (HANDOVER § 4): a hotel that forgets stays on yesterday, which is safe and visible. The GM runs it at 5 Elements (D21-77); the roles that may are unchanged, and the Revenue Manager and the Viewer, who may not, are not shown the button (D22-36, D27-305). It asks before running (D27-117).
  • A second press changes nothing and shows the record already made (D17-12). A history of closed days (D17-13).
  • Correcting a closed day: the owner, an admin or the GM, this month and last, with a reason; the old and new figures are both kept, and the audit's own record is never rewritten (D22-18, D24-1 to D24-6). Every charge may be corrected; payments, refunds and discounts never are (D25-5, D25-11). A bill with a tax invoice is refused: issue a credit note (D24-4).
  • No night is charged twice: the first is posted at check-in (D27-204), and a night already covered by a room line is skipped (D24-14).
Left outAn automatic, scheduled night audit (decided against). Changing money taken on a closed day: the difference is put right today (D25-11). What the audit refuses and why: B7.4.
OpenNA-4: a test helper loses the details of a refusal; the shared core's to fix.

B6.6Guests, companies and Form III

The guest directory, companies and agents, booking sources with each hotel's commission, and the register of foreign guests. Built.

ScreensGuests, Companies and agents, Booking sources, Form III.
HoldsGuests and their ID documents, companies, booking sources and their commission, Form III filings.
Decided
  • Form III replaces Form C (the Immigration and Foreigners Act 2025): arrival and departure each reported within 24 hours; every portal field recorded, the law's fields required at check-in; the guest signs a printed card on arrival and departure; the photo is taken on the portal, not kept here (D27-25, D27-72 to D27-80).
  • Who reads ID and Form III data: the owner, an admin, the GM, the hotel manager and reception, the people who check guests in; not the accountant (D25-38, D27-122).
  • Aadhaar: you chose to accept the full number, shown as the last four digits on every screen and in full only on the printed registration card (D21-17, D21-18); whether it may be kept waits for the lawyer, and nothing changes until then (D25-37).
  • A returning guest is suggested by exact phone or email, and the clerk confirms (D21-20; B6.27). A booking-site guest who is blacklisted warns the desk (D22-8).
  • A heading is its menu name (D17-22). An administrator counts as a manager for booking sources (D27-275).
Left outThe system records Form III filings; it does not file them on the portal. Adding and editing a company came with contracts (D27-184; B6.16); Edit is on Companies and agents too, for the owner, an admin and the GM (D27-382).
OpenNothing. Every adult in a room is recorded, and a foreigner has a row of their own on the register (D27-382), which replaced one portal number per person with no details (D27-75). An ID skipped at check-in is recorded on Complete details (D27-382).

B6.7Online check-in (the guest's own page)

A private page per booking: the guest proves who they are, sends their ID details and a photo, sees their proforma bill, messages the desk, and during the stay asks for things. Built. On for every hotel by default since 5 October (D27-281); DigiLocker is built and switched off.

ScreensThe guest's page (no menu; reached from the voucher's link and QR, a room's card, or the desk's link) and Online check-in at the desk.
HoldsEach booking's link, codes and unlocks, the guest's submitted details, ID photos (encrypted, in Google Drive), requests and messages.
Decided
  • One private page per booking, no public page (D18-9). A stranger who scans a room's card sees nothing; a forwarded link asks for a code again (D18-13, D21-6, D21-14).
  • Three ways to prove it is you, nothing sent until the guest chooses: a code by WhatsApp, a code by email, or Continue with Google (D27-207, D27-210). A verified phone stays unlocked for a day (D27-169).
  • Everything the guest sends is a submission, confirmed by the desk against the real ID, under the clerk's name; nothing reaches the guest's record or Form III unchecked (D21-8).
  • The ID photo: any government photo ID, Aadhaar only masked; encrypted per hotel and stored in Google Drive, never kept on the server; optional online, the desk can add it; after confirming, only the owner, an admin and the GM see kept photos, and every view is recorded (D27-207 to D27-212).
  • The bill the guest sees is exactly the desk's proforma bill, with "pay at the desk": the stay's facts, the payments and every line's HSN/SAC included, and only ever their own stay's (D21-10, D27-344, D27-365). A night still to be posted tonight is shown on the desk's print only (D27-205).
  • One fixed card per room, against the recommendation of a card per stay; a reprinted card stops the old one at once (D21-7, D21-16).
  • During the stay: one-tap requests, in-room dining, table booking, wake-up calls, messages with the desk (D27-221, D27-224, D27-225, D27-241).
Left outPaying online and choosing a room. The other adults' IDs: the desk records them (D27-382), the guest's own page does not, and the ID photo is one per stay (D27-212). DigiLocker, until the partner keys and the lawyer's answers arrive (D27-235). The WhatsApp template for the check-in code is waiting on Meta (D27-285); until then the code goes by email.
OpenNothing.

B6.8Guest messages

Everything the system sends a guest by itself, and the record of every attempt. Built; it sends nothing until the sending settings and your pace are set on the server.

ScreensGuest messages (with the guest's messages to the desk, and Reply); in Settings, Messages: Guest messages on/off, and Daily report emails.
HoldsEvery send and its result (one record per attempt), each hotel's switches, the daily report email lists.
Decided
  • One door out: every message leaves through one place in the server and goes to n8n as data; n8n writes the words, so wording changes without a release (D17-87). Since 30 September every guest message goes through the CRS's n8n, from one Fidato number (D27-186, D27-101).
  • Fewer messages: the voucher is the confirmation, sent once when the booking is made; no separate confirmation and no day-before reminder (D27-264). By email with the PDF, and on WhatsApp too where the guest agreed (D27-235, D21-72). The voucher email carries the check-in link (D27-283).
  • The WhatsApp template: for now the CRS's approved voucher template (D27-266); your own booking_confirmation takes over once Meta shows it Active again (D27-281).
  • The tax invoice goes by email only, when issued, where the hotel switches it on and only when it is made out to the guest; one made out to a company, an agent or a booking site goes by the desk's Send invoice (D27-261, D27-284, D27-313).
  • One message per group, to the lead (D22-41, D22-52). On switch-on day every future booking is owed, soonest arrival first, at your pace; catching up only 09:00 to 21:00 hotel time (D21-33, D21-34, D22-42; B7.8).
  • Daily report emails after each night audit, per hotel, the night audit report on by default, nothing sent until an address is typed, one email per address with a PDF for each report (D27-280, D27-282, D27-371). They are kept out of the Guest messages list.
  • English only (D21-73).
Left outThe sending pace is still yours to give, and nothing guesses it (D21-34). Your own booking_voucher template is on hold (D27-266). The invoice on WhatsApp, and a separate check-in-link template (D27-284). A "Rooms" line in the group's message, with the next template edit (D22-54). A second language.
OpenMSG-4: dates are formatted in two places.

B6.9Guest services

A guest's requests during the stay, wake-up calls and lost property. Built.

ScreensGuest requests, Wake-up calls, Lost property; on the guest's own page, "Ask for something", the one-tap choices and a wake-up request.
HoldsRequests (as work orders carrying the stay), wake-up calls, lost items.
Decided
  • A request is a work order that carries the stay, no new kind of record; three kinds, one per team: housekeeping, something broken (whoever handles repairs), food and drink (kitchen manager, chef, waiter). The desk sees, raises, takes and closes any (D27-181, D22-34).
  • No time targets for now. Guests may raise requests from their own page while checked in and see Open, Being done, Done. Food and drink carries no price: anything chargeable is rung on the Till (D27-181).
  • One-tap choices: drinking water, fresh towels, toiletries, clean my room; AC, plumbing, power, TV and Wi-Fi; something else; free, and the list fixed (D27-224).
  • Wake-up calls set by the desk or asked for from the guest's page, against the recommendation of the desk only; the bell reminds the desk from 15 minutes before until done, with no "missed" state (D27-241).
  • Lost property: the desk and housekeeping log a found item; only the desk marks it returned (to whom) or disposed of (with a reason); no automatic disposal, no photo (D27-241).
Left outTime targets. Holding a request offline. Photos of lost items.
OpenNothing.

B6.10Finance

The ledger: guests' bills, payments, tax invoices and credit notes, the VAT bill for alcohol, the cash drawers and deposits, company accounts and the tax rules. Built, always on; the alcohol (VAT) part is off by default per hotel.

ScreensFolios, Invoices, Payments, Cashiering, Cash deposits, Company accounts; one invoice, one VAT bill, the interim bill; the Bill tab in the stay panel; in Settings, Money: Payment methods, Extra charges, Discounts, Commission, Pickup and drop.
HoldsEvery line on every bill (append-only), payments, invoices, VAT bills, drawers and counts, deposits, company payments, payment methods, tax rules.
Decided
  • The ledger only grows. A wrong line is reversed by a line of its own, with a reason; only the owner, an admin, the GM or the accountant reverse a payment (D27-117, D27-125).
  • No bill is a dash, never ₹0 (D17-16); money figures are read again every time a screen is opened (D17-58).
  • Alcohol is VAT, not GST: a per-hotel switch, one "VAT 10%" line, its own VAT bill and series per hotel each year, cancelled like a credit note (D21-90, D21-91, D22-44).
  • Before check-out the print is an "Interim bill", its total exact with no round-off (D22-7, D24-25, D27-126). The bill is in sections, Room, Restaurant, Bar (D27-200); its headline is what is due, tonight's night shown "to be posted tonight" (D27-199, D27-204).
  • Edit and Change rate for the owner, an admin and the GM, with a reason; refused once a tax invoice stands (a credit note then) or on a closed day (D27-157, D27-162).
  • Cash: every drawer opens by itself after the night audit on the float kept at the last close; a float kept at the desk names the next person; the rest goes to deposit; the owner or the accountant verifies each deposit, never without its slip photo (D27-190, D27-191, D27-200 to D27-202). A cash paid-out waits for the GM's or owner's yes (D27-242).
  • Cash limits (B7.10): ₹2 lakh or more refused, a PAN or Form 97 above ₹1 lakh (D25-40, D26-8, D26-9). A payment larger than the bill is held as the guest's credit and refunded at check-out (D27-4, D27-11, D27-12).
  • A guest's own figures count only their own bill, never nights the group's host pays (D27-226). Company accounts shows the City ledger's figures; companies pay by bank transfer, cheque, UPI or card, never cash (D27-127, D27-242).
  • The GST series opens itself each financial year (D24-22); tax rules apply by the charge's business date, with a SAC per line (D27-258); the FSSAI number is frozen on an invoice when issued, like the GSTIN (D27-3).
Left outOnline payments (B6.12). E-invoicing (IRN): not required while the group is under ₹5 crore turnover (deploy/README.md). GST on advances (B6.35). Every money write is refused offline.
OpenNothing (FIN-1 to FIN-29 are all fixed).

B6.11Accounting export

The hotel's month handed to its accountant as a day book. Built: the CSV, the Excel file and the two Tally files. The Tally Prime file was proved on TallyPrime 7.2 in a practice company; the Tally ERP 9 file has had its shape tested only.

ScreensAccounting export (found by search).
HoldsThe Tally ledger names of each hotel, typed by the Accountant; no figure of its own: it reads the reports and finance.
Decided
  • Three formats offered, Tally Prime XML, Tally ERP 9 XML and a day-book CSV, so whoever exports picks what their accountant wants (D18-16); a real Excel file beside the CSV (D22-37).
  • Tally ledger names come from your accountant (D21-46): one form per hotel, no name ever suggested (D27-382).
  • Alcohol in its own VAT columns (D21-91); Restaurant and Restaurant tax columns (D24-24); food charged to a room apart from the other extras (D27-382); company payments as receipts, kept apart from sales, against the recommendation (D27-242). The accountant may export (D27-122).
Left outReading anything back from Tally, payroll and the bank; credit notes, cancelled VAT bills, supplier bills, cash expenses and cash banked in the Tally files.
OpenThe first real proof is the Accountant importing one day into a copy of the company in Tally. ACC-12: a voucher a corrected day no longer has stays in Tally until it is deleted there.

B6.12Online payments

Not built. A menu entry under Finance marked "Not built yet", for the owner, admins and GMs, and nothing behind it.

Decided
  • Excluded: guests pay at the desk (D17-57, D25-36). Asked for with the booking engine on 30 September (D27-178); the booking engine was then dropped (D27-180), and online payments were put after the release in hand (D27-239).
What it needsYour go-ahead, a payment gateway with a merchant account, and its keys in the server's settings. If it ever comes, the company that hosts the system must never hold guests' money, and no card number may be stored (docs/SELLING-IN-INDIA.md); card numbers from booking sites are already dropped on arrival (D17-83).

Chapter B4 has the detail.

B6.14Revenue outlook

Suggestions only: what the coming nights look like and which deserve a look. Built; it writes nothing.

Companies and agents, a contract per company and hotel, and bookings priced by it. Built.

ScreensContracts and a company's page; Add company also from Companies and agents.
HoldsCompanies, their contracts, credit terms.

The connection to SU, which carries rooms left, prices and closures out to the booking sites and brings their bookings in. Built; not connected: it waits on your SU account and keys, and each hotel's switch is off.

Not builtWhy, and what decides it

Watch out: briefs that are behind

  • Several services' MODULE.md files still carry old counts of routes and screens, the old way of claiming a service (a file in .claims/ instead of npm run claim), and lines written before a later decision. Where a brief and the code or a later decision differ, this chapter follows the code and the latest decision.
Chapter B7

Edge cases

For the owner. What the system does when the day does not go to plan: a full house, a guest who changes rooms, a group with one payer, a night audit with loose ends, no connection, a printer that is off, a message that fails, a hotel with nothing set up, cash over the legal limit, two people pressing at once, a day not closed. Read from the code and your decisions; the words in quotes are the system's own.

B7.1Overbooking

Two different questions: can a room type be sold past what is free, and can one room hold two guests at once.

Who booksWhen the room type is full
The desk, with "The desk may overbook" on (the default)The booking is made. New booking warns on the line, for example “2 left · this books more than that”.
The desk, with the switch offEvery room type and night is checked before anything is written: “Deluxe has no room free for every night from … to ….” A group is booked whole or not at all.
A booking site, through the channel managerAlways refused, whatever the switch says. No booking is made, the channel manager is told there are 0 rooms left on those dates at once, and Channel bookings lists it as “Refused: no room free” for the GM to sort out with the site and the guest.
The CRSRefused the same way: “Hotel full - not booked” on CRS bookings, and the salesperson is told.

One room, two guests: never. Two clerks giving the same room for overlapping nights at the same moment cannot both succeed: the database itself lets exactly one through, and a test races two of them to prove it. A guest still in a room blocks anyone else going in (B7.2).

Why it works this way

Deliberate overbooking is something every hotel does, and the desk decides; a machine has no judgement, so a booking site or the CRS is never allowed to do it (D17-43, D17-80, D27-35). A hotel that wants the desk held to the same rule switches it off (D27-243).

Watch out

  • New booking shows the same warning whether the switch is on or off; with it off, the refusal comes when the booking is saved.
  • Only New booking reads the switch. Whether changing a booking's dates also obeys it was not confirmed while writing this book.

B7.2A room move in the middle of a stay

  • Into a room somebody is still in: refused for a guest moving tonight or earlier: “… is still in room 204. Check them out first, or choose another room.” A move booked for a later night is allowed, and checked again on the night (D23-12, D24-15, D24-26).
  • Into a room booked for part of the time: “Room 204 is taken for part of that time. Pick another room, or move them on a different night.” Into a room out of service: “Room 204 is out of service.”
  • The old room is sent for cleaning, when the hotel's switch "A room a guest moved out of is sent for cleaning" is on (on by default, D27-260). A move booked for a later night dirties the old room at that night's audit (D24-15).
  • The money does not move. The bill belongs to the booking, not the room: nights already charged stay as they are, each line naming the room it was for. The dialog says “Moving rooms changes no charge on its own.”
  • A new rate on the arrival day: tonight's room line, already posted at check-in, is reversed and posted again at the new rate, with the reason "Room move" (D27-205). Later nights use the new rate.
  • Moving a guest is refused offline (A0.8).

Why it works this way

Until 23 September a mid-stay move left the old room marked as it was (FD-9), and check-in could give a room a late check-out guest was still in (FD-11). Both were fixed at your request (D23-12), and three close cousins the next day (D24-15), with the line drawn at "only when they go in now" (D24-26).

B7.3Groups, and a bill the host pays

  • A master bill. A group can have one open master bill, "Host pays". Each room is then ticked to send its room nights to the host, or to pay its own: “Nights already charged stay where they were posted.” Extras and late fees stay on the guest's own bill.
  • A guest's own figures count only the guest's own bill: the Bill tab, the Check out button, the In house list and Settle never ask a guest for nights the host pays. Folios lists the host's nights once, under Group bills, never under each guest (D27-226).
  • Check-out is per room. There is no group check-out: each room leaves against its own bill, and the master bill never holds a guest back.
  • One voucher per group, to the lead guest: the room booked first that still stands, unless the desk picks another; a changed lead says “The group's confirmation and its review request go to them.” (D22-41, D22-52).
  • A company's credit limit counts what the company owes across the whole group of hotels (D27-279).
  • Settling the master bill is done on the group's own page (Group bills on Folios opens it). The card The host's account says who it is billed to, the group's company, else the guest who leads the group, and carries the Bill tab's own Settle: any of the hotel's ways of paying, or Bill to company, which moves it to that company's City ledger. That is refused when the group is billed to no company, and over the company's credit limit it needs the reason of the owner, an Admin or the GM. Issue tax invoice comes only when every room has left and nothing is owed, after the same question as any invoice before a number is taken; it is made out to the company or else the lead guest, and nothing sends it by itself. The ₹2 lakh cash count takes the host's account together with the rooms' own bills (D27-305, D27-307; A2.6).

Watch out: found while writing this book

  • If the lead room is still a waiting booking (from the CRS), the whole group's voucher waits too (RES-6).

B7.4The night audit with loose ends

The audit refuses before it writes anything, and says all its reasons in one go:

Loose endWhat the audit says
Guests still showing due out“3 rooms are still showing due out. Check them out, or extend the stay - the audit will not decide which.”
No GST rule for rooms“This property has no GST rule for rooms, so a room charge has no rate to carry. … A missing rate is not zero - the audit will not invent one.”
A desk drawer not counted“A front-desk drawer is still open. Count the cash and close the shift - the audit cannot say what was taken at the desk until somebody has.”
The restaurant's day not closed“The till has not been closed for today. Run the day end on it first - the restaurant's takings belong in this audit, and they are not final until the drawer is counted.” Only for an outlet that had orders that day.

Open restaurant bills are stopped one step earlier: Close restaurant day refuses while a bill is open (“There is 1 bill still open.”, settle it or close it unpaid with a reason), and while a paid table was never cleared. So the audit cannot run over an open restaurant bill. A bill charged to a room while offline also keeps the day open until it reaches the server.

  • Pressed twice, at the same moment or later: the second press changes nothing and shows the record already made (D17-12). A unique record per day, and a lock, guarantee it. An audit stopped half-way can simply be run again: each night is checked for an existing charge first.
  • A night is never charged twice. The first night is posted at check-in, and the audit skips any night already covered by a room line (D27-204, D24-14). Earlier double charges were a moved guest charged twice a night, found only by closing real nights (MEMORY 171), and a split-bill stay charged twice (D27-89); both are fixed.
  • No-shows: a confirmed arrival that never came is marked no-show. A retention charge is posted only when the booking carries cancellation terms.
  • A hotel days behind closes one day per press, starting from its business date; there is no catch-up button. The first run after a gap marks every arrival up to that day that never came as a no-show (B7.13).

Correcting a day already closed

The owner, an admin or the GM, on Closed days, for this month and last, with a reason. A room, no-show or other charge is put right or taken off; the closed day's reports show the corrected figure, and the old one stays on the bill and on the correction list (D24-1 to D24-6, D25-5). Refused: a bill with a tax invoice (“Issue a credit note instead.”), drinks with an issued VAT bill, and money: payments, refunds and discounts are never changed on a closed day: “put the difference right today.” (D24-4, D25-7, D25-11).

Watch out

  • The checklist on the Night audit screen shows due-out rooms as a yellow note, yet they stop the run; and the screen does not list which rooms, drawers or outlets are in the way. Read the refusal sentence.

B7.5No connection

The rule everywhere: what can be safely held on the device is held and sent later; what cannot is refused with a sentence saying what to do instead (A0.8). In the restaurant:

ActionOffline
Building a round on the padWorks. The round is kept on the device until Send.
SendHeld: “The kitchen does not have it yet. It goes as soon as the connection is back.” It has no KOT number until it arrives. Tell the kitchen.
Cash, card or UPIRefused: “… take cash on paper and enter it when the connection is back.”
Charge to roomHeld, and sent when the line is back. The restaurant's day cannot close while it waits, so it cannot be lost.
Customise, Print bill, Close restaurant dayRefused. An add-on held offline could reach a dish after the kitchen has it.

Kept on the device for a week, so they open with no connection: properties and rooms, Arrivals, In house, Due out, Rooms and the Calendar (D22-23), Tables, Housekeeping, Work orders, the banquet diary, the menu and add-ons, and the rooms a bill can be charged to. Balances shown offline say how old they are (D27-271). Not kept: guests' documents, bills and reports, the Kitchen screen, the Till's orders.

Why it works this way

A waiter at a table should never wait on the internet, so the pad works offline until Send. Money is different: a cash payment recorded offline on two devices could be counted twice or not at all, so it is refused and written on paper; a room charge is safe to hold because the day cannot close without it (your choice of 8 September, recorded in MEMORY 199 and 200, with its risk written down).

Watch out: the risk you accepted

  • A guest can check out while a room charge is still held on a waiter's device. When it arrives, the server refuses it, because nobody is checked in there any more, and the device keeps the refusal on screen for a person. The money is not lost silently; somebody must collect it (MEMORY 200).

B7.6A KOT computer or the bill printer is off

  • Online means the printing computer was seen within the last 90 seconds, with a restaurant screen open on it (D27-161).
  • Its KOTs wait, and print when it is back, oldest first, for the current business day only. Older ones are reprinted from This computer's last 20 KOTs; the slip says REPRINT (D27-167, D27-292).
  • The red line on Tables, the Till, the Terminal and the Kitchen names it: “Bar KOTs wait: Bar PC not seen since 8:42”, or “No computer prints Bar KOTs - they are not printing” when no computer has that kind. It shows only for a kind some menu section prints to.
  • The bill printer off: “Bar PC is offline”, the bill waiting to print when it is back, with Print here to print it on the device instead. A bill printed here is taken off the printer's list, so it never prints twice.

Why it works this way

The website cannot reach a printer by its address on the hotel's network, so a printer is always reached through the computer it is connected to (D27-292). There is no fallback printer: with none, nobody prints and every restaurant screen says so in red (D27-161). Only the current business day's missed KOTs print by themselves; older ones are reprinted by hand (D27-167).

B7.7A restaurant bill closed unpaid

  • Who: anyone who may use the till, while nothing on the bill has gone to the kitchen. Once any dish was sent, only the owner, an admin, the GM, the hotel manager or the kitchen manager (D27-128, D27-130).
  • Always with a reason: “Close this bill unpaid?”, “It stays on the record with this reason - a walkout and a duplicate are different things at the end of a shift.” The bill then reads "Closed unpaid" with the reason.
  • The table turns grey, Closed unpaid - clear it, with no amount, and takes no more rounds until Clear frees it (D27-288).
  • Close restaurant day shows it as Walked out, with the amount. It is not in the night audit's restaurant takings, which count settled bills only.

Watch out

  • A table left "Closed unpaid" without Clear does not stop Close restaurant day (only paid tables do). Clear it anyway, so the next guests see a free table.

B7.8Messages to guests: failures, repeats and quiet hours

  • Retries. A sweep runs every minute. A message that fails is tried again, up to three tries, then left; each try is recorded as sent or failed, with the reason in words, such as “The receiver did not answer within twenty seconds.”
  • Never sent twice. Each message has one identity on every try, and the n8n workflow drops an identity it has already sent; a lock per booking and kind stops two sweeps sending at once (“It was sent already, so it is not sent again.”). The desk's Send voucher refuses a voucher that has gone already, or that failed three times.
  • Quiet hours. Catching up on older bookings happens only between 09:00 and 21:00, hotel time; a new booking is confirmed at once, at any hour (D22-42).
  • The switch-on day. Every confirmed future booking is owed its voucher, sent soonest arrival first, at the pace you set for the WhatsApp account; nobody guesses the pace (D21-33, D21-34).
  • Not set up: nothing is sent and nothing is recorded; the screens say “Sending is not set up yet.”
  • Groups: one voucher, to the lead guest (B7.3).
  • Two sends are new every time, by design: the desk's Send check-in link (each press is a new message), and a review request asked by hand, which is not refused a second time.

Watch out

  • After the third failed try nobody is told; the Guest messages screen shows it as failed. Look there when a guest says nothing arrived.
  • Read from the code while writing this book, not tried: the switch-on moment is recorded once for the whole system, so a hotel added later, or one that switches its vouchers off and on again, may send its backlog outside the quiet hours. Reported for checking.

B7.9A hotel with nothing set up

MissingWhat happens
No menuThe Till: “There is no menu yet”, “Nothing can be sold until the hotel enters what it sells. The prices are yours - this system ships none.” The Tables pad says the same; the Terminal, “Nothing on the menu”.
No tables“No tables have been laid out yet.” The owner, an admin or the GM get a button to set them up (D25-25).
No price for a nightNew booking shows the charges, GST and Due as a dash and says “No price for …. Set it on Rates, or type a rate on the line.” Saving without a typed rate is refused. A date with no price is sent to the channel manager as closed, so no booking site sells it (D17-81, D27-194).
No rooms“No rooms set up yet”, “Add them in Room types.” (D17-23). A hotel with no rooms reports nothing, because occupancy divides by rooms.
No GST rule for roomsThe guest is still checked in, but no room charge is posted, and the night audit refuses until the rule is set (D27-205, B7.4).
No banquet tax headingA function is warned when it is set up, and its bill is refused until the heading is set (D27-124).

Why it works this way

No default prices, anywhere: an unpriced thing shows a dash, never a zero, and nothing is ever charged at a figure nobody typed (HANDOVER § 5). A zero is allowed only when somebody ticks Free (D27-120). A night with no price is sent to the channel manager as closed, without anybody pressing anything, because the channel manager cannot take a price back once it has one (D17-81).

Watch out

  • "Add them in Room types" has no link, and Room types now lives in Settings, under Rooms.

B7.10Cash over the limit, and a payment larger than the bill

  • ₹2 lakh or more in cash from one guest is refused (Income-tax Act s.186): “Cash of ₹2,00,000 or more from one guest is not allowed (Income-tax Act s.186).”, then how much more may be cash, and the other ways to take the rest. At the desk the cash is counted across the stay, its group, and everything this guest paid in cash today on any stay; refunds do not bring it down (D25-40, D26-8). At the till, this bill's cash (D26-10).
  • More than ₹1 lakh in cash at one time needs the guest's PAN, or Form 97 ticked; a guest from abroad is not asked (D26-9, D26-10).
  • At the desk, a payment larger than the bill is held until the clerk ticks Hold it as the guest's credit: “This is ₹500.00 more than the bill; it will be held as the guest's credit.” It is refunded at check-out; no money is held for guests who have left (D27-4, D27-11, D27-12).
  • At the till the payments must equal the bill; extra cash is change, shown as Change due.
  • Cash with no drawer: the desk's drawer opens by itself the first time a receptionist takes cash after the audit; the restaurant refuses cash only before its very first float is counted (D27-200, D27-201).

B7.11Two people at once, or a double tap

Pressed twiceWhat stops a second one
A charge or payment at the deskEach press carries a key; the server answers a repeat with the line already posted, and the database refuses a second line with the same key. One guest's payments take turns (D27-2, D27-89).
Check-in, check-outThe booking is locked: “Already checked in.”, “This stay has already departed.”
A late check-out, pressed again after the guest paidThe stay keeps the reason, the charge or the waiver it already has: the window is not asked again and nothing is charged twice. On 13 October the second Check out asked for the reason again, replaced the first one and posted the late charge a second time (D27-314).
Reversing a lineA line can be reversed once; two clerks pressing Reverse together give the money back once (tested by racing them).
Settling a restaurant billThe order is locked: “This order is already settled.”
Send to the kitchenOnly unsent dishes go: “Everything on this order is already with the kitchen. Add something first.”
Close unpaid, Clear“That order is not open.”, “That table is already clear.”
The night auditOne record per day and a lock (B7.4).
Giving one room twiceThe database lets one through (B7.1).

Buttons are also disabled while a save is in flight. Before these guards a button pressed twice took two rooms for one walk-in (MEMORY 145), and a double tap could post a charge or payment twice (D27-89).

B7.12Arrivals out of the ordinary

  • Checking in days early is allowed, but warned and confirmed, naming the new nights and amount; the room hold moves with it (D27-193, D27-205).
  • Checking in and out the same day: the guest owes that night; check-out is refused until it is paid, or a manager reverses it with a reason (D27-205).
  • A day use is charged its typed day price with GST at check-in, never by the night audit, and does not take the room out of that night's sale. Change dates will not turn a day use into nights or the reverse: “A day use stays a day use: its price is the day's. To stay the night, book the nights.” (D27-227, D27-229, D27-230).
  • An advance before check-in, where the hotel asks one, is never asked of a company's booking, a room the host pays for, a complimentary room, or a booking prepaid on a booking site; there is no override, and the refusal names the amount (D27-243, D27-246).
  • A no-show who did arrive: only the retention charge is taken off on Closed days; putting the booking back is the desk's, separately (D24-7).

B7.13A business date behind the real day

  • Every screen says so in the top bar: “Business date 11 Sep, 21 days behind today (2 Oct). Close the days in Night audit.” (D27-237). All properties shows the same under "Needs you".
  • System health: "Up to date", amber "Yesterday not closed yet", red "Behind by 2 days" and more (D27-113).
  • Everything is still recorded, on the hotel's business date, never the clock's: a check-in at 5 a.m. before the audit belongs to the day not yet closed (D27-200). The only refusal is a booking arriving before the business date.
  • Other devices read the date again whenever a screen opens, so none keeps yesterday's date after the audit (D27-89).
  • Catching up means closing the days one by one, each with its checks (B7.4).

Why it works this way

A hotel's day ends when somebody closes it, not at midnight: a 00:40 receipt once landed on the wrong day because the clock was trusted (MEMORY 19). A day not closed is safe, because nothing is lost and nothing is charged twice, and it is loud, because every screen says so.

Chapter B8

Tests and checks

For the owner. What is checked before any change is called finished: each of the automatic checks (the "gates"), what each one proves and what it cannot prove, the latest counts, the habit of making a test fail before trusting it, and the check that keeps this book current.

B8.1Why there are gates at all

A change to the system is three kinds of risk at once: it may not do what was asked, it may break something it never touched, and it may work on this computer and fail on the server. Nobody can check all of that by eye, across every screen and a database built up by 211 migrations. So every change is run past the same set of automatic checks, called gates, and is finished only when all of them pass.

Three habits sit around the gates, and they come from your own rules (HANDOVER § 5, AGENTS.md):

  • Open the screen before saying it works. Most of the faults in the project's list of mistakes (MEMORY.md) were found by using the system, not by a gate.
  • Run the checks you quote. "2,546 tests pass" is only true if they were run on that exact code, in that session.
  • A guard is not a guard until it has refused something. A new test is trusted only after it has been seen to fail with the fault put back (B8.6).

Why it works this way

Since 19 September nothing leaves this machine (B9.2). Before that, the same checks also ran on a GitHub server on every push, and a push was not finished until that run was green (MEMORY 300). With no pushes, that second opinion is gone: a green run of scripts/gates.sh on this PC is the whole of the proof, so it is never skipped and never shortened before a merge or a release.

B8.2The full run: scripts/gates.sh

One command runs every gate, one after another, on the copy of the code it sits in:

  1. bash scripts/gates.sh <label> runs everything. This is the run that counts.
  2. bash scripts/gates.sh <label> quick runs only the type checks, the strip check and the website tests (about four minutes), for checking work in progress. It says on its last line that the rest were not run.

The full run has ten steps. The website build (B8.3) is run straight after it, by hand and again by the release script.

StepWhat it doesWhat it provesWhat it cannot prove
web typesReads the whole website's code and checks every piece fits the next (TypeScript, tsc).No screen passes the wrong kind of thing to another: a date where a price belongs, a missing field.That anything does the right thing. It also cannot see a fault that only shows when the page runs.
api typesThe same for the server's code.The same, for the server.The same.
stripReads every server file the way the live server loads it (Node's "strip types" mode) and names any line it cannot load. 216 files on 9 October.The server can start with this code.It is not a type check, and it proves nothing about behaviour.
web testsRuns the website's automatic tests (Vitest): each screen drawn with stand-in data and clicked through, and the project's own guards (B8.6).The screens behave as their tests describe; no service reaches into another; the menu, the migrations and this book follow their rules.That the real server answers the same way. The website tests use stand-in data, not the database.
api testsRuns the server's tests against a fresh database made for the run, migrated and filled with the demo hotel, and thrown away afterwards, pass or fail.Each route does what it should and refuses what it should, against a real PostgreSQL with the real rules.That WhatsApp, email, Google, Drive, the CRS or the channel manager really answer: those are stand-ins in the tests.
databaseBuilds an empty scratch database, applies every migration from the first, then runs the database's own assertions: the core suite, one file per service, and the isolation suite.The constraints, triggers and money rules hold (for example, the ledger only grows: a wrong line is reversed by a line of its own, never edited or deleted). The isolation suite runs as the application's own login and proves one hotel cannot read another's rows.That the screens use those rules well.
replayBuilds a scratch database, migrates it, adds a hotel as a real database would have, then applies every migration again.An update can be installed on a database that already holds data. Every deploy does exactly this.That a particular live database has no oddity the scratch one lacks.
pg16The database suite and the replay once more, on PostgreSQL 16.15, in a database of its own on this PC.Nothing in the code needs PostgreSQL 17 (this PC's version) when the live server runs 16.15.Anything about the server other than its database version.
restore 1Builds the demo hotel and two others, takes a backup, deletes one booking with its bill and guest, changes a room, then runs the one-hotel restore tool (deploy/restore-hotel.sh): a look, a refused wrong code, then the bring-back.Only what is missing comes back, exactly as it was; a record changed since stays as it is now; bill lines, payments and the invoice series are listed, never written; no other hotel moves.That last night's real backup is sound, or what the live server's own rules add on the way in. Your first look on the server proves that (B9.6).
to minuteOn PostgreSQL 16.15, in a throw-away server of its own: the journal saved and copied to a folder standing in for the bucket, a weekly base copy, a delete, then the system rebuilt to the minute before it as a new database beside the live one.Restore to any minute brings back what was there at that minute, refuses a minute past the last journal piece, and the alarms turn red when the journal stops.That the real bucket and the server's own settings work: the owner's one rehearsal on the server proves that (B9.6).

Why each step is there

  • strip: on 8 September one line of perfectly valid code took the live API down in a restart loop after three clean builds and every test had passed, because the live server loads code in a stricter way than any test did (MEMORY 209). The server's update script now runs the same check before it restarts anything.
  • api tests on a throw-away database: the tests once shared the database people were using. Clean-ups that did too little filled the demo with phantom guests; one that did too much deleted a real banquet booking somebody had just made (MEMORY 120). Each run now builds its own database and drops it.
  • database, as the application's login: a test run as the database's superuser passes every privacy rule, because a superuser ignores them. The isolation suite connects as the application does, so an open door shows.
  • replay: an early attempt to answer "can the migrations run twice?" was made on a real database, half-applied, and the database had to be rebuilt (MEMORY 119). Later, older migrations quietly undid newer ones on a second run (MEMORY 284, 293, 299). The replay runs on a scratch database holding a hotel, so it catches both.
  • pg16: the live server runs PostgreSQL 16.15 while this PC runs 17. A backup made on 17 could not be read by 16 (MEMORY 190); a migration using something only 17 knows would stop a live update half-way. Your yes, 4 October.
  • restore 1 and to minute: a restore is only needed on a bad day, which is the worst day to find it broken. A database change could quietly stop either one working; run on every release, they cannot break unseen. Your yes, 29 October (D27-376, D27-377).

B8.3The build, and "no test sign-in in the build"

npm run build compiles the website into the files Firebase serves. Its last step reads every built file and fails the build if any trace of the test sign-ins is there: the Owner, General Manager and Reception buttons that sign in on this PC without a password, and the guest page's development-only code display. A good build ends with “✓ no test sign-in in dist (40 files checked)”.

There is a second lock on the server: the API refuses to start at all when the test sign-in is switched on and it is running as production.

npm run build:app, used for a release, does the same and writes the live API's address into the website's settings file. It refuses an address that is missing or not https.

Why it works this way

Your instruction of 14 September: keep the test sign-ins simple on this PC and remove them from production. A passwordless owner sign-in on the live page would let a stranger in as you; it happened once, on the live login page, before the check existed (MEMORY 193). A build that succeeds says nothing about what it contains, so the check reads the output itself.

Watch out

  • The build is not one of the ten steps of gates.sh. It is run beside it, and the release script (B9.3) builds again in the release copy and checks the result. Twice the gates were green and the website would not build (MEMORY 337, 378).

B8.5A run is judged by what it did, not what it printed

  • Each step is judged by its exit code, the yes-or-no a program hands back, never by its summary line (MEMORY 274). A summary can say "all tests passed" while a whole test file failed while tidying up (MEMORY 25, 361).
  • And by its last line. A check killed from outside on Windows reports "success" with its log cut short; one database step "passed" in 22 seconds that way (MEMORY 333). Each test step now names the line a passing run ends with (“all 1578 assertions passed”), and a run without it is marked “CUT SHORT” and failed.
  • The run records what it judged. The first line of its progress file names the exact commit, whether it was a full or quick run, and dirty if the copy had changes not yet committed. The release script refuses a release unless a full, clean, green run exists for exactly the release's commit (B9.3).
  • One run at a time. Several at once exhausted the machine on 18 September and a whole round produced nothing. The steps that build databases also wait their turn in a queue shared by every working copy on the machine (MEMORY 341): two copies building at once collided on the shared database logins.
  • A step that writes as it goes. Each step writes a line to .local\gates\progress.txt as it finishes, so a run in progress can be watched. You stopped a run on 18 September because twenty minutes passed with no sign of life.

B8.6"Fails first": making a test prove itself

A test that passes proves nothing until it has been seen to fail. So every new guard is proven the same way:

  1. Write the test, and see it pass on the fixed code.
  2. Put the fault back: change the code to what it was, or break the one line the test is about.
  3. Run the test. It must fail, and fail for the right reason.
  4. Put the code back exactly as it was, byte for byte, and see it pass again.

The changelog says, for every change, which guards were proven this way. For the work of 9 October: custom add-ons, 6 server guards and 5 screen guards; the KOT section, 7 server and 6 screen guards. One of them passed with its fault put back: "Print here" cleared the waiting bills in two places, so removing one proved nothing. The two were folded into one, and then the test failed as it should.

Why it works this way

Eleven guards in this project once passed with the very fault they were written for put back (MEMORY 166, 195): a test compared a number with itself, a test that inserted nothing could never find anything, a check that quietly skipped when its subject was missing. Each looked like protection and was not. A test that has failed on purpose at least once is known to be looking at the right thing.

The guards in the website suite

Some tests check no screen at all: they keep the code in the shape your decisions gave it.

GuardWhat it refuses
boundaries.test.tsA service reaching into another's insides. Each service is used only through its front door, so a change inside the restaurant cannot quietly break finance (the service folders, 15 September).
migrationNumbers.test.tsTwo database changes with the same number, or a gap. The database's history is one sequence, replayed from the first on every update.
navigation.test.tsMenu entries that break the naming rules: two entries with one name, a word not in sentence case.
repositories.test.ts ("Rule 2b")A data function no screen calls: a capability nobody can reach. This is the guard that failed on 9 October (B8.4).
App.test.tsxA guarded address the menu does not know, which would otherwise be open to every role.
manual.test.tsThis book falling behind the system (B8.7).

B8.7The book's own check

Your rule of 9 October: a change to a screen updates its chapter in the same commit, and a test fails when the book falls behind (D27-293). src/test/manual.test.ts runs with the website tests and checks three things:

  1. Every menu screen of a written chapter's part is named in it. Each part of the menu that has its chapter is listed in the test; the restaurant's menu (Point of sale) is covered by A8 today. A new screen in that menu fails the test until A8 says what it is.
  2. manual.html is built from the chapters as they are. The book is one file per chapter; docs/manual/tools/build.mjs joins them. Nobody edits the joined book by hand.
  3. Every picture a chapter shows exists in docs/manual/img.

Each of the three was seen to fail before it was trusted (B8.6).

Watch out

  • When a chapter is added or changed, check 2 fails until the book is built again. When several people write at once, only the person merging runs the build (docs/manual/WRITING.md).
  • Part B chapters are not tied to a menu section, so check 1 does not cover them: keeping them true is a matter of writing, not of a test.

B8.8What no gate can see

The gates are necessary and they are not enough. These are the known blind spots:

The server is not this PC. Every gate runs on Windows here. Eight faults were found in one afternoon of the first deploy (scripts that were not marked runnable on Linux, Windows-only paths, the server's security layer, a backup the older database could not read), with every check green throughout (MEMORY 187 to 193, 197).The strip and pg16 steps, which copy two of the server's differences; the server's own readiness check (preflight) at every update (B9.3); a read-only look at live after a release.

A server route no screen calls. The website has a guard for its own unused functions (B8.6); the server has none yet.Done once by hand on 16 September (13 such routes found). Making it a test is open work (PENDING.md § 5).

The latest, a restaurant printing test that lost a race on a busy machine, was fixed on 9 October (POS-32).Each one is fixed when it is caught, and written down. Testing by hand, on this PC

  • The demo hotel, 5 Elements Akkalkot (5EL), in the local database, with made-up guests, loaded so that its business date is the real day (D27-193).
  • Two virtual printers stand in for the KOT and bill printers (B9.11), so every restaurant flow can be tried with no printer.
  • The test sign-ins (Owner, General Manager, Reception, and View as) let one person see each role's screens. They exist on this PC only (B8.3).

Running it

For the owner. Where the system runs, the rule that nothing leaves this machine, how a release is made and what the releases so far taught, the server's settings, backups and how to get one back, what watches the system, what to do when something breaks, the computer the work is done on, and the virtual printers used for testing.
